author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, whether they were mentioned in the Qur’an.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, in the words of Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic: ‘O you who believe,
bow and prostrate’.” (Surah Hajj 22:77)
I asked: “What is the minimum required for ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?”
Imam {a.s} said: “As for what suffices you in ‘ruku’, it is to say three ‘tasbihat’, ‘Subhan
Allah, Subhan Allah’ three times. And whoever is able to lengthen the ‘ruku’ and
‘sujud’, let him lengthen them as much as he is able. That should be in glorifying Allah
{SWT}, praising Him {SWT}, magnifying Him {SWT}, supplicating, and showing humility, for the
closest a servant is to his Lord {AZJ} is when he is in ‘sujud’.
As for the imam (of prayer), when he leads the people in prayer, he should not prolong
it for them, for among them are the weak and those who have needs. Indeed, the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, used to lighten the prayer
when leading the people.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرُّكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ هَلْ
نَزَلَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ قَوْلُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اِرْكَعُوا وَ أُسْجُدُوا» » فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ حَدْ ٱلرُّكُوعِ
وَ السَّجُودِ فَقَالَ «أَمّا مَا يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فَثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ ثَلاَثاً وَ مَنْ كَانَ
يَقْوَى عَلَى أَنْ يُطَوِّلَ الرُّكُوعَ وَ السُّجَودَ فَلْيُطَوَّلْ مَا اِسْتَطَاعَ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ فِي تَسْبِيحِ اللّهِ وَ تَحْمِيدِهِ وَ تَمْجِيدِهِ وَ
الدُّعَاءٍ وَ التَّضَرُّع فَإِنَّ أَقْرَبَ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ إِلَى رَبِّهِ وَ هُوَ سَاجِدٌ فَأَمّا ٱلْإِمَامُ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا قَامَ بِالنَّاسِ فَلاَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ
يُطَوِّلَ بِهِمْ فَإِنَّ فِي النَّاسِ الضَّعِيفَ وَ مَنْ لَهُ الْحَاجَةُ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللّهِ صَلِّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ إِذَا صَلِّى بِالنَّاسِ
خَفَّ بِهِمْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.77 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.706 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.3 p.910
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
text_chunk:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, whether they were mentioned in the Qur’an.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, in the words of Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic: ‘O you who believe,
bow and prostrate’.” (Surah Hajj 22:77)
I asked: “What is the minimum required for ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?”
Imam {a.s} said: “As for what suffices you in ‘ruku’, it is to say three ‘tasbihat’, ‘Subhan
Allah, Subhan Allah’ three times. And whoever is able to lengthen the ‘ruku’ and
‘sujud’, let him lengthen them as much as he is able. That should be in glorifying Allah
{SWT}, praising Him {SWT}, magnifying Him {SWT}, supplicating, and showing humility, for the
closest a servant is to his Lord {AZJ} is when he is in ‘sujud’.
As for the imam (of prayer), when he leads the people in prayer, he should not prolong
it for them, for among them are the weak and those who have needs. Indeed, the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, used to lighten the prayer
when leading the people.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “What is the lightest (minimum) amount of ‘tasbih’ in
prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Three ‘tasbihat’ with calm and clear recitation (‘tarassul’), saying:
‘Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah’.”
text_ar:
وَعَنَهُ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَ أَخَفٌ مَا يَكُونُ
مِنَ التَّسْبِيحِ فِي الصَّلاَةِ قَالَ «ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ مُتَرَسَّلاً تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللهِ ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.77 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.324 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.707 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.303

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Hariz from
Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “When you intend to go into bowing (ruku‘),
say while you are standing upright: ‘Allahu Akbar’, then bow and say:
‘My Lord {AZJ}, for You {AZJ} have I bowed, to You {AZJ} have I submitted, in You {AZJ} have I
believed, upon You {AZJ} have I relied, and You {AZJ} are my Lord {AZJ}. My hearing, my sight,
my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my brain, my nerves, my bones, and everything
my feet carry have humbled themselves to You {AZJ}, not arrogantly, nor proudly, nor
with weariness. Glory be to my Lord {AZJ}, the Mighty, and praise be to Him {AZJ}’, three
times, in a calm and deliberate manner (tarassul).
And in your bowing, align your feet, placing between them the distance of one span.
Place your palms firmly on your knees. Put your right hand on your right knee before
the left, press the tips of your fingers on the center of the kneecap, and spread your
fingers when placing them on your knees. Keep your back straight and extend your
neck, and let your gaze be between your feet.
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Then say: ‘Sami‘a Allahu liman hamidah’ (Allah {SWT} hears the one who praises Him
{AZJ}), while you are upright standing, and say: ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’ (Praise
be to Allah {SWT}, the Lord of the worlds), the One worthy of majesty, sovereignty, and
greatness. ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’, say it aloud.
Then raise your hands with the takbir and go down into prostration (sujud).”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: «إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ فَقُلْ وَ أَنْتَ مُنتَصِبٌ - اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ ثُمَّ اِرْكَغْ وَ قُلْ رَبِّ لَكَ رَكَفْتُ وَ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ وَ بِكَ
آَمَنْتُ وَ عَلَيْكَ تَوَكِّلْتُ وَ أَنْتَ رَبِّي خَشَعَ لَكَ سَمْعِي وَ بَصَرِي وَ شَعْرِي وَ بَشَرِي وَ لَحْمِي وَ دَمِي وَ مُخَي وَ عَصَبِي
وَ عِظَامِي وَ مَا أَقَلَّثهُ قَدَمَايَ غَيْرَ مُسْتَنْكِفٍ وَ لا مُسْتَكْبِرٍ وَ لاَ مُسْتَحْسِرٍ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ
فِي تَرَسُلٍ وَ تَصُفُّ فِي رُكُوعِكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ تَجْعَلُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرَ شِبْرٍ وَ تُمَكِّنُ رَاحَتَيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَنَيْكَ وَ تَضَّعُ يَدَكَ
الْيُمْنَى عَلَى رُكْبَتِكَ الْيُمْنَى قَبْلَ الْيُسْرَى وَ تَلْقُمُ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِكَ عَيْنَ الرُّكْبَةِ وَ فَرِّجْ أَصَابِعَكَ إِذَا وَضَعْتَهَا عَلَى
رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ أَقِمْ صُلْبَكَ وَ مُدَّ عُنُقَكَ وَ لَيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ ثُمَّ قُلْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ وَ أَنْتَ مُنْتَصِبٌ قَائِمٌ
«الْحَمْدُ لِلهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ» أَهلَ ٱلْجَبَرُوتِ وَ ٱلْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَ ٱلْعَظَمَةِ «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ» تَجْهَرُ بِهَا صَوْتَكَ ثُمَّ تَرْفَعُ
يَدَيْكَ بالتَّكْبِيرٍ وَ تَخِرُ سَاجِداً».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.319 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.77 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.701 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.295

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from a man from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you raise your head from bowing (ruku‘), straighten your
back, for there is no prayer for the one who does not straighten his back.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا رَفَعْتَ
رَأْسَكَ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فَأْقِمْ صُلْبَكَ فَإِنَّهُ لا صَلاَةَ لِمَنْ لاَ يُقِيمُ صُلْبَهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.320 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.703 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.321
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah {a.s} placing his hands before his knees when He {a.s} went into
prostration (sujud), and when He {a.s} wanted to rise, He {a.s} would raise his knees before
his hands.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْعَلَاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَضَّعُ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ
إِذَا سَجَدَ وَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَقُومَ رَفَعَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ قَبْلَ يَدَيْهِ.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.713 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.337
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN

And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala’, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who places his hands before his knees during
prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes (it is permissible).”
text_ar:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ ٱلْجَوْهَرِيّ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ
يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.325 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.713 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.338

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
He {a.s} was asked about a man who places his hands on the ground before his knees.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes,” meaning in prayer.
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ قَالَ
«نَعَمْ» يَعْنِي فِي الصَّلاَةِ.

He {a.s} was asked about a man who places his hands on the ground before his knees.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes,” meaning in prayer.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “There is no harm if a man, when praying, places his knees on
the ground before his hands.”

Scholar's Note:
For it is to be understood as applying to a case of necessity, and to one who is unable
to touch the ground with his hands first due to an ailment or illness.
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ إِذَا صَلَّى الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَضَعَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ يَدَيْهِ».
فانه محمول على حال الضرورة ومن لا يتمكن من تلقي الارض باليدين أولا لعلة أو مرض.
commentary:
For it is to be understood as applying to a case of necessity, and to one who is unable
to touch the ground with his hands first due to an ailment or illness.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman
from al-Halabi:

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah
ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs al-A‘war:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When (Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, performed
prostration, He {a.s} would collapse as the emaciated camel collapses, meaning the
way it kneels down.”

Scholar's Note:
If it is said: You have mentioned narrations that include the permissibility of limiting
oneself to a single tasbihah (saying "Subhan Allah") in bowing and prostration, while
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id and others have narrated what repels you from that: (see following
narration)
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ
سِئَانٍ عَنْ حَفْص الْأَعْوَرِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلَامُ قَالَ: «كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ إِذَا سَجَدَ يَتَخَوْى كَمَا يَتَخَوَّى
اَلْبَعِيرُ الضَامِرُ يَغِنِي بُرُوكَهُ».
فان قيل قد ذكرتم من الروايات ما يتضمن جواز الاقتصار على تسبيحة واحدة في الركوع والسجود، وقد روى الحسين
بن سعيد وغيره ما يدفعكم عن ذلك.

Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Safwan, from Misma‘:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “It does not suffice a man in his prayer with less than three
tasbihat or their equivalent.”

أَقَلُّ مِنْ ثَلاثِ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ أَوْ قَدْرِهِنَّ».

And from him, from al-Nadr, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Dawud al-Abzari:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “The minimum of tasbih is three times while you are in
prostration, do not hasten through them.”

وَعَنْهُ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ يَحْيَى الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ دَاوُدَ ٱلْأَبْزَارِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱَلسَّلامُ قَالَ: «أَدْنَى التَسْبِيحِ ثَلاَثُ
مَرَّاتٍ وَ أَنْتَ سَاجِدٌ لاَ تَعْجَلْ بِهِنَّ».

text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the minimum that suffices of tasbih in bowing and prostration.
Imam {a.s} said: “Three tasbihat.”

Scholar's Note:
So how do you reconcile these reports? It was said to him: The first thing we say is that
we do not permit a person to suffice with only one tasbih when they have the ability to
do more; rather, we only allowed that in cases of necessity and valid excuses. As for
when there is ability and choice, then that is not permitted.
And we only permitted limiting it to one tasbih when a specific phrase is mentioned,
which is to say: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih’ in bowing, or ‘Subhana Rabbi
al-A‘la wa bi-hamdih’ in prostration. But if one says only ‘Subhan Allah’, then it is not
permissible to say it less than three times.
Also, none of these reports state that whoever does less than three tasbihat, then his
prayer is invalid. It is possible that what was meant by them was the negation of
perfection and merit, not invalidation. And what clarifies what we have mentioned is:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ التَّسْبِيحِ فِي الرُّكُوعِ
وَ السُّجُودِ فَقَالَ «ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ».
فكيف تجمعون بين هذه الاخبار؟ قيل له : أول ما نقول أنا لا نجوز ان يقتصر الانسان على مرة واحدة من التسبيح مع
الاختيار وإنما جوزنا ذلك عند الضرورة والاعذار فاما مع الاختيار فلا يجوز ذلك ولانا إنما جوزنا الاقتصار على مرة واحدة
إذا ذكر تسبيحا مخصوصا وهو أن يقول: (سبحان ربي العظيم وبحمده) في الركوع أو (سبحان ربي الاعلى وبحمده) في
السحود فاما اذا قال : (سحان الله) فحسب فلا بحون اقا من ثلاث مرات وايضا لس ف شء من هذه الاخيار ان م.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu
Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I said to (Imam) Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him: “What is the limit of bowing and
prostration?”
Imam {a.s} said: “You say ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih’ three times in bowing,
and ‘Subhana Rabbi al-A‘la wa bi-hamdih’ three times in prostration. So whoever
omits one has omitted one-third of his prayer, and whoever omits two has omitted
two-thirds of his prayer, and whoever does not perform tasbih, then he has no prayer.”

Scholar's Note:
So this report indicates that they only intended to negate perfection and merit. Do you
not see that they said: whoever omits one has omitted a third of his prayer, and
whoever omits two has omitted two-thirds of his prayer? If the matter were not as we
have mentioned, then there would be no difference between failing to say one tasbih,
which, according to that interpretation, would invalidate the prayer, and failing to say
all of them, which indeed does invalidate the prayer. And yet, we know that they made
a distinction.
Moreover, we have already clarified in previous narrations what explicitly states that
one tasbih is obligatory, and whatever is beyond that is recommended. This is in the
narration of Hisham ibn Salim when he asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the tasbih, and
Imam {a.s} said to him: You say ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim’ in bowing and ‘Subhana Rabbi
al-A’la’ in prostration. Then Imam {a.s} said: The obligation of that is one tasbih, the
sunnah is three, and the merit is in seven, and this is explicit in what we have said.
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ الْحَضْرَمِيَّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ
لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَيْ شَيْءٍ حَدُّ الرُكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ قَالَ «تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاثاً فِي
اَلرُكُوعِ وَ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثاً فِي السُّجُودِ فَمَنْ نَقَصَ وَاحِدَةً نَقَصَ ثُلُثَ صَلاَتِهِ وَ مَنْ نَقَصَ اِثْنَتَيْنِ
نَقَصَ ثُلْثَيْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يُسَبِّحْ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ».
فدل هذا الخبر على أنهم إنما نفوا الكمال والفضل ألا ترى انهم قالوا من نقص واحدة نقص ثلث صلاته ومن نقص اثنتين
نقص ثلثي صلاته فلو لا أن الامر على ما ذكرناه كان لا فرق بين الاخلال بواحدة في أن ذلك يبطل الصلاة وبين الاخلال
بالجميع الذي يبطل الصلاة وقد علمنا انهم فرقوا ، مع انا قد بينا فيما تقدم من الاخبار ما يصرح بان الواحدة فريضة وما
زاد عليه مسنون وهو رواية هشام بن سالم حين سأل أبا عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام عن التسبيح فقال له تقول : (سبحان ربي
العظيم) ف الكوع وف السحود (سحان اي الاعل ) ثم قال الفريضة من ذلك تسحة والسنة ثلاث والفضا ف سبع

whoever omits two has omitted two-thirds of his prayer? If the matter were not as we
have mentioned, then there would be no difference between failing to say one tasbih,
which, according to that interpretation, would invalidate the prayer, and failing to say
all of them, which indeed does invalidate the prayer. And yet, we know that they made
a distinction.
Moreover, we have already clarified in previous narrations what explicitly states that

مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَوْماً
«يَا حَمَّادُ تُحْسِنُ أَنْ تُصَلَّيَ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ يَا سَيَّدِي أَنَا أَحْفَظُ كِتَابَ حَرِيزٍ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «لاَ عَلَيْكَ يَا حَمَّادُ قُمْ
فَصَلِّ» قَالَ فَقُمْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مُتَوَجِّها إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ فَاسْتَفْتَحْتُ الصّلاَةَ فَرَكَعْتُ وَ سَجَدْتُ فَقَالَ «يَا حَمَادُ لاَ تُحْسِنُ
أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ مَا أَقْبَحَ بِالرَّجُلِ مِنْكُمْ يَأْتِي عَلَيْهِ سِتُونَ سَنَةً أَوْ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً فَلاَ يُقِيمُ صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً بِحُدُودِهَا تَامَّةً)
قَالَ حَمَّادٌ فَأَصَابَنِي فِي نَفْسِي الذُّلُ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتْ فِدَاكَ فَعَلَّمْنِي الصَّلاةَ فَقَامَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلَامُ مُسْتَقْبِلَ
اَلْقِبْلَةِ مُنْتَصِباً فَأَرْسَلَ يَدَيْهِ جَمِيعاً عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ قَدْ ضَمَّ أَصَابِعَهُ وَ قَرَّبَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْهِ حَتَّى كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرُ ثَلاَثِ
أَصَابِعَ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ بِأَصَابِعِ رِجْلَيْهِ جَمِيعاً الْقِبْلَةَ لَمْ يُحَرِّفُهَا عَنِ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ قَالَ بِخَشوعِ « اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ » ثُمَّ قَرَأَ
الْحَمْدَ بِتَرْتِيلٍ وَ «قُل هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُمَّ صَبَرَ هُنَيْئَةً بِقَدْرِ مَا يَتَنَفَسُ وَ هَوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ جِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ وَ قَالَ
« اللهُ أَكْبَرُ » وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَكَعَ وَ مَلَاً كَفَّيْهِ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ رَدَّ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى خَلْفِهِ ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى ظَهْرُهُ حَتَّى
لَوْصُبَّ عَلَيْهِ قَطْرَةٌ مِنْ مَاءِ أَوْ دُهْنٍ لَمْ تَزُلُ لإِسْتِوَاءِ ظَهْرِهِ وَ مَدَّ عُنْقَهُ وَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ ثَلاَثاً بِتَرْتِيلٍ فَقَالَ
« سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ » ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى قَائِماً فَلَمَّا اِسْتَمْكَنَ مِنَ الْقِيَامِ قَالَ » سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ » ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ
وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ جِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ ثُمّ سَجَدَ وَ بَسَطَ كَفَّيْهِ مَضْمُومَتَي الْأَصَابِعِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ جِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ
فَقَالَ « سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ » ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئًا مِنْ جَسَدِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ - وَ سَجَدَ عَلَى
ثَمَانِيَةِ أَعْظُمِ الْكَفِّيْنِ وَ الرُكْبَتَيْنِ وَ أَنَامِلِ إِنْهَامَي الرَّجْلَيْنِ وَ الْجَبْهَةِ وَ الْأَتْفِ وَ قَالَ «سَبْعْ مِنْهَا فَرْضَ يُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهَا
وَ هِيَ الَّتِي ذَكَرَهَا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَ قَالَ «وَ أَنَّ الْمَسْاجِدَ لِلْهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللهِ أَحَداً» وَ هِيَ الْجَبْهَةُ وَ
الْكَفَّانِ وَ الرُّكْبَتَانِ وَ الْإِبْهَامَانِ وَ وَضْعُ الْأَنْفِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ سُنَّةٌ» ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ السُّجُودِ فَلَمَّا اِسْتَوَى جَالِساً
قَالَ « اللهُ أَكْبَرُ » ثُمَّ قَعَدَ عَلَى فَخِذِهِ الْأَيْسَرِ قَدْ وَضَعَ قَدَمَهُ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ عَلَى بَطْنِ قَدَمِهِ الْأَيْسَرِ وَ قَالَ « أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
رَبِّي وَ أَتُوبُ إلَيْهِ» ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ وَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ الثَّانِيَةِ وَ قَالَ كَمَا قَالَ فِي الْأَولَى وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئًا مِنْ
بَدَنِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فِي رُكُوعِ وَ لا سُجُودٍ وَ كَانَ مُجَنِّحاً وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ ذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فَصَلَّى رَكِّعَتَيْنِ عَلَى هَذَا
وَ يَدَاهُ مَضْمُومَةُ الْأَصَابِعِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ فِي التّشَهُدِ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ التّشَهُدِ سَلَّمَ فَقَالَ «يَا حَمَّادُ هَكَذَا صَلِّ».

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn
‘Awwad, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I saw Him {a.s}, when He {a.s} raised his head from the second prostration of the first
rak‘ah, He {a.s} would sit until He {a.s} was at ease, then He {a.s} would stand.
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ الْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ بْنِ عَوَّاضٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُهُ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ السَّجْدَةِ الثَانِيَةِ مِنَ الرَكْعَةِ الْأُولَى جَلَسَ حَتَّى يَطْمَئِنَ ثُمَ يَقُومُ.

Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you raise your head from the second prostration in the
first rak‘ah, when you intend to stand, then sit upright first, then stand.”
text_ar:
سَمَاعَةُ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «إِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ السَّجْدَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ
الْأُولَى جِينَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَقُومَ فَاسْتَوِ جَالِساً ثُمَّ قُمْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Ali ibn al-Hakam from Rahim, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, I see
you, when you pray and raise your head from prostration in the first and third rak‘ah,
you sit upright before standing. So should we do as you do?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Do not look at what I do, do what you have been commanded to do.”

Scholar's Note:
He {a.s}, peace be upon him, only said ‘Do not look at what I do’ so that it would not be
assumed that it is obligatory upon them in the manner of an obligation, and not
because He {a.s} forbade following his action in pursuit of virtue and the seeking of
perfection.
And sitting between the two prostrations and between the prostration and the
standing is among the etiquettes (adab) of prayer, not among its obligations (fara’id).
What clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيْ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ رَجِيمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَرَاكَ إِذَا صَلِّيْتَ
فَرَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ مِنَ السُّجُودِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى وَ الثَالِثَةِ تَسْتَوِي جَالِساً ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَنَصْنَعُ كَمَا تَصْنَعُ قَالَ «لا تَنظُرُوا
إِلَى مَا أَصْنَعُ أَنَا اِصْنَعُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ».
إنما قال عليه السلام لا تنظروا الى ما اصنع لئلا يعتقد ان ذلك يلزمهم على طريق الفرض دون أن يكون قد منعه أن يقتدي
بفعله على جهة الفضل وطلب الكمال ، والجلوس بين السجدتين وبين السجود والقيام من آداب الصلاة لا من فرائضها

Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
(Abu Abdillah {a.s} said) “When you sit in prayer, do not sit on your right side, rather, sit
on your left side. And when you prostrate, spread your palms on the ground. And when
you bow, place your knees into your palms.”
text_ar:
عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا جَلَسْتَ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَلاَ تَجْلِسْ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ اِجْلِسْ
عَلَى يَسَارِكَ فَإِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَابْسُطْ كَفَّيْكَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فَإِذَا رَكَفْتَ فَأَلْقِمْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ كَفَّيْكَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, and Muhammad ibn
Isma‘il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from
Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “When you stand in prayer, do not place one
foot directly against the other; rather, leave a gap between them, the minimum being
the width of a finger, and the maximum up to a span. Let your shoulders hang down,
release your arms, and do not interlock your fingers. Let your hands be upon your
thighs, opposite your knees, and let your gaze be toward the place of your prostration.
When you bow, align your position in bowing between your feet, making the distance
between them about a span. Firmly place your palms upon your knees. Place your
right hand on your right knee before the left, and let the tips of your fingers reach the
center of the kneecap. Spread your fingers when placing them on your knees, and if
the tips of your fingers reach in your bowing, reaching your kneecaps, that suffices
you. But what is more beloved to me is that you firmly place your palms on your knees,
so that your fingers are upon the center of the kneecap, and you spread them apart.
Keep your back straight, stretch your neck, and let your gaze be directed to the space
between your feet.
When you intend to go into prostration, raise your hands with the takbir and go down
into prostration, beginning with your hands, place them on the ground before your
knees. Place them together. Do not spread your forearms on the ground like a beast
spreads its forearms, and do not place your forearms on your knees or thighs. Rather,
raise your elbows outward. Do not press your palms to your knees, nor bring them
close to your face, let them be level with your shoulders. Do not place them in front of
your knees, but turn them slightly away from that. Spread them flat on the ground and
draw them toward yourself in a drawing motion. If there is a cloth beneath them, it
does not harm you; but if you place them directly on the earth, that is better.
Do not spread your fingers during prostration; rather, keep them joined together.”
Imam {a.s} said: “When you sit in tashahhud, press your knees to the ground and spread
them slightly. Let the top of your left foot be on the ground, and the top of your right
foot on the sole of your left foot. Your buttocks should be on the ground, and the tip of
your right big toe should be on the ground. Beware of sitting on your two feet, for that
causes discomfort, and you will not truly be sitting on the ground, it would be as if you
are sitting part of your body upon another part, and you will not be able to remain
patient in the tashahhud and in supplication.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ
وَ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قُمْتَ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَلاَ تُلْصِقَ قَدَمَكَ بِالْأُخْرَى وَ دَعْ بَيْنَهُمَا فَصْلا إِصْبَعاً أَقَلُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى شِبْرٍ أَكْثَرُهُ
وَ أُسْدُلْ مَنْكِبَيْكَ وَ أَرْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ وَ لا تُشَبِّكْ أَصَابِعَكَ وَ لْتَكُونَا عَلَى فَخِذَيْكَ قُبَالَةَ رُكْبَتِكَ وَ لَيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ إِلَى مَوْضِعٍ
سُجُودِكَ فَإِذَا رَكَعْتَ فَصُفّ فِي رُكُوعِكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ تَجْعَلُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرَ شِبْرٍ وَ تُمَكِّنُ رَاحَتَيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ تَضَعُ
يَدَكَ الْيُمْنَى عَلَى رُكْبَتِكَ الْيُمْنَى قَبْلَ الْيُسْرَى وَ بَلَّغْ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِكَ عَيْنَ الرُّكْبَةِ وَ فَرِّجْ أَصَابِعَكَ إِذَا وَضَعْتَهَ
عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ فَإِنْ وَصَلَتْ أَطْرَافُ أَصَابِعِكَ فِي رُكُوعِكَ إِلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ أَجْرَأَكَ ذَلِكَ وَ أَحَبّ إِلَيَّ أَنْ ثُمَكِّنَ كَفَّيْكَ مِنْ
رُكْبَتَيْكَ فَتَجْعَلَ أَصَابِعَكَ فِي عَيْنِ الرُّكْبَةِ وَ تُفَرِّجَ بَيْنَهُمَا وَ أَقِمْ صُلْبَكَ وَ مُدَّ عُنْقَكَ وَ لَيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ إِلَى مَا بَيْنَ
قَدَمَيْكَ فَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَسْجَدَ فَارْفَعْ يَدَيْكَ بِالتَكْبِيرِ وَ جِرَّ سَاجِداً وَ اِبْدَأُ بِيَدَيْكَ فَضَعْهُمَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْكَ
تَضَعُهُمَا مَعاً وَ لا تَفْتَرِش ذِرَاعَيْكَ اِفْتِرَاشَ السَّبُعِ ذِرَاعَيْهِ وَ لا تَضَعَنَّ ذِرَاعَيْكَ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ فَخِذَيْكَ وَ لَكِنْ
تَجَنَّح بِمِرْفَقَيْكَ وَ لا تُلْزِقْ كَفَّيْكَ بِرُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ لاَ تُذْنِهِمَا مِنْ وَجْهِكَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ حِيَالَ مَنكِبَيْكَ وَ لاَ تَجْعَلْهُمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ
رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ لَكِنْ تُحَرِّفُهُمَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئاً وَ أُبْسُطْهُمَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ بَسْطاً وَ اِقْبِضْهُمَا إِلَيْكَ قَبْضاً وَ إِنْ كَانَ تَحْتَهُمَا
ثَوْبٌ فَلاَ يَضُرُكَ وَ إِنْ أَفْضَيْتَ بِهِمَا إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ وَ لا تُفَرِّجَنَّ بَيْنَ أَصَابِعِكَ فِي سُجُودِكَ وَ لَكِنِ أُضْمُمْهُنَّ
جَمِيعاً قَالَ فَإِذَا قَعَدْتَ فِي تَشَهُدِكَ فَأَلْصِقُ رُكْبَتَيْكَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَ فَرِّج بَيْنَهُمَا شَيْئا وَ لَيَكُنْ ظَاهِرُ قَدَمِكَ ٱلْيُسْرَى عَلَى
الْأَرْضٍ وَظَاهِرُ قَدَمِكَ الْيُمْنَى عَلَى بَاطِنِ قَدَمِكَ ٱلْيُسْرَى وَ أَلْيَتَاكَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَ طَرَفُ إِبْهَامِكَ ٱلْيُمْنَى عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ
وَإِيَّاكَ وَ الْقُعُودَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْكَ فَنَتَأْذَى بِذَلِكَ وَ لا تَكُونُ قَاعِداً عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ إِنَّمَا قَعَدَ بَعْضُكَ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَلا
تَصْبِرَ لِلتَّشَهْدِ وَ الدُّعَاءِ».

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from
Hariz, from a man, from Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him {a.s} regarding the verse: ‘So pray to your Lord and sacrifice”’ (Surah
Kawthar 108:2).
He {a.s} said: “The ‘nahr’ (sacrifice) is uprightness in standing, that one straightens his
back and his neck.”
And Imam {a.s} said: “Do not place your hands on your hips (takfir), for that is what the
Magians do. Do not cover your mouth (talath-thum), do not squat (ihtifaz), do not sit
on your feet (iq‘aʾ), and do not spread your forearms on the ground.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيِى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ «فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَ إِنْحَر» قَالَ «النَّحرُ الاِعْتِدَالُ فِي الْقِيَامِ أَنْ يُقِيمَ صُلْبَهُ وَ نَحْرَهُ» وَ قَالَ «لاَ
تُكَفَّرْ إِنَّمَا يَصْنَعُ ذَلِكَ الْمَجُوسُ وَ لا تَلَثَّمْ وَ لا تَحْتَفِزْ وَ لاَ تُقْعِ عَلَى قَدَمَيْكَ وَ لا تَفْتَرِش ذِرَاعَيْكَ».

text_en:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi
Umayr, from Ja‘far ibn Ali, who said:
I saw Aba al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, and He {a.s} had performed a prostration
after the prayer, and He {a.s} spread his forearms on the ground and pressed his chest
to the ground, while still in his clothes.

Scholar's Note:
So this is specific to the prostration of gratitude (‘Sajdat al-Shukr’), not the prostration
that is within the prayer, because the sunnah in that (in the prayer) is that a person
should be close to the ground without fully resting on it. What clarifies what we have
mentioned is what was narrated:
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا
الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ وَ قَدْ سَجَدَ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ فَبَسَطَ ذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَ أَلْصَقَ جُوجُؤَهُ بِالْأَرْضِ فِي ثِيَابِهِ.

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khaqan,
who said:
I saw Aba al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s}, peace be upon him, perform the prostration of
gratitude (‘Sajdat al-Shukr’), and He {a.s} spread out his forearms and pressed his chest
and stomach to the ground.
So I asked Him {a.s} about that, and Imam {a.s} said: “This is how it should be.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ
الثَّالِثَ عَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ الشُّكْرِ فَافْتَرَشَ ذِرَاعَيْهِ وَ أَلْصَقَ صَدْرَهُ وَبَطْنَهُ فَسَأَلْثُهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ «كَذَا يَجِبُ».

text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace
be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the limit of prostration.
Imam {a.s} said: “Whatever part is placed from the area between the hairline and the
position of the eyebrows, it suffices you.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بَحْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُدَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنْ حَدٍّ
السُّجُود قَالَ «مَا بَيْنَ قُصَاصِ الشَّعْرِ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ الْحَاجِبِ مَا وَضَعْتَ مِنْهُ أَجْزَأَكَ».

and the hairline, then it suffices for him.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُدَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَلامُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ ٱلرَّجُلُ يَسْجُدُ وَ عَلَيْهِ
قَلَنْسُوَةٌ أَوْ عِمَامَةٌ فَقَالَ «إِذَا مَسَّ جَبْهَتُهُ الْأَرْضَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ حَاجِبَيْهِ وَ قُصَاصٍ شَعْرِهِ فَقَدْ أَجْرَأَ عَنْهُ».

Al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

be higher than the place where he stands?

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, from one of his companions, from
Musadif, who said:
A boil had appeared on me (forehead), so I was prostrating on one side.
Abu Abdillah {a.s} saw its mark and said: “What is this?”
I said: “I cannot prostrate because of the boil, so I prostrate while turned to the side.”
Imam {a.s} said to me: “Do not do that. Dig a small pit and place the boil into the pit so
that you may place your forehead on the ground.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفُوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ مُصَادِفٍ قَالَ: خَرَجَ بِي
دَمَّلٌ فَكُنْتُ أَسْجُدُ عَلَى جَانِبٍ فَرَأَى أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ أَثَرَهُ فَقَالَ «مَا هَذَا» فَقُلْتُ لاَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْجُدَ
مِنْ أَجْلِ الدُّمَّلِ فَإِنَّمَا أَسْجُدُ مُنْحَرِفاً فَقَالَ لِي «لا تَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ إِحْفِرْ حَفِيرَةً وَ اِجْعَلِ الدُّمَّلَ فِي الْحَفِيرَةِ حَتَّى تَضَعَ
جَبْهَتَكَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, by his chain of narration, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} was asked about someone who has an ailment on his forehead and is
unable to prostrate upon it.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should place his chin on the ground, for Allah {SWT} the Exalted says:
‘They fall down upon their chins in prostration’.” (Surah Isra 17:107)

Scholar's Note:
And the interpretation of these two narrations is that one who has a boil or something
similar on his forehead, if he is able to dig a small pit and place it in there, then he
should do so. But if he is not able to do that and it becomes too difficult for him, then
he should prostrate on his chin, as the last narration indicates.
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ بِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ: سُيِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَمَّنْ بِجَبْهَتِهِ عِلَّةٌ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى
السُّجُودِ عَلَيْهَا قَالَ «يَضَعُ ذَقَنَهُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِنَّ اللّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ «يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقانِ سُجَداً». ».
والوجه في هاتين الروايتين أن من بجبهته دمل أو ما يجري مجراه إذا استطاع أن يحفر حفيرة ويدعه فيها فليفعل ذلك
، وإن لم يستطع ذلك ويشتد عليه يسجد على ذقنه على ما تضمنه الخبر الاخير.
commentary:
And the interpretation of these two narrations is that one who has a boil or something
similar on his forehead, if he is able to dig a small pit and place it in there, then he
should do so. But if he is not able to do that and it becomes too difficult for him, then
he should prostrate on his chin, as the last narration indicates.

text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ
الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَسْجُدُ وَ عَلَيْهِ الْعِمَامَةُ لاَ تُصِيبُ جَبْهَتُهُ
اَلْأَرْضَ قَالَ «لَا يُجْزِيهِ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى تَصِلَ جَبْهَتُهُ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ».

source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn
Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who prostrates while wearing a turban, such that
his forehead does not touch the ground.
Imam {a.s} said: “That does not suffice him until his forehead reaches the ground.”

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you rise from prostration, say: ‘O Allah {SWT}, my Lord {AZJ},
by Your {AZJ} power and strength I rise and I sit.’
And if you wish, you may also say: ‘…and I bow and I prostrate.’”
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنَ
السُّجُودٍ قْلْتَ - اللّهُمَّ رَبِّي بِحَوْلِكَ وَ قُوَّتِكَ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قُلْتَ وَ أَرْكَعُ وَ أَسْجُدُ».

And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When a man rises from prostration, he says: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi
aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power of Allah {SWT} I rise and I sit).’”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلامُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قَامَ ٱَلرَّجُلُ مِنَ ٱلسُّجُودِ
قَالَ - بِحَوْلِ اللَهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ».

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Khala:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “It suffices you in qunut to say: ‘O Allah {SWT}, forgive us, have
mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.
Indeed, You {AZJ} have power over all things.’”

Scholar's Note:
And Shaykh (al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, mentioned in the book that
one raises his hands for qunut without a takbir. However, what is preferable in my view
is that he raises them with a takbir. And what indicates this is:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «يُجْزِيكَ فِي الْقُنُوتِ اللَهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ اِرْحَمْنَا وَ عَافِنَا وَ أُغْفُ عَنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ «إِنَّكَ عَلىٰ كُلِّ
شَيءٍ قَدِيرٌ» ».

على ذلك :

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr,
from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “The takbir in the obligatory prayer, in the five daily prayers, is
ninety-five takbirs, among them are five takbirs of qunut.”
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ
عَ قَالَ: «التَكْبِيرُ فِي صَلاَةِ ٱلْفَرْضِ فِي الْخَمْسِ الصَّلَوَاتِ خَمْسٌ وَ تِسْعُونَ تَكْبِيرَة مِنْهَا تَكْبِيرَةُ الْقُنُوتِ خَمْسٌ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.310 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.87 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.336 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.753 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.18 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.91

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah:
Imam {a.s} explained the (takbirs) as follows; In Dhuhr, twenty-one takbirs; in ‘Asr,
twenty-one takbirs; in Maghrib, sixteen takbirs; in the last Isha, twenty-one takbirs;
and in Fajr, eleven takbirs; and five takbirs of qunut in the five prayers.”

وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِبِهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ : «وَ فَسَّرَهُنَ فِي الظُهرِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ
فِي اَلْعَصْرٍ إِحْدَى وَ عِشَرُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ سِنَّ عَشرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي الْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشرُونَ
تَكْبِيرَةً وَ فِي الْفَجْرِ إحْدَى عَشَرَةَ تَكْبِيرَةَ وَ خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتِ الْقُنُوتِ فِي خَمْسِ صَلَوَاتُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Umar, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sabbah al-
Muzani, who said
Commander of the Faithful, (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}), peace be upon him, said:
“Ninety-five takbirs are (prescribed) in the day and night for the prayers, among them
is the takbir of qunut.”

Scholar's Note:
So these reports included the mention of ‘takbir’ along with ‘qunut’, both in general
terms and in detailed enumeration. They also included the number of ‘takbirs’ as
ninety-five. And if there were no ‘takbir’ in the ‘qunut’, then the ‘takbirs’ would have
been ninety only.
No one has the right to say; “I interpret the number beyond ninety as referring to the
‘takbir’ when the worshiper rises from the first ‘tashahhud’ to the third rak‘ah.” For
several reasons:
First; This situation does not apply to all prayers, only in four of them is there a rising
from the second to the third rak‘ah. If that had been intended, the narration would
have said: ninety-four ‘takbirs’.
Second; The detailed narration explicitly mentions eleven ‘takbirs’ in the morning
(‘Ghada’) prayer, and the ‘takbir’ of ‘qunut’ is included among them. If the matter were
as they claim, there would have only been eleven ‘takbirs’ in total.
Third; There are many narrations which state that a person should rise from the first
‘tashahhud’ to the third rak‘ah saying: ‘By the power and strength of Allah {SWT} I rise
and I sit.’ Had it been obligatory to rise with ‘takbir’, the narration would have said:
“Then he says the ‘takbir’ and rises to the third,” just as when they mention bowing
and prostrating, they say: “Then he says ‘takbir’ and bows,” and “he says ‘takbir’ and
prostrates,” and “he raises his head from prostration and says ‘takbir’.” If there were
a ‘takbir’ here as well, it would have been stated in the same manner.
And the one who narrated what we have mentioned is:
text_ar:
محَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ الصَّبَّاحِ الْمُرَنِيَّ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «خَمْسُ وَ تِسْعُونَ تَكْبِيرَةً فِي الْيَوْمِ وَ اللَّيْلَةِ لِلصَّلَوَاتِ مِنْهَا تَكْبِيرَةُ ٱلْقُنُوتِ».
فتضمنت هذه الاخبار ذكر التكبير مضافا الى القنوت على سبيل الجملة وعلى طريق التفصيل ، وتضمنت ايضا عدد
التكبيرات خمسا وتسعين تكبيرة ولو لم يكن في القنوت تكبير لكان التكبيرات تسعين تكبيرة. وليس لاحد أن يقول : اني
أحمل ما زاد على التسعين تكبيرة على انه إذا نهض المصلى من التشهد الاول الى الثالثة يقوم بتكبيرة لامور. أحدها : انه
ليس كالصلوات فيها نهوض من الثانية إلى الثالثة وإنما هو موجود في أربعة صلوات فلو كان المراد به ذلك لكان يقول :
اربعا وتسعين تكبيرة. والثاني : ان الحديث المفصل تضمن ذكر احدى عشرة تكبيرة في صلاة الغداة وتكبيرة القنوت

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you sit after the first two rak‘ahs and recite the
tashahhud, then stand, say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and
strength of Allah {SWT} I rise and I sit.)”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيز عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا
جَلَسْتَ فِي الرّكْعَتَيْنِ ٱلْأُولَيَيْنِ فَتَشَهَدْتَ ثُمَّ قُمْتَ فَقُلْ بِحَوْلِ اللّهِ وَ قُوّتِهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ».

text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: “When (Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, would rise from
the first two rak‘ahs, He {a.s} would say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power
and strength of Allah {SWT} I rise and I sit.)”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةً عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «كَانَ عَلِيْ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا
نَهَضَ مِنَ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأُولَيَيْنِ قَالَ » بِحَوْلِكَ وَ قُوَّتِكَ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ» ».

text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Sayf, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you rise from the two rak‘ahs, lean on your palms and
say: ‘Bi-hawli Allahi aqumu wa aq‘udu’ (By the power and strength of Allah {SWT} I rise
and I sit.) for indeed (Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, used to do that.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ ٱلْحَضْرَمِيّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلامُ : «إِذَا قُمْتَ مِنَ ٱلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ
فَاعْتَمِدْ عَلَى كَفِّيْكَ وَ قُلْ - بِحَوْلِ اللْهِ أَقُومُ وَ أَقْعُدُ فَإِنَّ عَلِياً عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ كَانَ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ».

text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah {a.s} for several days, and He {a.s} would perform ‘qunut’ in
every prayer, whether it was one in which the recitation was audible or not.
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ الْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيَّاماً
فَكَانَ يَقْنُتُ فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا أَوْ لا يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا.
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.339 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.318 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.89 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.338 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.747 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.261

Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every prayer, in the second rak‘ah,
before bowing.”
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُدَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «الْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلّ صَلاةٍ فِي
الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ قَبْلَ الرُّكُوعِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.340 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.89 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.338 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.749 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.266

And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every prayer, in the second rak‘ah,
before bowing.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim,
who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, about ‘qunut’ in all five prayers.
Imam {a.s} said: “Perform ‘qunut’ in all of them.”
He (Muhammad ibn Muslim) said: “Then I later asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about that, and
Imam {a.s} said: “As for the prayers in which you recite aloud, do not have any doubt
about it.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلَاَمُ
عَنِ الْقُنُوتِ فِي الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسِ جَمِيعاً فَقَالَ «أُقْنُتْ فِيهِنَّ جَمِيعاً» قَالَ فَسَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ بَعْدُ
عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ »أَمّا مَا جَهَرْتَ فِيهِ فَلاَ تَشْكَّ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.339 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.89 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.338 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.747 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.262

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Qunut in Maghrib is in the second rak‘ah, and in Isha and
Ghadah (Fajr) it is the same. And in Witr it is in the third rak‘ah.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ نَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «ٱلْقُنُوتُ فِي ٱلْمَغْرِبِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ وَ فِي
الْعِشَاءٍ وَ الْغَدَاةِ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ وَ فِي الْوَثْرِ فِي الرّكْعَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.89 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.338 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.749 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.267 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.209

And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Qunut in Maghrib is in the second rak‘ah, and in Isha and

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about ‘qunut’, about which prayer is it in?
Imam {a.s} said: “Every prayer in which the recitation is done aloud has ‘qunut’ in it, and
‘qunut’ is before bowing and after the recitation.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْقُنُوتِ فِي أَيِّ صَلاَةِ هُوَ فَقَالَ «كُلْ شَيْءٍ يُجْهَرُ فِيهِ
بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِيهِ قُنُوتُ وَ الْقُنُوتُ قَبْلَ الرُّكُوعِ وَ بَعْدَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.89 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.339 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.750 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.267

And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
One of our companions asked Him {a.s}, and I (Abu Basir) was present, about ‘qunut’ in
the Friday prayer.
Imam {a.s} said to him: “In the second rak‘ah.”
So the man said to Him {a.s}: “One of our companions narrated to us that you told him
it is in the first rak‘ah.”
Imam {a.s} said: “In the last.”
Then, when He {a.s} saw that the man was confused, Imam {a.s} said: “O Aba Muhammad,
(it is) in both the first and the last.”
Then Abu Basir asked after that: “Is it before the bowing or after it?”
So Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Every ‘qunut’ is before bowing, except in Friday prayer: in the
first rak‘ah it is before bowing, and in the last it is after bowing.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ الْخَزَّازِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ - عَنِ ٱلْقُنُوتِ فِي الْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ «فِي الرَكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ» فَقَالَ لَهُ قَدْ حَدَّثَنَا
بِهِ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّكَ قُلْتَ لَهُ فِي الرّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى فَقَالَ «فِي الْأَخِيرَةِ» فَلَمَّا رَأَى غَفْلَةً مِنْهُ فَقَالَ «يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ فِي
الْأُولَى وَ الْأَخِيرَةِ» فَقَالَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَقَبْلَ الرُّكُوعِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ «كُلُّ قُنُوتٍ
قَبْلَ الرُّكُوعِ إِلَّ الْجُمُعَةَ فَإِنَّ الرَّكْعَةَ الْأُولَى فِيهَا قَبْلَ الرُّكُوعِ وَ الْأَخِيرَةَ بَعْدَ الرُكُوعِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.90 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.339 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.273
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Wahb:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Qunut is in Friday prayer, Isha, ‘Atamah (night prayer), Witr, and
Ghadah (Fajr). Whoever abandons qunut out of aversion to it, then he has no prayer.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُدَيْنَةَ عَنْ وَهْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «آلْقُنُوتُ فِي ٱلْجُمُعَةِ وَ ٱلْعِشَاءِ وَ الْعَتَمَةِ وَ ٱلْوَثْرِ
وَ الْغَدَاةِ قَمَنْ تَرَكَ ٱلْقُنُوتَ رَغْبَةً عَنْهُ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.90 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.339 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.750 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.265
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
And from him, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Wahb:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Qunut is in Friday prayer, Isha, ‘Atamah (night prayer), Witr, and
Ghadah (Fajr). Whoever abandons qunut out of aversion to it, then he has no prayer.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in every two rak‘ahs, in
supererogatory (nafl) and obligatory prayers.”
Al-Hasan said: “And Abdullah ibn Bukayr informed me from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far
{a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Qunut is in all prayers.”
Muhammad ibn Muslim said: “So I mentioned that to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, and Imam {a.s}
said: “As for that in which there is no doubt, it is what is recited aloud.”

Scholar's Note:
He {a.s}, peace be upon him, specified in this narration, and in other previously
mentioned narrations, the prayers in which the recitation is aloud, to emphasize their
merit and to increase the reward, not to prohibit ‘qunut’ in the others. This is evident
from what we have presented of general wordings, such as:
Their saying (peace be upon them): ‘Qunut is in all prayers.’
And their saying: ‘In every two rak‘ahs, of obligatory and supererogatory (prayers).’
Likewise, there are narrations that appear to indicate the negation of qunut, such as
what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
«ٱلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي التَّطَوْعِ وَ الْفَرِيضَةِ» - قَالَ الْحَسَنُ وَ أَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ اللّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي
جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : قَالَ «الْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلِّ الصَّلَوَاتِ» قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لأَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
فَقَالَ «أَمَّا مَا لاَ يُشَكُ فِيهِ فَمَا جُهِرَ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ».
إنما خص عليه السلام في هذا الخبر وفي غيره مما تقدم من الاخبار الصلوات التي يجهر فيها بالقراءة تأكيدا للفضل وزيادة
اللثواب دون أن يكون حظرا فيما عداها بدلالة ما أوردناه من عموم الالفاظ مثل قَوْلِهِمْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلاَمُ : اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي كُلَ
الصَّلَوَاتٍ. قَوْلِهِمْ: «فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ النَّافِلَةِ». وكذلك ما روي من الاخبار التي تتضمن نفي القنوت مثل ما رواه:
commentary:
He {a.s}, peace be upon him, specified in this narration, and in other previously
mentioned narrations, the prayers in which the recitation is aloud, to emphasize their
merit and to increase the reward, not to prohibit ‘qunut’ in the others. This is evident
from what we have presented of general wordings, such as:
Their saying (peace be upon them): ‘Qunut is in all prayers.’
And their saying: ‘In every two rak‘ahs, of obligatory and supererogatory (prayers).’
Likewise, there are narrations that appear to indicate the negation of qunut, such as
what was narrated:

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abd
al-Malik ibn ‘Amr, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about ‘qunut’, is it before bowing or after?
Imam {a.s} said: “Neither before it nor after it.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحِ عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ عَمْرِو
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ عَنِ ٱلْقُنُوتِ قَبْلَ الرُكُوعِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ قَالَ «لا قَبْلَهُ وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُ».

text_en:
And from him, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon
him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about ‘qunut’, is ‘qunut’ performed in all the prayers, or only in those
in which the recitation is audible?
Imam {a.s} said: “Qunut is only in Ghadah (Fajr), Jumu‘ah (Friday prayer), Witr, and
Maghrib.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنِ الْبَرْقِيَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدِ الْأَشعَرِيّ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْقُنُوتِ هَلْ
يُقْنَتْ فِي الصَّلَوَاتِ كُلِّهَا أَمْ فِيمَا يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ قَالَ «لَيْسَ ٱلْقُنُوتُ إِلاّ فِي ٱلْغَدَاةِ وَ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ وَ ٱلْوَثْرِ وَ
الْمَغْرِبِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who
said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}: In which prayers should I perform ‘qunut’?
Imam {a.s} said: “Do not perform ‘qunut’ except in Fajr.”

Scholar's Note:
So this only entails the negation of merit and an emphasis on the recommended
nature (of qunut) which has been established in the other prayers in which recitation
is done aloud, and then after that in the obligatory prayers, because ‘qunut’ in these
prayers varies in terms of merit and is not uniformly applied in the same manner.
It is also possible that they negated it in some prayers and specified it in others due to
a kind of ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation) and consideration of public interest.
What clarifies this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ الْقُنُوتِ فِي أَيِّ الصَّلَوَاتِ أَقْنُتُ فَقَالَ «لا تَقْنُتْ إِلاّ فِي الْفَجْرِ».
فانما يتضمن نفي الفضل وتأكيد الندب الذى ثبت في غيرها من الصلوات التي يجهر فيها ثم بعد ذلك في الفرايض لان
القنوت في هذه الصلوات مترتب في الفضل غير منساق على وجه واحد، ويجوز أن يكون نفوا عن بعض الصلوات وخصوا
به بعضا لضرب من التقية والاستصلاح ، والذي يكشف عن ذلك ما رواه،

So this only entails the negation of merit and an emphasis on the recommended
nature (of qunut) which has been established in the other prayers in which recitation
is done aloud, and then after that in the obligatory prayers, because ‘qunut’ in these
prayers varies in terms of merit and is not uniformly applied in the same manner.
It is also possible that they negated it in some prayers and specified it in others due to
a kind of ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation) and consideration of public interest.
What clarifies this is what was narrated:

text_en:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon
him, who said:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding ‘qunut’: “If you wish, then perform
qunut; and if you wish, do not perform it.”
Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: ‘And when there is taqiyyah (precautionary
dissimulation), then do not perform qunut, and I adhere to this.’

Scholar's Note:
And this is also indicated by what was narrated:
text_ar:
عَلِي بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ الرَّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ فِي الْقُنُوتِ: «إِنْ شِئْتَ فَاقْنُتْ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ لاَ تَقْنُتْ» قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ: «وَ إِذَا كَانَتِ التَّقِيَّةُ فَلاَ
تَقْنُتْ وَ أَنَا أَتَقَلَّدُ هَذَا».
ويدل عليه ايضا ما رواه :
commentary: And this is also indicated by what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu
Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about ‘qunut’.
Imam {a.s} said: “In that which you recite aloud.”
So I said: “I asked your father {a.s} about that, and Imam {a.s} said: ‘In all five prayers.’”
Imam {a.s} said: “May Allah {SWT} have mercy on my father {a.s}. The companions of my
father {a.s} came to him and asked him, so He {a.s} informed them of the truth. Then they
came to me full of doubts, so I gave them a ruling based on ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary
dissimulation).”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَالٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الْقُنُوتِ فَقَالَ «فِيمَا تَجْهَرُ فِيهِ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي سَأَلْتُ أَبَاكَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ «فِي
الخَمْسٍ كُلِّها» فَقَالَ «رَجِمَ اللَّهُ أَبِي إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ أَبِي أَتَوْهُ فَسَأَلُوهُ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ بِالْحَقّ ثُمَّ أَتَوْنِي شُكَاكاً فَأَفْتَيْتُهُمْ
بِالتَّقِيَّةِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.339 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.91 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.340 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.748 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.263

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Sa‘d, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Abu al-Qasim Mu‘awiyah
narrated to me from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sammak, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
Imam {a.s} said to me regarding the ‘qunut’ of ‘witr’: ‘O Allah {SWT}, forgive us, have mercy
on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this world and the Hereafter.‘
And Imam {a.s} said: ‘Three tasbihat suffice for qunut.”’
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ آللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ مُعَاوِيَةُ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سَمَّاكِ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي: فِي قُنُوتِ الْوَثْرِ « اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ اِرْحَمْنَا وَ عَافِنَا وَ أُغْفُ عَنَّا فِي
الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ » وَقَالَ «يُجْزِي مِنَ الْقُنُوتِ ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.92 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.275
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn
‘Uthman, from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s} said: “Qunut is before bowing, and if you wish, then after it.”

Scholar's Note:
His {a.s} statement: ‘And if you wish, then after it’ is to be understood as referring to a
situation of making up (missed prayer) or due to ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary
dissimulation), according to the school of thought of some among the general
populace regarding the Fajr prayer.
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمِّدِ الْجَوْهَرِيّ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثِمَانَ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ الْجُعْفِيّ وَ مَعْمَرٍ
بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أُبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلْقُنُوتُ قَبْلَ الرُكُوعِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَبَعْدَهُ».
قوله : وان شئت فبعده محمول على حال القضاء أو التقية على مذهب بعض العامة في صلاة الغداة.
commentary:
His {a.s} statement: ‘And if you wish, then after it’ is to be understood as referring to a
situation of making up (missed prayer) or due to ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary
dissimulation), according to the school of thought of some among the general
populace regarding the Fajr prayer.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.92
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
text_chunk:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn
‘Uthman, from Isma‘il al-Ju‘fi and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s} said: “Qunut is before bowing, and if you wish, then after it.” Scholar's Note:
His {a.s} statement: ‘And if you wish, then after it’ is to be understood as referring to a
situation of making up (missed prayer) or due to ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary
dissimulation), according to the school of thought of some among the general
populace regarding the Fajr prayer.

text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan: Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr al-Ahwal:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “The ‘tashahhud’ in the first two rak‘ahs is: ‘Alhamdu lillah
ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan
abduhu wa rasuluh Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa Aali Muhammad wa taqabbal
shafaatahu fi ummatih wa irfa darajatah’ (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah
{SWT}, alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad {saws} is His servant and
messenger. O Allah {SWT}, send blessings upon Muhammad {saws} and the family of
Muhammad {saws}, and accept His {saws} intercession on behalf of His {saws} nation, and
raise His {saws} rank.’”

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: “The ‘taslim’ (salutation) in prayer is of four types;
If a man is an ‘imam’, he says one ‘taslim’. If he is a ‘follower (ma’mum)’ and there is
no one on his left, he also says one ‘taslim’. If there is someone on his left, he says
‘two taslims’. If he is praying ‘alone’, he says ‘one taslim’. What indicates this is:
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفُوَانَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عَمْرِو الْأَحْوَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «التَّشَهُدُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأُولَيَيْنِ - الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ أَشهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشَهَدُ
أنَّ مُحَمَداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ اللّهُمّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ تَقَبَّلْ شَفَاعَتَهُ فِي أَمْتِهِ وَ اِرْفَع دَرَجَتَهُ ».

ولم يكن عن شماله أحد يسلم واحدة أيضا ، وإن كان عن شماله انسان يسلم تسليمتين ، وإن كان منفردا يسلم تسليمة

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘Awwad:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “If you are leading a group in prayer, one ‘taslim’ to your right
suffices. If you are praying behind an imam, then (you do) two ‘taslims’. And if you are
alone, then one ‘taslim’ facing the qiblah suffices.”
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بَنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ بْنِ عَوَّاضٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «إِنْ كُنْتَ
تَوُمُ قَوْماً أَجَرَأَكَ تَسْلِيمَةً وَاحِدَةً عَنْ يَمِينِكَ وَ إنْ كُنْتَ مَعَ إِمَامِ فَتَسْلِيمَتَيْنِ وَ إنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَوَاحِدَةً مُسْتَقْبِلَ
الْقِبْلَةِ».

فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَنْ شِمَالِهِ أَحَدٌ سَلَّمَ وَاحِدَةً».

رَجُلٍ يَقُومُ فِي الصّفّ خَلْفَ ٱلْإمَامِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى يَسَارِهِ أَحَدٌ كَيْفَ يُسَلَّمُ قَالَ «تَسْلِيمَةً عَنْ يَمِينِهِ».

Zurarah, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Ma‘mar ibn Yahya, and Isma‘il:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “He performs one ‘taslim’, whether he is an
imam or not.”

Scholar's Note:

chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “If you are an imam, then the ‘taslim’ is that you send salam
upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and say: ‘Peace be upon us and
upon the righteous servants of Allah {SWT}.’ Once you say that, the prayer has ended.
Then you inform the people by saying, while facing the qiblah, ‘Peace be upon you.’
And likewise, if you are praying alone, you say: ‘Peace be upon us and upon the
righteous servants of Allah {SWT} ‘ just as you would say if you were the imam.
But if you are in a congregation, then say what you have said, and send salam upon
those on your right and your left. If there is no one on your left, then send salam upon
those on your right, and do not omit sending ‘taslim’ to your right even if there is no one
on your left.”

Scholar's Note:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “Then he performs the two
prostrations of gratitude” up to his words: “And it is recommended to begin with seven
‘takbirs’ in seven prayers”. We will mention this later when discussing the ‘ta‘qib’
(post-prayer supplication) of the obligatory prayer.
Then he (al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And it is recommended to
begin with seven ‘takbirs’ in seven prayers” up to his statement: “And the woman
gathers herself (tucks in) during her prayer”, this was mentioned by Ali ibn al-Husayn
ibn Babawayh in his treatise, but I have not found a reliably transmitted narration
regarding it.’ Its detail is as follows, the seven places mentioned by Ali ibn al-Husayn
are:
1. At the beginning of each obligatory prayer.
2. At the first rak‘ah of the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’).
3. In the single rak‘ah of ‘witr’ (in the optional night prayer).
4. In the first rak‘ah of the two rak‘ahs before ‘zawal’ (midday).
5. In the first rak‘ah of the ‘nawafil’ (supererogatory prayers) after Maghrib.
6. In the first rak‘ah of the two rak‘ahs of ‘ihram’ (entering the state of prayer for ‘hajj’
or ‘umrah’).
These six positions were mentioned by Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Shaykh added a seventh
in the ‘wutayrah’ (two rak‘ahs after Isha).
Then Shaykh (al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And the woman
gathers herself in her prayer” up to his statement: “When the one praying finishes the
eight rak‘ahs…”.
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا
كُنْتَ إِمَاماً فَإِنَّمَا التَّسْلِيمُ أَنْ تُسَلَّمَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ تَقُولَ ٱلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ
فَإِذَا قُلْتَ ذَلِكَ فَقَدِ اِنْقَطَعَتِ الصَّلاةُ ثُمَّ ثُوْذِنُ ٱلْقَوْمَ فَتَقُولُ وَ أَنْتَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةَ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ كَذَلِكَ إِذَا كُنْتَ
وَحْدَكَ تَقُولُ - السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اللّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ مِثْلَ مَا سَلَمْتَ وَ أَنْتَ إِمَامٌ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَقُلْ
مِثلَ مَا قُلْتَ وَ سَلِّمْ عَلَى مَنْ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ شِمَالِكَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى شِمَالِكَ أَحَدٌ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى الَّذِينَ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ
وَ لَاَ تَدَعِ التَّسْلِيمَ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى شِمَالِكَ أَحَدٌ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ثم يسجد سجدتي الشكر) إلى قوله: (ويستحب التوجه بسبع تكبيرات في سبع صلوات) فسنذكره
اصلاة الفيضة ثم قاا دحه
commentary:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “Then he performs the two

2. At the first rak‘ah of the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’).
3. In the single rak‘ah of ‘witr’ (in the optional night prayer).
4. In the first rak‘ah of the two rak‘ahs before ‘zawal’ (midday).
5. In the first rak‘ah of the ‘nawafil’ (supererogatory prayers) after Maghrib.
6. In the first rak‘ah of the two rak‘ahs of ‘ihram’ (entering the state of prayer for ‘hajj’

Then Shaykh (al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And the woman

But if you are in a congregation, then say what you have said, and send salam upon
those on your right and your left. If there is no one on your left, then send salam upon
those on your right, and do not omit sending ‘taslim’ to your right even if there is no one
on your left.”

Scholar's Note:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “Then he performs the two
prostrations of gratitude” up to his words: “And it is recommended to begin with seven
‘takbirs’ in seven prayers”. We will mention this later when discussing the ‘ta‘qib’
(post-prayer supplication) of the obligatory prayer.
Then he (al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And it is recommended to
begin with seven ‘takbirs’ in seven prayers” up to his statement: “And the woman
gathers herself (tucks in) during her prayer”, this was mentioned by Ali ibn al-Husayn
ibn Babawayh in his treatise, but I have not found a reliably transmitted narration
regarding it.’ Its detail is as follows, the seven places mentioned by Ali ibn al-Husayn
are:
1. At the beginning of each obligatory prayer.
2. At the first rak‘ah of the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’).
3. In the single rak‘ah of ‘witr’ (in the optional night prayer).
4. In the first rak‘ah of the two rak‘ahs before ‘zawal’ (midday).
5. In the first rak‘ah of the ‘nawafil’ (supererogatory prayers) after Maghrib.
6. In the first rak‘ah of the two rak‘ahs of ‘ihram’ (entering the state of prayer for ‘hajj’
or ‘umrah’).
These six positions were mentioned by Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Shaykh added a seventh
in the ‘wutayrah’ (two rak‘ahs after Isha).
Then Shaykh (al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And the woman
gathers herself in her prayer” up to his statement: “When the one praying finishes the
eight rak‘ahs…”.

وَحْدَكَ تَقُولُ - السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اللّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ مِثْلَ مَا سَلَمْتَ وَ أَنْتَ إِمَامٌ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَقُلْ
مِثلَ مَا قُلْتَ وَ سَلِّمْ عَلَى مَنْ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ شِمَالِكَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى شِمَالِكَ أَحَدٌ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى الَّذِينَ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ

قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ثم يسجد سجدتي الشكر) إلى قوله: (ويستحب التوجه بسبع تكبيرات في سبع صلوات) فسنذكره
