text_en:
And what was narrated by Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Ja‘far {a.s} say: "Indeed, I perform the night prayer, and I finish my prayer and
perform the two rak‘ahs, then I sleep for as long as Allah {SWT} wills before the Fajr rises.
Then if I wake at the time of Fajr, I repeat them."

Scholar's Note:
For indeed, these two reports concern the one who performs these two rak‘ahs while
a portion of the night still remains, before the rising of the first Fajr. In that case, it is
appropriate for him to repeat the two rak‘ahs. It is also possible that Abu Ja‘far and
Abu Abdillah, peace be upon them both, repeated them as a recommended act, and
there is nothing in the two reports stating that if you do this, and the matter is such,
then you must repeat them.
As for the recitation in them, it has been narrated:
text_ar:
وَ مَا رَوَاهُ صَفْوَانُ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِنِّي لَأُصَلِّي صَلاةَ اَللِّيْلِ
فَأَفْرُغُ مِنْ صَلاتِي وَ أُصَلِّي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَنَامُ مَا شَاءَ اللّهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ فَإِنِ اِسْتَيْقَظْتُ عِنْدَ الْفَجْرِ أَعَدْتُهُمَا».
فان هذين الخبرين وردا فيمن صلى هاتين الركعتين وعليه قطعة من الليل قبل طلوع الفجر الاول فحينئذ ينبغي له أن
يعيد الركعتين، ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون ابو جعفر وابو عبد اللّٰه عليهما السلام اعادا ذلك على طريق الاستحباب وليس في
الخبرين انكم إذا فعلتم ذلك والامر على ذلك اعيدوهما ثانيا ، فاما القراءة فيهما فقد روى.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Recite in the two rak‘ahs of Fajr any two
Surahs that you love."
And Imam {a.s} said: "As for me, I love to recite in them ‘Surah Al Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-
Kafirun’."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "Then let him lie down on his
right side" until his statement: "Then when the Fajr appears clearly and becomes
distinct."
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «اِقْرَأْ فِي رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ بِأَيَّ
سُورَتَيْنِ أَحْبَبْتَ» وَ قَالَ «أَمَّا أَنَا فَأُجِبُّ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فِيهِمَا بِ «قُلْ هُوَ آللَهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يَا أَيْهَا الْكَافِرُونَ» ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ثم ليضطجع على جنبه الايمن) الى قوله : (فإذا طلع الفجر واستبان).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "Then let him lie down on his
right side" until his statement: "Then when the Fajr appears clearly and becomes
distinct."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan, and Muhammad ibn Sinan
from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} what I should say when I lie on my right side after the two rak‘ahs of
Fajr.
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
"Recite the five verses at the end of Surah Al ‘Imran, until ‘'Indeed, You do not break
the promise.'‘ (Surah Al-'Imran 3:190-194).
Then say: I have held fast to the firm handhold of Allah {SWT} which ‘never breaks’, and I
have taken refuge with the strong rope of Allah {SWT}. I seek refuge in Allah {SWT} from the
evil of the wicked among the Arabs and non-Arabs. I believe in Allah {SWT}. I have placed
my trust in Allah {SWT}. I turn my back to Allah {SWT}. I have entrusted my affair to Allah
{SWT}. And whoever relies upon Allah {SWT}, then He {SWT} is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah
{SWT} will accomplish His {SWT} purpose. Allah {SWT} has set a measure for everything. Allah
{SWT} is sufficient for me, and He {SWT} is the best disposer of affairs.
O Allah {SWT}, whoever begins his morning in need of the creation, then indeed my need
and my longing is toward You {SWT}. Praise be to the Lord {SWT} of the morning! Praise be
to the cleaver of the dawn!" (Repeat this three times).

Scholar's Note:
And it is permissible, instead of lying down, to prostrate, or to walk, or to speak, but
lying down is better.
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ
بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَمَّا أَقُولُ إِذَا إِضْطَجَعْتُ عَلَى يَمِينِي بَعْدَ رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ (« إِقْرَأْ
اَلْخَمْسَ آيَاتِ الَّتِي فِي آخِرِ آلِ عِمْرَانَ إِلَى «إِنَّكَ لا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ» وَ قُلِ اِسْتَمْسَكْتُ بِعُزْوَةِ اللَّهِ اَلْوُثْقَى الَّتِي « لا
اِنْفِصامَ لَها» وَ اِغْتَصَمْتُ بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ الْمَتِينِ وَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَرِّ فَسَقَةِ الْعَرَبِ وَ الْعَجَمِ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ «تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى
الله» أَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ فَوَّضْتُ «أَمْرِي إِلَى اللّهِ» «وَ مَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَالغُ أَمْرِهِ قَذْ
جَعَلَ اللهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً» حَسبي «اللهُ وَ نِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ» اللَّهُمَّ مَنْ أَصْبَحَثْ حَاجَثُهُ إِلَى مَخْلُوقٍ فَإِنَّ حَاجَتِي وَ
رَغْبَتِي إِلَيْكَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِرَبِّ الصَّبَاحِ اَلْحَمْدُ لِفَالِقِ الْإِصْبَاحِ ثَلاَثاً».
ويجوز بدلا من الاضطجاع السجدة والمشي والكلام الا أن الاضطجاع افضل
commentary:
And it is permissible, instead of lying down, to prostrate, or to walk, or to speak, but
lying down is better.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Asbat from Ibrahim
ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
I performed the night prayer behind (Imam) al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, in the
Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram). When He {a.s} finished, He {a.s} placed a
prostration (sajdah) in place of lying down (al-daj‘ah).
text_ar:
رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَسْبَاطِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي الْبِلاَدِ قَالَ: صَلِّيْتُ
خَلْفَ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ صَلاَةَ اللَّيْلِ فَلَمَّا قَرَغَ جَعَلَ مَكَانَ الضَّجْعَةِ سَجْدَةً.
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.448 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.137 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1599 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.492
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}

ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
I performed the night prayer behind (Imam) al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, in the
Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram). When He {a.s} finished, He {a.s} placed a

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Ayyub ibn Nuh from al-Husayn ibn Uthman by a man:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Standing, sitting, and speaking after the two rak’ahs of Fajr
suffice you in place of lying down."
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوحِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثمَانَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ ٱلإِضْطِجَاعِ بَعْدَ رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ ٱلْقِيَامُ وَ ٱلْقُعُودُ وَ الْكَلاَمُ بَعْدَ رَكَعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.137 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1599 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.492
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Ayyub ibn Nuh from al-Husayn ibn Uthman by a man:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Standing, sitting, and speaking after the two rak’ahs of Fajr

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from
Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s} said: "It is only required of one of you, when midnight arrives, to rise and
perform his prayer all at once, thirteen rak‘ahs. Then, if he wishes, he may sit and
supplicate; if he wishes, he may sleep; if he wishes, he may go wherever he wishes."

Scholar's Note:
And it is recommended that a person does not sleep after these two rak‘ahs, and
instead engages in supplication and glorification, for sleeping at this time is disliked.
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ وَ عَبْدِ اللّهِ اِبْنَي مُحَمّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي
جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «إِنَّمَا عَلَى أَحَدِكُمْ إِذَا اِنْتَصَفَ اللَّيْلُ أَنْ يَقُومَ فَيُصَلِّيَ صَلاَتَهُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً ثَلاَثَ عَشَرَةَ
رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ إِنْ شَاءَ جَلَسَ فَدَعَا وَ إِنْ شَاءَ نَامَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ ذَهَبَ حَيْثُ شَاءَ».
ويستحب أن لا ينام الانسان بعد هاتين الركعتين ويشتغل بالدعاء والتسبيح فان النوم في هذا الوقت مكروه.
commentary:
And it is recommended that a person does not sleep after these two rak‘ahs, and
instead engages in supplication and glorification, for sleeping at this time is disliked.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-
Marwazi, who said:
Abu al-Hasan al-Akhir (the Last), peace be upon him, said: "Beware of sleeping
between the night prayer and the Fajr prayer. Rather, lie down without sleeping, for the
one who sleeps at that time is not praised for what he has performed of his prayer."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: ‘Then when the Fajr appears
clearly and becomes distinct, let him call the Adhan’ until his statement: ‘Then let him
raise his head and remember Allah {SWT} until the rising of the sun.’
All of that has already been explained in what has preceded.
Then he (Shaykh), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: ‘Then let him raise his head
and remember Allah {SWT} much until the rising of the sun,’ until the end of the chapter.
text_ar:
رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ ٱلْقَاسَانِيِّ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصِ ٱلْمَرْوَزِيَّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ
الْأَخِيرُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : «إِيَّاكَ وَ النَّوْمَ بَيْنَ صَلَاَةِ اللَّيْلِ وَ الْفَجْرِ وَ لَكِنْ ضَجْعَةً بِلاَ نَوْمِ فَإِنَّ صَاحِبَهُ لا يُحْمَدُ عَلَى مَا
قَدَّمَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (فإذا طلع الفجر واستبان فليؤذن) الى قوله : (ثم ليرفع رأسه فيذكر اللّٰه الى طلوع الشمس) .كل
ذلك قد مضى شرحه في جملة ما تقدم. ثم قال رحمه اللّٰه : (ثم ليرفع رأسه فيذكر اللّٰه كثيرا الى طلوع الشمس) الى آخر
الباب.

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja‘far al-Nahwi from Abu al-Jawza’ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan
from ‘Amr ibn Khallad from ‘Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Asadi from Ibn ‘Umar:
(Imam) al-Hasan ibn Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
“I heard my father (Imam) Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, say that the Messenger
of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
"Any Muslim who sits in his prayer place, in which he performed the Fajr prayer,
remembering Allah {SWT} until the sun rises, will have the reward of one who has
performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his
family, and he will be forgiven.
And if he remains sitting there until the time comes in which prayer is permitted, and
he then performs two rak‘ahs or four, he will be forgiven for what has passed, and he
will have the reward of one who has performed Hajj to the House of Allah {SWT}."
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرِ النَّحْوِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي الْجَوْزَاءِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَلاَّدٍ عَنْ
عَاصِمِ بْنِ أَبِي النَّجُودِ الْأَسَدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ عُمَرَ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبِي عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «أيْمَا اِمْرِي مُسْلِمِ جَلَسَ فِي مُصَلاَهُ اَلَّذِي صَلَّى فِيهِ
الْفَجْرَ يَذْكُرُ اللّهَ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ كَانَ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَجْرِ كَحَاجَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ غُفِرَ لَهُ فَإِنْ جَلَسَ
فِيهِ حَتَّى تَكُونَ سَاعَةٌ تَجِلُّ فِيهَا الصَّلاةُ فَصَلِّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ أَرْبَعاً غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا سَلَفَ وَ كَانَ لَهُ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْرِ كَحَاجَ بَيْتِ
اللَّه ».

text_en:
And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
“The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
‘Allah {SWT} said; "O son of Adam, remember Me {AZJ} for one hour after Fajr, and
remember Me {AZJ} for one hour after ‘Asr, I will suffice you concerning that which
troubles you."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ
قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «قَالَ اللَّهُ «يَا اِبْنَ آدَمَ أذْكُرْنِي بَعْدَ ٱلْفَجْرِ سَاعَةً وَ أُذْكُرْنِي بَعْدَ ٱلْعَصْرِ سَاعَةٌ
أَكْفِكَ مَا أَهَمَّكَ» ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.138 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.429

text_en:
And from him, from Mu’awiyah ibn Hakim from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad from al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon
him, who said:
I heard Him {a.s} say: "It is proper for a man, when he begins his morning, to recite fifty
verses after the ‘ta’qib’ (post-prayer supplication and remembrance)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ مُعَمَّرِ بْنِ خَلاَدٍ عَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: «يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّجْلِ إِذَا
أَصْبَحَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ بَعْدَ التَّعْقِيبِ خَمْسِينَ آيَةً».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And al-’Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them
both, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about sleeping after the dawn (al-ghadah) prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "Indeed, sustenance is distributed during that hour, so I dislike for a
man to sleep at that time."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْعَلاءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ النَّوْمِ بَعْدَ ٱلْغَدَاةِ فَقَالَ «إِنَّ الرِّزْقَ
بُبْسَطُ تِلْكَ السَّاعَةَ فَأَنَا أَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَنَامَ الرَّجَلُ تِلْكَ السَّاعَةً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.501 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.138 • Al-Wafi, Vol.2 6 p.543 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.496
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}

And al-’Ala’ narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them
both, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about sleeping after the dawn (al-ghadah) prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "Indeed, sustenance is distributed during that hour, so I dislike for a

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
(Imam) al-Sadiq {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Sitting after the dawn prayer in ‘ta’qib’
and supplication until the sun rises is more effective in seeking sustenance than
striking the earth (engaging in work and travel)."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ الصَادِقُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلامُ: «الْجُلُوسُ بَعْدَ صَلاَةِ الْغَدَاةِ فِي التَعْقِيبِ وَ الدُّعَاءِ حَتَى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ أَبْلَغُ فِي طَلَبِ
اَلرَّزْقٍ مِنَ الضَّرْبِ فِي الْأَرْضِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.329 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.138 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.784 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1553 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.459
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And (Imam) al-Sadiq {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The sleep of the early morning is
ominous, it drives away sustenance, makes the complexion pale, uglifies and alters it.
It is the sleep of every unfortunate one.
Indeed, Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, distributes sustenance between the rising of the dawn
and the rising of the sun. So beware of that sleep. The manna and quails used to
descend upon the Children of Israel between the rising of the dawn and the rising of
the sun. So whoever slept during that hour, his portion would not descend, and when
he awoke, he would not find his portion, and would be in need of begging and seeking."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ: «نَوْمَةُ ٱَلْغَدَاةِ مَشُومَةٌ تَطْرُدُ ٱلرِّزْقَ وَ تُصَفَّرُ اللّوْنَ وَ تُقَبِّحُهُ وَ تُغَيِّرُهُ وَ هُوَ نَوْمُ كُلِّ مَشُومِ إِنَّ
اَللهَ تَعَالَى يَقْسِمُ الْأَرْزَاقَ مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَ إِيَّاكُمْ وَ تِلْكَ النَّوْمَةَ وَ كَانَ ٱلْمَنّ وَ السَّلْوَى
يَنُزِلُ عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ قَمَنْ نَامَ تِلْكَ السَاعَةَ لَمْ يَنْزِلُ نَصِيبُهُ وَ كَانَ إِذَا
اِنْتَبَهَ فَلا يَرَى نَصِيبَهُ اِحْتَاجَ إِلَى السُّؤالِ وَ الطَّلَبِ».

text_en:
And (Imam) al-Sadiq {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah {SWT}, the
Majestic: ‘"By those who distribute [affairs] by command"‘: (Surah Dhariyat 51:4).
(Imam {a.s} said) "The angels distribute the sustenance of the children of Adam between
the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun. So whoever sleeps during that time has
slept away his sustenance."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ الصَادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ: فِي قَوْلِ اللّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَ «فَالمُقَسِّماتِ أَمْراً» قَالَ «الْمَلائِكَةُ تُقَسِّمُ أَرْزَاقَ بَنِي آدَمَ مَا
بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ فَمَنْ نَامَ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمَا نَامَ عَنْ رِزْقِهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
text_en:
And the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
"Whoever sits in his prayer place from the Fajr prayer until the rising of the sun, Allah
{SWT} will shield him from the Fire."
WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE
AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said:
"And that which is obligatory in prayer is its performance within its time, facing the
Qiblah for it, the opening Takbir, the recitation, the bowing, the glorification in the
bowing, the prostration, the glorification in the prostration, the tashahhud, and the
sending of blessings upon Muhammad {saws} and his family, peace be upon them. So
whoever deliberately leaves out any of these qualities that we have mentioned in his
prayer, his prayer is invalid and he must repeat it. And whoever leaves them out due to
forgetfulness, there are rulings pertaining to that."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَ : «مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي مُصَلاَهُ مِنْ صَلاَةِ ٱلْفَجْرِ إلَى طُلُوعِ ٱَلشَمْسِ سَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ النَّارِ».
٩ - باب تفصيل ما تقدم ذكره في الصلاة من المفروض والمسنون وما يجوز فيها وما لا
يجوز

sending of blessings upon Muhammad {saws} and his family, peace be upon them. So
whoever deliberately leaves out any of these qualities that we have mentioned in his
prayer, his prayer is invalid and he must repeat it. And whoever leaves them out due to
forgetfulness, there are rulings pertaining to that."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING
text_en:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and
al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far {a.s}: "What has Allah {SWT} made obligatory in the prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "The time, purification, bowing, prostration, facing the Qiblah,
supplication, and direction (intention)."
I asked: "And what about everything else?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is Sunnah within the obligatory prayer."
WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ
حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ مَا قَرَضَ اللّهُ فِي الصَّلاةِ
فَقَالَ «الْوَقْتَ وَ الطَّهُورَ وَ الرُّكُوعَ وَ السُّجَودَ وَ الْقِبْلَةَ وَ الدُّعَاءَ وَ التَوَجّهَ» قُلْتُ فَمَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ «سُنَّةٌ فِي
فَرِيضَةِ».

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-
Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, said: "Prayer is made up of three thirds: one third is purification, one
third is bowing, and one third is prostration."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: «الصَّلاةُ ثَلاَثَةُ أَثلاثٍ ثُلُثٌ طَهُورٌ وَ ثُلُثُ رُكُوعٌ وَ ثُلُثٌ سُجُودٌ».

text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, said: "There is no prayer without purification."
text_ar: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا صَلاةً إِلا بِطَهُورِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "When the time (for prayer) enters, purification and prayer become
obligatory, and there is no prayer without purification."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said:
"If one prays before the time deliberately, he must repeat it. But if he was mistaken in
that, and the time enters while he is still in some part of it, it suffices him. And if he
completes it before the time, then he must repeat it."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا دَخَلَ الْوَقْتُ وَجَبَ ٱلطَّهُورُ وَ الصَّلاَةُ
وَ لاَ صَلاَةَ إِلاَّ بِطَهُورٍ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (فان صلى قبل الوقت متعمدا أعاد، وان اخطأ في ذلك فادركه الوقت وهو منها في شئ اجزأته ،
بول فرغمنهاقا المقت أعادا

completes it before the time, then he must repeat it."

ibn Abi al-Bilad from his father from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Whoever performs the prayer outside of its appointed time,
there is no prayer for him."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي الْبِلاَدِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ
أبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ صَلَّى فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتٍ فَلاَ صَلاّةً لَهُ».

text_en:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah
from Aban from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} (said) concerning a man who performed the dawn prayer at night,
deceived by the moonlight, and then slept until the sun rose, and was informed that
he had prayed during the night.
Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "He must repeat his prayer."
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ آللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي
جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى الْغَدَاةَ بِلَيْلِ غَرَّهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ٱلْقَمَرُ وَ نَامَ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَأُخْبِرَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى
بِلَيْلٍ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ صَلاَتَهُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari said: Abdullah ibn Waddah narrated to me from Sama’ah ibn Mihran, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said to me: "Beware of praying before the sun passes the meridian
(before noon), for you would be praying in the time of ‘Asr. It is better for you to pray in
the time of ‘Asr than to pray before the sun has passed the meridian."
text_ar:
عَلِي بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الطَّاطَرِي قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ وَضَاحِ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ : «إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ فَإِنَّكَ تُصَلِّي فِي وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ خَيْرٌ لَكَ أَنْ ثُصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.141 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.70 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.167
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Isma‘il ibn
Riyah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If you perform the prayer while thinking that you are within the
time, but the time had not yet entered, and then the time enters while you are still in
the prayer, it suffices for you."
text_ar:
أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى عن الحسين بن سعيد عن محمد بن أبي عمير عن اسماعيل بن رياح عن أبي عبد
اللّه عليه السلام قال : إذا صليت وانت ترى انك في وقت ولم يدخل الوقت فدخل الوقت وأنت في الصلاة
فقد اجزأت عنك.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father
from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If you perform part of the prayer during travel outside of its
prescribed time, it does not harm (it is not invalid)."

Scholar's Note:
For what is meant by it is the permissibility of delaying the prayer from its time due to
a circumstance, excuse, or necessity. As for performing it early, it is not permissible in
any case.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "If one forgets to face the
Qiblah or errs in it, then remembers or becomes aware of it while the time for prayer
remains, he must repeat the prayer. But if the time has passed, then there is no
obligation to repeat it, unless his prayer, due to forgetfulness or mistake, was
performed while facing away from the Qiblah (to the point of having his back to it); in
that case, he must repeat the prayer whether the time remains or has passed."
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ
عُبَيْدِ اللهِ بْنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا صَلِّيْتَ فِي السَّفَرِ شَيْئاً مِنَ الصَّلاةِ فِي غَيْرٍ وَقْتِهَا
فَلاَ يَضُرُّ».
فان المراد به جواز تأخير الصلاة عن وقتها عند العارض والعذر والاضطرار فأما تقديمها فانه لا يجوز على كل حال.
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (فان نسي استقبال القبلة أو أخطأها ثم ذكرها أو عرفها ووقت الصلاة باق اعاد الصلاة، وان كان
المقت قدمض فلا اعادة عليه الا أنتكم صلاته عل السهمهالخطأ ال استيا القبلة فعليه اعادة الصلاة كل المقت

a circumstance, excuse, or necessity. As for performing it early, it is not permissible in
any case.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "If one forgets to face the
Qiblah or errs in it, then remembers or becomes aware of it while the time for prayer
remains, he must repeat the prayer. But if the time has passed, then there is no

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ya’qub ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked the Righteous servant (Abd al Salih {a.s}): “About a man who prays on a cloudy
day not facing the Qiblah, then the sun appears while he is still within the prayer time,
should he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the Qiblah? And if he had made
every effort to determine the Qiblah, does his prayer suffice?”
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat it as long as the time remains. But if the time has
passed, then there is no repetition upon him."
text_ar:
الحسين بن سعيد عن يعقوب بن يقطين قال سألت عبدا صالحا عليه السلام : عن رجل يصلي في يوم سحاب
على غير القبلة ثم تطلع الشمس وهو في وقت أيعيد الصلاة إذا كان قد صلى على غير القبلة؟ وان كان قد
تحرى القبلة بجهده أتجزيه صلاته؟ فقال : يعيد ما كان في وقت فإذا ذهب الوقت فلا اعادة عليه.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}

passed, then there is no repetition upon him."

chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "A man is in a deserted land on a cloudy day and he prays not
facing the Qiblah. Then it clears up, and he comes to know that he had prayed not
facing the Qiblah, what should he do?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If the time remains, then let him repeat his prayer. But if the time has
passed, then his effort suffices him."
text_ar:
وعنه عن النضر بن سويد عن هشام بن سالم عن سليمان ابن خالد قال قلت لابي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام : الرجل
يكون في قفر من الارض في يوم غيم فيصلي لغير القبلة ثم يصحي فيعلم انه قد صلى لغير القبلة كيف
يصنع؟ فقال : إن كان في وقت فليعد صلاته وإن كان قد مضى الوقت فحسبه اجتهاده.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from
Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If you prayed while not facing the Qiblah, and it becomes clear
to you that you prayed not facing the Qiblah while you are still within the time, then
repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."
text_ar:
محمد بن يعقوب عن الحسين بن محمد عن عبد اللّٰه بن عامر عن علي بن مهزيار عن فضالة بن أيوب عن عبد
الرحمن بن أبي عبد اللّٰه عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام قال : إذا صليت وأنت على غير القبلة واستبان لك انك
صليت على غير القبلة وانت في وقت فأعد، وان فاتك الوقت فلا تعد.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who prays not facing the Qiblah and then
realizes while he is still in the prayer before finishing it.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is facing a direction between the east and the west, then let him
turn his face toward the Qiblah as soon as he realizes. But if he is facing the rear of the
Qiblah, then he must break the prayer, turn his face toward the Qiblah, and then begin
the prayer anew."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And if one forgets the opening
Takbir, whether deliberately or out of forgetfulness, he must repeat the prayer."
text_ar:
وعنه عن أحمد بن ادريس عن أحمد بن محمد ومحمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن أحمد بن يحيى عن أحمد بن
الحسن بن علي عن عمرو بن سعيد عن مصدق بن صدقة عن عمار الساباطي عن أبي عبد اللّه عليه السلام في
رجل صلى على غير القبلة فيعلم وهو في الصلاة قبل أن يفرغ من صلاته قال : ان كان متوجها فيما بين
المشدة والمغب فلحما محمه ال القيلة حين يعلم ، مل كل متمحما السي القيلة فل قطع الصلاة ثم

Takbir, whether deliberately or out of forgetfulness, he must repeat the prayer."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who gave the ‘Iqamah’ for prayer but forgot to say
the Takbirat al-Ihram (opening Takbir) and began the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat it."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ
أَقَامَ الصَّلاةَ فَنَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبَّرَ حَتَّى اِفْتَتَحَ الصَّلاَةَ قَالَ «يُعِيدٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.142 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.351 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.914 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.13
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

the Takbirat al-Ihram (opening Takbir) and began the prayer.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far {a.s} about a man who forgets the Takbirat al-Iftitah (opening Takbir).
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat (the prayer)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ - عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى تَكْبِيرَةَ
الافْتِتَاحٍ قَالَ »يُعِيدُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.347 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.143 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.913 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.12

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah from Safwan from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams {a.s}),
peace be upon them:
(Imam {a.s}) was asked regarding the one who remembers that he did not say the Takbir
at the beginning of his prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is certain that he did not say the Takbir, then he must repeat (the
prayer); but how can he be certain?”
text_ar:
وَعَنَهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَلامُ : فِي الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُكَبَّرْ فِي
أَوْلِ صَلاتِهِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا اِسْتَيْقَنَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُكَبِّرْ فَلْيْعِذْ وَ لَكِنْ كَيْفَ يَسْتَيْقِنُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.143 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.351 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.914 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.13
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}

And from him, from Fadalah from Safwan from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams {a.s}),

(Imam {a.s}) was asked regarding the one who remembers that he did not say the Takbir
at the beginning of his prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is certain that he did not say the Takbir, then he must repeat (the

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dhurayh ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi from Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who forgets to say the Takbir until he has already recited
(Qur’an).
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him say the Takbir."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ ذَرِيحِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْمُحَارِبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ حَتَّى قَرَأَ قَالَ «يُكَبِّرُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.143 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.351 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.914 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.13
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who
said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who forgets to begin the
prayer (with the opening Takbir) until he has bowed.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat the prayer."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَجِيهِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى أَنْ يَفْتَتِحَ الصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ الصَّلاَةَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.143 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.351 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.914 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.13

I asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who forgets to begin the
prayer (with the opening Takbir) until he has bowed.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat the prayer."

text_en:
And from him, from al-Barqi from Dhurayh al-Muharibi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had already
recited (Qur’an).
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him say the Takbir."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْبَرْقِيّ عَنْ ذَرِيحِ الْمُحَارِبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبَّرَ حَتَّى قَرَأَ
قَالَ «يُكَبِّرُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from Abdullah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn
Mahziyar from Fadalah from Aban from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik and Ibn Abi Ya’fur:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who performs prayer but does not begin
with the Takbir, does the Takbir of bowing suffice him?
Imam {a.s} said: "No. Rather, he must repeat his prayer if he remembers that he did not
say the Takbir."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْأَشْعَرِيَّ عَنْ عَبْدِ آللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةً عَنْ أَبَانٍ
عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فَلَمْ يَفْتَتِحْ
بِالتَّكْبِيرِ هَلْ يُجْزِيهِ تَكْبِيرَةُ الرُكُوعِ قَالَ «لا بَلْ يُعِيدُ صَلاَتَهُ إِذَا حَفِظَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يُكَبَّرْ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.347 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.143 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.352 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.913 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.16
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who transmitted it with an elevated chain from al-Ridha {a.s}:
(Imam {a.s}) said: "The imam (of prayer) bears the mistakes of those behind him, except
for the Takbirat al-Iftitah (the opening Takbir)."
text_ar: وَعَنَهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى رَفَعَهُ عَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «الْإمَامُ يَحْمِلُ أَوْهَامَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ إِلاَ تَكْبِيرَةَ الاِفْتِتَاحِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.347 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.406 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.144 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.913 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.14 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.15 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.240 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.239 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.250

text_chunk:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who transmitted it with an elevated chain from al-Ridha {a.s}:
(Imam {a.s}) said: "The imam (of prayer) bears the mistakes of those behind him, except
for the Takbirat al-Iftitah (the opening Takbir)."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and
al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "If at the beginning of your prayer, after the opening (du’a’), you said
the first of the twenty-one Takbirs, then forgot all the rest of the Takbirs and did not say
them, that first Takbir suffices you for all the Takbirs of the prayer."
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ
حَمَّادٍ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ : «إِذَا أَنْتَ كَبَّرْتَ فِي أَوَّلِ
صَلآتِكَ بَعْدَ الاِسْتِفْتَاحِ بِإِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ تَكْبِيرَةً ثُمَ نَسِيتَ التَّكْبِيرَ كُلَّهُ وَ لَمْ تُكَبَّرْ أَجْزَأَكَ التَّكْبِيرُ الْأَوْلُ - عَنْ
تَكْبِيرٍ الصَّلاةٍ كُلَّهَا».

text_chunk:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and
al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "If at the beginning of your prayer, after the opening (du’a’), you said
the first of the twenty-one Takbirs, then forgot all the rest of the Takbirs and did not say
them, that first Takbir suffices you for all the Takbirs of the prayer."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from
Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had already entered
into the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "Was it not his intention to say the Takbir?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then let him continue with his prayer."
text_ar:
وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ
الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلثُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «أَ لَيْسَ
كَانَ مِنْ نِيَّتِهِ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ «فَلْيَمْضٍ فِي صَلاَتِهِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.343 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.144 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.352 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.915 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.15

As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from
Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who forgot to say the Takbir until he had already entered
into the prayer.

I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then let him continue with his prayer."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr
from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "A man forgot to say the Takbirat al-Iftitah (opening Takbir) until he
said the Takbir for bowing."
Imam {a.s} said: "It suffices him."

Scholar's Note:
So these two narrations are to be understood as referring to the one who forgot the
Takbirat al-Iftitah and then was not certain that he had failed to say it, but rather was
in doubt, then in such a case, he must continue with his prayer. As for when there is
certainty and knowledge that he did not say the Takbir, then it is obligatory for him to
repeat the prayer, based on the previously mentioned reports.
Also, the narration we previously cited from Ibn Abi Ya’fur and al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik
from Abu Abdillah {a.s} contains an explicit statement that the Takbir during bowing
does not suffice for the Takbirat al-Iftitah, and that with certainty (of omission), the
prayer must be repeated. Thus, we know that what is contained in these two reports,
that it is acceptable, is only in the case of doubt, not certainty.
What further confirms what we have mentioned, in addition to what has already been
presented, is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْخَطَابِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ تَكْبِيرَةَ الاِفْتِتَاحِ حَتَّى كَبَّرَ لِلرُكُوعِ فَقَالَ «أَجْزَأَهُ».
فهذان الحديثان محمولان على من نسي تكبيرة الافتتاح ثم لم يتحقق انه لم يكبر بل يكون شاكا فانه يجب عليه حينئذ
المضي في صلاته ، فأما مع اليقين والعلم بانه لم يكبر وجب عليه إعادة الصلاة بدلالة ما قدمناه من الاخبار، وأيضا الخبر
الذي قدمناه عن ابن أبي يعفور والفضل بن عبد الملك عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام تضمن التصريح بان التكبير في الركوع
لا يجزي عن تكبيرة الافتتاح، وأن مع العلم لا بد من إعادة الصلاة فعلمنا ان ما تضمنه هذان الخبران من ان ذلك جايز انما
هو مع الشك دون اليقين، والذي يؤكد ما ذكرناه ايضا مضافا الى ما قدمناه ما رواه:
commentary:
So these two narrations are to be understood as referring to the one who forgot the
Takbirat al-Iftitah and then was not certain that he had failed to say it, but rather was
in doubt, then in such a case, he must continue with his prayer. As for when there is
certainty and knowledge that he did not say the Takbir, then it is obligatory for him to
repeat the prayer, based on the previously mentioned reports.

does not suffice for the Takbirat al-Iftitah, and that with certainty (of omission), the
prayer must be repeated. Thus, we know that what is contained in these two reports,
that it is acceptable, is only in the case of doubt, not certainty.
What further confirms what we have mentioned, in addition to what has already been
presented, is what was narrated:

What further confirms what we have mentioned, in addition to what has already been

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Abu Ja’far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn
‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "A man forgets the first Takbir of the opening (Takbirat al-Iftitah)."
Imam {a.s} said: "If he remembers it before bowing, let him say the Takbir, then recite,
then bow. And if he remembers it during the prayer, let him say it while standing, in the
place of the Takbir, before the recitation and after the recitation."
I asked: "And if he remembers it after the prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Then let him make it up, and there is nothing upon him."

Scholar's Note:
His {a.s} saying, peace be upon him, ‘then let him make it up’, means the prayer, and He
{a.s} did not mean only the Takbir itself.
As for His {a.s} saying, ‘and there is nothing upon him’, it means that there is no
punishment upon him, because he did not deliberately omit it, but rather forgot. So if
he repeats the prayer, then there is nothing upon him. As for what was narrated:
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ
بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ يَنْسَى أَوَّلَ تَكْبِيرَةٍ مِنَ الاِفْتِتَاحِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ
ذَكَرَهَا قَبْلَ الرُّكُوعِ كَبَّرَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ثُمَّ رَكَعَ وَ إِنْ ذَكَرَهَا فِي الصَّلاَةِ كَبَّرَهَا فِي قِيَامِهِ فِي مَوْضِعِ التَّكْبِيرَةِ قَبْلَ الْقِرَاءَةِ
وَ بَعدَ الْقِرَاءَةِ» قُلْتُ فَإنْ ذَكَرَهَا بَعْدَ الصْلاَةِ قَالَ «فَلْيَقْضِهَا وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
قوله عليه السلام فليقضها يعني الصلاة ولم يرد التكبيرة وحدها ، وأما قوله ولا شئ عليه يعني من العقاب لانه لم يتعمد
تركها وإنما نسي فإذا أعاد الصلاة لم يكن عليه شئ، وأما ما رواه:
commentary:
His {a.s} saying, peace be upon him, ‘then let him make it up’, means the prayer, and He
{a.s} did not mean only the Takbir itself.
As for His {a.s} saying, ‘and there is nothing upon him’, it means that there is no
punishment upon him, because he did not deliberately omit it, but rather forgot. So if
he repeats the prayer, then there is nothing upon him. As for what was narrated:
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.343 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.145 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.352 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.916 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.14

text_chunk:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Abu Ja’far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn
‘Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "A man forgets the first Takbir of the opening (Takbirat al-Iftitah)."

I asked: "And if he remembers it after the prayer?"

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah ibn Mihran from Abu
Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who stood in prayer and forgot to say the Takbir,
so he began with the recitation.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he remembers it while he is still standing and before he bows, then
let him say the Takbir. But if he has already bowed, then let him continue with his
prayer."

Scholar's Note:
So this report is also like the two preceding ones, because the intended meaning of
the wording in the report is: ‘If he remembers it while standing before bowing, then let
him say the Takbir; but if he bows without remembering, then let him continue with his
prayer.’
There is nothing in the report that says: ‘If he bows while aware that he did not say the
Takbir, then let him continue with his prayer.’
And since the interpretation we have given is possible, it does not contradict what has
already been presented.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And if one leaves out the
recitation due to forgetfulness, then there is no obligation to repeat the prayer."
text_ar:
عَلِيْ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثِمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا
عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَامَ فِي الصَّلاةِ وَ نَسِيَ أَنْ يُكَبَّرَ فَبَدَأْ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ ذَكَرَهَا وَ هَوَ قَائِمٌ قَبْلَ
أَنْ يَزْكَعَ فَلْيُكَبِّزْ وَ إِنْ رَكَعَ فَلْيَمْضٍ فِي صَلاَتِهِ».
فهذا الخبر ايضا مثل الاولين لان تقدير الكلام في الخبر إن ذكرها وهو قائم قبل أن يركع فليكبر وإن ركع من غير أن يذكر
فليمض في صلاته ، وليس في الخبر انه إذا ركع وهو ذاكر انه لم يكبر فليمض في صلاته وإذا احتمل ما قلناه لم يناف ما
قدمناه. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (وإن ترك القراءة ناسيا فلا إعادة عليه).
commentary:
So this report is also like the two preceding ones, because the intended meaning of
the wording in the report is: ‘If he remembers it while standing before bowing, then let
him say the Takbir; but if he bows without remembering, then let him continue with his
prayer.’
There is nothing in the report that says: ‘If he bows while aware that he did not say the
Takbir, then let him continue with his prayer.’
And since the interpretation we have given is possible, it does not contradict what has
already been presented.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And if one leaves out the
recitation due to forgetfulness, then there is no obligation to repeat the prayer."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from
Rib’i ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them, who
said:
(Imams {a.s} said) "Indeed, Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, has made bowing and
prostration obligatory, and the recitation is Sunnah. So whoever leaves the recitation
deliberately must repeat the prayer, but whoever forgets the recitation, his prayer is
valid, and there is nothing upon him."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ
مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَرَضَ الرُكُوعَ وَ السُجُودَ وَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةُ سُنَّةٌ فَمَنْ
تَرَكَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةَ مُتَعَمَّداً أَعَادَ الصَّلاةَ وَ مَنْ نَسِيَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةَ فَقَدْ تَمَّثَ صَلاَثُهُ وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.347 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.345 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.146 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.353 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.83 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.919 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.87 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.94 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.142

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn
Ya’qub from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "I performed the obligatory prayer but forgot to recite
anything in my entire prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "Did you not complete the bowing and the prostration?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then your prayer is complete, if it was out of forgetfulness."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمِ قَالَ:
قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ إِنَّي صَلِّيْتُ الْمَكْتُوبَةَ فَنَسِيتُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فِي صَلاَتِي كُلَّهَا فَقَالَ «أَ لَيْسَ قَدْ أَتْمَمْتَ
الرُّكُوعَ وَ السُجُودَ» قُلْتُ بَلَى فَقَالَ «فَقَدْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُكَ إِذَا كَانَ نِسْيَاناً».

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn
Ya’qub from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "I performed the obligatory prayer but forgot to recite
anything in my entire prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "Did you not complete the bowing and the prostration?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then your prayer is complete, if it was out of forgetfulness."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa and Fadalah from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
who said:
I asked: "A man forgets the recitation in the first two rak’ahs, and then remembers
during the last two that he did not recite."
Imam {a.s} said: "Did he complete the bowing and the prostration?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} said: "I dislike to make the end of my prayer the beginning of it."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ
الرَّجُلُ يَسْهُو عَنِ الْقِرَاءَةِ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ فَيَذْكُرُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَقْرَأ قَالَ «أَتَمَّ الرُّكُوعَ وَ
السُّجُورَ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ «إِنِّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَجْعَلَ آخِرَ صَلاَتِي أَوَلَهَا».

And from him, from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah from Abu Basir, who said:
(It was said) "If one forgets to recite in the first and second rak’ahs, the glorification in
the bowing and prostration suffices him. And if it is the dawn (Fajr) prayer and he
forgets to recite in it, then let him continue with his prayer."

وَعَنَهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةً عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: «إِذَا نَسِيَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِي ٱلْأُولَى وَ الثَّانِيَةِ
أَجْزَأَهُ تَسْبِيحُ الرُكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ الْغَدَاةُ فَنَسِيَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِيهَا فَلْيَمْضٍ فِي صَلَاتِهِ».

text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad ibn Muslim
from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatihah in his prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no prayer for him unless he recites it, whether aloud or
silently."

Scholar's Note:
What is meant by this is that if he intentionally does not recite it, then there is no prayer
for him. But as for forgetting, then his prayer is valid. What clarifies what we have
mentioned is:
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ
عَنِ الَّذِي لا يَقْرَأَ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ فِي صَلاتِهِ قَالَ «لا صَلاَةً لَهُ إِلاّ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ بِهَا فِي جَهْرٍ أَوْ إِخفَاتِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who stands in prayer and forgets Surat al-Fatihah.
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him say: ‘I seek refuge in Allah {SWT} from the accursed Shaytan.
Indeed, Allah {SWT} is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,’ then let him recite it as long as
he has not bowed. For there is no (valid) recitation until he begins with it, whether
aloud or silently. But if he has bowed, it suffices him, if Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, wills."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَيَنْسَى
فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ قَالَ «فَلْيَقُلْ أَسْتَعِيذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرّجِيمِ إِنَّ آللَّهَ «هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ» ثُمَّ ليَقْرَأْهَا مَا دَامَ لَمْ
يَرْكَعْ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ قِرَاءَةَ حَتَّى يَبْدَأْ بِهَا فِي جَهْرٍ أَوْ إِخْفَاتٍ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا رَكَعَ أَجْرَأْهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ».

text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Indeed, Allah {SWT} has made bowing and prostration obligatory
in the prayer. Do you not see that if a man enters Islam and does not know how to recite
the Qur’an, it suffices him to say the Takbir, to glorify (Allah {SWT}), and to pray?"

Scholar's Note:
As for the one who deliberately leaves out the recitation, we have already clarified that
there is no prayer for him. What further reinforces and clarifies this is what was
narrated:
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بَنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : «إِنّ آَللَّهَ فَرَضَ مِنَ ٱلصَّلاةِ
الرّكُوعَ وَ السُّجُودَ أَلَا تَرَى لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلا دَخَلَ فِي الْإِسْلاَمِ لا يُحْسِنُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ أَجْزَأَهُ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ وَ يُسَبَّحَ وَ
يُصَلِّيّ».
فأما من ترك القراءة متعمدا فقد بينا انه لا صلاة له ويزيده بيانا ما رواه:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al-’Alaʾ from
Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the one who does not recite Surat al-Fatihah in his prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no prayer for him unless he begins with it, whether aloud or
silently."
I said: "Which of the two do you prefer: if he is fearful or in a hurry, should he recite a
(different) Surah or Surat al-Fatihah?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Surat al-Fatihah."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونَسَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ
عَنِ الّذِي لا يَقْرَأْ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ «لاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَبْدَأْ بِهَا فِي جَهْرٍ أَوْ إِخْفَاتِ» قُلْتُ أَيُّهُمَا أَحَبٌ
إِلَيْكَ إِذَا كَانَ خَائِفاً أَوْ مُسْتَعْجِلا يَقْرَأْ بِسُورَةٍ أَوْ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ قَالَ » بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.317 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.147 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.310 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.653 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.37

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Sa’d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn
‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "A man recites aloud in a place where he should not recite aloud, and
recites silently where he should not recite silently, or he omits recitation where
recitation is required, or he recites where recitation is not required."
Imam {a.s} said: "If he did any of that out of forgetfulness or inattentiveness, then there
is nothing upon him."
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ
زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجْلْ جَهَرَ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فِيمَا لا يَنْبَغِي الْجَهْرُ فِيهِ وَ أَخْفَى فِيمَا لا يَنْبَغِي
الْإِخْفَاتُ فِيهِ وَ تَرَكَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةَ فِيمَا يَنْبَغِي الْقِرَاءَةُ فِيهِ أَوْ قَرَأَ فِيمَا لا يَنْبَغِي الْقِرَاءَةُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ «أَيِّ ذَلِكَ فَعَلَ نَاسِياً
أَوْ سَاهِياً فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».

text_en:
And what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Abu al-Jawzaʾ from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from ‘Amr ibn
Khalid:
Zayd ibn Ali, peace be upon him, said: “I performed the Maghrib prayer with my father
(Imam Ali ibn Husayn {a.s}), peace be upon him, and He {a.s} forgot Surat al-Fatihah in the
first rak’ah, so He {a.s} recited it in the second.”
text_ar:
وَ الَّذِي رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِي الْجَوْزَاءِ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلَوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ عَلِيّ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ فَنَسِيَ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى فَقَرَأَهَا فِي الثَّانِيَةِ.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.148 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.354 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.922 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.92

text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from al-Husayn
ibn Hammad from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "I forget the recitation in the first rak’ah."
Imam {a.s} said: "Recite in the second."
I said: "I forget in the second."
Imam {a.s} said: "Recite in the third."
I said: "I forget in my entire prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "If you have maintained the bowing and the prostration, then your
prayer is complete."

Scholar's Note:
His saying, peace be upon him, ‘If you missed it in the first, then recite in the second,’
does not mean that he should repeat what was missed in the first rak’ah, but rather
that he should perform the recitation specific to the second and third rak’ahs, while
the ruling for the first rak’ah has already passed.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "If one omits the bowing
(ruku’), whether forgetfully or deliberately, he must repeat (the prayer)."
What indicates this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ بْنِ عَمْرِو عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أُسْهُو عَنِ الْقِرَاءَةِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى قَالَ «اِقْرَأْ فِي الثَانِيَةِ» قُلْتُ أَسْهُو فِي الثَّانِيَةِ قَالَ
«اِقْرَأُ فِي الثَّالِئَةِ» قُلْتُ أَسْهُو فِي صَلاَتِي كُلَّهَا قَالَ «إِذَا حَفِظْتَ الرُكُوعَ وَ السُّجُودَ تَمَّثَ صَلاَثُكَ».
قوله عليه السلام إذا فاتك في الاولى فاقرأ في الثانية لم يرد أن يعيد قراءة ما قد فاته في الاوله ، وإنما أراد أن يقرأ في
الثانية والثالثة ما يخصهما من القراءة فأما الاولة فقد مضى حكمها.
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (فان ترك الركوع ناسيا كان أو متعمدا أعاد). يدل على ذلك ما رواه :

Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If a man is certain that he has left out a rak’ah from the prayer,
and he has already performed two prostrations but omitted the bowing, then he must
begin the prayer anew."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا أَيْقَنَ الرَّجُلُ أَنَّهُ تَرَكَ رَكْعَةً
مِنَ الصَّلاَةِ وَ قَدْ سَجَدَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ وَ تَرَكَ الرُّكُوعَ اِسْتَأْنَفَ الصَّلاةَ».

And from him, from Fadalah from Rifa’ah from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who forgets to bow until he prostrates and stands up
again.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must begin the prayer anew."
text_ar:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَنْسَى أَنْ يَرْكَعَ حَتَّى يَسْجُدَ وَ

Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who forgets to bow.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must begin the prayer anew until he places everything in its proper
place."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى أَنْ
يَرْكَعَ قَالَ «يَسْتَقْبِلُ حَتَّى يَضَعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَوْضِعَهُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far {a.s} about a man who forgot to bow.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat (the prayer)."

Scholar's Note:
All of these narrations are to be understood as referring to someone who forgets the
bowing (ruku’) in the first two rak’ahs, then in that case, it is obligatory for him to begin
the prayer anew in all situations if he remembers.
However, if the forgetfulness occurs in the last two rak’ahs and he remembers while
still in the prayer, then he should disregard the two prostrations of the rak’ah in which
he forgot the bowing and complete the prayer.
What indicates this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ
يَزْكَعَ قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ الْإِعَادَةً».
هذه الاخبار كلها محمولة على انه ينسى الركوع في الركعتين الاولتين فانه يجب عليه استيناف الصلاة على كل حال إذا
اذكر، فأما إذا كان النسيان في الركعتين الاخيرتين وذكر وهو بعد في الصلاة فليلق السجدتين من الركعة التي نسي ركوعها
ويتم الصلاة ، والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:

All of these narrations are to be understood as referring to someone who forgets the

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Sa’d ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from al-’Alaʾ from Muhammad
ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who, after prostrating, doubts whether he
bowed.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he becomes certain, then let him disregard the two prostrations that
have no bowing associated with them, and let him continue his prayer to completion.
But if he only becomes certain after he has finished and exited the prayer, then let him
stand and pray one rak’ah and two prostrations, and there is nothing upon him."
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ الْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَدٍ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ شَكَّ بَعْدَ مَا سَجَدَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ قَالَ «فَإِنِ اِسْتَيْقَنَ فَلْيُلْقِ السَّجْدَتَيْنِ اللَّتَيْنِ لا رَكْعَةَ لَهُمَا
فَيَبْنِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ عَلَى التَّمَامِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَمْ يَسْتَيْقِنْ إِلاَّ بَعْدَ مَا قَرَغَ وَ اِنْصَرَفَ فَلْيَقُمْ فَلْيُصَلِّ رَكْعَةً وَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ
وَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.149 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.356 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.314

Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-’Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who forgot a rak’ah from his prayer until he
finished it, then remembered that he had not bowed.
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him stand, perform the bowing, and prostrate, and then perform
the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw)."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْعِيصِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ
نَسِيَ رَكْعَةً مِنْ صَلاتِهِ حَتَّى فَرَغَ مِنْهَا ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ قَالَ «يَقُومُ فَيَرْكَعُ وَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from Mansur from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If a man is certain that he left out a rak’ah from the prayer, and
he had already performed two prostrations but omitted the bowing, then he must
begin the prayer anew."

Scholar's Note:
The interpretation of this report is that it should be understood as referring to prayers
in which forgetfulness is not excused, such as the Fajr (dawn) and Maghrib (sunset)
prayers, and the like, or to the first two rak’ahs of the four-unit (ruba’iyyah) prayers, so
that the various narrations do not contradict one another.
It is also possible that what is meant by his saying ‘he must begin the prayer anew’ is
that he must begin the rak’ah that he missed, and the report does not state that he
must begin the entire prayer from the start. And what clarifies what we have mentioned
is:
text_ar:
فأما ما رواه الحسين بن سعيد عن صفوان عن منصور عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال : إذا
يقن الرجل أنه ترك ركعة من الصلاة وقد سجد سجدتين وترك الركوع استأنف الصلاة.
فالوجه في هذا الخبر ان نحمله على صلاة لا يجوز فيها السهو مثل الغداة والمغرب وما اشبههما، أو على الركعتين الاولتين
من الرباعيات لئلا تتنافى الاخبار، ويحتمل أن يكون أراد بقوله استأنف الصلاة يعني الركعة التي فاتته ، وليس في الخبر
أنه يستأنف الصلاة من اولها، والذي يكشف عما ذكرناه :
commentary:
The interpretation of this report is that it should be understood as referring to prayers
in which forgetfulness is not excused, such as the Fajr (dawn) and Maghrib (sunset)
prayers, and the like, or to the first two rak’ahs of the four-unit (ruba’iyyah) prayers, so
that the various narrations do not contradict one another.
It is also possible that what is meant by his saying ‘he must begin the prayer anew’ is
that he must begin the rak’ah that he missed, and the report does not state that he
must begin the entire prayer from the start. And what clarifies what we have mentioned
is:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
What was narrated by Sa’d from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman
from Hakam ibn Hukaym, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who forgets a rak’ah, or a prostration, or
something from his prayer, and then remembers afterward.
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him make up exactly that which he missed."
So I asked: "Should he repeat the entire prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "If one doubts whether he
performed the bowing while he is still standing, then let him bow. But if he has already
entered another position, such as prostration or otherwise, then let him continue with
his prayer and there is nothing upon him."
This also applies if he is in the last two rak’ahs (of a four-unit prayer), because if the
doubt occurs in the first two rak’ahs, he must restart the prayer, as he has not
completed their number with certainty, and there is a saying that any forgetfulness
that occurs in the first two rak’ahs obligates repeating the prayer.
What supports the first category (that he continues if the doubt occurs in the last two)
from what has preceded is what was narrated:
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ حَكَمِ بْنِ حُكَيْمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا

ذَلِكَ بِعَيْنِهِ» فَقُلْتُ أَ يُعِيدُ الصَّلاَةَ فَقَالَ «لا».

الانه انا كلف الكمت الاوات

Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Hammad from ‘Imran al-Halabi, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "A man doubts while he is standing and does not know whether he
has bowed or not."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then let him bow."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ ٱلْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ يَشُكْ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ فَلاَ يَدْرِي أَرَكَعَ
أَمْ لاَ قَالَ «فَلْيَرْكَعْ».

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan, and Fadalah from Husayn from Ibn Muskan
from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who doubts while he is standing and does not
know whether he has bowed or not.
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him bow and prostrate."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا

Imam {a.s} said: "Let him bow."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Aban from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "I complete my standing but do not know whether I have
bowed or not."
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, you have bowed, so continue with your prayer, for that is only from
Shaytan."

Scholar's Note:
This is not in contradiction to what we have previously mentioned, because what He
{a.s}, peace be upon him, intended was the case where a person has completed
standing in the fourth rak’ah and does not know whether he bowed in the third or not,
then, in such a situation, he must continue with his prayer. This falls under the second
category we previously explained, namely: if one doubts about the bowing after having
entered into another position, he continues with his prayer.
What confirms what we have said is:
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
أَسْتَتِمُ قَائِماً فَلاَ أَدْرِي رَكَعْتُ أَمْ لا قَالَ «بَلَى قَدْ رَكَعْتَ فَامْضٍ فِي صَلاَتِكَ فَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ».
فليس بمناف لما ذكرناه لانه إنما أراد عليه السلام إذا استتم قائما من الركعة الرابعة فلا يدري أركع في الثالثة أم لا فحينئذ
يجب عليه المضي في صلاته لانه صار من القسم الثاني الذي قدمناه ، وهو انه إذا شك في الركوع وقد دخل في حالة
اخرى يمضي في صلاته، ويؤكد ما ذكرنا :

This is not in contradiction to what we have previously mentioned, because what He

then, in such a situation, he must continue with his prayer. This falls under the second
category we previously explained, namely: if one doubts about the bowing after having
entered into another position, he continues with his prayer.
What confirms what we have said is:

text_en:
What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "I am in prostration and I doubt, did I bow or not?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Continue (with your prayer)."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ أَشُكْ وَ أَنَا سَاجِدٌ
فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَرَكَعْتُ أَمْ لاَ قَالَ «إِمْضٍ».

Sa’d from Abu Ja’far from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn

I asked Him {a.s} about a man who, after prostrating, doubts whether he had bowed.
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him continue with his prayer."
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا
السَّلَامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ شَكَّ بَعْدَ مَا سَجَدَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ قَالَ «يَمْضِي فِي صَلاتِهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Him from Abu Ja’far from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "A man moves down toward prostration and does not know
whether he bowed or not."
Imam {a.s} said: "He has bowed."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said:
"And if someone omits two prostrations from one rak’ah, he must repeat (the prayer)
in all cases. But if he forgets one of them and then remembers it in the second rak’ah
before bowing, he should lower himself, perform that prostration, then stand up and
resume the recitation, or the glorification (tasbih) if he is in the last two rak’ahs, as we
have previously explained. And if he does not remember it until after bowing in the
second rak’ah, then he must make it up after the salam and perform two prostrations
of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي
عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ أَهْوَى إِلَى السُّجُودِ فَلَمْ يَدْرِ أَرَكَعَ أَمْ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ قَالَ «قَدْ رَكَعَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (وإن ترك سجدتين من ركعة واحدة اعاد على كل حال ، فان نسي واحدة منهما ثم ذكرها في الركعة
الثانية قا الكم أسا نفسه مسحدهاثه قاه فاستأنف القداءة أمالت
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said:
"And if someone omits two prostrations from one rak’ah, he must repeat (the prayer)
in all cases. But if he forgets one of them and then remembers it in the second rak’ah
before bowing, he should lower himself, perform that prostration, then stand up and
resume the recitation, or the glorification (tasbih) if he is in the last two rak’ahs, as we
have previously explained. And if he does not remember it until after bowing in the
second rak’ah, then he must make it up after the salam and perform two prostrations
of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."
