author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah,
from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “We commonly say that whoever prays while sitting without an
excuse, his prayer counts as two rak’ahs for one, and two prostrations for one.”
Imam {a.s} said: "It is not like that, it is complete for you."
text_ar:
رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ
سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّا
نَتَحَدَّثُ نَقُولُ مَنْ صَلَّى وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ كَانَتْ صَلاَتُهُ رَكَعَتَيْنِ بِرَكْعَةٍ وَ سَجْدَتَيْنٍ بِسَجْدَةٍ فَقَالَ «لَيْسَ
هُوَ هَكَذَا هِيَ تَامَّةً لَكُمْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Sa’d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Mu’awiyah ibn
Maysarah:
That he (narrator) heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say, or He {a.s} was asked: “Whether a man
may pray while sitting cross-legged (‘mutarabbi’an’) or with his legs stretched out.”
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
text_ar:
سَغدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ : أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ أَوْ سُئِلَ أَيُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ مُتَرَبِّعاً وَ مَبْسُوطَ الرِّجْلَيْنِ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.170 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.111
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Humran ibn
A’yan, from one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them, who said:
(Imam {a.s} said) "My father, when He {a.s} prayed sitting, would sit cross-legged
(‘tarrabba’a’), and when He {a.s} bowed, he would fold his legs."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘And it suffices for the sick
person and the one in haste to recite only Surat al-Hamd in the first two rak’ahs of their
obligatory prayers’ up to his statement: ‘And whoever forgets an obligatory prayer’, all
of this has already been explained previously, so there is no need to repeat it.
Then he said, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him: ‘Whoever forgets an obligatory prayer,
let him make it up whenever he remembers it, unless it is at the end time of a second
prayer, in which case making up the missed one would cause him to miss the second;
in that case, he should not delay the second.’
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ حُمْرَانَ بْنِ أَغْيَنَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا
السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «كَانَ أَبِي إِذَا صَلَّى جَالِساً تَرَبَّعَ فَإِذَا رَكَّعَ ثَنَى رِجْلَيْهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ويجزي للعليل والمستعجل ان يصليا في الركعتين الاولتين من فرايضهما بسورة الحمد وحدها)

ح4 فلا محه لاعليته ثمقا حمهالله . لمصن فضة فلقضه

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Tatari, from Ibn Ziyad, from Hammad, from Nu’man al-Razi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who missed some prayers and then remembered
them at sunrise or at sunset.
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him pray as soon as he remembers."
text_ar:
الطَّاطَرِيّ عَنِ اِبْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ نُعْمَانَ ٱلرَّازِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ فَاتَهُ شَيْءٌ مِنَ
الصَّلَوَاتِ فَذَكَرَ عِنْدَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِهَا قَالَ «فَلْيُصَلّ جينَ ذَكَرَهُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.171 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.354 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.240 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.244
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Ibn Ziyad, from Zurarah and others, from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
He {a.s} was asked about a man who prayed without ‘taharah’ (ritual purity), or who
forgot prayers and did not perform them, or who slept through them.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should perform them whenever he remembers them, at whatever
hour he remembers, whether night or day."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى بِغَيْرِ طَهُورِ أَوْ نَسِيَ
صَلَوَاتُ لَمْ يُصَلَّهَا أَوْ نَامَ عَنْهَا قَالَ «يُصَلَّيهَا إِذَا ذَكَرَهَا فِي أَيَّةٍ سَاعَةٍ ذَكَرَهَا لَيْلاً أَوْ نَهَاراً».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.171 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.354
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Hashim ibn Abi
Sa’id al-Makkari, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "There are five prayers which you may perform at any time:
the prayer of the eclipse (‘salat al-kusuf’), the funeral prayer (‘salat al-mayyit’), the
prayer of ‘ihram’, a missed prayer that was not performed (‘salat allati tafut’), and the
circumambulation prayer (‘salat al-tawaf’).
All of these may be performed from Fajr until sunrise, and after ‘Asr until night."
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ هَاشِمِ بْنِ أَبِي سَعِيدِ الْمُكَارِي عَنْ أَبِي
بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «خَمْسُ صَلَوَاتُ تُصَلَّيهِنَّ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتِ صَلاَةُ ٱَلْكُسُوفِ وَ الصَّلاَةُ عَلَى
الْمَيَّتِ وَصَلاَةُ الْإِحْرَامِ وَ الصَّلاَةُ اَلَّتِي تَفُوتُ وَ صَلَاَةُ الطَّوَافِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْعَصْرِ إِلَى
اللّيْلِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.287 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.171 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.353 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.241 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.70
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma’il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris, from
Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: "There are five prayers that are never to be abandoned
under any circumstance: when you perform ‘tawaf’ of the House (Ka’bah), when you
intend to enter into ‘ihram’, the prayer of the eclipse (‘salat al-kusuf’), when you forget
a prayer, then pray it when you remember, and the funeral prayer (‘salat al-janazah’)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ
صَفَوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «خَمْسُ صَلَوَاتُ لاَ تُثْرَكُ عَلَى
كُلِّ حَالٍ إِذَا طُفْتَ بِالْبَيْتِ وَ إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تُحْرِمَ وَ صَلاَةُ الْكُسُوفِ وَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ فَصَلِّ إِذَا ذَكَزْتَ وَ الْجِنَازَةُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.287 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.172 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.353 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.241 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.70
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma’il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris, from
Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: "There are five prayers that are never to be abandoned
under any circumstance: when you perform ‘tawaf’ of the House (Ka’bah), when you
intend to enter into ‘ihram’, the prayer of the eclipse (‘salat al-kusuf’), when you forget
a prayer, then pray it when you remember, and the funeral prayer (‘salat al-janazah’)."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya’qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn
Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who forgets the Dhuhr prayer until the time of ‘Asr enters.
Imam {a.s} said: "He begins with Dhuhr, and likewise with the (other) prayers, begin with
the one you forgot, unless you fear that the time of the current prayer will end. In that
case, begin with the one whose time you are in, and then make up the one you forgot."
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ الظُهْرَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ وَقْتُ ٱلْعَصْرِ قَالَ «يَبْدَأُ بِالظُهْرِ وَ كَذَلِكَ الصَّلَوَاتُ تَبْدَأُ بِالَتِي نَسِيتَ إِلَّ أَنْ
تَخَافَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ وَقْتُ الصَّلاةِ فَتَبْدَأ بِالَّتِي أَنْتَ فِي وَقْتِهَا ثُمَّ تَقْضِي الَّتِي نَسِيتَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.292 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.172 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.268 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.287 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1012 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.290

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah,
from Abu Ja’far {a.s}:
He {a.s} was asked about a man who prayed without ritual purification (‘tahur’), or forgot
a prayer and did not perform it, or slept through it.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should make it up whenever he remembers it, at whatever hour he
remembers, by night or by day. But if the time of another prayer enters and he has not
yet completed the missed one, then let him continue, as long as he does not fear that
the time for the present prayer will expire. If he fears that, then this current prayer takes
precedence, so let him pray it. Then, once he has prayed it, he should make up the
missed prayer afterwards. And he must not perform any supererogatory (‘nafl’) rak’ah
until he has made up all of the obligatory (‘faridah’) prayers."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ : أَنَّهُ
سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلِّى بِغَيْرِ طَهُورِ أَوْ نَسِيَ صَلاَةً لَمْ يُصَلَّهَا أَوْ نَامَ عَنْهَا فَقَالَ «يَقْضِيهَا إِذَا ذَكَرَهَا فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ
ذَكَرَهَا مِنْ لَيْلِ أَوْ نَهَارٍ فَإِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ الصَّلاَةِ وَ لَمْ يُتِمَّ مَا قَدْ فَاتَهُ فَلْيَمْضِ مَا لَمْ يَتَخَوَّف أَنْ يَذْهَبَ وَقْتُ هَذِهِ
الصَّلَاَةِ الْتِي قَدْ حَضَرَتْ وَ هَذِهِ أَحَقُّ بِوَقْتِهَا فَلْيُصَلَّهَا فَإِذَا قَضَاهَا فَلْيُصَلِّ مَا فَانَهُ فِيمَا قَدْ مَضَى وَ لاَ يَتَطَوَّعْ
بِرَكْعَةٍ حَتَّى يَقْضِيَ الْفَرِيضَةَ كُلَّهَا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Ubayd, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "If you miss a prayer and then remember it during the time of
another prayer, and you know that if you perform the one you missed first, you will still
be within the time for the current prayer, then begin with the one you missed.
For Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘And establish the prayer for My
remembrance’ (Surah Taha 20:14).
But if you know that by praying the one you missed first, you will miss the current one,
then begin with the one whose time you are in, and make up the other afterwards."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “There is no harm in a person
making up his ‘nawafil’ (supererogatory prayers) after the morning prayer (‘salat al-
ghadah’) until the sun rises, or after the afternoon prayer (‘salat al-’asr’) until the
sunlight begins to turn yellow.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا فَانَثكَ صَلاَةً
فَذَكَرْتَهَا فِي وَقْتِ أُخْرَى فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ إِذَا صَلِّيْتَ آَلَّتِي فَاتَثكَ كُثْتَ مِنَ الْأُخْرَى فِي وَقْتِ فَابْدَأُ بِالَتِي فَاتَثَكَ
فَإِنَّ اللهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ »وَ أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي » وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ إِذَا صَلِّيْتَ الْتِي فَاتَثكَ فَاتَثكَ اَلَّتِي بَعْدَهَا
فَابْدَأُ بِالَّتِي أَنْتَ فِي وَقْتِهَا وَ اِقْضِ الْأُخْرَى».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولا بأس أن يقضي الانسان نوافله بعد صلاة الغداة الى أن تطلع الشمس أو بعد صلاة بعد العصر
الى أن يتغير ضوء الشمس بالاصفرار).

ghadah’) until the sun rises, or after the afternoon prayer (‘salat al-’asr’) until the
sunlight begins to turn yellow.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn
Buzay’ al-’Adawi, from Abu al-Hasan Abdullah ibn ‘Awn al-Shami, who said Abdullah ibn Abi Ya’fur narrated
to me:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding making up the night prayer (‘salat al-layl’) and
‘witr’ that a man misses, may he make it up after the morning prayer and after ‘Asr?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that."
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعِ الْعَدَوِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ
عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَوْنِ الشَّامِيِّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي يَعْفُورِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي قَضَاءِ صَلاةٍ
اللَّيْلِ وَ الْوَثْرِ تَفُوتُ الرَّجُلَ أَ يَقْضِيهَا بَعْدَ صَلَاَةِ الْفَجْرِ وَ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.173 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.289 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.357 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.242

text_en:
And from him, from Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Abi Ja’far, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Maymun, from
Muhammad ibn Faraj, who said:
I wrote to the Righteous Servant (al Abd al-Salih {a.s}) asking Him {a.s} about certain
issues.
Imam {a.s} wrote back to me: "Pray as many ‘nafilah’ (supererogatory) prayers as you
wish after ‘Asr, and pray as many ‘nafilah’ prayers as you wish after the morning (‘al-
ghadah’) prayer."
text_ar:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ فَرَجِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ
إلَى الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ أَسْأَلْهُ عَنْ مَسَائِلَ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيَّ «وَ صَلِّ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ مِنَ النَّوَافِلِ مَا شِئْتَ وَ صَلِّ بَعْدَ الْغَدَاةِ مِنْ
اَلنَّوَافِلِ مَا شِنْتَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar al-Zayyat, from Jamil ibn
Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s} (the First), peace be upon him, about making up the
night prayer (‘salat al-layl’) after Fajr until the sun rises.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, and also after ‘Asr until night. This is from the concealed secrets
of the family of Muhammad {saws}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَرَ الزَّيَّاتِ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوْلَ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنْ قَضَاءِ صَلَاَةِ اللَّيْلِ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ بَعْدَ اَلْعَصْرِ إِلَى اللِّيْلِ فَهُوَ مِنْ سِرَّ
آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ الْمَخْزُونِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.173 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.290 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.357 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.243 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.273

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn ‘Umayrah, from Sulayman ibn Harun, who
said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about making up prayers after ‘Asr.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, they are merely ‘nawafil’ (supererogatory prayers), so make them
up whenever you wish."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ هَارُونَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ قَضَاءِ الصَّلاَةِ بَعْدَ ٱلْعَصْرِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ إِنَّمَا هِيَ النَّوَافِلُ فَاقْصِهَا مَتَى مَا شِئْتَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.173 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.358
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn ‘Umayrah, from Sulayman ibn Harun, who
said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about making up prayers after ‘Asr.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, they are merely ‘nawafil’ (supererogatory prayers), so make them
up whenever you wish."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-’Alaʾ:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Make up the daytime prayer at whatever hour you wish, by night
or by day, all of it is the same."
text_ar:
ٱلْحُسَيْنُ بَنْ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ وَ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اِقْضِ صَلاَةَ النَّهَارِ أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلِ أَوْ نَهَارِ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ سَوَاء».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.173 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.168 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.290 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.358 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.243 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.277 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.71

Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-’Alaʾ:

or by day, all of it is the same."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya’fur, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: "The daytime prayer may be made up at whatever hour
you wish, whether by night or by day."
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
يَقُولُ: «صَلاَةُ ٱَلنَّهَارِ يَجُوزُ قَضَاؤُهَا أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلِ أَوْ نَهَارِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr and Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr in one of their chains of
transmission, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} was asked about making up prayers (‘qadah’) before sunrise and after
‘Asr.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, make it up, for this is from the secret knowledge of the Family of
Muhammad {saws}, peace be upon them."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “It is not permissible to begin
supererogatory prayers (‘nawafil’) nor to make up any of them at the time of sunrise or
at the time of sunset.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ النَّضْرِ وَ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ فِي بَعْضِ أَسَانِيدِهِمَا قَالَ: سُنِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الْقَضَاءِ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ قَاقْضِهِ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ سِرِّ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِمُ
السَّلامٌ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولا يجوز ابتداء النوافل ولا قضاء شئ منها عند طلوع الشمس ولا عند غروبها).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “It is not permissible to begin
supererogatory prayers (‘nawafil’) nor to make up any of them at the time of sunrise or
at the time of sunset.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn al-
Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "There is no prayer after Fajr until the sun rises. Indeed, the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
‘The sun rises between the horns of Satan and sets between the horns of Satan.’
And Imam {a.s} said: “There is no prayer after ‘Asr until Maghrib is performed.”
text_ar:
الطّاطَرِي عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ وَ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِبَاطِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: «لَا صَلَاةَ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلهِ قَالَ «إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ تَطْلُعُ
بَيْنَ قَرْنَي شَيْطَانٍ وَ تَغْرُبُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ » وَ قَالَ «لاَ صَلاَةَ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ حَتَّى تُصَلَّى الْمَغْرِبُ» ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.174 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.290 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.348 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.234
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}

Al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn al-
Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "There is no prayer after Fajr until the sun rises. Indeed, the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
‘The sun rises between the horns of Satan and sets between the horns of Satan.’
And Imam {a.s} said: “There is no prayer after ‘Asr until Maghrib is performed.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn, from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "There is no prayer after ‘Asr until Maghrib, and no prayer after
Fajr until the sun rises."

Scholar's Note:
These narrations and those similar to them are to be understood as referring to the
‘initiation’ of supererogatory (‘nafilah’) prayers during these times, not the making up
(‘qadha’) of missed prayers. And the earlier narrations are to be understood as
referring specifically to ‘qadha’, not initiation. Thus, there is no contradiction between
them. What supports this explanation and the distinction we have mentioned is what
has been narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُكَيْنٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا صَلاةَ بَعْدَ ٱلْعَصْرِ حَتَّى
الْمَغْرِبٍ وَلَا صَلَاةَ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ».
هذه الاخبار وما أشبهها محمولة على ابتداء النوافل في هذه الاوقات دون القضاء والاخبار الاولة محمولة على القضاء
دون الابتداء، ولا تنافي بينهما ، والذي يدل على ما ذكرناه من التفصيل ما رواه:

referring specifically to ‘qadha’, not initiation. Thus, there is no contradiction between
them. What supports this explanation and the distinction we have mentioned is what

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s} regarding making up supererogatory prayers (‘nafilah’) from the rising
of Fajr until sunrise, and from after ‘Asr until sunset.
He {a.s} wrote back: "That is not permissible except for one who is making up missed
prayers (‘al-muqtadi’); as for anyone else, it is not."

Scholar's Note:
And it has been narrated that there is a concession (‘rukhsah’) permitting prayer at the
time of sunrise and at the time of sunset.
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ بِلالِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ فِي قَضَاءِ ٱلنَّافِلَةِ
مِنْ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ إِلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْعَصْرِ إِلَى أَنْ تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ فَكَتَبَ «لا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ إِلاّ لِلْمُقْتَضِي
فَأَمًا لِغَيْرِهِ فَلا».
وقد روي رخصة في الصلاة عند طلوع الشمس وعند غروبها:
commentary:
And it has been narrated that there is a concession (‘rukhsah’) permitting prayer at the
time of sunrise and at the time of sunset.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali narrated: A group of our elders narrated to me (narrator)
from Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Asadi, may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him,
that among the responses received to his questions from Muhammad ibn Uthman al-
’Amri, may Allah {SWT} sanctify his soul, regarding the questions he had sent, was:
"As for what you asked about, prayer at the time of sunrise and at the time of sunset,
even if people say that the sun rises between the horns of Satan and sets between the
horns of Satan, then there is nothing by which the nose of Satan is more forcefully
rubbed in humiliation than prayer. So perform the prayer and humiliate Satan."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘And whoever wishes to rise
at the end of the night…’ up to his statement: ‘And whoever stands at the end of his
night…’, all of this refers to the encouragement and merit of performing the night
prayer (‘salat al-layl’) in its preferred time, particularly in the latter part of the night.
text_ar:
رَوَى أَبُو جَعْفَرِ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ قَالَ رَوَى لِي جَمَاعَةٌ مِنْ مَشَايِخِنَا عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جَعْفَرِ ٱلْأَسَدِيِّ رَضِيَ
اللهُ عَنْهُ: أَنَّهُ وَرَدَ عَلَيْهِ فِيمَا وَرَدَ مِنْ جَوَابٍ مَسَائِلِهِ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ الْعَمْرِيِّ قَدَّسَ اللهُ رُوحَهُ «وَ أَمَّا مَا سَأَلْتَ
عَنْهُ مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ عِنْدَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِهَا فَلَئِنْ كَانَ يَقُولُ اَلنَّاسُ إِنَّ الشَّمْسَ تَطْلُعُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَي شَيْطَانٍ وَ
تَغْرُبُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَي شَيْطَانٍ فَمَا أَرْغِمَ أَنفُ الشِّيْطَانِ بِشَيْءٍ أَفْضَلَ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ فَصَلَّهَا وَ أَرْغِمِ الشِّيْطَانَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ومن أحب ان يقوم في آخر الليل) الى قوله : (ومن قام في آخر ليله).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘And whoever wishes to rise
at the end of the night…’ up to his statement: ‘And whoever stands at the end of his
night…’, all of this refers to the encouragement and merit of performing the night
prayer (‘salat al-layl’) in its preferred time, particularly in the latter part of the night.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.175 • Al-Ghaybah (Lil-Tusi), Vol.1 p.296

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
‘Amir ibn Abdillah ibn Juda’ah narrated:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "There is no servant who recites the end of Surat al-Kahf when
he goes to sleep except that he will wake up at the hour he desires."
text_ar:
رَوَى عَامِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جُذَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «مَا مِنْ عَبْدِ يَقْرَأُ آخِرَ الْكَهْفِ جِينَ يَنَامُ إِلاَّ
اِسْتَيْقَظَ فِي السَّاعَةِ الَّتِي يُرِيدُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.471 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.175 • Miftah Al-Falah, Vol.1 p.283 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.229 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.3 p.610
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
‘Amir ibn Abdillah ibn Juda’ah narrated:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "There is no servant who recites the end of Surat al-Kahf when
he goes to sleep except that he will wake up at the hour he desires."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE DETAILED EXPLANATION OF PRAYER, INCLUDING THE OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED, AND WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE AND NOT PERMISSIBLE.
text_en:
And it has been narrated from the Prophet {saws}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family,
that He {saws} said: "Whoever recites this verse at the time of sleep:
‘Say: I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God {AZJ} is One
God {AZJ}. So whoever hopes to meet his Lord {AZJ}, let him do righteous work and not
associate anyone in the worship of his Lord {AZJ}’ (Surah Kahf 18:110).
(Thus) a light will shine for him extending to the Sacred Mosque (‘al-Masjid al-Haram’),
and within that light will be angels seeking forgiveness for him until morning."
WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER

Scholar's Note:
As for what he, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, mentioned after that until the end of
the chapter, its explanation has already been fully presented, and all praise is due to
Allah {SWT}.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘And every instance of
forgetfulness that befalls a person during the first two units of his obligatory prayer
requires him to repeat the prayer.’ What indicates this is:
text_ar:
وَرُوِيَ عَنِ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَنْ قَرَأْ هَذِهِ آلْآيَةَ عِنْدَ مَنَامِهِ «قُلْ إِنّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِثلُكُمْ يُوحى إلَيَّ
أَنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمْ إِنَهُ وَاجِدٌ فَمَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُوا لِقَاءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلا صالِحاً وَ لا يُشرِك بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَداً» سَطَعَ لَهُ نُورْ إِلَى
الْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ حَشوُ ذَلِكَ النُّورِ مَلاَئِكَةٌ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لَهُ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ».
وأما ما ذكره رحمه اللّه بعد ذلك الى آخر الباب فقد مضى شرحه مستوفى والمنة لله.

And it has been narrated from the Prophet {saws}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family,
that He {saws} said: "Whoever recites this verse at the time of sleep:
‘Say: I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God {AZJ} is One
God {AZJ}. So whoever hopes to meet his Lord {AZJ}, let him do righteous work and not
associate anyone in the worship of his Lord {AZJ}’ (Surah Kahf 18:110).

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND
text_en:
What was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id, from al-Nadr, from ‘Asim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who
said:
I asked Abu Ja’far {a.s} about a man who has doubt in the first rak’ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must start over."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ عَاصِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ عَنْ رَجُلِ
شَكٍّ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى قَالَ «يَسْتَأْنِفٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.176 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.363 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.973 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.190

text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Ibn Maskan and Fadalah, from Husayn bin Uthman, from
Ibn Maskan, from Anbasah bin Mus'ab, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to me: "If you are doubtful regarding the first
two rak‘ahs, then repeat (the prayer)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ إِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عَنْبَسَةَ بْنِ مُصْعَبِ
قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : «إِذَا شَكَكْتَ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ فَأَعِدْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi

text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad al-Qarawi, from Aban, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi and Ibn Abi Ya'fur:
Abu Ja'far {a.s} and Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon them both, they said:
"If you do not know whether you prayed one rak‘ah or two, then start over."
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ ٱلْقَرَوِيَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ ٱلْجُعْفِيّ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرِ وَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا
السَّلامُ أَنَّهُمَا قَالا: «إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ أَوَاجِدَةً صَلِّيْتَ أَمْ ثِنْتَيْنِ فَاسْتَقْبِل».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.176 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.363 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.973 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.191

Imam {a.s} said: "If you are doubtful about first two (rak‘ahs), then repeat (the prayer)."
text_ar: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ ٱلْفُضَيْلُ عَنِ ٱلسَّهْوِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا شَكَكْتَ فِي ٱلْأُولَيَيْنِ فَأَعِدْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
Imam {a.s} said: "If a man is forgetful in the first two rak‘ahs of the Dhuhr and ‘Asr prayers
and does not know whether he prayed one or two, then it is obligatory upon him to
repeat the prayer."
text_ar:
الْحَسَنُ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ قَالَ: «إِذَا سَهَا الرَّجُلُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ مِنَ الظُّهْرِ وَ الْعَصْرِ وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ وَاحِدَةً
صَلَّى أُمْ ثِئْتَيْنِ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ الصَّلاَةَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.350 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.176 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.364 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.971 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.191

And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn bin Uthman, from Harun bin Kharijah, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you are forgetful in the first two rak‘ahs,
then repeat them until you establish them firmly."
text_ar:
وَعَنَهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
«إِذَا سَهَوْتَ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ فَأَعِدْهُمَا حَتَّى ثُثُبِتَهُمَا)».

And from him, from Fadalah, from Hammad, from al-Fadl bin Abd al-Malik, who said:

prayer."

وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ قَالَ قَالَ لِي: «إِذَا لَمْ تَحْفَظِ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ فَأَعِدْ
صَلاتَكَ».

Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from
his father, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon
them both, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “A man does not know whether he prayed one rak‘ah or two.”
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat (the prayer)."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ عَلِيّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ
عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ لاَ يَدْرِي أَوَاحِدَةَ صَلَّى أَمْ يِنْتَيْنِ قَالَ
«يُعِيدُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Washa’
and al-Husayn bin Muhammad, from Mu‘alla bin Muhammad, from al-Washa’, who said:
Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to me: "Repetition is for the first
two rak‘ahs, and forgetfulness is for the last two rak‘ahs."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ الْوَشَّاءِ وَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ
مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْوَشَّاءِ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «الْإِعَادَةُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوِّلَتَيْنِ وَ السَّهْوُ فِي
الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الأَخِيرَتَيْنِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Ali bin al-Hakam, from al-Husayn bin Abi
al-‘Ala’, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or one.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should complete (the prayer)."
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي أَرَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ وَاحِدَةً قَالَ «يُتِمّ)».

source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:

I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or one.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should complete (the prayer)."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from al-Sindi bin al-Rabi‘, from al-Hasan bin
Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman bin al-Hajjaj:
Abu Ibrahim {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who does not know whether
he prayed one rak‘ah or two.
Imam {a.s} said: "He builds upon the one rak‘ah."
text_ar:
وَ مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ السِّنَدِيَّ بْنِ الرَّبِيعِ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَاجِ
عَنْ أَبِي إبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي الرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي رَكْعَةً صَلَّى أُمِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ قَالَ «يَبْنِي عَلَى الرَّكْعَةِ».

text_chunk:
And what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from al-Sindi bin al-Rabi‘, from al-Hasan bin
Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman bin al-Hajjaj:
Abu Ibrahim {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who does not know whether
he prayed one rak‘ah or two.
Imam {a.s} said: "He builds upon the one rak‘ah."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ahmad bin Muhammad
bin Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim bin ‘Amr, from Abdillah bin Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or one.
Imam {a.s} said: "He completes (the prayer) with one rak‘ah."
text_ar:
وما رواه سعد بن عبد اللّٰه عن محمد بن الحسين عن أحمد ابن محمد بن أبى نصر عن عبد الكريم بن عمرو عن
عبد الله بن أبي يعفور قال سألت أبا عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام : عن الرجل لا يدري أركعتين صلى ام واحدة فقال :
يتم بركعة.

source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
And what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ahmad bin Muhammad
bin Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim bin ‘Amr, from Abdillah bin Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or one.
Imam {a.s} said: "He completes (the prayer) with one rak‘ah."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And what was narrated by Sa‘d also, from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah bin Ayyub,
from al-Husayn bin Abi al-‘Ala’:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who does not know
whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or one.
Imam {a.s} said: "He completes according to his prayer."

Scholar's Note:
The first point regarding these reports is that they do not contradict the reports we
presented earlier, because those are far more numerous than these, and it is not
permissible to abandon the more numerous in favor of the fewer without a proof. Even
if these reports were contradictory and equal in number, they still would not invalidate
what we have previously presented, because none of these reports states that the
doubt occurred in the first or second rak‘ah of the obligatory prayers or the
recommended prayers.
And since this is not stated in the reports, we interpret them as referring to the
recommended prayers, because according to our view, there is no (legal)
forgetfulness in the recommended prayers. A person may build upon the lesser if he
wishes, or upon the greater if he wishes, though building upon the lesser is preferable.
And if we interpret these reports as we have mentioned, then we have reconciled all
of them together and have not discarded any of them.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "Whoever is forgetful in the
obligatory (prayer of) Fajr or Maghrib must repeat (the prayer)."
This is supported by what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ أَيْضاً عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاءِ عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : فِي الرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ وَاحِدَةً قَالَ «يُتِمُّ عَلَى صَلاتِهِ».
فاول ما في هذه الاخبار انها لا تعارض ما قدمناه من الاخبار لانها اضعاف هذه ولا يجوز العدول عن الاكثر الى الاقل إلا
الدليل، ولو كانت هذه الاخبار معارضة لها ومساوية لم يكن فيها ما ينقض ما قدمناه ، لانه ليس في شئ من هذه الاخبار
أن الشك إذا وقع في الاولة والثانية من صلاة الفرايض أو صلاة النوافل، وإذا لم يكن هذا في الخبر حملناها على النوافل
الان النوافل عندنا لا سهو فيها ويبني الانسان إن شاء على الاقل وإن شاء على الاكثر وإن كان البناء على الاقل افضل ،
ومتى حملنا هذه الاخبار على ما ذكرناه كنا قد جمعنا بينها اجمع ولم نكن قد اطرحنا منها شيئا .قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه :
(. سل فف يضة الغداة أه المغرب اعاد) بدا على. ذلك ما دماه :

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl
bin Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs bin al-Bakhtari and others:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you are doubtful in Maghrib, then repeat
(the prayer), and if you are doubtful in Fajr, then repeat (the prayer)."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي
عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بُنِ الْبَخْتَرِيَّ وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا شَكَكْتَ فِي ٱلْمَغْرِبِ فَأَعِدْ وَ إِذَا
شَكَكْتَ فِي الْفَجْرِ فَأْعِدْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad bin Muslim,
who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who is praying and does not
know whether he prayed one rak‘ah or two.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should start over until he is certain that he has completed (the
prayer), and this applies in Jumu‘ah, in Maghrib, and in prayer during travel."
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
- عَن آَلَّ حُا ئُصَلً . هَ لاَ يَذْهى أَوَاحدَةً صَلَّ . أَد اثنَتَنْ. قَال «يَسْتَقْأُ حَدَّ. تَسْتَنْقءَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ أَتَمَّ هَ ف الْحُمُعَة ةَ

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from a man:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no forgetfulness in Maghrib and Fajr."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ:
«ليْسَ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ وَ الْفَجْرِ سَهْوُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Safwan and Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from one of
them (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about forgetfulness in Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat (the prayer) until he remembers, for it is not like the
Shaf‘ (even-numbered prayers)."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ
عَنِ السَّهْوِ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ حَتَّى يَحْفَظَ إِنَّهَا لَيْسَتْ مِثْلَ الشَّفْعِ».

And from him, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Ibn Maskan, and Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Maskan,
from Anbasah bin Mus‘ab, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you are doubtful in Maghrib, then repeat
(the prayer), and if you are doubtful in Fajr, then repeat (the prayer)."
text_ar:
وعنه عن محمد بن سنان عن ابن مسكان وفضالة عن حسين عن ابن مسكان عن عنبسة بن مصعب قال قال
أبو عبد اللّه عليه السلام : إذا شككت في المغرب فأعد ، وإذا شككت في الفجر فأعد.

chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER

And from him, from al-Nadr, from Musa bin Bakr, from al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about forgetfulness.
Imam {a.s} said: "In the Maghrib prayer, if you do not remember whether it was three or
four (rak‘ahs), then repeat your prayer."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ ٱلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ السَّهْوِ فَقَالَ «فِي صَلاَةِ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا لَمْ تَحْفَظْ مَا
بَيْنَ الثَّلاَثِ إِلَى الْأَرْبَعِ فَأَعِدْ صَلاَتَكَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah bin Muhammad, from al-Hadrami, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about forgetfulness in the Fajr prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you do not know whether you prayed one rak‘ah or two, then repeat
the prayer from the beginning. And Jumu‘ah also, if the Imam (of prayer) is forgetful in
it, then he must repeat the prayer, because it is two rak‘ahs.
And Maghrib, if one is forgetful in it and does not know how many rak‘ahs he prayed,
then he must repeat the prayer."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَضْرَمِيَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلسّهْوِ فِي صَلاَةِ الْغَدَاةِ قَالَ
«إِذَا لَمْ تَذْرِ وَاحِدَةً صَلَّيْتَ أَمْ ثِنْتَيْنِ فَأَعِدِ الصَّلاَةَ مِنْ أَوْلِهَا وَ الْجُمُعَةُ أَيْضا إِذَا سَهَا فِيهَا الْإِمَامُ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ
الصَّلاَةَ لِأَنَّهَا رَكْعَتَانِ وَ الْمَغْرِبُ إِذَا سَهَا فِيهَا وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ كَمْ رَكْعَةً صَلَّى فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ الصَّلاَةَ».

text_en:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah,
from Sayf bin Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami:
He (Abu Bakr al-Hadrami) said: “I led my companions in the Maghrib prayer, and when
I had prayed two rak‘ahs, I performed the taslim. Some of them said, ‘You only prayed
two rak‘ahs.’
So I repeated the prayer.
Then I informed Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.
Imam {a.s} said: "Perhaps you repeated it?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} laughed and then said: "It would have sufficed you to stand and perform one
rak‘ah. The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, once forgot and
performed the taslim after two rak‘ahs.”
And then He {a.s} mentioned the narration of Dhu al-Shimalayn, and said: “Then he
stood and added two rak‘ahs to it."
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ
الْحَضْرَمِيّ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ بِأَصْحَابِيَ الْمَغْرِبَ فَلَمَّا أَنْ صَلَّيْتُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ سَلَّمْتُ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِنَّمَا صَلَّيْتَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
فَأَعَدْتُ فَأَخْبَرْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ فَقَالَ «لَعَلِّكَ أَعَدْتَ» فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَضَحِكَ ثُمَّ قَالَ «إِنَّمَا كَانَ يُجْزِيكَ أَنْ
تَقُومَ وَ تَرْكَعَ رَكْعَةً إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ سَهَا فَسَلَّمَ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ حَدِيثَ ذِي الشِّمَالَيْنِ فَقَالَ
ثُمَّ قَامَ فَأَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And Sa‘d narrated from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja‘far bin Bashir, from al-Harith bin al-Mughirah al-
Nasri, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “We prayed Maghrib, and the imam (of
prayer) was forgetful and performed the taslim after two rak‘ahs, so we repeated the
prayer.”
Imam {a.s} said: "And why did you repeat it? Did not the Messenger of Allah {SWT} (peace
be upon him and his family) once leave the prayer after two rak‘ahs and then complete
it with two more (rak’ahs)? Should you not have completed it?"

Scholar's Note:
There is nothing in these two reports that contradicts what we have previously
presented, because the forgetfulness here occurred in that the taslim was performed
in the second rak‘ah, and not in the counting of the number of rak‘ahs of the prayer.
And whoever is forgetful in the taslim is not obligated to repeat the prayer; rather, it is
obligatory upon him to compensate for it with one rak‘ah, as these two reports
indicate. But if the forgetfulness had occurred in the number (of rak‘ahs), then the
prayer would have to be repeated from the beginning, as we have previously stated.
What clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ النَّصْرِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ إِنَّا صَلِّيْنَا الْمَغْرِبَ فَسَهَا الْإِمَامُ فَسَلَّمَ فِي الرّكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَعَدْنَا الصَّلاةَ فَقَالَ «وَ لِمَ أَعَدْتُمْ أَ لَيْسَ قَدِ
انْصَرَفَ رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَتَمَّ بِرَكْعَتَيْنِ أَلاَ أَثْمَمْتُمْ».
فليس في هذين الخبرين ما ينافي ما قدمناه لان السهو إنما وقع هاهنا في ان سلم في الركعة الثانية ولم يكن السهو قد
وقع في اعداد الصلاة ومن سها في التسليم لم يجب عليه إعادة الصلاة بل يجب عليه جبرانه بركعة حسب ما تضمنه
الخبران، ولو كان السهو واقعا في العدد لوجب اعادة الصلاة من أولها حسب ما قدمناه، والذي يكشف عما ذكرناه ما رواه:

indicate. But if the forgetfulness had occurred in the number (of rak‘ahs), then the
prayer would have to be repeated from the beginning, as we have previously stated.
What clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Sa‘d, from Ayyub bin Nuh, from Ali bin al-Nu‘man al-Razi, who said:
I (al-Razi) was with some companions of mine on a journey, and I was their Imam (of
prayer). I led them in the Maghrib prayer and performed the taslim after the first two
rak‘ahs.
My companions said: "You only prayed two rak‘ahs with us."
We spoke to each other, and they said: "As for us, we will repeat (the prayer)."
So I said: "As for me, I will not repeat it; I will complete it with one rak‘ah."
So I completed it with one rak‘ah.
Then we continued our journey, and I came to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him and
mentioned to Him {a.s} what had happened with us.
Imam {a.s} said to me: "You acted more correctly than they did. Only the one who does
not know what he has prayed must repeat (the prayer)."

Scholar's Note:
He {a.s}, peace be upon him, clarified in this report that whoever does not know what he
has prayed is obligated to repeat the prayer, as we have previously mentioned.
Moreover, in the first two reports, there is what prevents relying upon them, namely,
the hadith of Dhu al-Shimalayn and the forgetfulness of the Prophet (peace be upon
him and his family), and this is something that reason rejects.
As for the other report, which we used as supporting evidence for the first two,
containing the statement: "We spoke to each other, and they spoke to me", this does
not contradict what we have mentioned, namely that whoever speaks deliberately
during prayer must repeat the prayer, for two reasons.
First: the report does not state whether he spoke deliberately or out of forgetfulness,
so we interpret it as being due to forgetfulness.
Second: even if the report had clearly stated that it was deliberate, it would still be
possible that what was meant is that he had performed the taslim out of forgetfulness
and thought that this permitted speaking, just as it is permitted after the completion
of prayer. Therefore, he would not be obligated to repeat the prayer due to his
ignorance of the ruling and his lack of knowledge that such speech was not allowed.
As for what was narrated:
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوحِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ ٱلنُّعْمَانِ الرَّازِيِّ قَالَ: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَصْحَابٍ لِي فِي سَفَرٍ وَ أَنَا إِمَامُهُمْ فَصَلَّيْتُ بِهِمُ
اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَسَلَمْتُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ أَصْحَابِي إِنَّمَا صَلِّيْتَ بِنَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَكَلَّمْتُهُمْ وَ كَلَّمُونِي فَقَالُوا أَمَّا نَحْنُ
فَنُعِيدُ فَقُلْتُ لَكِنِّي لاَ أُعِيدُ وَ أَتِمُ بِرَكْعَةِ فَأْتْمَمْتُ بِرَكْعَةِ ثُمَّ سِرْنَا فَأَتَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ فَذَكَرْتُ لَهُ آلَّذِي
كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا فَقَالَ لِي «أَنْتَ كُنْتَ أَصْوَبَ مِنْهُمْ فِعْلاً إِنَّمَا يُعِيدُ مَنْ لاَ يَدْرِي مَا صَلَّى».
فبين عليه السلام في هذا الخبر أن من لا يدري ما صلى يجب عليه الاعادة حسب ما قدمناه، مع ان في الحديثين الاولين
ما يمنع من التعلق بهما وهو حديث ذي الشمالين وسهو النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وآله وهذا مما تمنع العقول منه ، فاما ما تضمن
الحديث الآخر الذي جعلناه شاهدا على الحديثين الاولين من قوله فكلمتهم وكلموني ليس يناقض ما نذكره من إن من
تكلم في الصلاة عامدا وجب عليه اعادة الصلاة لشيئين، احدهما : انه ليس في الخبر انه قال كلمتهم وكلموني عامدا أو
ناسيا وإذا لم يكن ذلك فيه حملناه على السهو ، والثاني : انه لو كان فيه تصريح بالعمد لجاز أن يكون المراد به من سلم
في الصلاة ناسيا وظن ان ذلك سبب لاستباحة الكلام كما انه سبب لاستباحته بعد الانصراف من الصلاة فلم يجب عليه
إعادة الصلاة لجهله به ولارتفاع علمه بانه لا يسوغ ذلك، فاما ما رواه:

him and his family), and this is something that reason rejects.
As for the other report, which we used as supporting evidence for the first two,

Second: even if the report had clearly stated that it was deliberate, it would still be

كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا فَقَالَ لِي «أَنْتَ كُنْتَ أَصْوَبَ مِنْهُمْ فِعْلاً إِنَّمَا يُعِيدُ مَنْ لاَ يَدْرِي مَا صَلَّى».
فبين عليه السلام في هذا الخبر أن من لا يدري ما صلى يجب عليه الاعادة حسب ما قدمناه، مع ان في الحديثين الاولين
ما يمنع من التعلق بهما وهو حديث ذي الشمالين وسهو النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وآله وهذا مما تمنع العقول منه ، فاما ما تضمن
الحديث الآخر الذي جعلناه شاهدا على الحديثين الاولين من قوله فكلمتهم وكلموني ليس يناقض ما نذكره من إن من
تكلم في الصلاة عامدا وجب عليه اعادة الصلاة لشيئين، احدهما : انه ليس في الخبر انه قال كلمتهم وكلموني عامدا أو
ناسيا وإذا لم يكن ذلك فيه حملناه على السهو ، والثاني : انه لو كان فيه تصريح بالعمد لجاز أن يكون المراد به من سلم
في الصلاة ناسيا وظن ان ذلك سبب لاستباحة الكلام كما انه سبب لاستباحته بعد الانصراف من الصلاة فلم يجب عليه
إعادة الصلاة لجهله به ولارتفاع علمه بانه لا يسوغ ذلك، فاما ما رواه:
commentary:
He {a.s}, peace be upon him, clarified in this report that whoever does not know what he
has prayed is obligated to repeat the prayer, as we have previously mentioned.
Moreover, in the first two reports, there is what prevents relying upon them, namely,
the hadith of Dhu al-Shimalayn and the forgetfulness of the Prophet (peace be upon
him and his family), and this is something that reason rejects.
As for the other report, which we used as supporting evidence for the first two,
containing the statement: "We spoke to each other, and they spoke to me", this does
not contradict what we have mentioned, namely that whoever speaks deliberately
during prayer must repeat the prayer, for two reasons.
First: the report does not state whether he spoke deliberately or out of forgetfulness,
so we interpret it as being due to forgetfulness.
Second: even if the report had clearly stated that it was deliberate, it would still be
possible that what was meant is that he had performed the taslim out of forgetfulness
and thought that this permitted speaking, just as it is permitted after the completion
of prayer. Therefore, he would not be obligated to repeat the prayer due to his
ignorance of the ruling and his lack of knowledge that such speech was not allowed.
As for what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad and al-Hakam bin Miskin, from ‘Ammar al-Sabati,
who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “A man doubts in the Maghrib prayer and
does not know whether he has prayed two rak‘ahs or three.”
Imam {a.s} said: "He performs the taslim, then stands and adds to it one rak‘ah."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "By Allah {SWT}, this is something that is never made up (qadha)."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ وَ الْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ عَمَّارِ السَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَجُلْ شَكَّ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ فَلَمْ يَدْرٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثَةً قَالَ «يُسَلَّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُضِيفُ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَةً» ثُمَّ
قَالَ «هَذَا وَ اللَّهِ مِمَّا لا يُقْضَى أَبَداً».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Mu‘awiyah bin Hakim, from Muhammad bin
Abi Umayr, from Hammad al-Nabb, from ‘Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or one in the Fajr prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should recite the tashahhud and conclude (the prayer), then stand
and pray one rak‘ah. If he had prayed two rak‘ahs, then this (extra) rak‘ah is a
recommended prayer (nafilah), and if he had prayed only one rak‘ah, then this is the
completion of the prayer."
I asked: "And what if he prayed Maghrib and does not know whether he prayed two
rak‘ahs or three?"
Imam {a.s} said: "He should recite the tashahhud and conclude (the prayer), then stand
and pray one rak‘ah. If he had prayed three, then this (extra) rak‘ah is a recommended
prayer (nafilah), and if he had prayed two, then this is the completion of the prayer.
And by Allah {SWT}, this is something that is never made up (qadah’)."
text_ar:
وَ مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَادِ النَّابِ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ
السَّابَاطِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَمْ يَدْرٍ صَلَّى الْفَجْرَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ رَكْعَةً قَالَ «يَتَشَهَدُ وَ
يَنْصَرِفُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً فَإِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَطَوُعاً وَ إِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَمَامَ
الصَّلَةِ قُلْتُ فَصَلَّى الْمَغْرِبَ فَلَمْ يَدْرِ إِثْنَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثَةً» قَالَ «يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً فَإِنْ
كَانَ صَلَّى ثَلاَثاً كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَطَوْعاً وَ إِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى اِثْنَتَيْنِ كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَمَامَ الصَلاَةِ وَ هَذَا وَ اللَّهِ مِمَّا لا يُقْضَى أَبَدا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And from him, from al-Hajjal, from Abdillah {a.s}, from ‘Ubayd:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who prayed one rak‘ah of
Fajr, then went away and came back after morning had begun and remembered that
he had prayed only one rak‘ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should add one rak‘ah to it."

Scholar's Note:
There is nothing in these reports that contradicts what we have mentioned, because
there is nothing apparent in these reports indicating whether the forgetfulness
occurred in a recommended prayer (nafilah) or an obligatory one (fard). They only
mention the Fajr and Maghrib prayers, and it is possible that what is meant by them
are the recommended prayers (nawafil), because the recommended prayers are often
attributed to Fajr, just as the nawafil of Maghrib are attributed to Maghrib, just as the
obligatory prayers are attributed to their times. And if what we said is possible, we
interpret these reports in a way that avoids contradiction between them.
Another possibility in understanding the first two reports is that the person who
doubted in Fajr or Maghrib had a predominant assumption (ghalabat al-zann) toward
the higher number, and for that reason, it was permitted for him to build upon it,
because predominant assumption takes the place of certainty, as we have explained
previously. Even if a minor doubt remains, it holds no legal weight.
Therefore, His {a.s} statement, peace be upon him, "He adds a rak‘ah to it" would be
from the standpoint of precaution and recommendation, not obligation and
requirement. What indicates this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى ٱلْفَجْرَ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ
ذَهَبَ وَ جَاءَ بَعْدَ مَا أَصْبَحَ وَ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً قَالَ «يُضِيفُ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَةً».
فليس في هذه الاخبار ما يضاد ما ذكرناه لانه ليس في ظاهر هذه الاخبار ان السهو وقع في النافلة أو الفريضة وإنما
تضمنت ذكر صلاة الفجر وصلاة المغرب، ويجوز أن يكون المراد بها النوافل لان النوافل قد تنسب الى الفجر وكذلك نوافل
المغرب تنسب الى المغرب كما ان الفريضة تنسب إليه وإذا احتمل ما قلناه حملناه على ما لا تتناقض فيه الاخبار، ويحتمل
الخبر ان الاولان وجها آخر وهو أن يكون من شك في الفجر والمغرب فغلب على ظنه الاكثر فلاجل ذلك جاز له أن يبني
عليه لان غلبة الظن تقوم مقام العلم وقد بيناه فيما مضى ، وإن كان مع هذا يعترضه أدنى شك إلا أنه لا حكم له ويكون
قوله عليه السلام : يضيف إليها ركعة يكون من جهة الاستظهار والاستحباب دون الفرض والايجاب ، والذي يدل على ذلك
مارواه :

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya al-Mu‘adhi, from al-Tayalisi, from Sayf bin Umayrah, from Ishaq bin
‘Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If your assumption always leans toward
completion (the higher number) in every prayer, then perform two prostrations
(sajdatayn) without a ruku‘. Do you understand?"
I said: "Yes."

Scholar's Note:
As for the last report which includes mention of the Fajr prayer, it may be interpreted
in accordance with what we previously stated, that it refers to the recommended
prayers (nawafil). It is also possible that this report is specific to someone who prayed
and assumed that he had prayed two rak‘ahs, then became certain that he had only
prayed one; in such a case, he adds another rak‘ah to it, and the repetition of the
prayer is not obligatory upon him.
Repetition is only obligatory upon the one who doubts in the prayer and does not know
whether he prayed one rak‘ah or two, and the matter is not clarified for him, then, in
that case, he must repeat the prayer.
What clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيِى الْمُعَاذِيُّ عَنِ الطَّيَالِسِيَّ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ إسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «إِذَا ذَهَبَ وَهْمُكَ إِلَى التَّمَامِ أَبَداً فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ فَاسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيْنِ بِغَيْرِ رُكُوعِ أَ فَهِمْتَ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ.
وأما الخبر الاخير الذي تضمن ذكر صلاة الفجر فيحتمل ما قدمناه من النوافل ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون هذا الخبر مخصوصا
بمن صلى وظن انه صلى ركعتين ثم تيقن انه صلى ركعة واحدة فانه يضيف إليها ركعة اخرى ولا تجب عليه إعادة الصلاة
، والاعادة إنما تجب على من يشك فيها فلا يدري صلى ركعة أو ركعتين ولم يتبين ذلك فيجب عليه حينئذ إعادة الصلاة،
والذي يكشف عما ذكرناه ما رواه:

Repetition is only obligatory upon the one who doubts in the prayer and does not know

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far bin Ahmad, who said: Ali bin al-Husayn and Ali bin Muhammad narrated to me, from
al-‘Ubaydi, from Yunus, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from one of them (Imams {a.s}), peace be
upon them both, who said:
He {a.s} was asked about a man who joined the imam (of prayer) in prayer while the
imam (of prayer) had already completed one rak‘ah before him. When the imam
finished the prayer, the man left with the people, then remembered that he had missed
a rak‘ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat one rak‘ah, it is permissible for him to do so as long
as he has not turned his face away from the qiblah. But if he has completely turned his
face away, then he must start the prayer anew from the beginning."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “Whoever is forgetful in the
last two rak‘ahs of the Dhuhr, ‘Asr, or Isha prayer and does not know whether he is in
the third or fourth rak‘ah, then he should refer to his assumption regarding that. If his
assumption inclines more strongly toward either one of them, he should act upon it.
But if his assumption is equal between both possibilities, he should act upon the
greater number (assume it is the fourth rak‘ah), and then make up what he assumes
he has missed.
For example, if he doubts between the third and fourth and his assumption is balanced
between them, he should assume he is in the fourth, perform the tashahhud, give the
taslim, then stand and perform one rak‘ah with tashahhud in it, or perform two rak‘ahs
while sitting, and perform tashahhud in the second of them.”

عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ قَالَ: سُيْلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ مَعَ ٱلْإِمَامِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ قَدْ سَبَقَهُ بِرَكْعَةٍ
فَلَمَّا قَرَغَ الْإِمَامُ خَرَجَ مَعَ النَّاسِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ فَاتَتْهُ رَكْعَةٌ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً يَجُوزُ لَهُ إِذَا لَمْ يُحَوِّلْ وَجْهَهُ

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Husayn bin
Sa‘id, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman bin Sayabah and Abu al-‘Abbas:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you have
prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and your inclination falls upon three, then build upon
three. And if your inclination falls upon four, then give the taslim and depart. But if your
doubt is balanced (with no inclination toward either), then depart and pray two rak‘ahs
while sitting."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ
عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ وَ أَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ ثَلاَثاً صَلَّيْتَ أَوْ أَرْبَعاً وَ
وَقَعَ رَأْيُكَ عَلَى الثَّلاَثِ فَابْنٍ عَلَى الثَّلاَثِ وَ إِنْ وَقَعَ رَأْيُكَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْبَعِ فَسَلَّمْ وَ اِنْصَرِفُ وَ إِنِ اِعْتَدَلَ وَهْمُكَ فَانْصَرِفْ
وَاصَلً رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسْ».

And from him, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ali bin Hadid, from Jamil,
from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding someone who does not know
whether he prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and his doubt between them is equal.
Imam {a.s} said: "When the doubt is equal between three and four, then he has a choice:
if he wishes, he may pray one rak‘ah while standing, and if he wishes, he may pray two
rak‘ahs with four prostrations."

وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيِى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: فِيمَنْ لا يَدْرِي أَثَلَاثاً صَلّى أَمْ أَرْبَعاً وَ وَهْمُهُ فِي ذَلِكَ سَوَاءً قَالَ فَقَالَ «إِذَا اِعْتَدَلَ الْوَهْمُ
فِي الثَّلَاَثِ وَ الْأَرْبَعِ فَهُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شَاءَ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ».

text_en:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who prayed and did not know
whether he was in the third rak‘ah or the fourth.
Imam {a.s} said: "Whatever his assumption inclines toward, if he thinks he is in the third
and there is still something in his heart about the fourth, then he should conclude (the
prayer) between himself and his Lord {AZJ}, then pray two rak‘ahs in which he recites the
Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in both."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةً عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ
صَلَّى فَلَمْ يَدْرِ أ فِي الثَّالِثَةِ هُوَ أَمْ فِي الرَّابِعَةِ قَالَ «فَمَا ذَهَبَ وَهمُهُ إِلَيْهِ إِنْ رَأْى أَنَّهُ فِي الثَالِثَةِ وَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِنَ
الرَّابِعَةٍ شَيْءً سَلَّمَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ نَفْسِهِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ ».

And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin Abi al-‘Ala’:

four, then he should give the taslim and pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting
the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, while he is seated, shortening the
tashahhud."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “And likewise, if one is
forgetful and does not know whether he is in the second or the fourth rak‘ah, if his
assumption is stronger toward one of them, then he should act according to his
assumption. But if his assumption is equal between them, then he should act as if he
is in the fourth rak‘ah, perform the tashahhud, and when he gives the taslim, he should
stand and pray two rak‘ahs while standing, reciting al-Hamd (Surah al-Fatiha) alone in
each of them, and if he wishes, he may recite tasbih instead.”

chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad bin Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs and
does not know whether they were two or four.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should give the taslim, then stand and pray two rak‘ahs, reciting
the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, perform the tashahhud, and then
conclude (the prayer), and nothing is required of him."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى
رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَلا يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَانِ هِيَ أَوْ أَرْبَعْ قَالَ «يُسَلَّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَ يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ
وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.185 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.372 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.984 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.221

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And from him, from Hammad, from Shu‘ayb, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you prayed four
rak‘ahs or two, then stand and perform two rak‘ahs, then give the taslim. Then perform
two more rak‘ahs, then give the taslim, and then perform two prostrations (sajdatayn)
while sitting, and then give the taslim after them."
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ أَرْبَعاً صَلِّيْتَ أَمْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
فَقُمْ وَ اِزْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ سَلَّمْ وَ اِرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ سَلَّمْ وَ اُسْجُدْ سَجَدَتَيْنِ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسْ ثُمَّ تُسَلَّمُ بَعْدَهُمَا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Maskan, from
Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or four.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should recite the tashahhud and give the taslim, then stand and
pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-
Fatiha) in both of them, then recite the tashahhud and give the taslim. If he had already
prayed four, then these two are (counted as) recommended prayers (nafilah), and if he
had only prayed two, then these complete the four. And if he spoke (during this state),
then he must perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ أَرْبَعاً قَالَ »يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يُسَلَّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي
رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتِ يَقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يُسَلَّمُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى أَرْبَعاً كَانَتْ هَانَانِ نَافِلَةً
وَ إِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ كَانَتْ هَاتَانِ إِثْمَامَ الْأَرْبَعَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ تَكَلَّمَ فَلْيَسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.352 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.186 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.372 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.979 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.219

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin
Shadhan, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon
them both, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “A person does not know whether he is in the fourth rak‘ah or the
second, but he is certain that he has completed two rak‘ahs.”
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations while standing,
reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha), and perform the tashahhud, and
nothing is upon him. And if he does not know whether he is in the third or the fourth,
and he is certain he has completed three rak‘ahs, then he should stand and add one
more, and nothing is upon him. One does not nullify certainty with doubt, and one
should not insert doubt into certainty, nor mix the two together. Rather, doubt is
nullified by certainty, and he completes the prayer based on what is certain and builds
upon it, and doubt is not to be regarded in any situation."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ
حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسِّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَنْ لَمْ يَدْرٍ فِي أَرْبَعِ هَوَ أَوْ فِي ثِنْتَيْنِ وَ قَدْ أَحْرَزَ الثَّنْتَيْنِ
قَالَ «رَكَعَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ وَ هَوَ قَائِمٌ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَ يَتَشَهْدُ وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِذَا لَمْ يَدْرٍ فِي ثَلاَثِ
هُوَ أَوْ فِي أَرْبَعِ وَ قَدْ أَحْرَزَ الثَّلاَتَ قَامَ فَأَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا أُخْرَى وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لا يَنْقُضِ ٱلْيَقِينَ بِالشَّكَّ وَ لا يُدْخِلِ
الشَّكَّ فِي الْيَقِينِ وَ لَا يَخْلِطْ أَحَدَهُمَا بِالْآخَرِ وَ لَكِنَّهُ يَنْقُضُ الشَّكَّ بِالْيَقِينِ وَ يُتِمُّ عَلَى الْيَقِينِ فَيَبْنِي عَلَيْهِ وَ لا
بَعْتَدَّ بِالشَّكٍّ فِي حَالٍ مِنَ الْحَالاَتِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.351 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.186 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.373 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.979 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.2 p.281 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.180

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or four.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat the prayer."

Scholar's Note:
So this does not contradict the earlier reports, because this narration is to be
understood as referring to the Maghrib or Fajr prayers, in which doubt is not permitted,
as we have already explained.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “And if one doubts between
two, three, and four rak‘ahs, and his assumption is balanced among them, then he
should build upon four, perform the tashahhud, give the taslim, then pray two rak‘ahs
while standing, perform the tashahhud, give the taslim, and then pray two rak‘ahs
while sitting, also performing the tashahhud and giving the taslim.”
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمِّدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي صَلّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَمْ
أَرْبَعاً قَالَ «يُعِيدُ الصَّلاَةَ».
فلا ينافي الاخبار الاولة لان هذا الخبر محمول على صلاة المغرب أو الغداة التي لا يجوز فيهما الشك على ما بيناه. قال
الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولو شك في اثنتين وثلاث واربع واعتدل وهمه بنى على الاربع وتشهد وسلم ثم صلى ركعتين من قيام
وتشهد وسلم وصلى ركعتين من جلوس يتشهد أيضا ويسلم).
commentary:
So this does not contradict the earlier reports, because this narration is to be
understood as referring to the Maghrib or Fajr prayers, in which doubt is not permitted,
as we have already explained.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “And if one doubts between
two, three, and four rak‘ahs, and his assumption is balanced among them, then he
should build upon four, perform the tashahhud, give the taslim, then pray two rak‘ahs
while standing, perform the tashahhud, give the taslim, and then pray two rak‘ahs
while sitting, also performing the tashahhud and giving the taslim.”
