author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from more than one person:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (said) regarding the carcass (maytah).
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in anything from it, not even a sandal strap."
text_ar:
أحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ : فِي الْمَيْتَةِ قَالَ
«لاَ تُصَلًّ فِي شَيْءِ مِنْهُ وَ لاَ شِسْعٍ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the skin of a dead animal, can it be worn in prayer if it has been
tanned?
Imam {a.s} said: "No, even if it is tanned seventy times."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الْجِلْدِ الْمَيَّتِ أَيُلْبَسُ فِي
الصَلاَةٍ إِذَا دُبِغَ فَقَالَ «لا وَ لَوْ دُبِغَ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.203 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.415 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.343
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali,
from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from ‘Aytham ibn Aslam al-Najashi, from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about praying in fur garments.
Imam {a.s} said: "(Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn {a.s} was a man sensitive to cold, and the furs
of the Hijaz would not keep him warm because their tanning was done with qaraz (a
plant extract). So He {a.s} would send to Iraq and He {a.s} would be brought fur from your
region, and He {a.s} would wear it. But when the time for prayer arrived, He {a.s} would
take it off, and also take off the shirt that was in contact with it.
He {a.s} was asked about that, and He (Imam Husayn {a.s}) said: 'Indeed, the people of
Iraq deem it permissible to wear the skins of dead animals, and they claim that tanning
it is its purification (that tanning makes it lawful).’"
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ إسْحَاقَ ٱلْعَلَوِيّ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ
اَلدَّيْلَمِيّ عَنْ عَيْثَمِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ النَّجَاشِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي الْفِرَاءِ
فَقَالَ «كَانَ عَلِي بْنُ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسَلاَمُ رَجْلاً صَرِداً فَلاَ تُذْفِئُهُ فِرَاءُ ٱلْحِجَازِ لِأَنَ دِبَاغَهَا بِالْقَرَظِ فَكَانَ يَبْعَثُ
إِلَى الْعِرَاقِ فَيُوتَى مِمَّا قِبَلَكُمْ بِالْفَرْوِ فَيَلْبَسُهُ فَإِذَا حَضَرَتِ الصِّلاةُ أَلْقَاهُ وَ أَلْقَى الْقَمِيصَ الَّذِي يَلِيهِ فَكَانَ يُسْأَلُ
عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَيَقُولُ «إِنَّ أَهْلَ الْعِرَاقِ يَسْتَجِلُونَ لِبَاسَ الْجُلُودِ الْمَيْتَةِ وَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ دِبَاغَهُ ذَكَاتُهُ» ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.203
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Imam Ali ibn Husayn Zayn al-Abidin {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
With this same chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about wearing fur garments and praying in them.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them except in what has been ritually slaughtered."
I asked: "Isn’t dhakiyy what is slaughtered with iron (a blade)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if it is from that which its meat is eaten."
So I asked: "What about what is not eaten from animals other than sheep?"
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with (wearing) squirrel (al-sinjab), for it is a
creature that does not eat meat, and it is not from those things which the Messenger
of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, prohibited when He {saws} prohibited all
animals with fangs or talons."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنْ لِبَاسِ
الْفِرَاء وَ الصِّلاةٍ فِيهَا فَقَالَ «لا تُصَلَّ فِيهَا إلاَّ فِيمَا كَانَ مِنْهُ ذَكِيّا» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَوَ لَيْسَ الذَّكِيْ مَا ذُكِّيَ بِالْحَدِيدِ فَقَالَ
«بَلَى إِذَا كَانَ مِمَّا يُوكَلُ لَحْمُهُ» فَقُلْتُ وَ مَا لا يُؤكَلُ لَحْمُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ ٱلْغَنَمِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِالسِّنْجَابِ فَإِنَّهُ دَابَّةٌ لا تَأْكُلُ
اللَّحْمَ وَ لَيْسَ هُوَ مِمَّا نَهَى عَنْهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذْ نَهَى عَنْ كُلِّ ذِي نَابٍ أَوْ مِخْلَبٍ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.397 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.203 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.402 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.348

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from
Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: "I enter the market of the Muslims, I
mean this group who ‘claim’ Islam, and I buy fur garments from them for trade.
So I say to the seller: 'Is it not from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah)?'
And he (seller) replies: 'Yes.'
So is it permissible for me to sell it on the basis that it is dhakiyyah?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No. But there is no harm in selling them if you say: ‘The one I bought
them from claimed they were from a slaughtered animal.’”
I asked: “What invalidates that? (makes it impermissible to sell as definitely pure)”
Imam {a.s} said: "The people of Iraq making carrion (maytah) lawful, and they claimed
that the tanning of the skin of carrion renders it ritually pure (as its slaughter). Then
they were not content with lying about that except by attributing it to the Messenger of
Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ إسْحَاقَ ٱلْعَلَوِيّ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ
عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَاجِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِنِّي أَدْخَلُ سُوقَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَغْنِي هَذَا الْخَلْقَ
آلَّذِي يَدَّعُونَ الْإِسْلَامَ فَأَشتَرِي مِنْهُمُ الْفِرَاءَ لِلتَّجَارَةِ فَأَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهَا أَلَيْسَ هِيَ ذَكِيَّةً فَيَقُولُ بَلَى فَهَلْ يَصْلُحُ لِي
أَنْ أَبِيعَهَا عَلَى أَنَّهَا ذَكِيَّةٌ فَقَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ لا بَأْسَ أَنْ تَبِيعَهَا وَ تَقُولَ قَدْ شَرَطَ آلَّذِي اِشتَرَيْتُهَا مِنْهُ أَنَّهَا ذَكِيَّةٌ)» قُلْتْ
وَ مَا أَفْسَدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ «اِسْتِخْلاَلُ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ لِلْمَيْتَةِ وَ زَعَمُوا أَنْ دِبَاغَ جِلْدِ ٱلْمَيْتَةِ ذَكَاتُهُ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْضَوْا أَنْ يَكْذِبُوا
فِي ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.398 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.204 • Al-Wafi, Vol.1 7 p.285 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.503
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from
Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: "I enter the market of the Muslims, I
mean this group who ‘claim’ Islam, and I buy fur garments from them for trade.
So I say to the seller: 'Is it not from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah)?'
And he (seller) replies: 'Yes.'
So is it permissible for me to sell it on the basis that it is dhakiyyah?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No. But there is no harm in selling them if you say: ‘The one I bought
them from claimed they were from a slaughtered animal.’”
I asked: “What invalidates that? (makes it impermissible to sell as definitely pure)”
Imam {a.s} said: "The people of Iraq making carrion (maytah) lawful, and they claimed
that the tanning of the skin of carrion renders it ritually pure (as its slaughter). Then
they were not content with lying about that except by attributing it to the Messenger of
Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from
Asim ibn Humaid, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: "May I be ransomed for you, can anything
from a dead animal (maytah) be benefitted from?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
I asked: "It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah {SWT} (peace be upon him and his
family) passed by a dead sheep and said: 'What would have been upon the people of
this sheep if they could not benefit from its meat, to at least benefit from its hide?'"
Imam {a.s} said: "That was a sheep belonging to Sawdah bint Zam‘ah, the wife of the
Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and it was an emaciated sheep whose
meat was of no benefit, so they left it until it died.
Then the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, said: 'What would
have been upon its people, if they could not benefit from its meat, to benefit from its
hide, that is, by making it ritually slaughtered (tudhakka)'."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ
قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ يُنْتَفَعُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْهَا قَالَ «لا» قُلْتُ بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ
صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ مَرَّ بِشَاةٍ مَيْتَةٍ فَقَالَ «مَا كَانَ عَلَى أَهلِ هَذِهِ الشَّاةِ إِذْ لَمْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِلَحْمِهَا أَنْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِإِهَابِهَا»
فَقَالَ «تِلْكَ شَاةٌ لِسَوْدَةَ بِنتِ زَمْعَةَ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ كَانَتْ شَاةَ مَهْزُولَةً لاَ يُنْتَفَعُ بِلَحْمِهَا فَتَرَكُوهَا
حَتَّى مَاتَتْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ «مَا كَانَ عَلَى أَهْلِهَا إِذْ لَمْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِلَحْمِهَا أَنْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بإِهَابِهَا أَيْ
تُذَكّى» ».

text_en:
Sa‘d narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Sama’ah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about wearing a sword in prayer when it
contains fur or ‘kaymukht’ (a type of soft leather).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with it as long as it is not known to be from a dead
animal."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
in the skins of other impure animals, such as the dog, the pig, the fox, the rabbit, and
anything similar to that, and (their skins) are not purified by tanning."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn
Khalid, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d ibn al-Ahwas, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, about praying in the skins of
wild beasts.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them."
He (narrator) said: “And I asked Him {a.s}: ‘Can a man pray in a garment made of silk?’"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدِ بْنِ ٱلْأَحْوَصِ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ - عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي جُلُودِ السِّبَاعِ فَقَالَ «لا تُصَلَ فِيهَا» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْثُهُ هَلْ
يُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ فِي ثَوْبِ إِبْرِيسَمِ قَالَ «لا».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.400 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.205
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the meat of wild beasts and their skins.
Imam {a.s} said: "As for the meat of wild beasts, from birds and animals, we dislike it.
And as for the skins, ride upon them, but do not wear anything from them in which you
pray."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةً قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ لُحُومِ السِّبَاعِ وَ جُلُودِهَا فَقَالَ «أَمَّا لُحُومُ
السَّبَاعِ مِنَ الطَّيْرِ وَ الدَّوَابِ فَإِنَّا نَكْرَهُهُ وَ أَمَّا اَلْجُلُودُ فَارْكَبُوا عَلَيْهَا وَ لا تَلْبَسُوا مِنْهَا شَيْئاً تُصَلُونَ فِيهِ».

And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the skins of foxes, can one pray in

Imam {a.s} said: "I do not like to pray in them."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَعَثَهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلَامُ - عَنْ جُلُودِ التَّعَالِبِ
أَيْصَلَّى فِيهَا فَقَالَ «مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ فِيهَا».

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s} asking about prayer in the skins of rabbits.
Imam {a.s} wrote in reply: "It is makrooh (disliked)."
text_ar: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي جُلُودِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ «مَكْرُوهَةٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Bunan ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn
Ishaq al-Abhari, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s}: "May I be ransomed for you, we have socks and padding that are
made from rabbit fur. Is it permissible to pray in rabbit fur without necessity or
taqiyyah?"
Imam {a.s} wrote in reply, peace be upon him: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ الْأَبْهَرِيَّ قَالَ:
كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ عِنْدَنَا جَوَارِبُ وَ تِكَكْ تُعْمَلُ مِنْ وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَهَلْ تَجُوزُ الصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ مِنْ غَيْرٍ
ضَرُورَةٍ وَ لاَ تَقِيَّةٍ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «لا تَجُوزُ الصَّلاَةُ فِيهَا».

text_ar:
علي بن مهزيار قال : كتب إليه ابراهيم بن عقبة عندنا جوارب وتكك تعمل من وبر الارانب فهل تجوز الصلاة
في وبر الارانب من غير ضرورة ولا تقية؟ فكتب عليه السلام : لا تجوز الصلاة فيها.

text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, was asked about the tanned skins of foxes.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them."

And as for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer in the skins of foxes.
Imam {a.s} said: "If they are from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then there
is no problem."

Scholar's Note:
It is possible that what he meant is that there is no problem if it is on something like a
cap or something similar, which one does not complete the prayer with. And what
clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصّلاَةِ فِي
جُلُودِ اَلتَّعَالِبِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَتْ ذَكِيَّةً فَلاَ بَأْسَ».
فيحتمل أن يكون أراد أنه لا بأس به إذا كان على مثل القلنسوة أو ما اشبهها مما لا يتم الصلاة بها ، والذي يكشف عما
ذكرناه ما رواه :

clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
I wrote to Abu Muhammad {a.s}, peace be upon him, asking: "Is it permissible to pray in
a cap that has upon it the fur of an animal whose meat is not permissible to eat, or in
a waistband of silk, or in a waistband made from rabbit fur?"
Imam {a.s} wrote: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk. And if the fur is from a properly
slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then prayer in it is permissible, Allah {SWT} willing."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
And it is also possible that what is meant by "fi" in the narration is "on", as if He {a.s},
peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem with standing upon it during prayer."
And we have already explained, from the narrations, what indicates the prohibition of
prayer in it, and that is sufficient, Allah {SWT} willing. This is also further confirmed by
what was narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلْهُ هَلْ يُصَلَّى فِي
قَلَنْسُوَةٍ عَلَيْهَا وَبَرُ مَا لا يُوْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ أَوْ تِكَّةِ حَرِيرٍ أَوْ تِكَّةٍ مِنْ وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ «لاَ تَحِلُّ الصَّلاَةُ فِي الْحَرِيرِ
اَلْمَخْضٍ وَ إِنْ كَانَ الْوَبَرُ ذَكِيّاً حَلَّتِ الصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ».
ويجوز ايضا أن يكون المراد بفي في الخبر على فكأنه عليه السلام قال : لا بأس بالوقوف عليه في حال الصلاة وقد بينا
ما يقتضي تحريم الصلاة فيها من الروايات ما فيها كفاية ان شاء اللّٰه تعالى، ويؤكد ايضا ذلك ما رواه:

prayer in it, and that is sufficient, Allah {SWT} willing. This is also further confirmed by
what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Walid ibn Aban, who said:
I said to (Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him: "May I pray in the fur of the fennec
and the squirrel?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
So I asked: "Is it permissible to pray in fox skins if they are from a properly slaughtered
animal (dhakiyyah)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And it is not permissible for
men to pray in pure silk (ibrisim) when there is choice, nor to wear it except in cases of
necessity."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمّدٍ عَنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ أَبَانِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أُصَلِّي فِي الْفَنَكِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» فَقُلْتُ
يُصَلَّى فِي التَّعَالِبِ إِذَا كَانَتْ ذَكِيَّةً قَالَ «لا تُصَلِّ فِيهَا)».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (ولا تجوز الصلاة للرجال في الابريسم المحض مع الاختيار ولا لبسه إلا مع الاضطرار).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And it is not permissible for
men to pray in pure silk (ibrisim) when there is choice, nor to wear it except in cases of
necessity."

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
I wrote to Abu Muhammad {a.s}, peace be upon him, asking Him {a.s}:
"Is it permissible to pray in a cap made of pure silk or a cap made of brocade (dibaj)?"
Imam {a.s} wrote in reply: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلْهُ
هَلْ يُصَلَّى فِي قَلَنْسُوَةِ حَرِيرٍ مَحْضٍ أَوْ قَلَنْسُوَةِ دِيبَاجٍ فَكَتَبَ «لا تَجِلُ الصَّلاَةُ فِي حَرِيرٍ مَحْضٍ».

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a garment made of silk, can men pray in it?
He said: "No."

Scholar's Note:
And the narration that we presented earlier from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya,
from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, also indicates what we have said.
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدِ الْأَشعَرِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الثَّوْبِ الإبْرِيسَمِ هَلْ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ الرِّجَالُ
قَالَ «لا».
والحديث الذي قدمناه من رواية محمد بن أحمد بن أحمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن عبد الجبار يدل على ما قلناه ايضا.
commentary:
And the narration that we presented earlier from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya,
from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, also indicates what we have said.

I asked (Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him: "Can a man pray in a garment made
of silk?"

text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ أَسْبَاطِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَارِثِ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ هَلْ يُصَلِّي الرَجُلُ فِي ثَوْبِ إِبْرِيسَمِ قَالَ «لا».

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO

PRAY IN, FROM THAT
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, who
said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him ,about prayer in a garment of brocade
(dibaj), and he said: "As long as it does not have images (tamathil), then there is no
problem."

Scholar's Note:
The first issue with this report is that we have already narrated from (Imam) Al-Ridha
{a.s}, peace be upon him, that which contradicts this narration, and it is not permissible
for His {a.s}, peace be upon him, statements to be in contradiction. Moreover, the
apparent wording of this narration does not indicate that there is no problem praying
in it under all circumstances. And since this is not apparent in its wording, we restrict
its meaning to the condition of war, not to a situation of choice. What indicates this is
what was narrated:
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلَاَمُ - عَنِ
الصَّلاة فِي ثَوْبِ دِيبَاجِ فَقَالَ «مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ اَلتَّمَاثِيلُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ».

ليس في ظاهر هذا الخبر انه لا بأس بالصلاة فيه في أي حال ، وإذا لم يكن هذا في ظاهره خصصناه بحال الحرب دون
حال الاختيار والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:

{a.s}, peace be upon him, that which contradicts this narration, and it is not permissible
for His {a.s}, peace be upon him, statements to be in contradiction. Moreover, the
apparent wording of this narration does not indicate that there is no problem praying
in it under all circumstances. And since this is not apparent in its wording, we restrict
its meaning to the condition of war, not to a situation of choice. What indicates this is
what was narrated:

text_en:
Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Sama‘ah ibn Mihran, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about wearing silk and brocade.
Imam {a.s} said: "As for during war, there is no problem, even if it contains images
(tamathil)."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
And it is also possible that what He, peace be upon him, intended was that if the
brocade (dibaj) had its warp and weft made of spun thread or linen, rather than being
entirely pure silk, then, in that case, prayer in it would be permissible. The narration
does not state that the brocade mentioned contained nothing of spun thread or linen,
so it remains open to the interpretation we have mentioned. What supports what we
have said is what was narrated:
text_ar:
سَعَدْ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ لِبَاسِ الْحَرِيرِ وَ الدِّيبَاجِ
فَقَالَ «أمًا فِي الْحَرْبِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ تَمَاثِيلُ».
ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون أراد عليه السلام إذا كان الديباج سداه ولحمته غزلا أو كتانا دون أن يكون مبهما لانه متى كان الامر
على ذلك جازت الصلاة فيه وليس في الخبر انه ديباج ليس فيه شئ من الغزل ولا من الكتان بل هو يحتمل لما ذكرناه،
والذي يدل على ما قلناه ما رواه:

does not state that the brocade mentioned contained nothing of spun thread or linen,
so it remains open to the interpretation we have mentioned. What supports what we
have said is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn Ibrahim:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem with a garment whose
warp, buttons, and embroidery are of silk. What is disliked for men is pure silk (al-harir
al-buhm)."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And one does not pray in
garments made of fennec or sable, and it is not permissible to pray in the furs of
animals whose meat is not lawful to eat."
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنْ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ
بِالثَّوْبِ أَنْ يَكُونَ سَدَاهُ وَ زِرُّهُ وَ عَلَمُهُ حَرِيراً وَ إِنَّمَا كُرِهَ الْحَدِيرُ الْبُهْمُ لِلرِّجَالِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولا يصلى في الفنك والسمور ولا تجوز الصلاة في أوبار ما لا يؤكل لحمه).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And one does not pray in
garments made of fennec or sable, and it is not permissible to pray in the furs of
animals whose meat is not lawful to eat."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
Zurarah asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in the skins of foxes,
fennec, squirrels, and other types of fur.
So He {a.s} took out a book, which He {a.s} claimed was dictated by the Messenger of Allah
{SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, (and it said):
"Indeed, prayer in the fur of every animal whose meat is forbidden to eat, then prayer
in its fur, hair, skin, urine, feces, and everything from it, is invalid. That prayer is not
accepted until one prays in something other than it, from that which Allah {SWT} has
permitted its meat to be eaten."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "O Zurarah, this is from the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon
him and his family, by Allah {SWT}.
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
So preserve it, O Zurarah. For if it is from that whose meat is permissible to eat, then
prayer in its fur, urine, hair, feces, milk, and everything from it is permissible, if you
know that it is from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyy), slaughtered by the proper
method. But if it is other than that, from what you have been prohibited from eating or
what is forbidden for you to eat, then prayer in anything from it is invalid, whether it
was ritually slaughtered or not."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ زُرَارَةُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي التَّعَالِبِ وَ الْفَنَكِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ وَ غَيْرِهِ مِنَ الْوَبَرِ فَأْخِرَجَ كِتَاباً زَعَمَ أَنَّهُ إِمْلاءُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ
صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ «أنَّ الصَّلاةَ فِي وَبَرِ كُلّ شَيْءٍ حَرَامٍ أكْلُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِهِ وَ شَعْرِهِ وَ جِلْدِهِ وَ بَوْلِهِ وَ رَوْتِهِ
وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فَاسِدَةٌ لا تُقْبَلُ تِلْكَ الصَّلاةُ حَتّى يُصَلِّيَ فِي غَيْرِهِ مِمَّا أَحَلَ اللَّهُ أَكْلَهُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ «يَا زُرَارَةُ هَذَا عَنْ
رَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ اللّهِ فَاحْفَظُ ذَلِكَ يَا زُرَارَةُ فَإِنْ كَانَ مِمَّا يُوكَلُ لَحْمُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِهِ وَ بَوْلِهِ
وَشَعْرِهِ وَ رَوْتِهِ وَ أَلْبَانِهِ وَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ جَائِزَةٌ إِذَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهُ ذَكِيْ قَدْ ذَكَاهُ الذَّبْحُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِمّا قَدْ
نَهِيتَ عَنْ أَكْلِهِ أَوْ حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكَ أَكْلُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي كُلَ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فَاسِدَةٌ ذَكَاهُ الذِّبْحُ أَوْ لَمْ يُذَكَهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-
Hamadhani, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s}: "Fur and hair from animals whose meat is not lawful to eat fall onto
my garment, without any taqiyyah or necessity, what is the ruling?"
He {a.s} wrote in reply: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ إبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْهَمَذَانِيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ
يَسْقُطُ عَلَى تَوْبِيَ الْوَبَرُ وَ الشَّعْرُ مِمَّا لا يُوْكَلُ لَحَمُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ تَقِيَّةٍ وَ لا ضَرُورَةِ فَكَتَبَ «لا تَجُوزُ الصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ».

And from him, from a man, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, used to dislike prayer in the fur of anything whose
meat is not lawful to eat.
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوحِ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ ٱلْوَشَاءِ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱَلسَّلامُ يَكْرَهُ الصْلاَةَ
فِي وَبَرٍ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لاَ يُوْكَلُ لَحَمُهُ.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from someone who mentioned
it, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in garments made from
sable, squirrel, and fox.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no good in any of that, except for the squirrel, for it is a creature
that does not eat meat."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ إسْحَاقَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ مُقَاتِلِ بْنِ مُقَاتِلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللّه عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي السَّمُورِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ وَ التَّعَالِبِ فَقَالَ «لا خَيْرَ فِي ذَا كُلَّهِ مَا خَلاَ السِّنْجَابَ فَإِنَّهُ
دَابَّةٌ لا تَأْكُلُ اللَّحْمَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him: "What do you say about fur garments, can
one pray in them?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Which fur garments?"
I said: "The fennec, the squirrel, and the sable."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then pray in the fennec and the squirrel. As for the sable, do not pray
in it."
I said: "Can one pray in fox furs?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No, but they may be worn after the prayer."
I said: "Can I pray in the garment that touches it (worn underneath it)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
عَلِيْ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيَّ بْنِ رَاشِدِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الْفِرَاءِ أَيّ شَيْءٍ يُصَلّى
فِيهِ قَالَ «أيُّ ٱلْفِرَاءِ» قُلْتُ الْفَنَكَ وَ السِّنْجَابَ وَ السَّمُورَ قَالَ «فَصَلٌ فِي الْفَنَكِ وَ ٱلسِّنْجَابِ فَأمَا السَّمُورُ فَلاَ تُصَلَّ
فيهِ» قُلْتُ فَالتَعَالِبُ يُصَلّى فِيهَا قَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ تُلْبَسُ بَعْدَ الصَّلاَةِ» قُلْتُ أُصَلِّي فِي الثَّوْبِ الَّذِي يَلِيهِ قَالَ «لا)».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said Bashir ibn
Bashshar narrated to me, saying:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer in garments made from fennec, fur, squirrel, sable, and
decorative collars (hawasil) that are hunted in the lands of polytheism or the lands of
Islam, whether I may pray in them when not under taqiyyah.
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray in the squirrel and the Khwarazmian collars, and do not pray in
foxes or sable."
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ الصِّرْمِيّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي بَشِيرُ بْنُ بَشَارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ
الصَّلاَةِ فِي الْفَنَكِ وَ ٱلْفِرَاءِ وَ السَّنْجَابِ وَ السَّمُورِ وَ الْحَوَاصِلِ الَتِي تُصَادُ بِبِلاَدِ الشَّرْكِ أَوْ بِلادِ ٱلْإِسْلامِ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ
فِيهِ لِغَيْرِ تَقِيَّةٍ قَالَ فَقَالَ «صَلِّ فِي السِّنْجَابِ وَ ٱلْحَوَاصِلِ الْخُوارَزْمِيَّةِ وَ لاَ تُصَلَّ فِي التَعَالِبِ وَ لا السِّمُّورِ».

text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said Bashir ibn
Bashshar narrated to me, saying:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer in garments made from fennec, fur, squirrel, sable, and
decorative collars (hawasil) that are hunted in the lands of polytheism or the lands of
Islam, whether I may pray in them when not under taqiyyah.
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray in the squirrel and the Khwarazmian collars, and do not pray in
foxes or sable."

I asked Him {a.s} about garments made from furs, sable, squirrel, foxes, and similar

text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ ٱلْعَبَّاسِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنِ الْفِرَاءِ وَ السَّمُورِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ وَ التَعَالِبِ وَ أَشبَاهِهِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ».

text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin,
who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, about wearing garments made from fur,
sable, fennec, foxes, and all types of skins.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with that."

Scholar's Note:
These two narrations are to be understood as applying to the condition of taqiyyah
(dissimulation), because they also include mention of foxes, and we have already
clarified that prayer in them is not permissible. As for the squirrel (sanjab) specifically,
there is a dispensation for us to pray in it, and we have explained that. And as for sable
(sammur), we have clarified in the narration of Zurarah and others that prayer in it is
not permissible. What further clarifies this is:
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ لِبَاسِ الْفِرَاءِ وَ السَّمُورِ وَ الْفَنَكِ وَ التَّعَالِبِ وَ جَمِيعِ الْجُلُودِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ».

السنجاب خاصة فقد رخص لنا الصلاة فيه وقد بيناه، وأما السمور فقد بيناه في حديث زرارة وغيره انه مما لا تجوز
الصلاة فيه، ويزيده بيانا :

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, from (Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be
upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the skins of sable (sammur).
Imam {a.s} said: "What is that? The dark one?"
I said: "It is the black one."
Imam {a.s} said: "Does it hunt?"
I said: "Yes, it takes chickens and pigeons."
Imam {a.s} said: "No (do not pray in it)."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
And it is also possible that what He {a.s}, peace be upon him, intended was in
accordance with what we have previously mentioned, that it refers to a situation of
compulsion or necessity. It is also permissible that he meant when it is on a cap or a
garment not sufficient on its own for the completeness of prayer. And all the narrations
that mention a concession for wearing these things during prayer, the discussion
concerning them is as we have already explained.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no problem with
praying in pure khazz (a type of fine fabric), but prayer is not permissible in it if it is
mixed with rabbit fur or anything similar."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْبَرْقِيَّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدِ الْأَشعَرِيَّ عَنِ أَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ جُلُودِ
السَّمُورِ فَقَالَ «أَيُّ شَيْءٍ هُوَ ذَاكَ الْأَدْبَسُ» فَقُلْتُ هُوَ ٱلْأَسْوَدُ فَقَالَ «يَصِيدُ» فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ يَأْخَذُ ٱلدَّجَاجَ وَ ٱلْحَمَامَ قَالَ
«لا».
ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون أراد بغي على حسب ما قدمناه قبل هذا الموضع ويجوز ايضا أن يكون أراد إذا كان على قلنسوة
أوثوب لايتم الصلاة به وكل ما ورد من الاخبار في رخص لبس هذه الاشياء في حال الصلاة فالكلام عليه ما ذكرناه.
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا بأس بالصلاة في الخز الخالص ولا تجوز الصلاة فيه إذا كان مغشوشا بوبر الارانب وما اشبهها).

And it is also possible that what He {a.s}, peace be upon him, intended was in
accordance with what we have previously mentioned, that it refers to a situation of
compulsion or necessity. It is also permissible that he meant when it is on a cap or a
garment not sufficient on its own for the completeness of prayer. And all the narrations
that mention a concession for wearing these things during prayer, the discussion
concerning them is as we have already explained.

praying in pure khazz (a type of fine fabric), but prayer is not permissible in it if it is
mixed with rabbit fur or anything similar."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali,
from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from Furayt, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I was with Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, when a man from the dealers in khazz
(a type of fine fabric) entered and said to Him {a.s}:
"May I be your ransom, what do you say about prayer in khazz?"
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with praying in it."
The man said to Him {a.s}: "May I be your ransom, it is from a dead animal, and I prepare
it myself, I know it."
So Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to him: "I know it better than you."
The man said to Him {a.s}: "It is my work, and no one knows it better than me."
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, smiled and then said to him: "Do you say it is a
creature that is brought out from the water, or is caught from the water, and when
water is lost, it dies?"
The man said: "You have spoken the truth, may I be your ransom, that is how it is."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
So Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Then you are saying it is a creature that
walks on four legs, and it is not considered among the category of fish so that its
slaughter would be its exit from water?"
The man said: "Yes, by Allah {SWT}, that is what I say."
So Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to him: "Indeed Allah {SWT}, the Exalted,
has made it lawful and has made its death its slaughter, just as He {SWT} has made fish
lawful and made their death their slaughter."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ ٱلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ
الدَّيْلَمِيّ عَنْ فُرَيْتِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورِ قَالَ: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ إِذْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْخَزَّازِينَ
فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الصَّلاةِ فِي الْخَزِّ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاةِ فِيهِ» فَقَالَ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّهُ
هُوَ مَيَّتٌ وَ هُوَ عِلاجِي وَ أَنَا أَعْرِفُهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «أَنَا أَعْرَفُ بِهِ مِنْكَ» فَقَالَ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ إِنّهُ
عِلاجِي وَ لَيْسَ أَحَدْ أَعْرَفَ بِهِ مِنِّي فَتَبَسَّمَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ «تَقُولُ إِنَّهُ دَابَّةً تُخْرَجُ مِنَ الْمَاءِ
أَوْ تُصَادُ مِنَ الْمَاءِ فَتُخْرَجُ فَإِذَا فُقِدَ الْمَاءُ مَاتَ» فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ صَدَقْتَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ هَكَذَا هُوَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ «فَإِنَّكَ تَقُولُ إِنَّهُ دَابَّةً تَمْشِي عَلَى أَرْبَعِ وَ لَيْسَ هُوَ فِي حَدَّ ٱلْجِيتَانِ فَتَكُونَ ذَكَاتُهُ خُرُوجَهُ مِنَ ٱلْمَاءِ»
فَقَالَ الرَّجْلُ إي وَ اللَّهِ هَكَذَا أَقُولُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ «فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى أَحَلَّهُ وَ جَعَلَ ذَكَاتَهُ مَوْتَهُ
كَمَا أَحَلَّ الْحِيثَانَ وَ جَعَلَ ذَكَاتَهَا مَوْتَهَا».

مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَنِمِ عَنْ مُعَمَّرِ بْنِ خَلاَّدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرَّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱَلسَّلَامُ -

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
(Imam {a.s} was asked) regarding prayer in pure khazz (a type of fine fabric).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with it. But as for that which is mixed with rabbit
fur or anything similar to it, do not pray in it."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
مُحَمّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلامُ : عَنِ ٱلصَّلاةِ فِي
الخَزَّ الْخَالِصٍ «أَنَّهُ لا بَأْسَ بِهِ فَأَمَّا الَّذِي يُخْلَطُ فِيهِ وَبَرُ الْأَرَانِبِ أَوْ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يُشْبِهُ هَذَا فَلا تُصَلَّ فِيهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud
al-Sarmi, who said:
I asked him about prayer in khazz that is lined with rabbit fur.
And he wrote in reply: "That is permissible."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
This is a solitary and irregular narration (hadith shadh), reported only by Dawud al-
Sarmi, and despite him being the sole narrator, its wording varies. For in this narration,
he said: "I asked him," attributing the question to himself without clarifying who the
one being asked was, and it is possible that the person questioned is someone whose
statement is not binding or authoritative. Then he said in his narration that he
mentioned:
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيِى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ الصَّرْمِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي ٱلْخَزَّ
يُغَشُّ بِوَبَرٍ الْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ «يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ».
فهذا حديث شاذ ما رواه إلا داود الصرمي ومع تفرده بروايته تختلف ألفاظه لان في هذه الرواية قال : سألته فأضاف
السؤال الى نفسه ولم يبين من المسؤول ويحتمل أن يكون المسؤول عنه من لا يجب المصير الى قوله ثم قال في روايته
التي ذكرها،

he said: "I asked him," attributing the question to himself without clarifying who the
one being asked was, and it is possible that the person questioned is someone whose
statement is not binding or authoritative. Then he said in his narration that he
mentioned:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi,
who said:
A man asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in khazz (a
fine fabric) that is lined with rabbit fur.
He wrote in reply: "That is permissible."

Scholar's Note:
As you can see in this narration, it mentions that the questioner was someone else and
the one being asked was named, this is clearly contradictory. For if the questioner
were the narrator himself, then the later narration must be false; and if the questioner
were someone else, then the first narration must be false. When two narrations are in
contradiction and there is nothing to support either of them, both must be discarded.
Moreover, even if this hadith were authentic, it would not contradict what we have
already mentioned from the other narrations. And it is possible that this narration
came in the context of taqiyyah, just as many similar narrations have.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "Prayer in black garments is
disliked, and wearing a turban from such garments is disliked in certain contexts, but
there is no problem praying in them even if they are black."
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ وَ عَبْدِ اللّهِ اِبْنَي مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ دَاوُدَ الصِّرْمِيَ قَالَ: سَأَلَ رَجُلٌ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثَ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي الْخَزِّ يُغَشُّ بِوَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ «يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ».
فذكر على ما ترى في هذه الرواية ان السائل كان غيره وسمى المسؤول وهذا ظاهر التناقض لانه لو كان السائل هو نفسه
الوجب أن تكون الرواية الاخيرة كذبا ولو كان السائل غيره لوجب أن تكون الاولى كذبا وإذا تقابل الروايتان ولم يكن هناك
ما يعضد أحداهما وجب اطراحهما مع أنه لو صح هذا الحديث لم يكن معترضا على ما ذكرناه من الاحاديث ، ويحتمل أن
يكون ورد هذا الخبر مورد التقية كما وردت أخبار كثيرة في مثله. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (وتكره الصلاة في الثياب السود
ولبس العمامة من الثياب في شئ ولا بأس بالصلاة فيها وان كانت سوداء).
commentary:
As you can see in this narration, it mentions that the questioner was someone else and
the one being asked was named, this is clearly contradictory. For if the questioner
were the narrator himself, then the later narration must be false; and if the questioner
were someone else, then the first narration must be false. When two narrations are in
contradiction and there is nothing to support either of them, both must be discarded.
Moreover, even if this hadith were authentic, it would not contradict what we have
already mentioned from the other narrations. And it is possible that this narration
came in the context of taqiyyah, just as many similar narrations have.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "Prayer in black garments is
disliked, and wearing a turban from such garments is disliked in certain contexts, but
there is no problem praying in them even if they are black."

source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hadi {a.s}

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
(Imam {a.s} said) "Black is disliked except in three things; the shoes, the turban, and the
cloak."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «يُكْرَهُ
السَّوَادُ إلاَّ فِي ثَلَاَثَةٍ الْخُفّ وَ الْعِمَامَةِ وَ الْكِسَاءِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.213 • Miftah Al-Falah, Vol.1 p.167 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.382 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.3 p.306
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
(Imam {a.s} said) "Black is disliked except in three things; the shoes, the turban, and the
cloak."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from someone who
mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "Shall I pray in a black cap?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in it, for it is the clothing of the people of the Fire."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “It is not permissible to pray
in a thin garment that is transparent due to its thinness, unless there is something
beneath it like an izar (waist wrap), trousers, or a shirt that is not see-through."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَسِّنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
قُلْتُ لَهُ أَصَلِّي فِي الْقَلَسُوَةِ السَّوْدَاءِ فَقَالَ «لا تُصَلَ فِيهَا فَإِنَّهَا لِبَاسُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ».
قال الشيخ: ولا تجوز الصلاة في ثوب رقيق يشف لرقته حتى يكون تحته كالمنزر أو السراويل أو قميص سواه غير شفاف.
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “It is not permissible to pray
in a thin garment that is transparent due to its thinness, unless there is something
beneath it like an izar (waist wrap), trousers, or a shirt that is not see-through."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Sayyari, from Ahmad ibn Hammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah
{a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
(Imam {a.s} said) "Do not pray in what is transparent or see-through" (meaning a garment
that is thin and clings to the body)
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ السَّيَّارِيَّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «لا تُصَلَ
فيمَا شَفَّ أَوْ صَفَّ يَعْنِي التَّوْبَ الْمُصَفَّلَ».

revealing" (meaning a garment that is thin and clings to the body).
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, from some of our
companions, from one of them (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them, who said:
(Imam {a.s} said) "Wearing a cloak (irtida’) over a wrapped garment (tawashshuh; piece
of cloth over one's shoulder) in prayer is disliked, and wrapping a garment
(tawashshuh) over a shirt is also disliked."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحَدِهِمْ عَلَيْهِمُ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ: «الإِرْتِدَاءُ فَوْقَ التَوَشُحِ فِي الصَّلاَةِ مَكْرُوهٌ وَ التَّوَشُحُ فَوْقَ الْقَمِيصِ مَكْرُوهٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO

Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-

Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "It is not appropriate to wrap yourself with
an izar over the shirt when you pray, for that is from the dress of the Days of Ignorance."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَتَوَشَّحَ بِإِزَارٍ فَوْقَ الْقَمِيصِ إِذَا أَنْتَ صَلَّيْتَ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ زِيِّ
الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Beware wrapping yourself in ‘al-samma’."
I asked: "What is the ‘al-samma’ wrap?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is to insert the garment from beneath your arms and place it over one
shoulder."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
«إيَّاكَ وَ الْتِحَافَ الصَّمَّاءِ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا الْتِحَافُ الصَّمَّاءِ قَالَ «أَنْ تُدْخِلَ الثَوْبَ مِنْ تَحْتِ جَنَاحَيْكَ فَتَجْعَلَهُ عَلَى
مَنْكِبٍ وَاجِدٍ».

text_chunk:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Beware wrapping yourself in ‘al-samma’."
I asked: "What is the ‘al-samma’ wrap?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is to insert the garment from beneath your arms and place it over one
shoulder."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn ‘Umar ibn Bazi‘, who said:
I said to Al-Ridha {a.s}: "I tie the izar or the scarf over my shirt during prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with it."
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ بَزِيعِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ
أَشُدُّ الإزَارَ أَوِ الْمِنْدِيلَ فَوْقَ قَمِيصِي فِي الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «لا يَأْسَ بِهِ».

And from him, from Abu Ja‘far, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, who said:
I saw Abu Ja‘far al-Thani {a.s}, peace be upon him, praying in a shirt, and He {a.s} had
wrapped a cloth (mindil) over it as a waist-wrapper (izar) while he was praying.
text_ar:
وَ عَثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ ٱلْبَجَلِيّ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرِ الثَانِيَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يُصَلَّي فِي قَمِيص

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Ali ibn Isma‘il, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin wrote to the Righteous Servant (al-Abd al-Salih {a.s}) asking:
"Can a man pray while wearing an izar wrapped over his shirt?"
He {a.s} wrote in reply: "Yes."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
There is no contradiction between these narrations and what we mentioned earlier,
because the intended meaning of the earlier narrations is that a person should not
wrap himself completely and enclose his body with the izar in the manner that the Jews
would do. Whereas what we presented later refers to a person wrapping an izar across
his body in order to cover what may have become exposed or to conceal what has
been uncovered of his body. What supports what we have said is:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ كَتَبَ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ إِلَى اَلْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ : هَلْ
يُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ الصَّلاةَ وَ عَلَيْهِ إِذَارْ مُتَوَشِّحْ بِهِ فَوْقَ ٱلْقَمِيصِ فَكَتَبَ «نَعَمْ».
فليس بين هذه الاخبار وبين ما ذكرناه أولا تناقض لان المراد بالاخبار المتقدمة هو أن لا يلتحف الانسان ويشتمل به كما
بلتحف اليهود، وما قدمناه أخيرا هو ان يتوشح بالازار ليغطى ما قد كشف منه ويستر ما تعرى من بدنه ،

would do. Whereas what we presented later refers to a person wrapping an izar across
his body in order to cover what may have become exposed or to conceal what has
been uncovered of his body. What supports what we have said is:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn,
from Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who wraps himself in a single garment during prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should not wrap himself in a single garment completely. But if he
wraps it across himself (tawashshaha) and covers his shoulders, then there is no
problem."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is disliked for a person to
pray wearing a turban that does not have a hanak (the part of the turban that is
wrapped under the chin)."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَشْتَمِلُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ بِثَوْبِ وَاحِدٍ قَالَ «لا يَشْتَمِلُ بِتَوْبِ وَاجِدٍ فَأَمَا أَنْ يَتَوَشَّحَ فَيُغَطَّيَ مَنْكِبَنْهِ فَلاَ
بَأْسَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ويكره أن يصلي الانسان بعمامة لا حنك لها).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is disliked for a person to
pray wearing a turban that does not have a hanak (the part of the turban that is
wrapped under the chin)."

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from someone who
mentioned it:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever wears a turban and does not
wrap it under the chin (yatanahhak), and then suffers from an illness for which there is
no cure, let him blame no one but himself."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
«مَنْ تَعَمَّمَ وَ لَمْ يَتَحَنَّك فَأَصَابَهُ دَاءَ لا دَوَاءَ لَهُ فَلاَ يَلُومَنَ إلاَّ نَفْسَهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.6 p.460 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.215 • Al-Wafi, Vol.2 0 p.745 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.401 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.194

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from a group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja‘far, from Amr ibn
Sa‘id, from Isa ibn Hamzah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever wears a turban and does not
wrap the turban under his chin (hanak), and then is afflicted with a pain for which there
is no cure, let him blame no one but himself."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no problem if a
person prays in a single izar (waist wrap), wrapping part of it around his waist and using
the other part as an upper covering."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدِ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ حَمْرَةَ عَنْ
أبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنِ اِعْتَمَّ فَلَمْ يُدِرِ الْعِمَامَةَ تَحْتَ حَنَكِهِ فَأَصَابَهُ أَلَمٌ لا دَوَاءَ لَهُ فَلاَ يَلُومَنَّ إِلاّ
نَفْسَهُ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا بأس أن يصلي الانسان في ازار واحد يأتزر ببعضه ويرتدي بالبعض الآخر).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no problem if a
person prays in a single izar (waist wrap), wrapping part of it around his waist and using
the other part as an upper covering."

text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from his father,
who said:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s} led us in prayer wearing a single garment.
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَذَيْنَةَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.216 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.383 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.391

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Isma‘il, from Safwan, from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, who said:
Someone who asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, narrated to me (Rifa‘ah ibn
Musa), about a man who prays in a single garment, wrapping it around his lower body.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with it if he raises it up to his chest."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
محَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي مَنْ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاجِدٍ يَأْتَزِرُ بِهِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِهِ إِذَا رَفَعَهُ إِلَى الثَّذْيَيْنِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.216
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri’ab, from Ziyad ibn
Suqah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if one of you prays in a
single garment with its buttons undone. Indeed, the religion of Muhammad {saws} (peace
be upon him and his family) is upright and simple (hanif)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ سُوقَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: «لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الثَّوْبِ الْوَاجِدِ وَ أَزْرَارُهُ مَحْلُولَةٌ إِنَّ دِينَ مُحَمَّدِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ
حَنِيفٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his
brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far, peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prayed while his private part was exposed, and he
did not know about it. Does he have to repeat the prayer, or what is his situation?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no repetition upon him, and his prayer is complete."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ الْعَمْرَكِيَّ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا
السَّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ صَلَّى وَ فَرْجُهُ خَارِجْ لاَ يَعلَمُ بِهِ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةٌ أُوْ مَا حَالُهُ قَالَ «لا إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ وَ
قَدْ تَمْثْ صَلاَثُهُ».

source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from his
brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far, peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prayed while his private part was exposed, and he
did not know about it. Does he have to repeat the prayer, or what is his situation?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no repetition upon him, and his prayer is complete."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, by Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prays in a single shirt, or a narrow-sleeved robe
(qabaʾ taq), or a padded robe, and he is not wearing an izar (waist wrap).
Imam {a.s} said: "If the shirt is thick, and the robe (qabaʾ) is not split wide open in the
front, and the single garment if he wraps it across himself, and the trousers (sarawil)
are of that same type, then there is no problem with all of that. But when he wears
trousers, he should put something over his shoulders, even if it is just a rope."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "A free woman should not pray
without a khimar (head covering) on her head, but this is permissible for slave women
and for young girls among the free women."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ
عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي قَمِيص وَاجِدٍ أَوْ قَبَاءِ طَاقٍ أَوْ قَبَاءٍ مَحْشُوَّ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِزَارْ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ ٱلْقَمِيصُ صَفِيقاً
وَ الْقَبَاءُ لَيْسَ بِطَوِيلِ الْفُرَجِ وَ التَّوْبُ الْوَاحِدُ إِذَا كَانَ يَتَوَشَّحُ بِهِ وَ السَّرَاوِيلُ بِتِلْكَ الْمَنْزِلَةِ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ
لَكِنْ إِذَا لَبِسَ السَّرَاوِيلَ جَعَلَ عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ شَيْئاً وَ لَوْ حَبْلاً».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا تصلي المرأة الحرة بغير خمار على رأسها ويجوز ذلك للاماء والصبيان من حرائر النساء).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "A free woman should not pray
without a khimar (head covering) on her head, but this is permissible for slave women
and for young girls among the free women."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far {a.s} about the minimum clothing in which a woman may pray.
Imam {a.s} said: "A long shirt (dir‘) and an large wrap (milhafah), which she spreads over
her head and covers herself with."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ - عَنْ أَدْنَى
مَا تُصَلِّي فِيهِ الْمَرْأَةُ قَالَ «دِزعْ وَ مِلْحَفَةً فَتَنْشُرُهَا عَلَى رَأْسِهَا وَ تَتَجَلِّلُ بِهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.217 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.388 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.376 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.407

text_en:
And from him, from Safwan, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj:
Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "It is not obligatory for slave women to
cover their heads in prayer, and it is not appropriate for a woman to pray except in two
garments."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لَيْسَ عَلَى الْإمَاءِ أَنْ يَتَقَنِّعْنَ
فِي الصَّلاةٍ وَ لا يَنْبَغِي لِلْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ إلاَّ فِي ثَوْبَيْنِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam,
from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I saw Abu Ja‘far {a.s} praying in a single izar (waist wrap) that was not wide, and He {a.s}
had tied it around His {a.s} neck.
I said to Him {a.s}: "What do you say about a man who prays in a single shirt?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If it is thick, then there is no problem with it. And a woman prays in a
long shirt (dir‘) and a head covering (miqna‘ah), if the shirt is thick, meaning if it is
concealing."
I asked: "May Allah {SWT} have mercy on you, does a slave woman cover her head when
she prays?"
Imam {a.s} said: "A slave woman is not required to wear a head covering."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أُحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ ٱلْحَكَمِ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَدِ بْنِ
مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ صَلَّى فِي إِزَارٍ وَاحِدٍ لَيْسَ بِوَاسِع قَدْ عَقَدَهُ عَلَى عُنُقِهِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا تَرَى
لِلرَّجُلٍ يُصَلِّي فِي قَمِيص وَاجِدٍ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ كَثِيفا فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ تُصَلِّي فِي الدَّرْعِ وَ ٱلْمِقْتَعَةِ إِذَا كَانَ
الدَّرْعُ كَثِيفاً يَعْنِي إذَا كَانّ سَتِيراً» قُلْتُ رَجِمَكَ اللَّهُ الْأَمَةُ تُغَطَّي رَأْسَهَا إِذَا صَلَّتْ فَقَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَى ٱلْأَمَةِ قِنَاعٌ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.394 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.217 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.375

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from
Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "A woman prays in three garments: an izar
(waist wrap), a dir‘ (long shirt), and a khimar (head covering). It does not harm her to
wrap herself with the khimar. But if she does not find (all three), then two garments:
she wraps the lower part of her body with one and covers her head with the other."
I asked: "And if it is a dir‘ and a milhafah (outer wrap) and she does not have a miqna‘ah
(headscarf)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem if she covers her head with the milhafah. If it does
not suffice her, then she should wear it lengthwise."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَعَثَهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثَمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ
اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «تُصَلِّي الْمَرْأَةُ فِي ثَلَاَثَةِ أَثْوَابِ إِزَارٍ وَ دِزعِ وَ جِمَارٍ وَ لا يَضُرُهَا
بِأَنْ تَقَنَّعَ بِالْخِمَارِ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدْ فَثَوْبَيْنِ تَأْتَزِرُ بِأَحَدِهِمَا وَ تَقَنَّعُ بِالآخَرِ» قُلْتُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ دِزْعاً وَ مِلْحَفَةً لَيْسَ عَلَيْهَا
مِقْنَعَةٌ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ إِذَا تَقَنَّعَتْ بِالْمِلْحَفَةِ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُفِهَا فَلْتَلْبَسْهَا طُولاً».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.395 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.217 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.389 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.376 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.406

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah
al-Ansari, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem for a free Muslim
woman to pray with her head uncovered."
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ الْأَنْصَارِيّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ
عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ بِالْمَرْأَةِ ٱلْمُسْلِمَةِ الْحُرَّةِ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ وَ هِيَ مَكْشُوفَةُ الرَّأْسِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.218
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah
al-Ansari, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem for a free Muslim
woman to pray with her head uncovered."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Abu Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Ayyub al-Makki, from
Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem if a Muslim woman
prays and there is no head covering (qina‘) on her head."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
It is possible that what is meant by these two narrations is young girls from among the
women, not adult women, because it is permissible for them to pray without a head
covering (qina‘). It is also possible that this permission was granted in a situation
where they are unable or do not have access to a head covering, then in such a case,
it is permissible for them to pray without one.
Another possibility is that the meaning of the phrase "she prays without a head
covering" refers to when she is wearing a garment that covers her from head to toe.
As for the second narration, it does not mention a "free woman" (hurrah), but only
refers to a "Muslim woman," and it is possible that the intent was a slave woman
(amah), as it is not obligatory for her to wear a head covering, as we have previously
mentioned. What further clarifies this is:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي أَيُوبَ الْمَكِّيَّ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي
عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ الْمَرْأَةُ ٱلْمُسْلِمَةُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى رَأْسِهَا قِنَاعٌ».
فيحتمل أن يكون المراد بهذين الخبرين الصغيرة من النساء دون البالغات لانه يجوز لهن أن يصلين بغير قناع ، ويحتمل
أيضا أن يكون إنما سوغ لهن هذا في حال لم يتمكن ولا يقدرن على القناع فحينئذ يجوز لهن أن يصلين بغير قناع ، ويحتمل
أيضا أن يكون المراد بقوله تصلي بغير قناع إذا كان عليها ثوب يسترها من رأسها الى قدميها، فأما الحديث الثاني فليس
فيه ذكر الحرة وإنما تضمن ذكر المرأة المسلمة ويجوز أن يكون المراد بها أمة لان الامة لا يجب عليها القناع حسب ما
ذكرناه ، ويزيده بيانا :

where they are unable or do not have access to a head covering, then in such a case,
it is permissible for them to pray without one.
Another possibility is that the meaning of the phrase "she prays without a head
covering" refers to when she is wearing a garment that covers her from head to toe.
As for the second narration, it does not mention a "free woman" (hurrah), but only
refers to a "Muslim woman," and it is possible that the intent was a slave woman
(amah), as it is not obligatory for her to wear a head covering, as we have previously
mentioned. What further clarifies this is:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
What was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan
ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who
said:
I (narrator) said to Him {a.s}: "Does the slave woman (amah) cover her head?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No. And it is not obligatory for umm al-walad (a slave woman who has
borne a child) to cover her head, if she has not borne a child."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ سَعدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ وَ عَبْدِ اللّهِ اِبْنَيْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ الْأَمَةُ تُفَطَّي رَأْسَهَا فَقَالَ «لا وَ لاَ عَلَى أَمِّ ٱلْوَلَدِ أَنْ تُغَطَّيَ رَأْسَهَا إِذَا لَمْ
يَكُنْ لَهَا وَلَدٌ».

text_en:
And what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a woman praying in a dir‘ (long
shirt) and a khimar (head covering).
Imam {a.s} said: "There should be over her a milhafah (outer wrap) that she gathers
around herself."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The mention of the milhafah in addition to the dir‘ (long shirt) and khimar (head
covering) is intended to indicate an increase in virtue and reward. It is also possible
that what is meant is when the dir‘ and khimar do not cover sufficiently, so in such a
case, regardless of the situation, a proper covering (satir) is required.
What supports what we have said is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ اَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ
الْمَرْأَةِ تُصَلِّي فِي دِزعِ وَ جِمَارٍ فَقَالَ «تَكُونُ عَلَيْهَا مِلْحَفَةُ تَضُمُهَا عَلَيْهَا».
فان المراد بذكر الملحفة زيادة على الدرع والخمار زيادة الفضل والثواب ، ويجوز أن يكون المراد به إذا كان الدرع والخمار
لا يواريان شيئا فانه مهما كانت الحال على هذا فلا بد من ساتر، والذي يدل على ما قلناه، ما رواه:

case, regardless of the situation, a proper covering (satir) is required.
What supports what we have said is what was narrated:

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, by Ali ibn Ibrahim, by his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "It is not proper for a Muslim woman to wear
of head coverings (khumur) and long shirts (duru‘) that do not conceal anything."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ ٱلْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: «لَا يَصْلُحُ لِلْمَرْأَةِ الْمُسْلِمَةِ أَنْ تَلْبَسَ مِنَ الْخُمُرِ وَ الدُّرُوعِ مَا لا يُوَارِي شَيْئًا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa‘id ibn ‘Uqda, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who said: My father
narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Jamil ibn ‘Ayyash Abu Ali al-Bazzaz, who said: My father informed me,
saying:
I asked (Imam) Ja‘far ibn Muhammad {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a garment made
by the People of the Book, may I pray in it before it is washed?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem, though it is more beloved to me that it be
washed."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
in latrines, or fire temples, or places where wine is kept, nor on the middle of roads,
nor in camel resting places, nor on salty barren land (ard al-sabkha)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ اِبْنُ عُقْدَةَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي عَنْ عَبْدِ آللَّهِ بْنِ
جَمِيلِ بْنِ عَيَّاشِ أَبِي عَلِيَّ ٱلْبَزَّازِ قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبِي قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ التَّوْبِ يَعْمَلُهُ أَهْلُ
الْكِتَابِ أُصَلِّي فِيهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُفْسَلَ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ وَ أَنْ يُغْسَلَ أَحَبُ إِلَيَّ».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (ولا تجوز الصلاة في بيوت الغائط أو بيوت النيران وبيوت الخمور وعلى جواد الطرق وفي معاطن
الابل وفي أرض السبخة).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
in latrines, or fire temples, or places where wine is kept, nor on the middle of roads,
nor in camel resting places, nor on salty barren land (ard al-sabkha)."

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibn al-Barqi, from his father, from
Abdullah ibn al-Fadl, from someone who narrated to him:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There are ten places in which prayer is not
to be performed: mud, water, bathhouses, graves, the resting places along roads, ant
colonies, camel resting spots, water channels, salty barren land (al-sabkha), and
snow."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ الْبَرْقِيَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «عَشَرَةُ مَوَاضِعَ لا يُصَلَّى فِيهَا الطَّينُ وَ الْمَاءُ وَ الْحَمَّامُ وَ الْقُبُورُ وَ مَسَانُ الطُرُقِ وَ
قُرَى اَلنَّمْلِ وَ مَعَاطِنُ الْإِبِلِ وَ مَجْرَى الْمَاءِ وَ السِّبَخُ وَ الثَّلْجٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.219 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.142
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

عَنْ عَمَّارِ السَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا تُصَلِّ فِي بَيْتٍ فِيهِ خَمْرٌ أوْ مُسْكِرٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer in sheep enclosures.
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray in them. But do not pray in camel enclosures unless you fear for
the loss of your belongings, then sweep it and sprinkle it with water, and pray."
And I asked him about prayer on the side of the road.
He said: "There is no problem with praying on the edges between the main pathways.
But as for on the main roads themselves, do not pray on them."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي مَرَابِضِ ٱلْغَنَمِ فَقَالَ «صَلِّ فِيهَا وَ لا تُصَلَّ فِي أَعْطَانِ الْإِبِلِ إِلَّ أَنْ تَخَافَ عَلَى مَتَاعِكَ ٱلضَّيْعَةَ
فَاكْنُسْهُ وَرُشَّهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَ صَلّ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي ظَهْرِ الطَّرِيقِ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ تُصَلِّيَ فِي ٱلظَوَاهِرِ الْتِي
بَيْنَ الْجَوَادَ فَأَمَا عَلَى الْجَوَادِ فَلا تُصَلِّ فِيهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.220

text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl,
who said:
(Imam {a.s}) Al-Ridha {a.s} said: "Every pathway that is walked upon or passed through,
whether it has a main road (jadah) or not, it is not appropriate to pray in it."
I asked: "Then where should I pray?"
Imam {a.s} said: "To the right or to the left (off the path)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمّدِ بْنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ قَالَ ٱلرّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ: «كُلْ طَرِيقٍ
يُوطَأُ أَوْ يُتَطَرَّقُ وَ كَانَتْ فِيهِ جَادَةً أَوْ لَمْ تَكُنْ فَلا يَنْبَغِي الصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ» قُلْتُ فَأَيْنَ أُصَلّي فَقَالَ «يَمْنَةً وَ يَسْرَةً».
