text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about praying in camel enclosures, and in the pens of cows and sheep.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you sprinkle them with water and they are dry, then there is no
problem in praying there. But as for the stables of horses and mules, no."

Scholar's Note:
This concession is to be understood as applying in cases of necessity and fear of losing
one's belongings. What clarifies this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي أَعْطَانِ الْإِبِلِ وَ فِي مَرَابِضِ الْبَقَرِ
وَ الْغَنَمِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ نَضَحْتَهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَ قَدْ كَانَ يَابِساً فَلا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلَاةِ فِيهَا فَأَمَا مَرَابِطُ ٱلْخَيْلِ وَ الْبِغَالِ فَلا)».
فهذه الرخصة محمولة على حال الضرورة والخوف على تضييع المتاع ، والذي يبين ذلك ما رواه :
commentary:
This concession is to be understood as applying in cases of necessity and fear of losing
one's belongings. What clarifies this is what was narrated:

text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in camel enclosures.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you fear the loss of your belongings, then sweep it, sprinkle it with
water, and pray. And there is no problem with praying in sheep enclosures."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ فِي أَعْطَانٍ
الْإبِل فَقَالَ «إِنْ تَخَوَّفْتَ الضَّيْعَةَ عَلَى مَتَاعِكَ فَاكُتُسْهُ وَ اِنْضِحْهُ وَ صَلِّ وَ لا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِي مَرَابِضِ الْغَنَمِ».

Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer during travel.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray on the main road (jadah); rather, move to its sides."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي
السَّفَرِ فَقَالَ «لا تُصَلِّ عَلَى الْجَادَّةِ وَ اِعْتَزِلْ عَلَى جَانِبَيْهَا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm:
Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Every path that is walked upon,
do not pray on it."
I asked: "It has been narrated from your grandfather that 'there is no problem with
praying on the edges (zawahir) of the roads.'"
Imam {a.s} said: "That might be when a man accompanied me on it."
I asked: "And if a man fears the loss of his belongings?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If he fears loss, then let him pray."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَالٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ الْجَهْمِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَ قَالَ:
«كُلّ طَرِيقٍ يُوطَأ فَلا تُصَلِّ عَلَيْهِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ إِنَّهُ قَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ جَدِّكَ «أنَّ الصَّلاَةَ عَلَى ٱلظَوَاهِرِ لا بَأْسَ بِهَا» قَالَ
«ذَاكَ رُبَّمَا سَايَرَنِي عَلَيْهِ الرَّجُلُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإنْ خَافَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مَتَاعِهِ ٱلضَّيْعَةَ قَالَ «فَإنْ خَافَ الضَّيْعَةَ فَلْيُصَلَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.221 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.448 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.148

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi
Nasr, from someone who asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
(Imam {a.s} was asked) about a mosque whose wall in the direction of the qiblah is
leaking from a drainage hole (balu‘ah) into which people urinate.
He said: "If the leakage is from the drainage hole (balu‘ah), then do not pray in it. But if
it is from something else, then there is no problem."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ: عَمَّنْ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ يَنِزّ حَائِطُ قِبْلَتِهِ مِنْ بَالُوعَةٍ يُبَالُ فِيهَا فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ نَزُّهُ مِنَ الْبَالُوعَةِ فَلاَ تُصَلِّ فِيهِ وَ
إِنْ كَانَ مِنْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer on salty barren land (al-sibakh).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem."

Scholar's Note:
What is meant by it is when there is a place within the salty barren land (al-sabkha)
where the forehead can rest flatly, because the prohibition is specifically regarding
prostrating on land that prevents proper prostration.
What supports what we have said is what was narrated:
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصْلاَةِ فِي السَّبَاخِ فَقَالَ «لا
بَأُسَ».
فالمراد به إذا كان فيها موضع تقع الجبهة عليه مستويا لان النهي إنما وقع عن السجود في أرض السبخة لان الانسان لا
يتمكن فيها من السجود، والذي يدل على ما ذكرناه ما رواه :

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Shu‘ayb ibn Ya‘qub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah
{a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer on salty barren land (al-sabkha), why is it disliked?
Imam {a.s} said: "Because the forehead does not rest evenly."
So I said: "And if there is flat ground within it?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Then there is no problem."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no problem with
praying in churches (biya’) and synagogues (kanaʾis) if the Muslim faces the Qiblah.
But prayer should not be performed in Zoroastrian fire temples (buyut al-majus) until
they are sprinkled with water."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنْ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبِ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي السِّبَخَةِ لِمَ تَكْرَهُهُ قَالَ «لأَّنَّ الْجَبْهَةَ لا تَقَعُ مُسْتَوِيَةً» فَقُلْتُ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهَا أَرْضٌ مُسْتَوِيَةً
فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا بأس بالصلاة في البيع والكنايس إذا توجه الانسان المسلم إلى قبلته ولا يصلى في بيوت
المجوس حتى ترش بالماء).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no problem with
praying in churches (biya’) and synagogues (kanaʾis) if the Muslim faces the Qiblah.
But prayer should not be performed in Zoroastrian fire temples (buyut al-majus) until
they are sprinkled with water."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-‘Ayyas ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about churches (biya’) and synagogues
(kanaʾis), can one pray in them?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
And I asked Him {a.s}: "Is it permissible to tear them down and build a mosque in their
place?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بَنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْعِيصِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الْبِيَعِ وَ
الْكَنَائِسِ يُصَلَّى فِيهِمَا فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ نَقْضُهَا مَسْجِداً فَقَالَ « نَعَمْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.222 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.454 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.138 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.211

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about praying in churches (biya’), synagogues (kanaʾis), and
Zoroastrian fire temples (buyut al-majus).
Imam {a.s} said: "Sprinkle (them with water), and then pray."
text_ar:
وَعَنَهُ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي ٱلْبِيَعِ وَ الْكَنَائِسِ
وَبُيُوتِ الْمَجُوسِ فَقَالَ »رُشَ وَ صَلَّ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.222 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.138 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.331

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
And from him, from Fadalah, from Hammad al-Nab, from al-Hakam ibn al-Hakam, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} being asked about prayer in churches (biya’) and synagogues
(kanaʾis).
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray in them, I have seen how clean they are!"
I asked: "Is it permissible to pray in them even though they (non-Muslims) pray in
them?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes. Do you not read the Qur’an: 'Say, each works according to his own
way, but your Lord {AZJ} is most knowing of who is best guided in path'? (Surah Isra 17:84)
Pray facing the Qiblah, and let them go their way."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ النَّابِ عَنِ الْحَكَمِ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ يَقُولُ: وَ سُئِلَ عَنِ
الصَّلاةِ فِي الْبِيَعِ وَ الْكَنَائِسِ فَقَالَ «صَلِّ فِيهَا قَدْ رَأَيْتُهَا مَا أَنظَفَهَا» قُلْتُ أَيُصَلَّى فِيهَا وَ إِنْ كَانُوا يُصَلُّونَ فِيهَا
فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ أَ مَا تَقْرَأَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ «قُلْ كُلُّ يَعْمَلُ عَلى شاكِلَتِهِ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهدىٰ سَبِيلاً» صَلِّ عَلَى الْقِبْلَةِ وَ
غَرَّبْهُمْ ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.222 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.454 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.138 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.3 p.582 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.330 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.3 p.214 • Tafsir Kanz Al- Daqaiq, Vol.7 p.499 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.3 p.336

text_en:
And from him, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa, from Shu‘ayb ibn Ya‘qub, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in the houses of the Magians
(Zoroastrians).
Imam {a.s} said: "Sprinkle (them with water), and then pray."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
in a garment that has been contaminated with wine, any intoxicating drink, or foqqa‘
(a mildly intoxicating barley drink), until it is purified by washing."
A full explanation of this has already been given in the Book of Purity, in a way that
leaves nothing further to be added, Allah {SWT} willing.
Then he said, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him: "Nor is it permissible to pray in a
garment that has semen on it until it is washed; and the same ruling applies to all other
impurities (najasat)." This too has already been detailed in the Book of Purity.
What confirms this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبِ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ
فِي بُيُوتِ الْمَجُوسِ قَالَ «رُشَّر وَ صَلَّ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولا تجوز الصلاة في ثوب قد أصابه خمر أو شراب مسكر أو فقاع حتى يطهر بالغسل). فقد مضى
شرح ذلك مستوفى في كتاب الطهارة بما لا مزيد عليه إن شاء اللّٰه تعالى. ثم قال رحمه اللّه : (ولا يصلى في ثوب فيه مني
حتى يغسل وكذلك الحكم في سائر النجاسات). فقد مضى أيضًا ما في ذلك في كتاب الطهارة، والذي يؤكد ذلك ما رواه:
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
in a garment that has been contaminated with wine, any intoxicating drink, or foqqa‘
(a mildly intoxicating barley drink), until it is purified by washing."
A full explanation of this has already been given in the Book of Purity, in a way that
leaves nothing further to be added, Allah {SWT} willing.
Then he said, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him: "Nor is it permissible to pray in a
garment that has semen on it until it is washed; and the same ruling applies to all other
impurities (najasat)." This too has already been detailed in the Book of Purity.
What confirms this is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad, from one of the two Imams, peace be
upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about madhi (pre-ejaculatory fluid) that gets on a garment.
Imam {a.s} said: "Sprinkle it with water if you wish."
And regarding mani (semen) that gets on a garment.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you know its location, then wash it. And if it is not clear to you, then
wash the entire garment."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمَذْيِ يُصِيبُ
التَّوْبَ فَقَالَ «يَنضَحُهُ بِالْمَاءِ إنْ شَاءَ» وَ قَالَ فِي الْمَنِيِّ يُصِيبُ التَّوْبَ قَالَ «إِنْ عَرَفْتَ مَكَانَهُ فَاغْسِلَهُ وَ إِنْ خَفِيَ
عَلَيْكَ فَاغْسِلْهُ كُلَّهُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be
upon him, who said:
Imam {a.s} mentioned semen (mani) and emphasized its impurity, considering it more
severe than urine.
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
Then Imam {a.s} said: "If you see semen before or after entering the prayer, you must
repeat the prayer. But if you looked at your garment and did not see it, and then prayed
in it, and later saw it, then there is no need for you to repeat the prayer. And the same
applies to urine."

Scholar's Note:
If a person's garment is contaminated with impurity (najasah) and he has no other
clothing available, then he should remove it and pray naked while seated.
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: ذَكَرَ ٱلْمَنِيَ فَشَدَدَهُ وَ جَعَلَهُ
أَشَدَّ مِنَ الْبَوْلِ ثُمَّ قَالَ «إِنْ رَأَيْتَ الْمَنِيَّ قَبْلَ أَوْ بَعْدَ مَا تَدْخُلُ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَعَلَيْكَ إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ وَ إِنْ أَنْتَ نَظَرْتَ
فِي ثَوْبِكَ فَلَمْ تُصِبْهُ ثُمَّ صَلَّيْتَ فِيهِ ثُمَّ رَأَيْتَهُ بَعْدُ فَلاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْكَ وَ كَذَلِكَ الْبَوْلُ».
فان أصاب ثوب الانسان نجاسة ولم يكن معه غيره من الاثواب ينزعه ويصلي عريانا من قعود، والذي يدل على ذلك :

clothing available, then he should remove it and pray naked while seated.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group (of our companions), from Ahmad ibn
Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who is in a deserted land and has only one garment, and
he becomes in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) in it, and he does not have water,
what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He performs tayammum and prays naked, seated, and gestures (for
bowing and prostration)."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ
سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَكُونُ فِي فَلاَةٍ مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّ ثَوْبٌ وَاجِدٌ وَ أُجْتَبَ فِيهِ وَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ مَاءً
كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يَتَيَمَمُ وَ يُصَلِّي عُرْيَاناً قَاعِداً وَ يُومِى».

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Mansur
ibn Hazim, who said Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi narrated to me:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who becomes junub
(in a state of major ritual impurity) while in the open desert and has only one garment,
and semen (mani) has gotten on that garment.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should perform tayammum, remove his garment, sit with his body
gathered (to cover his private parts), and pray, gesturing with motions (imaʾ)."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَرَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ الْحَلَبِيْ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ أَصَابَثْهُ جَنَابَةٌ وَ هُوَ بِالْفَلاةِ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ ثَوْبٌ
وَاجِدٌ وَ أَصَابَ ثَوْبَهُ مَنِيٌّ قَالَ «يَتَيَمّمُ وَ يَطْرَحُ ثَوْبَهُ وَ يَجْلِسُ مُجْتَمِعاً وَ يُصَلِّي وَ يُومِئُ إِيمَاءَ».

text_en:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman,
from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who becomes junub in his
garment or it is soiled with urine, and he has no other garment besides it.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in it if he is forced to do so."
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ ٱلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللّه عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ فِي التَّوْبِ أَوْ يُصِيبُهُ بَوْلٌ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ ثَوْبٌ غَيْرُهُ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي فِيهِ إِذَا أضْطُرِّ
إِليْهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ali ibn Ja‘far narrated from his brother (Imam al Kadhim {a.s}), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who is naked and the time for prayer arrives, and he finds
a garment, but half of it or all of it is stained with blood, should he pray in it, or should
he pray naked?
Imam {a.s} said: "If he finds water, he should wash it. If he does not find water, then he
should pray in it and not pray while naked."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَلِي بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجْلٍ عُرْيَانٍ وَ حَضَرَتِ الصَلاةُ فَأَصَابَ ثَوْباً نِصْفُهُ
دَمْ أَوْ كُلّهُ أَيُصَلِّي فِيهِ أَوْ يُصَلِّي عُرْيَاناً فَقَالَ «إِنْ وَجَدَ مَاءَ غَسَلَهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ مَاءً صَلَّى فِيهِ وَ لَمْ يُصَلَ عُزْيَاناً».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Abu Ja‘far, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah,
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who becomes junub in a garment and has no other
garment, nor is he able to wash it.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in it."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
Discussion on these narrations can be approached from several angles:
The first is that none of them explicitly state which prayer is being performed in such a
state. And since this is not specified, we interpret them as referring to the funeral
prayer (salat al-janazah), because it is among those prayers that a person is allowed
to perform even if his garment is not pure, just as he may perform it even if he himself
is not in a state of ritual purity.
The second is that it may be permissible to pray in such a condition, but once water is
available, the garment must be washed and the prayer repeated.
What supports this interpretation is what was narrated:
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ فِي ثَوْبٍ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ غَيْرُهُ وَ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى غَسْلِهِ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي فِيهِ».
الكلام على هذه الاخبار من وجوه: أحدها : أنه ليس في ش منها انه يصلي فيه أي صلاة وإذا لم يكن هذا فيه حملناه
على صلاة الجنازة لان صلاة الجنازة مما يجوز أن يصليها الانسان وإن لم يكن ثوبه طاهرا كما أنه يجوز أن لا تكون نفسه
طاهرة، والآخر: انه يجوز أن يصلي إلا انه يجب عليه عند وجود الماء غسله وإعادة الصلاة، والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:
commentary:
Discussion on these narrations can be approached from several angles:
The first is that none of them explicitly state which prayer is being performed in such a
state. And since this is not specified, we interpret them as referring to the funeral
prayer (salat al-janazah), because it is among those prayers that a person is allowed
to perform even if his garment is not pure, just as he may perform it even if he himself
is not in a state of ritual purity.
The second is that it may be permissible to pray in such a condition, but once water is
available, the garment must be washed and the prayer repeated.
What supports this interpretation is what was narrated:

text_chunk:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah, from Abu Ja‘far, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah,
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who becomes junub in a garment and has no other
garment, nor is he able to wash it.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in it."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT Scholar's Note:
Discussion on these narrations can be approached from several angles:
The first is that none of them explicitly state which prayer is being performed in such a
state. And since this is not specified, we interpret them as referring to the funeral
prayer (salat al-janazah), because it is among those prayers that a person is allowed
to perform even if his garment is not pure, just as he may perform it even if he himself
is not in a state of ritual purity.
The second is that it may be permissible to pray in such a condition, but once water is
available, the garment must be washed and the prayer repeated.
What supports this interpretation is what was narrated:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from

to pray in it, and he does not find water to wash it, what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He performs tayammum and prays. Then when he obtains water, he
washes the garment and repeats the prayer."

Scholar's Note:
As for the narration of Ali ibn Ja’far in particular, it is possible that the blood on the
garment was the blood of a fish, since it is permissible to pray in both a small or large
amount of it.
And if a person has two garments, and one of them is contaminated with an impurity
that renders it impermissible to pray in, then he should pray in each of them (one

عَمَّارِ السَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ ثَوْبٌ وَ لاَ تَجِلُّ الصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ وَ
لَيْسَ يَجِدُ مَاءَ يَغْسِلُهُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يَتَيَمَّمُ وَ يُصَلِّي فَإِذَا أَصَابَ مَاءَ غَسَلَهُ وَ أَعَادَ الصَّلاَةَ».

وكثيره، فان كان مع الانسان ثوبان وأصاب واحدا منهما نجاسة لا تحل الصلاة فيه فليصل في كل واحد منهما ، يدل على
ذلك ما رواه :

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Sa’d, from Ali ibn Isma’il, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s} asking about a man who had two garments, and one of them was
contaminated with urine, but he did not know which one. The time for prayer arrived,
and he feared missing it, and he had no water, what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in both of them together."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is disliked for a person to
pray while there is fire in front of him, or a bare weapon, or an image, or anything
impure in his direction of prayer."
text_ar:
سَعدٌ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلاَمُ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ
كَانَ مَعَهُ ثَوْبَانِ فَأَصَابَ أَحَدَهُمَا بَوْلٌ وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَيُهُمَا هُوَ وَ حَضَرَتِ الصَّلاَةُ وَ خَافَ فَوْتَهَا وَ لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ مَاءْ كَيْفَ
يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي فِيهِمَا جَمِيعاً».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ويكره للانسان أن يصلي وفي قبلته نار أو سلاح مجرد أو فيها صورة أو شئ من النجاسات).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is disliked for a person to
pray while there is fire in front of him, or a bare weapon, or an image, or anything
impure in his direction of prayer."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from ‘Imran ibn Musa and Muhammad ibn Ahmad,
from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prays while
there is an open Qur'an (mushaf) in front of him in the direction of the Qiblah.
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
I asked: "What if it is in a cover?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
And Imam {a.s} said: "A man should not pray while there is fire or iron in his (direction of)
Qiblah."
I asked: "Can he pray while there is a brass incense burner (mijmarah shabah) in front
of him?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, but if it contains fire, then he should not pray until he moves it
away from his (direction of) Qiblah."
And (Imam {a.s} said) about a man who prays while there is a hanging lamp (qindil) in
front of him with fire in it, but it is level with him.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it is raised high, it is worse, he should not pray directly in line with it."
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ مُوسَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ
عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمّارِ السَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ
بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مُصْحَفٌ مَفْتُوحْ فِي قِبْلَتِهِ قَالَ «لا» قُلْتُ فَإِنْ كَانَ فِي غِلَاَفٍ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» وَ قَالَ «لا يُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ وَ فِي
قِبلَتِهِ نَارْ أَوْ حَدِيدٌ» قُلْتُ أَلَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِجْمَرَةُ شَبَهِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ فَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهَا نَارْ فَلا يُصَلِّي حَتَّى
يُنَحِّيَهَا عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِ» وَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ قِنْدِيلٌ مُعَلَّقٌ وَ فِيهِ نَارْ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ بِحِيَالِهِ قَالَ «إِذَا اِرْتَفَعَ كَانَ شَرّاً
لاَ يُصَلِّي بِحِيَالِهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.390 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.225 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.460

text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja‘far, from Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon
him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man praying while a lamp (siraj) is placed in front of him in the
direction of the Qiblah.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is not proper for him to face the fire."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
And it has also been narrated that there is no harm in that, because the One {AZJ} to
whom the prayer is directed is nearer to him than the object (such as the fire or lamp)
in front of him.
text_ar:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْعَمْرَكِيّ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرِّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ
اَلسِّرَاجُ مَوْضُوعٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فِي الْقِبْلَةِ فَقَالَ «لا يَصْلُحُ لَهُ أَنْ يَسْتَقْبِلَ النَّارَ».
وقد روى أنه لا بأس بذلك لان الذي يصلي له أقرب إليه من ذلك.
commentary:
And it has also been narrated that there is no harm in that, because the One {AZJ} to
whom the prayer is directed is nearer to him than the object (such as the fire or lamp)
in front of him.

This was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn ‘Amr, from his
father ‘Amr ibn Ibrahim al-Hamdani.
He (al Hamdani) raised the narration, saying that Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him,
said: "There is no harm if a man prays while there is fire, a lamp, or an image in front of
him, indeed, the One {AZJ} to whom he is praying is nearer to him than that which is in
front of him."

Scholar's Note:
This narration is anomalous (shadhdhah), and moreover, it is not musnad (not fully
and reliably transmitted through a continuous chain). Reports of this nature, which
lack full reliability and proper chains of transmission, are not to be preferred over the
many other well-supported and fully transmitted narrations.
text_ar:
رَوَى ذَلِكَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَمْرِو عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَمْرِو بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ الْهَمْدَانِيّ رَفَعَ
الْحَدِيث قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : «لا بَأْسَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ الرَّجُلُ وَ النَّارُ وَ السِّرَاجُ وَ الصُّورَةُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ إِنَّ
الَّذِي يُصَلِّي لَهُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ».
فهذه رواية شاذة ومع هذا ليست مسندة وما يجرى هذا المجرى لا يعدل إليه عن أخبار كثيرة مسندة.
commentary:
This narration is anomalous (shadhdhah), and moreover, it is not musnad (not fully
and reliably transmitted through a continuous chain). Reports of this nature, which
lack full reliability and proper chains of transmission, are not to be preferred over the
many other well-supported and fully transmitted narrations.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-‘Ala’, from
Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him: "Shall I pray while statues (tamathil) are in
front of me and I am looking at them?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No, throw a cloth over them. There is no problem if they are to your
right, or your left, or behind you, or beneath your feet, or above your head. But if they
are in the direction of the Qiblah, then cover them with a cloth and pray."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

يَمِينِكَ أَوْ شِمَالِكَ أَوْ خَلْفِكَ أَوْ تَحْتَ رِجْلِكَ أَوْ فَوْقَ رَأْسِكَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ فِي الْقِبْلَةِ فَأَلْقٍ عَلَيْهَا ثَوْباً وَ صَلّ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from
Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: "I stand for prayer and I see excrement
(al-’adhirah) in front of me in the direction of the Qiblah."
Imam {a.s} said: "Move away from it as much as you can, and do not pray on the main
roads (al-jawadd)."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no harm if a person
prays while wearing a sword in its sheath or a knife in its scabbard in his sleeve, or any
other item of iron, if he needs to safeguard it in that way. And if he prays with an iron
ring on his finger, it will not harm him, Allah {SWT} willing."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ وَ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ
عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحِ عَنِ الْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ أَقُومُ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَأَرَى قُدَّامِي
فِي الْقِبْلَةِ الْعَذِرَةَ فَقَالَ «تَنَحَّ عَنْهَا مَا اِسْتَطَعْتَ وَ لاَ تُصَلِّ عَلَى اَلْجَوَادً».
وقال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا بأس أن يصلي الانسان متقلدا سيفا في غمد أو في كمه سكين في قرابها أو غير ذلك من
بلانا احتاحال احلنهفه ملناصلمة اصمه خاته
با لم بضده ذلك
بالله تمالا
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no harm if a person
prays while wearing a sword in its sheath or a knife in its scabbard in his sleeve, or any
other item of iron, if he needs to safeguard it in that way. And if he prays with an iron
ring on his finger, it will not harm him, Allah {SWT} willing."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from a man, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn Uqbah,
from Musa ibn Ukayl al-Numayri:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "As for iron, it is the adornment of the
people of Hell, and gold is the adornment of the people of Paradise. Allah {SWT} has
made gold in this world the adornment of women, so He {AZJ} prohibited it for men to
wear and to pray while wearing it.
And Allah {SWT} has made iron in this world the adornment of the jinn and the devils, so
He {AZJ} prohibited the Muslim man from wearing it during prayer, except if he is facing
an enemy, in which case there is no harm in it."
He (narrator) said: “I asked Him {a.s}: ‘What about a man while traveling who has with
him a knife in his boot, which he cannot do without, or it is tied in his trousers, or a key,
fearing that if he sets it down, it will be lost, or he wears a belt with iron in it, what
then?"
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in the knife and the belt for the traveler or in times of
necessity. Likewise, there is no harm in the key if he fears loss or forgetting it. And there
is no harm in the sword and every kind of weapon during war. But outside of that, it is
not permissible to pray in anything made of iron, for it is impure (najis) and accursed
(mamsukh)."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
And we have already presented the narration of ‘Ammar al-Sabati, which states that if
the iron is in a sheath or covering, then there is no harm in praying while wearing it.
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ أَكَيْلِ النُمَيْرِيِّ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «فِي الْحَدِيدِ أَنَّهُ جِلْيَةُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ وَ الذَّهَبَ حِلْيَةُ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ وَ جَعَلَ اللهُ الذَّهَبَ
فِي الدُّنْيَا زِينَةَ النَّسَاءِ فَحَرَّمَ عَلَى ٱلرِّجَالِ لُبْسَهُ وَ الصَّلاَةَ فِيهِ وَ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الْحَدِيدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا زِينَةَ الْجِنَّ وَ
اَلشَّيَاطِينِ فَحَرَّمَ عَلَى الرَّجُلِ الْمُسْلِمِ أَنْ يَلْبَسَهُ فِي الصَّلَاَةِ إِلَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ قِبَالَ عَدُوٍّ فَلا بَأْسَ بِهِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ
فَالرَّجُلُ فِي السِّفَرِ يَكُونُ مَعَهُ السِّكِّينُ فِي خَفِّهِ لا يَسْتَغْنِي عَنْهُ أَوْ فِي سَرَاوِيلِهِ مَشدُوداً وَ ٱلْمِفْتَاحُ يَخْشَى إِنْ
وَضَعَهُ ضَاعَ أَوْ يَكُونُ فِي وَسَطِهِ ٱلْمِنْطَقَةُ مِنْ حَدِيدِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِالسِّكَّينِ وَ الْمِنْطَقَةِ لِلْمُسَافِرِ أَوْ فِي وَقْتِ
ضَرُورَةٍ وَ كَذَلِكَ الْمِفْتَاحُ إِذَا خَافَ الضَّيْعَةَ وَ النَّسْيَانَ وَ لا بَأْسَ بِالسَّيْفِ وَ كُلِّ آلَةِ السِّلَاَحِ فِي الْحَرْبِ وَ فِي غَيْرٍ
ذَلِكَ لاَ يَجُوزُ الصَّلاَةُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْحَدِيدِ فَإِنَّهُ نَجَسٌ مَمْسُوخٌ».
وقد قدمنا رواية عمار الساباطي ان الحديد متى كان في غلاف فانه لا بأس بالصلاة فيه
commentary:
And we have already presented the narration of ‘Ammar al-Sabati, which states that if
the iron is in a sheath or covering, then there is no harm in praying while wearing it.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, said:
"A man should not pray while there is an iron ring on his hand."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
facing any of the graves unless there is a barrier between the person and the grave."
text_ar:
عَلِي عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ النَّوْفَلِيّ عَنِ السَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ
: «لا يُصَلِّي الرَجُلُ وَ فِي يَدِهِ خَاتَمُ حَدِيدٍ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا تجوز الصلاة الى شئ من القبور حتى يكون بين الانسان وبينه حايل).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
facing any of the graves unless there is a barrier between the person and the grave."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad
ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prays among the graves.
Imam {a.s} said: "That is not permissible unless he places between himself and the
graves, when he prays, a distance of ten cubits in front of him, ten cubits behind him,
ten cubits to his right, and ten cubits to his left. Then he may pray if he wishes."
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ
سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدَّقٍ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَارِ السَابَاطِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي بَيْنَ
الْقُبُورِ قَالَ «لَا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ الْقُبُورِ إِذَا صَلَّى عَشَرَةَ أَذْرُعِ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَ عَشَرَةَ أَذْرُعِ مِنْ
خَلْفِهِ وَ عَشَرَةَ أَذْرُعِ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ عَشَرَةَ أَذْرُعِ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي إنْ شَاءَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakim, from Mu‘ammar ibn Khallad:
(Imam) al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no harm in praying among the
graves as long as one does not take the grave as a Qiblah."

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It has been narrated that
there is no harm in praying toward a (direction of) Qiblah in which there is the grave of
an Imam {a.s}. However, the foundational principle is what we have previously
mentioned."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمِ عَنْ مُعَمَّرِ بْنِ خَلاَّدٍ عَنِ آلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاةِ
بَيْنَ الْمَقَابِرِ مَا لَمْ يَتَّخِذِ الْقَبْرَ قِبْلَةَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (وقد رُوى: أَنَّهُ لا بَاأسَ بالصَلاَةِ إلَى قِبْلَةِ فِيهَا قَبْدُ إمَامِ والاصل ما قدمناه).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It has been narrated that
there is no harm in praying toward a (direction of) Qiblah in which there is the grave of
an Imam {a.s}. However, the foundational principle is what we have previously
mentioned."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Himyari narrated
to us, saying:
I (al-Himyari) wrote to the Jurist (peace be upon him), asking him about a man who
visits the graves of the Imams, peace be upon them;
‘Is it permissible for him to prostrate upon the grave or not?
And is it permissible for someone who prays near their graves to stand behind the
grave and make the grave his Qiblah? And to stand by its head or feet?
And is it permissible to stand in front of the grave and pray with the grave behind him,
or not?
So He (the Jurist {a.s}), peace be upon him, replied and I read the tawqi’ (written
response), and from it I (al-Himyari) copied;
"As for prostration on the grave, it is not permissible in an obligatory or supererogatory
prayer, nor during a visitation. Rather, he should place his right cheek on the grave (of
Imam {a.s}).
As for prayer, it should be behind the grave, making it (the grave of Imam {a.s}) as his
Imam (leader of prayer), and it is not permissible to pray in front of it, because the
Imam (of prayer) is not preceded. He may pray to its right or left."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible for a man
to pray while wearing a turban (‘imamah) or a veil (litham) such that his forehead is
covered; he must uncover the spot of prostration on his forehead and uncover his
mouth for recitation of the Qur'an.”
As for uncovering the forehead, we have already explained earlier that it is necessary,
and it is further clarified by what was narrated:
text_ar:
رَوَى مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْحِمْيَرِيّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى ٱلْفَقِيهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ
أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَزُورُ قُبُورَ الأَئِمَّةِ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَاَمُ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ عَلَى الْقَبْرِ أَمْ لا وَ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لِمَنْ صَلَّى
عِنْدَ قُبُورِهِمْ أَنْ يَقُومَ وَرَاءَ الْقَبْرِ وَ يَجْعَلَ ٱلْقَبْرَ قِبْلَةً وَ يَقُومَ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ وَ رِجْلَيْهِ وَ هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ الْقَبْرَ وَ
يُصَلِّيَ وَ يَجْعَلَهُ خَلْفَهُ أَمْ لا فَأَجَابَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ وَ قَرَأْتُ التّوْقِيعَ وَ مِنْهُ نَسَحْتُ «أَمَّا السُّجُودُ عَلَى ٱلْقَبْرِ فَلاَ يَجُوزُ
فِي نَافِلَةٍ وَلَا فَرِيضَةٍ وَ لا زِيَارَةِ بَلْ يَضَعُ خَدَّهُ الْأَيْمَنَ عَلَى الْقَبْرِ وَ أَمَّا الصَّلاَةُ فَإِنَّهَا خَلْفَهُ يَجْعَلُهُ الْأَمَامَ وَ لا يَجُوزُ
أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ لأَنَّ الإِمَامَ لا يُتَقَدَّمُ وَ يُصَلِّي عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ شِمَالِهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا يجوز للرجل أن يصلي وعليه عمامة أو لثام حتى يكشف عن جبهته موضع السجود ويكشف
عن فيه لقراءة القرآن). اما كشف الجبهة فقد بيناه فيما تقدم أنه لا بد منه ويزيده بيانا ما رواه:
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible for a man
to pray while wearing a turban (‘imamah) or a veil (litham) such that his forehead is
covered; he must uncover the spot of prostration on his forehead and uncover his
mouth for recitation of the Qur'an.”
As for uncovering the forehead, we have already explained earlier that it is necessary,
and it is further clarified by what was narrated:

text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud, from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Himyari narrated
to us, saying:
I (al-Himyari) wrote to the Jurist (peace be upon him), asking him about a man who
visits the graves of the Imams, peace be upon them;
‘Is it permissible for him to prostrate upon the grave or not?
And is it permissible for someone who prays near their graves to stand behind the
grave and make the grave his Qiblah? And to stand by its head or feet?
And is it permissible to stand in front of the grave and pray with the grave behind him,
or not?
So He (the Jurist {a.s}), peace be upon him, replied and I read the tawqi’ (written
response), and from it I (al-Himyari) copied;
"As for prostration on the grave, it is not permissible in an obligatory or supererogatory
prayer, nor during a visitation. Rather, he should place his right cheek on the grave (of
Imam {a.s}).
As for prayer, it should be behind the grave, making it (the grave of Imam {a.s}) as his
Imam (leader of prayer), and it is not permissible to pray in front of it, because the
Imam (of prayer) is not preceded. He may pray to its right or left."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible for a man
to pray while wearing a turban (‘imamah) or a veil (litham) such that his forehead is
covered; he must uncover the spot of prostration on his forehead and uncover his
mouth for recitation of the Qur'an.”
As for uncovering the forehead, we have already explained earlier that it is necessary,
and it is further clarified by what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad,
from Ali ibn al-Nu’man, from the one who narrated it:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who prays while gesturing on his mount
(dabbah) while wearing a turban.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must uncover the spot of prostration."

Scholar's Note:
As for the litham (veil covering the mouth), that it is not permissible is indicated by
what was narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ عَمَّنْ رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السِّلاَمُ : فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ يُومِئُ عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ مُتَعَمَّماً قَالَ «يَكْشِفُ مَوْضِعَ السُجُودِ».
فأما اللثام فالذي يدل على أنه لا يجوز ما رواه:
commentary:
As for the litham (veil covering the mouth), that it is not permissible is indicated by
what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from
Rib‘i from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “Can a man pray while he is veiled (covering his face with a cloth)?”
Imam {a.s} said: “As for on the ground, then no; but as for on a riding animal, then there
is no harm.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ
مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسِّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتْ لَهُ أَيُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ مُتَلَثُمْ فَقَالَ «أَمًا عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَلا وَ أَمَّا عَلَى
اَلدَّابَّةِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ».

text_en:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who prays and recites the Qur’an while he is
veiled (covering his face with a cloth).
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm.”
text_ar:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثُمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجْلِ
يُصَلِّي وَ يَقْرَأْ الْقُرْآنَ وَ هُوَ مُتَلَتَّمْ فَقَالَ »لا بَأْسَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Sa‘d ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja‘far from Abu Abdillah from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-
Hasan ibn Ali from someone he mentioned among our companions from one of the two (Imams {a.s}):
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm if a man recites (the Qur’an) in prayer while his
garment is over his mouth.”

Scholar's Note:
For the intended meaning of these two reports is that if the veil (covering the mouth)
does not prevent the Qur’an from being heard, then there is no harm in it. But whenever
it prevents it from being heard, then it is not permissible, as we have already stated.
And what indicates this is:
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنِ ٱلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ
عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يَقْرَأَ الرَّجُلُ فِي الصَّلاةِ وَ ثَوْبُهُ عَلَى
فيهِ».
فان المراد بهذين الخبرين هو أنه إذا لم يمنع اللثام من سماع القرآن فانه لا بأس به فأما مهما منع من سماعه فانه لا يجوز
ذلك حسب ما قدمناه ، والذي يدل على ذلك :

For the intended meaning of these two reports is that if the veil (covering the mouth)
does not prevent the Qur’an from being heard, then there is no harm in it. But whenever
it prevents it from being heard, then it is not permissible, as we have already stated.
And what indicates this is:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
Narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Al-Halabi:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “Can a man recite in his prayer while his garment is over his
mouth?”
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in that if he can hear the murmuring (of his own
recitation).”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is disliked for a woman to
pray while wearing a niqab, when she is able and has the choice (in a state of ability
and without compulsion)."
text_ar:
ما رواه سعد عن أحمد بن محمد عن الحسن بن محبوب عن علي بن رئاب عن الحلبي قال سألت أبا عبد اللّٰه
عليه السلام : هل يقرأ الرجل في صلاته وثوبه على فيه؟ فقال : لا بأس بذلك إذا سمع الهمهمة.
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ويكره للمرأة أن تصلي وعليها نقاب مع التمكن والاختيار).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is disliked for a woman to
pray while wearing a niqab, when she is able and has the choice (in a state of ability
and without compulsion)."
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prays and recites the Qur’an while he is veiled
(covering his face).
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in it, but if he uncovers his mouth, that is better.”
He (Sama’ah) said: “And I asked Him {a.s} about a woman who prays while wearing a
niqab”.
Imam {a.s} said: “If she uncovers the place of prostration, then there is no harm in it, and
if she unveils (her face), that is better.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible for a man
to pray while a woman is praying beside him or in the same row. And whenever he
prays while she is aligned with him in his row, both of their prayers are invalid. It is
appropriate that if her prayer coincides with his in the same room or similar setting,
she should pray in such a way that her place of prostration is aligned with his feet at
the time of his prostration. And likewise, if she prays following his prayer, her position
should be as we have described."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فَيَثلُو الْقُرْآنَ وَ هُوَ مُتَلَتَّمْ فَقَالَ
«لا بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ كَشَفَ عَنْ فِيهِ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمَرْأَةِ تُصَلِّي مُتَنَقَبَةً قَالَ «إِذَا كَشَفَتْ عَنْ مَوْضِعٍ
السُّجُودٍ فَلاً بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ أَسْفَرَتْ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولا يجوز للرجل أن يصلي وامرأة تصلي الى جانبه أو في صف واحد، ومتى صلى وهي مسامتة
اله في صفه بطلت صلاتهما ، وينبغي إذا اتفق صلاتها في حال صلاته في بيت واحد ونحوه أن تصلي بحيث يكون سجودها
تجاه قدميه في سجوده، وكذلك إن صلت بصلاته كانت حالها ما وصفناه).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible for a man
to pray while a woman is praying beside him or in the same row. And whenever he
prays while she is aligned with him in his row, both of their prayers are invalid. It is
appropriate that if her prayer coincides with his in the same room or similar setting,
she should pray in such a way that her place of prostration is aligned with his feet at
the time of his prostration. And likewise, if she prays following his prayer, her position
should be as we have described."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams {a.s}),
peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prays in one corner of the room and his wife or
daughter prays beside him in the other corner.
Imam {a.s} said: “That is not appropriate. But if there is a span (shibr) of distance
between them, it is sufficient” (meaning if the man is ahead of the woman by a span).
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ الْعَلَاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ
يُصَلِّي فِي زَاوِيَةِ الْحُجْرَةِ وَ اِمْرَأَتُهُ أَو اِبْنَتُهُ تُصَلِّي بِجِذَاهُ فِي الزَّاوِيَةِ الْأُخْرَى قَالَ «لا يَنْبَغِي ذَلِكَ فَإِنْ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا
شِبْرّ أَجْرَأَهُ يَغْنِي إذَا كَانَ الرَّجَلُ مُتَقَدَّماً لِلمَرْأَةِ بِشِبْرِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.230 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.398 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.123
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams {a.s}),
peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prays in one corner of the room and his wife or
daughter prays beside him in the other corner.
Imam {a.s} said: “That is not appropriate. But if there is a span (shibr) of distance
between them, it is sufficient” (meaning if the man is ahead of the woman by a span).

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal from Ibn Muskan from Abu
Basir, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man and a woman who pray in the same house, with the
woman at the man's right side, aligned with him.
Imam {a.s} said: “No, unless there is between them a span (shibr) or an arm’s length
(dhira‘).”
Then Imam {a.s} said: “The length of the mount of the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah
{SWT} bless him and his family, was an arm’s length, and He {saws} used to place it in front
of him when He {saws} prayed to screen himself from those who might pass in front of
him.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَعَتُهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ ٱلصَّيْقَلِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ
وَ الْمَرْأَةٍ يُصَلّيَانِ فِي بَيْتِ وَاجِدِ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ عَنْ يَمِينِ الرَّجْلِ بِجِذَاهُ قَالَ «لا إلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُمَا شِبْرٌ أَوْ ذِرَاعٌ» ثُمَّ قَالَ
«كَانَ طُولُ رَحْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ذِرَاعاً فَكَانَ يَضَعُهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ إِذَا صَلَّى لِيَسْتُرَهُ مِمَّنْ يَمُرُّ بَيْنَ
يَدَيْهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.230 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.398 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.124
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Safwan and Fadalah from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad from one of the two (Imams {a.s}),
peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a woman who shares a howdah (a carriage on a riding animal)
with a man, and they both pray together.
Imam {a.s} said: “No, rather the man should pray, and when he finishes, the woman
should pray.”
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسَلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمَرْأَةِ تُزَامِلُ الرَّجُلَ
فِي الْمَحْمِلٍ يُصَلِّيَانٍ جَمِيعا فَقَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ يُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ فَإِذَا فَرَغَ صَلَّتِ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ».

text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s},

woman at the man's right side, aligned with him.

(dhira‘), or something like that.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أبِي عَبْدِ اللْهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنِ
الرَّجُلٍ وَ الْمَرْأَةِ يُصَلَّيَانِ جَمِيعاً فِي بَيْتِ الْمَرْأَةُ عَنْ يَمِينِ الرَّجُلِ بِجِذَاهُ قَالَ «لا حَتَّى يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُمَا شِبْرٌ أَوْ ذِرَاعْ
أَوْ نَحوُهُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Sa‘d from Sindi ibn Muhammad Al-Bazzaz from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “I pray and a woman is beside me, and she is also praying.”
Imam {a.s} said: “No, unless she moves forward or you do. But there is no harm if she is
beside you while sitting or standing (and not praying).”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
سَعَدٌ عَنْ سِنْدِيّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْبَزَّازِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَغْفُورِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَامُ أُصَلِّي وَ الْمَرْأَةُ إِلَى جَنْبِي وَ هِي تُصَلِّي فَقَالَ «لا إِلَّ أَنْ تَتَقَدَّمَ هِي أَوْ أَنْتَ وَ لا بَأْسَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ وَ هِيَ
بِجِذَاكَ جَالِسَةٌ أَوْ قَائِمَةٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.231 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.477 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.124
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Idris
ibn Abdullah Al-Qummi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who is praying while directly in line with him is a
woman standing, in a state of janabah, on her bed.
Imam {a.s} said: “If she is sitting, she does not harm you; but if she is praying, then no (it
is not permissible).”
text_ar:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ إِذْرِيسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ الْقُمَّيَّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ
أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ بِحِيَالِهِ اِمْرَأَةُ قَائِمَةٌ جُنُبٌ عَلَى فِرَاشِهَا فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَتْ قَاعِدَةً فَلاَ
تَضُرُّكَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ تُصَلِّي فَلاَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.298 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.231 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.475 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.121
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id Al-
Mada’ini from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar Al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} was asked about a man who is able to pray while in front of him a
woman is also praying.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should not pray until he places between himself and her more than
ten arm-lengths (adhru‘). And if she is on his right or on his left, he should place the
same distance between himself and her. But if she is praying behind him, then there
is no harm, even if she touches his garment. And if the woman is sitting, or sleeping,
or standing without praying, then there is no harm wherever she may be.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدِ الْمَدَائِنِيَّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ
صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ السَّابَاطِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : أَنَّهُ سُيْلَ عَنِ الرَجْلِ يَسْتَقِيمُ لَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
اِمْرَأَةٌ تُصَلِّي قَالَ «لا يُصَلِّي حَتَّى يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ عَشَرَةِ أَذْرُعِ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ
جَعَلَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَهَا مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ تُصَلِّي خَلْفَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ تُصِيبُ ثَوْبَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ قَاعِدَةً أَوْ
نَائِمَةً أَوْ قَائِمَةً فِي غَيْرٍ صَلاَةٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ حَيْثُ كَانَتْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.231 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.399 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.477 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.128

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from someone who
informed him from Jamil ibn Darraj:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who is praying and a woman is praying
beside him.
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm.”

Scholar's Note:
It is possible that He {a.s}, peace be upon him, meant this in the case where there is
more than ten arm-lengths between the man and the woman, as mentioned by
‘Ammar Al-Sabati in his earlier narration, or that she is behind him. And it is also
possible that what is meant is if there is a barrier between him and her, as has been
mentioned in many narrations in which a man places a covering or screen between
himself and the woman.
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي
عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ الْمَرْأَةُ تُصَلِّي بِحِذَاهُ قَالَ « لا بَأْسَ».
فيحتمل أن يكون أراد عليه السلام إذا كان الرجل بينه وبين المرأة أكثر من عشرة اذرع حسب ما ذكره عمار الساباطي في
روايته المتقدمة أو تكون من ورائه، ويحتمل أن يكون المراد به إذا كان بينه وبينها حايل حسب ما ذكرناه في أخبار كثيرة
في أنه يجعل الرجل ساترا بينه وبينها.
commentary:
It is possible that He {a.s}, peace be upon him, meant this in the case where there is
more than ten arm-lengths between the man and the woman, as mentioned by
‘Ammar Al-Sabati in his earlier narration, or that she is behind him. And it is also
possible that what is meant is if there is a barrier between him and her, as has been
mentioned in many narrations in which a man places a covering or screen between
himself and the woman.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.232
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
Al-‘Ayyashi from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, who said: Al-‘Amraki narrated to me from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his
brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about an Imam (of prayer) who was leading the noon prayer, and his
wife stood beside him and prayed with him, thinking it was the afternoon (‘Asr) prayer.
Does that invalidate the prayer of the congregation?
And what is the ruling of the woman’s prayer with them, considering she had already
prayed the noon prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: “That does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman
must repeat her prayer.”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible for
anyone to pray while wearing a tightly fastened cloak (qaba’) unless he is in a state of
war and unable to loosen it, then it is permitted due to necessity."
This was mentioned by Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, and we heard it from the
scholars in discussion, though I have not come across any supported narration on it.
The Shaykh, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him also said: "It is not appropriate for a man
who has hair to pray while it is tied up; rather, he should untie it before praying.
However, this has been permitted for women."
text_ar:
الْعَيَّاشِي عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي الْعَمْرَكِيْ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَجِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ إِمَامِ كَانَ فِي الظُّهْرِ فَقَامَتِ اِمْرَأَتُهُ بِحِيَالِهِ تُصَلِّي مَعَهُ وَ هِيَ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّهَا الْعَصْرُ هَلْ يُفْسِدُ ذَلِكَ
عَلَى الْقَوْمِ وَ مَا حَالُ الْمَرْأَةِ فِي صَلاَتِهَا مَعَهُمْ وَ قَدْ كَانَتْ صَلَّتِ الظُّهْرَ فَقَالَ «لا يُفْسِدُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ وَ تُعِيدُ
الْمَرْأَةُ صَلاَتَهَا».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا يجوز لاحد أن يصلي وعليه قباء مشدود إلا أن يكون في الحرب فلا يتمكن من أن يحله فيجوز
ذلك للاضطرار). ذكر ذلك علي بن الحسين بن بابويه وسمعناها من الشيوخ مذاكرة ولم أعرف به خبرا مسندا. قال الشيخ
رحمه اللّه : (ولا ينبغي للرجل إذا كان له شعر أن يصلي وهو معقوص حتى يحله وقد رخص ذلك للنساء).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible for
anyone to pray while wearing a tightly fastened cloak (qaba’) unless he is in a state of
war and unable to loosen it, then it is permitted due to necessity."
This was mentioned by Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, and we heard it from the
scholars in discussion, though I have not come across any supported narration on it.
The Shaykh, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him also said: "It is not appropriate for a man
who has hair to pray while it is tied up; rather, he should untie it before praying.
However, this has been permitted for women."

Al-‘Ayyashi from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, who said: Al-‘Amraki narrated to me from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his
brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about an Imam (of prayer) who was leading the noon prayer, and his
wife stood beside him and prayed with him, thinking it was the afternoon (‘Asr) prayer.
Does that invalidate the prayer of the congregation?
And what is the ruling of the woman’s prayer with them, considering she had already
prayed the noon prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: “That does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman
must repeat her prayer.” Scholar's Note:

Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il, who said:

text_ar: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ: رَأَيْتُهُ يُصَلِّي فِي نَعْلَيْهِ لَمْ يَخْلَعْهُمَا وَ أَحْسَبُهُ قَالَ «رَكْعَتَيِ الطَّوَافِ».

And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar, who said:

لَمْ أَرَهُ يَنْزِعُهُمَا قَطْ.

Sa‘d from Abu Ja‘far from his father from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah, who said:
“When you pray, then pray in your sandals if they are pure, for that is from the Sunnah.”

سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ آللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ: «إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فَصَلَ فِي نَعْلَيْكَ إِذَا كَانَتْ طَاهِرَةً فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ
مِنَ السُّنَّةٍ».

And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
I saw Abu Ja‘far {a.s} pray when the sun had passed its zenith on the Day of Tarwiyah, six
units of prayer behind the Maqam, and He {a.s} had his sandals on; He {a.s} did not remove
them.
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ صَلَّى حِينَ
زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ خَلْفَ ٱَلْمَقَامِ وَ عَلَيْهِ نَعْلاَهُ لَمْ يَنْزِعْهُمَا.

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-‘Abbas from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Aban from Abd Al-
Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you pray, then pray in your sandals if they are pure, for it
is said that this is from the Sunnah.”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "A person may pray in khuff
(leather socks) and jarmuq (overshoes) if they have a shaft (they cover the lower leg)."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فَصَلِّ فِي نَعْلَيْكَ إِذَا كَانَتْ طَاهِرَةً فَإِنَّهُ يُقَالُ ذَلِكَ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ويصلي في الخف والجرموق إذا كان له ساق).
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "A person may pray in khuff
(leather socks) and jarmuq (overshoes) if they have a shaft (they cover the lower leg)."

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the leather socks (khifaf) that are sold in the market.
Imam {a.s} said: “Buy them and pray in them unless you come to know that it is (from) a
dead animal with certainty.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ عَنِ
الْخِفَافٍ الَّتِي تُبَاعُ فِي السُّوقِ فَقَالَ «اِشتَرِ وَ صَلِّ فِيهَا حَتَّى تَعْلَمَ أَنَّهُ مَيَّتْ بِعَيْنِهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.234 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.418 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.490 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.427

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Sahl from some of his companions from Al-Hasan Al-Jahm, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I pass through the market
and buy leather socks (khuff), and I do not know whether they are from a ritually
slaughtered animal (dhaki) or not.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Pray in them.”
I asked: “And what about sandals?”
Imam {a.s} said: “The same applies.”
I said: “This makes me uneasy.” (concerning the purity of the leather)
Imam {a.s} said: “Do you turn away from us? Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him used
to do that.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ سَهْلٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ ٱلْجَهْمِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
أَعْتَرِضُ السُّوقَ فَأَشتَرِي خُفّا لا أَدْرِي أَذَكِيٌّ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ قَالَ «صَلِّ فِيهِ» قُلْتُ وَ النَّعْلُ قَالَ «مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ» قُلْتُ إِنَّي
أَضِيقُ مِنْ هَذَا قَالَ «أَ تَرْغَبُ عَنَّا كَانَ أُبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَفْعَلُهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.404 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.234 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.419 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.493

text_en:
Sa‘d from Abu Ja‘far from Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Aban from Isma‘il ibn Al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about wearing leather garments, leather socks (khiffaf), and
sandals, and praying in them if they are not from the land of the Muslims.
Imam {a.s} said: “As for the sandals and the leather socks, there is no harm in them.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةً عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ عَنْ لِبَاسِ الْجُلُودِ وَ الْخِفَافِ وَ النَّعَالِ وَ الصَّلَاَةِ فِيهَا إِذَا لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنْ أَرْضِ الْمُصَلِّينَ فَقَالَ «أَمَّا النَّعَالُ وَ
اَلْخِفَافُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.234 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.418 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.427

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, who said:
I asked him about praying in a jurmuq (a type of overshoe), and I brought him a jurmuq
which I sent to him.
He said: “It is permissible to pray in it.”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "A shirt (qamis) is sufficient
for a man in prayer if it is thick (non-transparent), and a woman must wear a gown (dir‘)
and a head covering (khimar) in prayer."
The explanation of this has already been fully discussed previously, so there is no need
to repeat it, Allah {SWT} willing.
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي جُرْمُوقٍ وَ أَتَّيْتُهُ بِجُرْمُوقٍ بَعَثِتُ بِهِ
إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ «يُصَلَّى فِيهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ويكفي الرجل في الصلاة قميص إذا كان صفيقا ولا بد للمرأة من درع وخمار في الصلاة) فقد مضى
شح ذلك فرما مض مستوف فا محه لاعلاتهاشا الله تمال
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "A shirt (qamis) is sufficient
for a man in prayer if it is thick (non-transparent), and a woman must wear a gown (dir‘)
and a head covering (khimar) in prayer."
The explanation of this has already been fully discussed previously, so there is no need
to repeat it, Allah {SWT} willing.

except what is eaten or worn.”

text_en:
And Hisham ibn Al-Hakam said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “Inform me about what is
permissible to prostrate upon and what is not permissible.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Prostration is not permissible except upon the earth or that which the
earth grows, except what is eaten or worn.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَقَالَ هِشَامُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ - لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ : أَخْبِرْنِي عَمَّا يَجُوزُ السُجُودُ عَلَيْهِ وَ عَمَّا لاَ يَجُوزُ قَالَ
«السُجُودُ لا يَجُوزُ إِلاَّ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ أَوْ عَلَى مَا أَنْبَتَتِ الْأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا أُكِلَ أَوْ لُبِسَ».

“Prostration upon the earth is an obligation, and upon other than the earth is a

chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
And it was narrated from Yasir, the servant, that he said:
Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, passed by me while I was praying on a piece of
tabari (a type of mat or plant material), and I had placed something over it.
Imam {a.s} said: “Why do you not prostrate upon it? Is it not from vegetation of earth?”

Scholar's Note:
And Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Babawayh said in his Risalah: “Prostrate upon the earth or
upon what the earth produces, and do not prostrate upon the mats of Madinah,
because their bindings are made of leather.”
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ يَاسِرِ ٱلْخَادِمِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: مَرّ بِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ وَ أَنَا أُصَلِّي عَلَى الطَّبَرِيِّ وَ قَدْ أَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْهِ شَيْئاً
فَقَالَ «مَا لَكَ لا تَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ أَلَيْسَ هُوَ مِنْ نَبَاتِ ٱلْأَرْضِ».
وقال علي بن الحسين بن بابويه في رسالته اسجد على الارض أو على ما أنبتت الارض ولا تسجد على الحصر المدنية لان
سيورها من جلد

upon what the earth produces, and do not prostrate upon the mats of Madinah,
because their bindings are made of leather.”

text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub asked Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, about gypsum (jiss)
that had been fired using excrement and the bones of the dead, and then the mosque
was plastered with it, whether it is permissible to prostrate upon it.
So Imam {a.s} wrote to him in His {a.s} own handwriting:
“Indeed, water and fire have purified it.”
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
text_ar:
وَسَأَلَ الْحَسَنْ بْنُ مَحْبُوبِ - أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلامُ: عَنِ الْجِصِّ يُوقَدُ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَذِرَةِ وَ عِظَامِ ٱلْمَوْتَى ثُمَّ يُجَصَّصُ
بِهِ الْمَسْجِدُ أَيُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهِ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ بِخَطَّهِ «أَنَّ الْمَاءَ وَ النَّارَ قَدْ طَهَّرَاهُ».

Dawud ibn Yazid asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s} (the Third), peace be upon him,
about paper (qaratis) and parchment (kawaghidh) that have writing on them, whether
it is permissible to prostrate upon them.
So He {a.s} wrote: “It is permissible.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
text_en:
Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s} (the First), peace be upon him, about
a man who prostrates on a covering (mishh) or a carpet (bisat).
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in it if it is in a situation of taqiyyah (precautionary
dissimulation), and there is no harm in prostrating on clothes in a situation of
taqiyyah.”
text_ar:
وَسَأَلَ عَلِيْ بْنُ يَقْطِينٍ - أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ : عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلٍ يَسْجُدُ عَلَى ٱلْمِسْحِ وَ الْبِسَاطِ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ
إِذَا كَانَ فِي حَالِ التَّقِيَّةِ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ بِالسُّجُودِ عَلَى الثَّيَابِ فِي حَالِ التَّقِيَّةِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi

text_en:
And it was narrated from one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them, who said:
I said: "A man prostrates while wearing a cap or a turban?"
He said: “If something from his forehead touches the ground, between his eyebrows
and the beginning of his hairline, then it is sufficient for him."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah from Mu‘awiyah
ibn Wahb:
He asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the best thing by which the servants may draw near
to their Lord {AZJ}.
Imam {a.s} said: “I do not know anything, after recognition (of Allah {AZJ}), better than
prayer.”

text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd from Abdullah ibn
Yahya Al-Kahili from his father, who said:
The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
“Satan remains fearful of the believer and in awe of him as long as he maintains the
five daily prayers. But when he neglects them, Satan becomes bold against him.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ رَيْدِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى الْكَاهِلِيّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ
اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «لَا يَزَالُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذَعِراً مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمُوُمِنِ هَائِباً لَهُ مَا حَافَظَ عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسِ فَإِذَا
ضَيَّعَهُنَّ اِجْتَرَاَ عَلَيْهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MERIT OF PRAYER, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED FROM IT
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “A man came to the Messenger of Allah {SWT},
may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, and said:
“Pray to Allah {SWT} for me that He {AZJ} admits me into Paradise.”
He {saws} said: “Help me by increasing your prostration.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «أَتَّى
رَسُولَ اللّهِ صَلّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ رَجُلْ فَقَالَ أَدْعُ ٱللَّهَ لِي أَنْ يُدْجِلَنِي الْجَنَّةَ فَقَالَ «أَعِنَي بِكَثرَةِ السُّجُودِ» ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MERIT OF PRAYER, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED FROM IT
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Sinan from Isma‘il
ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “One obligatory prayer is better than twenty pilgrimages, and
one pilgrimage is better than a house filled with gold that is given away in charity until
nothing remains of it.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلاَةٌ فَرِيضَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ عِشَرِينَ حَجَّةً وَ حَجَّةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ بَيْتٍ مَمْلُوِّ مِنْ ذَهَبِ
بُتَصَدَّقُ مِنْهُ حَتَّى يَفْنَى».

text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Sinan from Isma‘il
ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “One obligatory prayer is better than twenty pilgrimages, and
one pilgrimage is better than a house filled with gold that is given away in charity until
nothing remains of it.”

text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurarah from Isa ibn
Abdullah Al-Hashimi from his father from his grandfather:
(Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
“The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
‘Indeed, the pillar of the religion is prayer, and it is the first thing from the deeds of the
son of Adam that will be looked into. If it is sound, the rest of his deeds will be
examined, and if it is not sound, none of his other deeds will be looked at.’”
text_ar:
وَعَنَهُ عَنْ مُحَمّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ الْهَاشِمِيّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ
عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «إِنَّ عَمُودَ آَلدِّينِ الصَّلاَةُ وَ هِيَ أَوْلُ مَا يُنْظَرُ فِيهِ
مِنْ عَمَلٍ اِبْنِ آدَمَ فَإِنْ صَحْتْ نُظِرَ فِي عَمَلِهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَصِحَ لَمْ يُنْظَرْ فِي بَقِيَّةِ عَمَلِهِ».

(Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:

text_ar:
وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «اِنْتِظَارُ الصَّلاَةِ بَعْدَ الصَّلاَةِ كَنْزُ
مِنْ كَنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ ».
