A man asked (Imam {a.s}) while I was present, and he said: "Sometimes I enter the
mosque and some of our companions are praying Asr while others are praying Dhuhr."
Imam {a.s} said: "I am the one who ordered them to do this. If they were to pray at the
same time, they would be recognized and seized by their necks."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
As for what Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "(Archangel) Jibrail, peace be upon him,
came to the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, with the
timings of the prayer.
He (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when the sun had passed the meridian and (conveyed
the) order (to) him, so He {saws} prayed Dhuhr.
Then he (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when the shadow had increased by the length of a
span and ordered him, so he prayed Asr. Then he came to him when the sun had set
and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He {saws} prayed Maghrib.
Then he (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when the twilight had disappeared and (conveyed
the) order (to) him, so He {saws} prayed Isha.
Then he (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when the dawn had risen and (conveyed the) order
(to) him, so He {saws} prayed Subh.
Then he {Jibrail) came to Him {saws} on the next day when the shadow had increased by
the length of a span and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He {saws} prayed Dhuhr.
Then he {Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when the shadow had increased by the length of two
spans and (conveyed the) order (to) him, so He {saws} prayed Asr.
Then he (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when the sun had set and (conveyed the) order (to)
him, so He {saws} prayed Maghrib.
Then he (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when a third of the night had passed and (conveyed
the) order (to) him, so He {saws} prayed Isha.
Then he (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} when the light of dawn had spread and (conveyed
the) order (to) him, so He {saws} prayed Subh."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "What is between these two times is (considered) time (for the
prayer)."
text_ar:
فَأَمًّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
«أَنَى جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِمَوَاقِيتِ الصَّلاةِ فَأَتَاهُ حِينَ زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَأَمَرَهُ
فَصَلَّى الظُّهرَ ثُمَّ أَنَاهُ حِينَ زَادَ الظَّلُ قَامَةً فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى ٱلْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى ٱلْمَغْرِبَ
ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ جِينَ سَقَطَ الشَّفَقُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى الْعِشَاءَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ حِينَ طَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى الصُّبْحَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ مِنَ الْغَدِ
جينَ زَادَ فِي الظَّلِّ قَامَةً فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَى الظُهْرَ ثُمْ أَتَاهُ جِينَ زَادَ فِي الظَّلِّ قَامَتَانٍ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلّى الْعَصْرَ ثُمّ أَتَاهُ جِينَ
غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى الْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ جِينَ ذَهَبَ ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلّى ٱلْعِشَاءَ ثُمَّ أَتَاهُ جِينَ نَوْرَ الصُّبْحُ
فَأَمَرَهُ فَصَلَّى الصُّبْحَ» ثُمَّ قَالَ «مَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَقْتٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir, from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
"Jibrail, peace be upon him, came", and he mentioned the narration similar to that of
Abu Khadijah, except that instead of saying "one span and two spans (qamah and
qamatayn)," he said "one forearm length and two forearm lengths (dhiraʿ and
dhira’ayn)."
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي بَشِيرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «أَتَّى جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ » وَ ذَكَرَ مِثْلَ حَدِيثِ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ إِلاَّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ بَدَلَ ٱلْقَامَةِ وَ ٱلْقَامَتَيْنِ «ذِرَاعِ وَ ذِرَاعَيْنِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Ribaat from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, descended
upon the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family,"
And he continued the narration similar to the first one, and he mentioned in place of
"one span and two spans" (qamah wa qamatayn), "two feet and four feet" (qadamayn
wa arbaʿat aqdam).

Scholar's Note:
So no one has the right to say: ‘These narrations indicate that the beginning of the time
and its end are the same’.
This is because he said: "Between them is the time," for it is not impossible that what
is between the two times is made a time, even though the beginning is better than it.
What indicates this is what has been narrated:
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ رِبَاطِ عَنْ مُفَضَّلِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : «نَزَلَ جَبْرَئِيلُ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ » وَ سَاقَ الْحَدِيثَ مِثْلَ الْأَوَّلِ وَ ذَكَرَ بَدَلَ الْقَامَةِ وَ الْقَامَتَيْنِ
«قَدَمَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَةَ أقْدَامٍ».
فليس لاحد أن يقول : ان هذه الاخبار تنبئ ان أول الوقت والآخر سواء لانه قال : ما بينهما وقت لانه لا يمتنع أن يجعل ما
بين الوقتين وقتا وان كان الاول أفضل منه، والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه :

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Dharih:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, and informed him of
the timings of the prayer.
He (Jibrail) said: “Pray Fajr when the dawn breaks, and pray the first prayer (Dhuhr)
when the sun passes the meridian, and pray Asr shortly after it, and pray Maghrib when
the disk (of the sun) sets, and pray the night prayer (Isha) when the twilight
disappears.”
Then he (Jibrail) came to Him {saws} on the next day and said: “Brighten the Fajr (delay it
until the light is widespread), so He {saws} delayed it until the light spread. Then He {saws}
delayed Dhuhr until the time when He {saws} had prayed Asr on the previous day, and He
{saws} prayed Asr shortly after it, and He {saws} prayed Maghrib before the twilight
disappeared, and He {saws} prayed the night prayer (Isha) when a third of the night had
passed.
Then he (Jibrail) said: “Between these two times there is time, and the best time is its
beginning."
Then He {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT}
bless him and his family, said: ‘Were it not that I dislike to burden my nation, I would
have delayed it (Isha) until the middle of the night.’
And he (Dhurayh) said: "I said to Him {a.s};There are people among the companions of
Abu Al-Khattab who delay Maghrib until the stars become entangled."
He (Dhurayh) said: "He, (Imam al Sadiq {a.s}), said: ‘I disassociate myself before Allah
{SWT} from whoever does this intentionally.’"
text_ar:
الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ ذَرِيحِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «أَتَى جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ
رَسُولَ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَأَعْلَمَهُ مَوَاقِيتَ الصَّلَاَةِ فَقَالَ صَلِّ الْفَجْرَ حِينَ يَنْشَقُّ الْفَجْرُ وَ صَلِّ الْأُولَى إِذَا
زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَ صَلِّ الْعَصْرَ بُعَيْدَهَا وَ صَلِّ الْمَغْرِبَ إِذَا سَقَطَ الْقُرْصُ وَ صَلِّ الْعَتَمَةَ إِذَا غَابَ الشَّفَقُ ثُمَّ أَنَاهُ مِنَ
اَلْغَدِ فَقَالَ أَسْفِرْ بِالْفَجْرِ فَأَسْفَرَ ثُمَّ أَخِّرَ الظُّهْرَ حَتَّى كَانَ الْوَقْتُ الَّذِي صَلَّى فِيهِ اَلْعَصْرَ وَ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ بُعَيْدَهَا وَ
صَلَّى اَلْمَغْرِبَ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ الشَّفَقِ وَ صَلَّى الْعَتَمَةَ جِينَ ذَهَبَ ثُلْثُ ٱللَّيْلِ ثُمّ قَالَ مَا بَيْنَ هَذَيْنِ الْوَقْتَيْنِ وَقْتُ وَ
أفْضَلُ الوَقْتِ أُوَّلُهُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ «قَالَ رَسُولُ ٱللّهِ صَلّى اللَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ «لَوْ لاَ أَنَّي أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أُشَقَّ عَلَى
أَمَّتِي لَأَخْرْتُهَا إِلَى نِصْفِ اللِّيْلِ » » وَ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ أَنَاساً مِنْ أَصْحَابٍ أَبِي الْخَطَابِ يُمَسُونَ بِالْمَغْرِبِ حَتَّى
تَشَتَبِكَ النُجُومُ قَالَ فَقَالَ «أَبْرَأُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِمَّنْ يَفْعَلُ هَذَا مُتَعَمِّداً ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.253

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Al-Mitami from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever prays outside of the (prescribed)
time, his prayer is not considered a prayer.”
text_ar:
الحسن بن محمد عن الميثمي عن معاوية بن وهب عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام قال : من صلى
في غير وقت فلا صلاة له.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from his father:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "For me to pray Dhuhr at the time of Asr is
more beloved to me than to pray before the sun passes the meridian, for if I pray before
the sun passes the meridian, it will not be counted for me, and if I pray at the time of
Asr, it will be counted for me."
text_ar:
عَنَهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ الْعَطَارِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «لَأَنْ أُصَلِّيَ الظُهْرَ فِي وَقْتِ ٱلْعَصْرِ
أَحَبّ إِلَيّ مِنْ أَنْ أَصَلِّيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ فَإِنِّي إِذَا صَلَّيْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ الشَمْسُ لَمْ تُحْتَسَبْ لِي وَ إِذَا صَلَّيْتُ
فِي وَقْتِ اَلْعَصْرِ حُسِبَثْ لِي».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman:

text_ar:
عنه عن محمد بن الحسن العطار عن عبد اللّٰه بن سليمان عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام قال : لان أصلي الظهر
في وقت العصر أحب إلي من أن أصلي قبل أن تزول الشمس فاني إذا صليت قبل أن تزول الشمس لم تحسب
لي ، وإذا صليت في وقت العصر حسبت لي.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Attar, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "For me to pray Dhuhr at the time of Asr is
more beloved to me than to pray before the sun passes the meridian, for if I pray before
the sun passes the meridian, it will not be counted for me, and if I pray at the time of
Asr, it will be counted for me."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who prayed the morning
prayer during the night, being deceived by the moon, and then slept until the sun rose,
and was informed that he had prayed during the night.
Imam {a.s} said: “He must repeat his prayer.”
text_ar:
علي بن مهزيار عن فضالة عن أبان عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في رجل صلى الغداة بليل غره من ذلك
القمر ونام حتى طلعت الشمس فاخبر انه صلى بليل قال : يعيد صلاته.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who
said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about praying during the night and day when neither the sun nor the
moon nor the stars are visible.
Imam {a.s} said: “Exert your judgment and face the qiblah as best as you can.”
text_ar:
محمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن الحسين عن عثمان بن عيسى عن سماعة قال : سألته عن الصلاة بالليل والنهار
إذا لم تر الشمس ولا القمر ولا النجوم قال : اجتهد رأيك وتعمد القبلة جهدك.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Implicit (Muzmar)

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Ali narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Abdillah Al-Farra' from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be
upon him, who said:
A man from among our companions said to Imam {a.s}: “Sometimes the time becomes
unclear to us on a cloudy day.”
Imam {a.s} said: "Do you know those birds you have in Iraq that are called roosters?"
I said: “Yes”.
Imam {a.s} said: "When their voices rise and they call to each other, then the sun has
passed the meridian," or Imam {a.s} said: "then pray."
text_ar:
عَلِيّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ الْفَرَّاءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ
أَصْحَابِنَا رُبَّمَا اِشتَبَهَ الْوَقْتُ عَلَيْنَا فِي يَوْمِ ٱلْغَيْمِ فَقَالَ «تَعْرِفُ هَذِهِ الطُيُورَ الَّتِي عِنْدَكُمْ بِالْعِرَاقِ يُقَالُ لَهَا الدِّيَكَةُ»
قُلْثُ نَعَمْ قَالَ «إِذَا اِرْتَفَعَتْ أَصْوَاثُهَا وَ تَجَاوَبَتْ فَقَدْ زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ» أَوْ قَالَ «فَصَلِّهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.284 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.255 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.171
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from Al-Nawfali from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar from
a man who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I am a man who gives the call to prayer,
and when it is a cloudy day, I do not know the time.”
Imam {a.s} said: "When the rooster crows three continuous times, then the sun has
passed the meridian and the time of prayer has entered."
text_ar:
سَهْلُ بَنْ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنِ النَّوْفَلِيَّ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ ٱلْمُخْتَارِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ إِنَّي رَجُلٌ مُؤَذِّنْ فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْغَيْمِ لَمْ أَعْرِفِ الْوَقْتَ قَالَ «إِذَا صَاحَ الدِّيكُ ثَلاَثَةَ أَصْوَاتٍ وِلاءً فَقَدْ زَالَتِ
الشَّمْسُ وَ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ الصَّلاَةِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.285 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.255
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Zurarah ibn A'yan and
Bukayr ibn A'yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah Al-Ijli who said:
Abu Ja'far {a.s} and Abu Abdullah {a.s}, peace be upon them, said:
"The time of Dhuhr is after the sun has passed the meridian by two feet, and the time
of Asr is after that by two feet, and this is the beginning of the time until four feet have
passed for Asr."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنِ الْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ وَ زُرَارَةَ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ وَ بُكَيْرِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ وَ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ
مُسْلِمٍ وَ بُرَيْدِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ الْعِجْلِيَّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرِ وَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ : «وَقْتُ الظُهْرِ بَعْدَ ٱلزَّوَالِ
قَدَمَانٍ وَ وَقْتُ ٱلْعَصْرِ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَدَمَانِ وَ هَذَا أَوْلُ وَقْتٍ إلَى أَنْ يَمْضِيَ أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ لِلْعَصْرِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.255 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.248
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far {a.s}: “Is there a known limit between Dhuhr and Asr?”
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
text_ar:
اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ بَيْنَ الظُهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرِ حَدَّ
مَعْرُوفٌ فَقَالَ «لا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.255 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.240 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.126
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
text_chunk:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far {a.s}: “Is there a known limit between Dhuhr and Asr?”
Imam {a.s} said: "No."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Ubaydi from Sulayman ibn Ja'far who said:
Al-Faqīh (the Jurist) said: "The end of the time for Asr is six and a half feet."

Scholar's Note:
As for what has been narrated from the reports we have mentioned earlier, that the
time extends until the setting of the sun, it is to be understood regarding the one who
has an excuse or one who has a necessity that prevents him from praying, as we have
explained. And similar to that is to be understood what has been narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ الْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ قَالَ الْفَقِيهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «آخِرُ وَقْتِ ٱلْعَصْرِ
سِتَّةُ أقْدَامٍ وَ نِصفٌ».
وأما ما روي من الاخبار التي قدمناها من أن الوقت ممتد الى غروب الشمس فمحمول على صاحب الاعذار ومن به ضرورة
تمنعه من الصلاة على ما بيناه، وعلى مثل ذلك يحمل ما رواه :
commentary:
As for what has been narrated from the reports we have mentioned earlier, that the
time extends until the setting of the sun, it is to be understood regarding the one who
has an excuse or one who has a necessity that prevents him from praying, as we have
explained. And similar to that is to be understood what has been narrated:
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.256 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.259 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.246 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.153
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hadi {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Ya'qub Al-
Hashimi from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The prayer is not missed by one who
intends to pray. The prayer of the day is not missed until the sun sets, and the prayer
of the night is not missed until the dawn rises, and the prayer of Fajr is not missed until
the sun rises."

Scholar's Note:
And what further clarifies what we have mentioned is what has been narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ ٱلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنٍ
مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا يَفُوتُ الصَّلاَةُ مَنْ أَرَادَ الصَلاَةَ لا يَفُوتُ صَلاَةُ
النَّهَارٍ حَتَّى تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ وَ لَا صَلَاَةُ اللّيْلِ حَتَّى يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ وَ لاَ صَلاَةُ الفَجْرِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ».
والذي يزيد ما ذكرناه بيانا ما رواه :
commentary: And what further clarifies what we have mentioned is what has been narrated:
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.355 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.256 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.260 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.273 • Al-Sarair, Vol.3 p.602 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.289 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.159 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.7 9 p.363

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Asr is at two arm's lengths, and whoever
delays it until it reaches six feet, then he is the one who has neglected it."
text_ar:
الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «الْعَصْرُ
عَلَى ذِرَاعَيْنِ فَمَنْ تَرَكَهَا حَتَّى تَصِيرَ عَلَى سِنَّةِ أَقْدَامٍ فَذَلِكَ الْمُضَيِّعُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.256 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.259 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.234 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.152
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Asr is at two arm's lengths, and whoever
delays it until it reaches six feet, then he is the one who has neglected it."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Ja'far, from Mathna, from Mansur ibn Hazim:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Pray Asr at four feet (of shadow)."
Mathna said: “Abu Basir said to me that Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
‘Pray Asr on the day of Friday at six feet (of shadow).’"
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُتَّنِّى عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «صَلَّ الْعَصْرَ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْدَامٍ
» قَالَ مُتَنَّى قَالَ لِي أَبُو بَصِيرٍ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ «صَلِّ الْعَضْرَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ عَلَى سِنَّةِ أَقْدَاحٍ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.256 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.259 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.236
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Ja'far, from Mathna, from Mansur ibn Hazim:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Pray Asr at four feet (of shadow)."
Mathna said: “Abu Basir said to me that Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
‘Pray Asr on the day of Friday at six feet (of shadow).’"

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The one deprived of his family and his
wealth is the one who neglects the Asr prayer."
I asked: “What does 'deprived' mean?”
Imam {a.s} said: "He will have neither family nor wealth in Paradise."
I asked: “And what is the neglect of it?”
Imam {a.s} said: "He delays it until the sun yellows and sets."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلَاَمُ : «إِنَّ ٱلْمَوْتُورَ أَهْلَهُ وَ
مَالَهُ مَنْ ضَبَّعَ صَلاةَ ٱلْعَصْرِ» قُلْتُ وَ مَا ٱلْمَوْتُورُ قَالَ «لا يَكُونْ لَهُ أَهْلَ وَ لاَ مَالٌ فِي ٱلْجَنَّةِ » قُلْتُ وَ مَا تَضْبِيعُهَا
قَالَ «يَدَعُهَا حَتَّى تَصْفَرَّ وَ تَغِيبَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.256 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.259 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.246 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.152
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The one deprived of his family and his
wealth is the one who neglects the Asr prayer."
I asked: “What does 'deprived' mean?”
Imam {a.s} said: "He will have neither family nor wealth in Paradise."
I asked: “And what is the neglect of it?”
Imam {a.s} said: "He delays it until the sun yellows and sets."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, mentioned the beginning of the time and its
virtue. So I asked: “How should I manage the eight rak'ahs (of recommended prayers
before Dhuhr)?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Lighten them as much as you are able."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: ذَكَرَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَوَّلَ ٱلْوَقْتِ وَ
فَضْلَهُ فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ بِالثَّمَانِي رَكَعَاتٍ قَالَ «خَفَّفْ مَا اِسْتَطَعْتَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.257 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.225 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.121 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.172

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Salih ibn Khalid, from Safwan Al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who
said:
I asked: “When should I pray Asr if I am not traveling?”
Imam {a.s} said: "After Dhuhr by the measure of two-thirds of a foot (of shadow)."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ الْجَمَالِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ ٱلْعَضْرُ مَتَى أُصَلِّيهَا إِذَا كُنْتُ
فِي غَيْرٍ سَفَرٍ قَالَ «عَلَى قَدْرٍ ثُلْثَيْ قَدَمِ بَعْدَ الظُهْرِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.257 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.232 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.128 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.153

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Faddal from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Burayd from
one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them:
Imam {a.s} said: "When the redness disappears from the east, then the sun has set from
the east of the earth and its west."
text_ar:
الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ بُرَيْدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا
غَابَتِ الْحُمْرَةُ مِنَ الْمَشرِقِ فَقَدْ غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ مِنْ شَرْقِ الْأَرْضِ وَ غَرْبِهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.257 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.176
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Dharih:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed Jibrail, peace be upon him, came
to the Prophet, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, at the second time for Maghrib
before the disappearance of the twilight."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ ذَرِيحِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «أَنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّى النَّبِيّ صَلِّى
اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الثَّانِي فِي الْمَغْرِبِ قَبْلَ سُقُوطِ الشَّفَقِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.257 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.263 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.214 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.190

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is from when the sun
sets until the stars become intertwined."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «وَقْتُ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ مِنْ جِينِ تَغِيبُ
اَلشَّمْسُ إِلَى أَنْ تَشْتَبِكَ النُّجُومُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.257 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.263 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.277 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.182 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.190

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ali ibn Al-Harith, from Bakkar, from Muhammad ibn Shurayh,
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the time of Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "When the redness in the horizon changes and the yellowness
disappears, and before the stars become intertwined."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ عَنْ بَكَّارٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ شُرَيْحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا تَغَيَّرَتِ الْحُمْرَةُ فِي الْأُفُقِ وَ ذَهَبَتِ الصُفْرَةُ وَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَشَتَبِكَ النُّجُومُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.257 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.277 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.176
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Al-Mitami, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn Al-Fadl Al-Hashimi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT}
bless him and his family, used to pray Maghrib when the sun set, when its edge
disappeared."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ الْمِيثَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ الْهَاشِمِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «كَانَ رَسُولُ اللهِ
صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يُصَلِّي الْمَغْرِبَ جِينَ تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ حَيْثُ يَغِيبُ حَاجِبُهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.258 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.263 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.258 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.182
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is when the sun sets."

عَنْهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي .

حِينَ تَغِيبُ الشَّمْسُ».

From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is when the sun sets."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, by Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, byIbrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah and Abu Usamah:
They asked the Shaykh about Maghrib, and some of them said: “May I be your ransom,
we wait until a star appears.”
Imam {a.s} said: “This is (the practice of) the Khattabiyyah. Indeed, Jibrail, peace be
upon him, brought it (the timing of Maghrib) to Muhammad, may Allah {SWT} bless him
and his family, when the disk (of the sun) had set."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ عَنِ الصَّبَّاحِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ وَ أَبِي أُسَامَةً قَالا: سَأَلُوا الشَّيْخَ عَنِ
الْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاكَ نَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى يَظلُعَ كَوْكَبٌ «فَقَالَ خَطَّابِيَّةٌ إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ نَذَلَ بِهَا
عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ حِينَ سَقَطَ الْقُرْصُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.258 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.261 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.190
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, by Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, byIbrahim ibn Abdul Hamid, from Al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah and Abu Usamah:
They asked the Shaykh about Maghrib, and some of them said: “May I be your ransom,
we wait until a star appears.”
Imam {a.s} said: “This is (the practice of) the Khattabiyyah. Indeed, Jibrail, peace be
upon him, brought it (the timing of Maghrib) to Muhammad, may Allah {SWT} bless him

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Husayn ibn Hammad ibn Udays, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Al-Qasim ibn Salim, from Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Abu Al-Khattab was mentioned, so Imam {a.s} cursed him, then said:
"He did not retain anything (correctly). I had narrated to him (Abu Al-Khattab) that the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, had the sun set for
Him {a.s} in such-and-such a place, and He {a.s} prayed Maghrib at Al-Shajarah, and the
distance between them was six miles. I informed him (Abu Al-Khattab) of this regarding
travel, but he applied it to a state of residence."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ [حُسَيْنِ خ ل] بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُدَيْسِ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: ذْكِرَ أَبُو الْخَطَابِ فَلَعَنَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ «إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَحْفَظُ شَيْئاً حَدَّثُتُهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ
وَ آلِهِ غَابَتْ لَهُ الشَّمْسُ فِي مَكَانِ كَذَا وَ كَذَا وَ صَلَّى الْمَغْرِبَ بِالشَّجَرَةِ وَ بَيْنَهُمَا سِتَّةُ أَمْيَالٍ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِذَلِكَ فِي
السَّفَرٍ فَوَضَعَهُ فِي الْحَضَرِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.258 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.292 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.191
source_scholar: Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him::
I asked Him {a.s} about the time of Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is from the setting of the sun until the disappearance of the twilight."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتِ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ
قَالَ «مَا بَيْنَ غُرُوبِ الشَمْسِ إلَى سُقُوطِ الشَّفَقِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.258 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.263 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.277 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.182 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.190
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him::
I asked Him {a.s} about the time of Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is from the setting of the sun until the disappearance of the twilight."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn
Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam {a.s} said to me: "Delay Maghrib a little, for the sun sets from your location before
it sets from ours."
text_ar:
فَأَمًا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي: «مَسُّوا بِالْمَغْرِبِ قَلِيلاً فَإِنَّ الشَّمْسَ تَغِيبُ مِنْ عِنْدِكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَغِيبَ مِنْ عِنْدِنَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.258 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.269 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.176
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
As for what was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn
Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam {a.s} said to me: "Delay Maghrib a little, for the sun sets from your location before
it sets from ours."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Abdullah ibn Waddah who said:
I wrote to the Righteous Servant (Abd al Salih {a.s}), peace be upon him:
“The disk disappears and the night approaches, then the night continues to rise, and
the sun is hidden from us, and above the mountain a redness appears, and the callers
to prayer make the Adhan among us; should I pray at that time and break my fast if I
am fasting, or should I wait until the redness above the mountain disappears?”
So Imam {a.s} wrote to me: "I see for you that you should wait until the redness
disappears and take precaution for your religion."

text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ دَاوُدَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ وَضَاحِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إلَى الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَتَوَارَى اَلْقُرْصُ وَ
يُقْبِلُ اللَّيْلُ ثُمَّ يَزِيدُ اللَّيْلُ اِرْتِفَاعاً وَ تَسْتَتِرُ عَنَّا الشَّمْسُ وَ تَرْتَفِعُ فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ حُمْرَةُ وَ يُؤْذِّنَ عِنْدَنَا الْمُؤْذَّنُونَ
فَأُصَلِّي جِينَئِذٍ وَ أُفْطِرُ إِنْ كُنْتُ صَائِماً أَوْ أَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى تَذْهَبَ الْحُمْرَةُ آَلَّتِي فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ فَكَتَّبَ إِلَيَّ «أَرَى لَكَ أَنْ
نَنْتَظِرَ حَتَّى تَذْهَبَ الْحُمْرَةُ وَ تَأْخُذَ بِالْحَائِطَةِ لِدِينِكَ».

تغيب الحمرة من ناحية المشرق وكذلك قوله في الخبر الثاني ، وقد دللنا على ذلك بما تقدم من الاخبار ، ويزيد ذلك بيانا

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Ibn Ribaat from Jarud or Isma'il ibn Abi Sammal from
Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Jarud who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to me: "O Jarud, they are advised, but they
do not accept. And when they hear something, they cry out about it, or if they are told
something, they spread it.
I (Imam al Sadiq {a.s}) said to them: ‘Delay Maghrib a little, but they abandoned it until
the stars became intertwined. Now I pray it when the disk (of the sun) sets.’"
text_ar:
الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةً عَنِ اِبْنِ رِبَاطِ عَنْ جَارُودِ أَوْ [أَوْ خ ل] إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي سَمَّالٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي
حَمْزَةَ عَنْ جَارُودِ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «يَا جَارُودُ يُنْصَحُونَ فَلاَ يَقْبَلُونَ وَ إِذَا سَمِعُوا بِشَيْءٍ
نَادَوْا بِهِ أَوْ حُدِّثُوا بِشَيْءٍ أَذَاعُوهُ قُلْتُ لَهُمْ مَسُوا بِالْمَغْرِبِ قَلِيلاً فَتَرَكُوهَا حَتَّى اِشتَبَكَتِ النُجُومُ فَأَنَا الْآنَ أُصَلَّيهَا
إِذَا سَقَطَ الْقُرْصُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.259 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.270 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.177
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan from Ali ibn Ya'qub
from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ammar Al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "I had commanded Abu Al-Khattab to pray
Maghrib when the redness had disappeared, but he took it to mean the redness from
the direction of the west, and he would pray when the twilight disappeared."

Scholar's Note:
As for cases of excuses and obstacles, it is permissible to delay it until a quarter of the
night, as we have already presented in the narrations. What further clarifies this is
what has been narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ عَمَّارِ السَّابَاطِيّ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «إِنَّمَا أَمَرْتُ أَبَا الْخَطَابِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ الْمَغْرِبَ حِينَ زَالَتِ الْحُمْرَةُ فَجَعَلَ هُوَ
الْحُمْرَةَ الْتِي مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَغْرِبِ وَ كَانَ يُصَلِّي جِينَ يَغِيبُ الشَّفَقُ».
فاما عند الاعذار والموانع فانه يجوز تأخيرها الى ربع الليل على ما قدمنا الاخبار فيه، ويزيد ذلك وضوحا ما رواه:
commentary:

night, as we have already presented in the narrations. What further clarifies this is
what has been narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdul Hamid from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn
Yazid from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the time of Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it is easier for you and more suitable for your prayer, and you are
occupied with your needs, then you have until a quarter of the night."
He (Umar ibn Yazid) said: “and that was while He (Imam {a.s}) was present in his
hometown.”
text_ar:
محمد بن علي بن محبوب عن محمد بن عبد الحميد عن محمد ابن عمر بن يزيد عن محمد بن عذافر عن عمر
بن يزيد قال : سألت أبا عبد اللّه عليه السلام عن وقت المغرب فقال : إذا كان ارفق بك وامكن لك في صلاتك
وكنت في حوائجك فلك الى ربع الليل ، قال : فقال لي وهو شاهد في بلده.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Udym ibn Al-Hurr who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: "Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him,
(conveyed the) command to the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and
his family, regarding all the prayers, and assigned for each prayer two times, except
for Maghrib, for he (Jibrail) assigned for it only one time."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ أُدَيْمِ بْنِ الْحُرِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ
جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ أَمَرَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِالصَّلَوَاتِ كُلَّهَا فَجَعَلَ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ وَقْتَيْنِ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ
فَإِنَّهُ جَعَلَ لَهَا وَقْتاً وَاحِداً».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.260 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.245 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.269 • Miftah Al- Falah, Vol.1 p.234 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.262 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.189
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Udym ibn Al-Hurr who said:

(conveyed the) command to the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zayd Al-Shahham who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the time of Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "Indeed, Jibrail, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet {saws}, may
Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, for each prayer with two times, except for the
Maghrib prayer, for its time is one, and its time is its obligation."

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “There is no contradiction between these two
narrations and what we have presented previously from the narrations that Maghrib
has two times: its beginning is the setting of the sun, and its end is the disappearance
of the twilight or the intermingling of the stars.
This is because if a person prays at the time when the redness disappears from the
eastern horizon and performs his prayer with calmness, then he will not finish his
obligatory and supererogatory prayers except that the twilight will have disappeared
and the stars will have appeared.”
And what further clarifies what we have already presented; that these two prayers
(Maghrib and ʿIshaʾ) have two time ranges, and that the earlier narrations only negate
the extension of the time, is what has been narrated:
text_ar:
عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زَيْدِ ٱلشَّحَامِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ وَقْتِ
الْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ «إِنَّ جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّى النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ بِوَقْتَيْنِ غَيْرَ صَلاَةِ الْمَغْرِبِ فَإِنَّ
وَقْتَهَا وَاحِدٌ وَ وَقْتَهَا وُجُوبُهَا».
قال محمد بن الحسن : لا تنافي بين هذين الخبرين وبين ما قدمناه من الاخبار من ان للمغرب وقتين واوله سقوط الشمس
وآخره ذهاب الشفق أو اشتباك النجوم لان الانسان إذا صلى في وقت ذهاب الحمرة من ناحية المشرق وتأنى في صلاته
فانه لا يفرغ من صلاة فريضة ونافلة إلا ويكون قد غاب الشفق وظهرت النجوم، والذي يزيد ما قدمناه وضوحا من ان
لهاتين الصلاتين وقتين وإنما نفي بالخبرين المتقدمين سعة الوقت ما رواه:
commentary:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “There is no contradiction between these two
narrations and what we have presented previously from the narrations that Maghrib
has two times: its beginning is the setting of the sun, and its end is the disappearance
of the twilight or the intermingling of the stars.
This is because if a person prays at the time when the redness disappears from the
eastern horizon and performs his prayer with calmness, then he will not finish his
obligatory and supererogatory prayers except that the twilight will have disappeared
and the stars will have appeared.”
And what further clarifies what we have already presented; that these two prayers
(Maghrib and ʿIshaʾ) have two time ranges, and that the earlier narrations only negate
the extension of the time, is what has been narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Isma'il ibn Mihran who said:
I wrote to (Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, mentioning that:
“Our companions say that when the sun passes the meridian, the time for Dhuhr and
Asr has entered, and when it sets, the time for Maghrib and Isha enters, except that
Maghrib is before Isha, whether in travel or residence, and that the time for Maghrib
extends until a quarter of the night.”
So Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, wrote: "Such is the time, except that the time for
Maghrib is narrow, and its end is when the redness disappears and it turns into
whiteness in the western horizon."
text_ar:
سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إلَى آلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ ذَكَرَ أَصْحَابُنَا أَنَّهُ إِذَا زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَقَدْ
دَخَلَ وَقْتُ الظُّهْرِ وَ الْعَصْرِ وَ إِذَا غَرَبَتْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَ الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا أَنَّ هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ
الْحَضَرِ وَ أَنَّ وَقْتَ الْمَغْرِبِ إِلَى رُبُعِ اللِّيْلِ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ «كَذَلِكَ الْوَقْتُ غَيْرَ أَنَّ وَقْتَ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ ضَيِّقٌ وَ آخِرَ
وَقْتِهَا ذَهَابُ الْحُمْرَةِ وَ مَصِيرُهَا إِلَى ٱلْبَيَاضِ فِي أَفُقِ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.281 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.260 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.270 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.276
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}

“Our companions say that when the sun passes the meridian, the time for Dhuhr and

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ali ibn Al-Rayan who said:
I wrote to Imam {a.s}, asking; “About a man who is inside a house, and its walls prevent
him from seeing the redness of the Maghrib and from knowing the disappearance of
the twilight and the time for the Isha prayer; when should he pray it, and what should
he do?”
So Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, wrote in response: "He should pray it, in this case,
when the stars begin to scatter and Isha when they become intertwined and the
whiteness of the sunset appears."

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “The meaning of ‘qasr al-nujum’ (the abbreviation or
shortening regarding the stars) is their visibility and appearance.”
text_ar:
سَهْلُ بنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الرَّيَّانِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ الرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ فِي الدَّارِ تَمْنَعُهُ حِيطَانُهَا النَّظَرَ إِلَى حُمْرَةِ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ
وَ مَعْرِفَةَ مَغِيبِ الشَّفَقِ وَ وَقْتِ صَلاَةِ الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ مَتَى يُصَلَّيهَا وَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فَوَقَّعَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «يُصَلَّيهَا إِذَا
كَانَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ عِنْدَ قَصْرِ النُّجُومِ وَ الْعِشَاءَ عِنْدَ اِشتِبَاكِهَا وَ بَيَاضٍ مَغِيبِ الشَّمْسِ».
قال محمد بن الحسن : معنى قصر النجوم بيانها.
commentary:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “The meaning of ‘qasr al-nujum’ (the abbreviation or
shortening regarding the stars) is their visibility and appearance.”
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.281 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.261 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.269 • Al-Sarair, Vol.3 p.582 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.297 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.205
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hadi {a.s}
text_chunk:
Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ali ibn Al-Rayan who said:
I wrote to Imam {a.s}, asking; “About a man who is inside a house, and its walls prevent
him from seeing the redness of the Maghrib and from knowing the disappearance of
the twilight and the time for the Isha prayer; when should he pray it, and what should
he do?”
So Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, wrote in response: "He should pray it, in this case,
when the stars begin to scatter and Isha when they become intertwined and the
whiteness of the sunset appears." Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “The meaning of ‘qasr al-nujum’ (the abbreviation or
shortening regarding the stars) is their visibility and appearance.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Ali narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "The time for Maghrib is when the disk (of the sun)
disappears. If you see it after that and you have already prayed, you must repeat the
prayer, but your fast remains valid, and you must refrain from food if you have eaten
anything."
text_ar:
عَلِي عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أُبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «وَقْتُ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا غَابَ ٱلْقُرْصُ
فَإِنْ رَأَيْتَهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ أَعَدْتَ الصَّلاةَ وَ مَضَى صَوْمُكَ وَ تَكُفُ عَنِ الطَّعَامِ إنْ كُنْتَ أَصَبْتَ مِنْهُ شَيْئًا».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.279 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.2 p.121 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.261 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.4 p.271 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.2 p.115 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.260 • Al-Wafi, Vol.1 1 p.291 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.178 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.10 p.122

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from
Muhammad ibn Hakim from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "O Shihab, I like that when I pray Maghrib, I
see a star in the sky."

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “The aspect of recommendation in this narration is
that a person should be deliberate in his prayer and perform it with calmness, for if he
does so, he will finish it at the time when the stars appear.”
text_ar:
فَأَمًا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ شِهَابٍ
بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : «يَا شِهَابُ إِنَّي أُجِبُّ إِذَا صَلَّيْتُ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ أَنْ أَرَى فِي السَّمَاءِ كَوْكَباً».
قال محمد بن الحسن : وجه الاستحباب في هذا الخبر أن يتأنى الانسان في صلاته ويصليها على تؤدة فانه إذا فعل كذلك
يكون فراغه منها عند ظهور الكواكب.
commentary:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “The aspect of recommendation in this narration is
that a person should be deliberate in his prayer and perform it with calmness, for if he
does so, he will finish it at the time when the stars appear.”
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.261
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Harun ibn Kharijah from
Abu Basir:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless
him and his family, said: ‘Were it not that I fear burdening my nation, I would have
delayed the night prayer (Isha) until a third of the night. And you are in a state of
concession until midnight, and that is the darkening of the night. When the darkening
has passed, two angels call out: Whoever has slept through the obligatory prayer after
midnight, may his eyes never taste sleep.’"
text_ar:
الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «لَوْ لا أَنَّي أَخَافُ أَنْ أُشُقَ عَلَى أَمَّتِي لَأَخَرْتُ ٱلْعَتَمَةَ إِلَى ثُلُثِ اللَّيْلِ وَ
أَنْتَ فِي رُخْصَةٍ إِلَى نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ وَ هُوَ غَسَقُ اللَّيْلِ فَإِذَا مَضَى اَلْغَسَقُ نَادَى مَلَكَانِ مَنْ رَقَدَ عَنْ صَلاّةِ ٱلْمَكْتُوبَةِ بَعْدَ
نصْفِ اللّيْلِ فَلاَ رَقَدَتْ عَيْنَاهُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.261 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.272 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.278 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.185 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.200

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Safwan, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The end of the time for the night prayer
(Isha) is midnight."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مُعَلَّى أَبِي عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «آخِرُ وَقْتِ ٱلْعَتَمَةِ
بصفُ اللّيْلِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.262 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.273 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.279 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.185

From him, from Safwan, from Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The time for the night prayer (Isha) extends
until a third of the night or until midnight, and that (delay) is considered negligence."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ هَاشِمِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «الْعَتَمَةُ إِلَى ثُلُثِ اللَّيْلِ
أَوْ إِلَى نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ وَ ذَلِكَ التَّضْيِيعُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.262 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.273 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.280 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.185
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal
from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar Al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah {a.s} said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about a man who is overcome by sleep or prevented by something
from praying Fajr on time.
Imam {a.s} said: "He may pray Fajr any time between the rising of the dawn and the rising
of the sun, and that is specifically for the obligatory prayer. So if he has prayed one
rakʿah of the dawn prayer and then the sun rises, he should complete the prayer, and
his prayer is valid. But if the sun rises before he has prayed a single rakʿah, then he
should break off the prayer and not pray until the sun has risen and its glare has
passed."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ
مُصَدِّقٍ بْنِ صَدَقَةً عَنْ عَمَّارِ السَابَاطِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ إِذَا غَلَبَثهُ عَيْنُهُ أوْ
عَاقَهُ أَمْرٌ «أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ الْفَجْرَ مَا بَيْنَ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ وَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْمَكْتُوبَةِ خَاصَّةً فَإِنْ صَلَّى
رَكْعَةً مِنَ الْغَدَاةِ ثُمَّ طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَلْيُتِمَّ الصَّلاَةَ وَ قَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ إِنْ طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ رَكْعَةً
فَلْيَقْطَعِ الصَّلاَةَ وَ لا يُصَلِّي حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ وَ يَذْهَبَ شُعَاعُهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.262
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, say: "The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT}
bless him and his family, would not pray anything during the day until the sun had
passed the meridian. When the day had declined by about half a finger's width, He {saws}
would pray eight rak'ahs.
When the shadow extended to the length of one arm, He {saws} would pray Dhuhr, then
He {saws} would pray two rak'ahs after Dhuhr. He {saws} would pray two rak'ahs before the
time of Asr. When the shadow extended to two arms' length, He {saws} would pray Asr.
He {saws} would pray Maghrib when the sun set. When the twilight disappeared, the time
for Isha would begin. The end of the time for Maghrib is the return of the twilight.
When the twilight returns, the time for Isha enters. The end of the time for Isha is a third
of the night. He would not pray after Isha until midnight; then he would pray thirteen
rak'ahs, including the Witr prayer and including the two rak'ahs of Fajr before the
morning prayer. When the dawn rose and became bright, he would pray the morning
(Fajr) prayer."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:
«كَانَ رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لا يُصَلِّي مِنَ النَّهَارِ شَيْئاً حَتَّى تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا زَالَ النَّهَارُ قَدْرَ نِصْفِ
إصْبَع صَلَّى ثَمَانَ رَكَعَاتٍ فَإِذَا فَاءَ الْفَيْءُ ذِرَاعاً صَلِّى الظُّهْرَ ثُمَّ صَلَّى بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُصَلِّي قَبْلَ وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ
رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَإِذَا قَاءَ الْفَيْءُ ذِرَاعَيْنِ صَلَّى الْعَصْرَ وَ صَلَّى الْمَغْرِبَ جِينَ تَغِيبُ الشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا غَابَ الشَّفَقُ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ
الْعِشَاءٍ وَ آخِرُ وَقْتِ الْمَغَرِبِ إِيَابُ الشَفَقِ فَإِذَا آبَ ٱلشَفَقُ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ ٱلْعِشَاءِ وَ آخِرُ وَقْتِ الْعِشَاءِ ثُلْثُ اللّيْلِ وَ كَانَ
لاَ يُصَلِّي بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ حَتَّى يَنْتَصِفَ اللَّيْلُ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي ثَلاَثَ عَشرَةَ رَكْعَةً مِنْهَا ٱلْوَثْرُ وَ مِنْهَا رَكْعَتَا ٱلْفَجْرِ قَبْلَ ٱلْغَدَاةِ
فَإِذَا طَلَعَ الْفَجْرُ وَ أَضَاءَ صَلَّى الْغَدَاةَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.262 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.269 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.312 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.156

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT}
bless him and his family, prayed Dhuhr and Asr with the people when the sun had
passed the meridian, in congregation, without any excuse.
And He {saws} prayed Maghrib and the night prayer (Isha) with them before the twilight
disappeared, without any excuse, in congregation. The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may
Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, only did that to widen the time for his nation."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمْدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: « صَلَّى
رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِالنَّاسِ الظُهْرَ وَ الْعَصْرَ جِينَ زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ وَ صَلَّى بِهِمُ
الْمَغْرِبَ وَ الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ قَبْلَ الشَّفَقِ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ إِنَّمَا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ
ليَتَّسِعَ الْوَقْتُ عَلَى أُمَّتِهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Musa ibn Umar from Abdullah ibn Al-
Mughira from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “May we combine between Maghrib and
Isha while residing, before the twilight disappears, without any excuse?”
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُمَرَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ نَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ الْمَغْرِبِ وَ الْعِشَاءِ فِي الْحَضَرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةِ قَالَ
«لا بَأْسَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.263
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali from Al-Fadl ibn Muhammad from Yahya ibn Abi Zakariyya from Al-
Walid ibn Aban from Safwan Al-Jammal who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, prayed Dhuhr and Asr with us when the sun had
passed the meridian, with one Adhan and two Iqamahs.
Then Imam {a.s} said: "I have something I need to attend to, so offer your recommended
prayers."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي زَكَرِيَّا عَنِ ٱلْوَلِيدِ بْنِ أَبَانٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ ٱلْجَمَالِ
قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ الظُهْرَ وَ الْعَصْرَ عِنْدَ مَا زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ بِأَذَانٍ وَ إِقَامَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ قَالَ « إِنّي عَلَى
حَاجَةٍ فَتَنَفَّلُوا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated from Abbas Al-Naqid who said:
My possessions were scattered, and the craftsmen working for me dispersed, so I
complained about that to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.
Imam {a.s} said to me: "Combine between the two prayers, Dhuhr and Asr, and you will
see what you love (desire)."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَبَّاسِ النَّاقِدِ قَالَ: تَفَرَّقَ مَا كَانَ فِي يَدِي وَ تَفَرَّقَ عَنِّي حُرَفَائِي فَشَكَوْتُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ فَقَالَ لِي «اِجْمَع بَيْنَ الصَّلَاَتَيْنِ الظُّهْرِ وَ الْعَصْرِ تَرَى مَا تُجِبُّ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.263
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Salamah ibn Al-Khattab from Al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Hammad ibn
Uthman from Muhammad ibn Hakim from Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}, who said:
I heard Imam {a.s} say: "If you combine between the two prayers, then do not offer any
supererogatory prayer between them."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ الْخَطَابِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَيْفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ أَبِي
الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا جَمَعْتَ بَيْنَ الصَّلَاتَيْنِ فَلا تَطَوَّعْ بَيْنَهُمَا».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.287 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.263 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.284 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.224 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.7 9 p.337
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who
said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who comes to the mosque
and the people there have already prayed. Should he start with the obligatory prayer
or with a supererogatory prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: "If it is within a good time, then there is no harm in performing the
supererogatory prayer before the obligatory one. But if he fears missing the obligatory
prayer because a lot of time has passed, then he should start with the obligatory
prayer, as it is the right of Allah {SWT}. Then he may pray as many supererogatory prayers
as he wishes.
The matter is flexible; a person may pray at the beginning of the obligatory prayer’s
time. And it is better, if a person is praying alone, to begin with the obligatory prayer
once its time has entered, so that the best part of the time is devoted to the obligatory
prayer. However, it is not prohibited for him to perform supererogatory prayers from
the beginning of the time until near the end of the time."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثُمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي الْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى أَهْلُهُ أَيَبْتَدِئ بِالْمَكْتُوبَةِ أَوْ يَتَطَوَّعُ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ حَسَنٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ
بالتَّطَوْعِ قَبْلَ الْفَرِيضَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ خَافَ ٱلْفَوْتَ مِنْ أَجْلِ مَا مَضَى مِنَ ٱلْوَقْتِ فَلْيَبْدَأُ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ وَ هُوَ حَقُّ اللّهِ ثُمَّ
ليَتَطَوَّعُ مَا شَاءَ الْأَمْرُ مُوَسَّعْ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ ٱلْإِنْسَانُ فِي أَوْلٍ وَقْتِ ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ الْفَضْلُ إِذَا صَلَّى ٱلْإِنْسَانُ وَحْدَهُ أَنْ يَبْدَأَ
بِالْفَرِيضَةِ إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُهَا لِيَكُونَ فَضْلُ ٱلْوَقْتِ لِلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ لَيْسَ بِمَحْظُور عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ النَّوَافِلَ مِنْ أَوْلِ ٱلْوَقْتِ
إلَى قَرِيبٍ مِنْ آخِرِ ٱلْوَقْتِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.288 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.264 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.362 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.226

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Uthman ibn Isa
from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
I asked: “May I pray a supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer?”
He said: "Yes, at the beginning of the time, if you are with an Imam whom you follow.
But if you are alone, then start with the obligatory prayer."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَخْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ
أُصَلِّي فِي وَقْتِ فَرِيضَةِ نَافِلَةً قَالَ «نَعَمْ فِي أَوَّلِ الْوَقْتِ إِذَا كُنْتَ مَعَ إِمَامِ تَقْتَدِي بِهِ فَإِذَا كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَابْدَأُ
بِالْمَكْتُوبَةِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.289 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.264 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.362 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.226

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Sa'd narrated from Ahmad from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Usamah or
someone else who said:
I once climbed Mount Abu Qubays while the people were praying Maghrib, and I saw
that the sun had not actually set; it had only been concealed behind the mountain from
the people.
I then met Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, and informed him of this.
Imam {a.s} said to me: "And why did you do that? What a bad thing you have done! You
should pray it when you do not see it, whether it has set behind a mountain or
disappeared, so long as it is not hidden by a cloud or darkness that covers it. What is
required of you is your east and your west, and it is not upon the people to investigate
further."
text_ar:
سَعدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ قَالَ: صَعِدْتُ مَرَّةً
جَبَلَ أَبِي قُبَيْسِ وَ النَّاسُ يُصَلُونَ الْمَغْرِبَ فَرَأَيْتُ الشَّمْسَ لَمْ تَغِبْ إِنَّمَا تَوَارَثْ خَلْفَ الْجَبَلِ عَنِ النَّاسِ فَلَقِيتُ أَبَا
عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِذَلِكَ فَقَالَ لِي «وَ لِمَ فَعَلْتَ ذَلِكَ بِئْسَ مَا صَنَعْتَ إِنَّمَا تُصَلَّيهَا إِذَا لَمْ تَرَهَا خَلْفَ
جَبَلٍ غَابَتْ أَوْ غَارَتْ مَا لَمْ يُجَلِّلْهَا سَحَابٌ أَوْ ظُلَمْ تُظِلَّهَا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ مَشرِقُكَ وَ مَغْرِبُكَ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى النَّاسِ أَنْ
يَبْحَثُوا»،

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Musa ibn Al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn
Uthman, from Sama'ah ibn Mehran who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, regarding Maghrib: “Sometimes we pray
while we fear that the sun might still be behind the mountain or that the mountain has
hidden it from us.”
Imam {a.s} said: "You are not required to climb the mountain."
text_ar:
عنه عن موسى بن الحسن عن أحمد بن هلال عن محمد ابن أبي عمير عن جعفر بن عثمان عن سماعة بن مهران
قال قلت: لابي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام في المغرب انا ربما صلينا ونحن نخاف ان تكون الشمس خلف الجبل أو
قد سترنا منها الجبل قال فقال : ليس عليك صعود الجبل.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the Maghrib prayer when its time arrives, is it permissible to delay
it for a while?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm if he is fasting, he should break his fast and then pray,
and if he has a need, he should fulfill it and then pray."
text_ar:
عنه عن أحمد بن الحسن بن علي بن فضال عن عمرو ابن سعيد المدائني عن مصدق بن صدقة عن عمار بن
موسى الساباطي عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام قال : سألته عن صلاة المغرب إذا حضرت هل يجوز أن تؤخر
ساعة؟ قال : لا بأس ان كان صائما افطر ثم صلى وان كانت له حاجة قضاها ثم صلى.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id Al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the Maghrib prayer when its time arrives, is it permissible to delay
it for a while?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm if he is fasting, he should break his fast and then pray,
and if he has a need, he should fulfill it and then pray."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises,
should he pray as soon as he wakes up or wait until the sun has risen fully?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray as soon as he wakes up."
I asked: “Should he perform the Witr prayer or the two rak'ahs (of Nafila)?”
Imam {a.s} said: "No, rather he should begin with the obligatory prayer."
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَنَامُ عَنِ ٱلْغَدَاةِ حَتَّى تَبْزُغَ الشَّمْسُ أَ يُصَلِّي جِينَ يَسْتَيْقِظُ أَوْ يَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى تَنْبَسِطَ الشَّمْسُ
فَقَالَ «يُصَلِّي جينَ يَسْتَيْقِظُ» قُلْتُ يُوتِرُ أَوْ يُصَلِّي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَالَ «لا بَلْ يَنْدَأْ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.265 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.286 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.354 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.284
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from
Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray the two rak'ahs and then pray the morning (Fajr)
prayer."
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَامَ عَنِ الْغَدَاةِ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ «يُصَلِّي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي الْغَدَاةَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.265 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.355
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from
Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who sleeps through the morning prayer until the sun rises.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
And from him, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon
him, who said:
I heard Him {a.s} say: "The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his
family, once slept and his eyes were overcome by sleep, and He {saws} did not wake up
until the heat of the sun troubled him. Then He {saws} awoke, called his group for a
moment, prayed two rak'ahs, and then prayed the morning (Fajr) prayer.
He {saws} said: 'O Bilal, what happened to you?'
Bilal replied: 'The one who caused you to sleep, O Messenger of Allah {SWT}, also caused
me to sleep.'
He {saws} disliked staying in that place and said: 'You (Bilal) have slept in the valley of
Shaytan.'"

Scholar's Note:
Thus, the meaning of these two narrations is that it is only permissible to perform two
rak'ahs of supererogatory prayer so that the people who missed the prayer may gather
and pray in congregation, just as the Prophet, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family,
did. But if a person is alone, it is not permissible for him to begin with any
supererogatory prayer at all, as we have previously mentioned. What further clarifies
this is what has been narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ رَسُولَ
اللّه صَلّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلهِ رَقَدَ فَغَلَبَتْهُ عَيْنَاهُ فَلَمْ يَسْتَيْقِظُ حَتَّى آذَاهُ حَر لَ م قَ ا هُ اَ
رَكَعَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى الصُّبْحَ وَ قَالَ «يَا بِلالُ مَا لَكَ» فَقَالَ بِلاَلْ أَرْقَدَنِي الَّذِي أَرْقَدَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللّهِ قَالَ وَ كَرِهَ
الْمُقَامَ وَ قَالَ «نِمْتُمْ بِوَادِي الشَّيْطَانِ» ».
فهذان الخبران المعنى فيهما انه إنما يجوز التطوع ركعتين ليجتمع الناس الذين فاتتهم الصلاة ليصلوا جماعة كما فعل
النبي صلى اللّه عليه وآله فاما إذا كان الانسان وحده فلا يجوز له أن يبدأ بشئ من التطوع أصلا على ما قدمناه ، ويزيده
بيانا ما رواه :
commentary:
Thus, the meaning of these two narrations is that it is only permissible to perform two
rak'ahs of supererogatory prayer so that the people who missed the prayer may gather
and pray in congregation, just as the Prophet, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family,
did. But if a person is alone, it is not permissible for him to begin with any
supererogatory prayer at all, as we have previously mentioned. What further clarifies
this is what has been narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, was asked about a man who prayed without
purification, or forgot prayers and did not perform them, or slept through them.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must make them up whenever he remembers them, at whatever
time he remembers, by night or by day. If the time of a present prayer comes and he
has not yet finished making up what he missed, then he should make up what he can
without fearing that the time of the present prayer will expire.
The present prayer has greater right to its time, so he should perform it first. When he
has prayed it, he should then complete whatever he had missed from before. And he
should not perform even a single rak'ah of supererogatory prayer until he has made up
the obligatory prayer."
text_ar:
الحسين بن سعيد عن ابن أبي عمير عن عمر بن اذينة عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام انه سئل عن رجل
صلى بغير طهور أو نسي صلوات لم يصلها أو نام عنها فقال : يقضيها إذا ذكرها في أي ساعة ذكرها من ليل أو
نهار فإذا دخل وقت صلاة ولم يتم ما قد فاته فليقض ما لم يتخوف أن يذهب وقت هذه الصلاة التي قد
حضرت وهذه أحق بوقتها فليصلها فإذا قضاها فليصل ما قد فاته مما قد مضى ولا يتطوع بركعة حتى يقضي
الفريضة.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from a group of our
companions:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon
him, would not pray during the day until the sun had passed the meridian, nor at night
after praying the night prayer (Isha) until midnight."
text_ar:
عَلِي بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَذَيْنَةَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّهُمْ سَمِعُوا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ يَقُولُ: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُومِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ لا يُصَلِّي مِنَ النَّهَارِ حَتَّى تَزُولَ الشّمْسُ وَلَا مِنَ اللِّيْلِ بَعْدَ مَا
يُصَلِّي اَلْعِشَاءَ حَتَّى يَنْتَصِفَ اللَّيْلُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.289 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.266 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.277 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.311 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.230 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.135
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn
Darraj from Zurarah:
Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: "(Imam {a.s}) Ali, peace be upon him, would not
pray anything during the night after praying the night prayer (Isha) until midnight, and
He {a.s} would not pray during the day until the sun had passed the meridian."

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “What I act upon is what is contained in this narration
and the one before it, that it is not permissible to offer any of the noon supererogatory
prayers before the sun passes the meridian. However, a concession has been
narrated permitting their offering before the meridian.”
text_ar:
مُحَمّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ السِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي
جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ لا يُصَلِّي مِنَ اللِّيْلِ شَيْئاً إِذَا صَلِّى الْعَتَمَةَ حَتَّى يَنْتَصِفَ اَللَّيْلُ وَ
لاَ يُصَلِّي مِنَ اَلنَّهَارِ حَتَّى تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ».
قال محمد بن الحسن: الذي اعمل عليه ما تضمنه هذا الحديث والذي قبله من أنه لا يجوز تقديم شئ من نوافل الزوال
قبل الزوال، وقد روي رخصة في جواز تقديمها.
commentary:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “What I act upon is what is contained in this narration
and the one before it, that it is not permissible to offer any of the noon supererogatory
prayers before the sun passes the meridian. However, a concession has been
narrated permitting their offering before the meridian.”
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.266 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.311 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.231 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.136
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub from Isma'il ibn Jabir who
said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I get occupied (and cannot pray at the
usual time)”.
Imam {a.s} said: "Then do as we do, pray six rak'ahs when the sun is at the same position
it is at during the Asr prayer,” (meaning at the height of the greater forenoon ‘al-duha
al-akbar’), “and count them as if you had performed them at zawal (midday)."
text_ar:
رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ إِنَّي أَشْتَغِلُ قَالَ «فَاصْنَعْ كَمَا نَصْنَعُ صَلِّ سِتْ رَكَعَاتٍ إِذَا كَانَتِ الشَّمْسُ فِي مِثْلِ مَوْضِعِهَا صَلاَةَ
اَلْعَصْرِ يَعْنِي اِرْتِفَاعَ الضُّحَى الْأَكْبَرِ وَ اِعْتَدَّ بِهَا مِنَ الزَّوَالِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.267 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.277 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.329 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.232
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Ammar ibn Al-Mubarak, from Zharif ibn Nasih, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Walid Al-Ghassani,
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “May I be your ransom, the daytime prayer, the prayer of the
supererogatory (nawafil), how many are they?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Sixteen. You may pray them at any hour of the day you wish, but if you
pray them at their proper times, it is better."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ ٱلْمُبَارَكِ عَنْ ظَرِيفِ بْنِ نَاصِحٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ ٱلْغَسَانِيَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ:
قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتْ فِدَاكَ صَلاَةُ ٱلنَّهَارِ صَلاَةُ النَّوَافِلِ فِي كَمْ هِيَ قَالَ «سِتَّ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّ سَاعَاتِ النَّهَارِ شِئْتَ تُصَلَّيهَا
صَلِّيْتَهَا إِلَّ أَنَّكَ إِذَا صَلِّيْتَهَا فِي مَوَاقِيتِهَا أَفْضَلُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.267 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.277 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.233
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Ammar ibn Al-Mubarak, from Zharif ibn Nasih, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Walid Al-Ghassani,
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “May I be your ransom, the daytime prayer, the prayer of the
supererogatory (nawafil), how many are they?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Sixteen. You may pray them at any hour of the day you wish, but if you
pray them at their proper times, it is better."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER TIMES (MAWAQIT)
text_en:
From him, from Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him,
who said:
Imam {a.s} said to me: "The daytime prayer is sixteen rak'ahs, whichever part of the day
you wish, if you wish at its beginning, or if you wish in its middle, or if you wish at its
end."
text_ar:
عنه عن علي بن الحكم عن بعض أصحابه عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام قال قال لي : صلاة النهار ست عشرة
ركعة أي النهار شئت ان شئت في أوله وإن شئت في وسطه وإن شئت في آخره.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
