author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Aban from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be
upon him, who said:
I asked: “A man enters the mosque and the people have already prayed; should he give
the Adhan and the Iqamah?”
Imam {a.s} said: "If he enters and the rows have not dispersed, he should pray with their
Adhan and Iqamah. But if the rows have dispersed, he must give the Adhan and the
Iqamah."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ الرَّجُلُ يَدْخُلُ
ٱلْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى الْقَوْمُ أَيُوَذِّنُ وَ يُقِيمُ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ دَخَلَ وَ لَمْ يَتَفَرَّقِ الصَّفُ صَلَّى بِأَذَانِهِمْ وَ إِقَامَتِهِمْ وَ إِنْ
كَانَ تَفَرَّقَ الصَّفُ أَذْنَ وَ أَقَامَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.281 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.607 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.430 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.414

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurarah from Isa ibn
Abdullah Al-Hashimi from his father from his grandfather:
(Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Mu'adhdhin is entrusted, and the Imam
is responsible."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ الْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدَّهِ
عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «الْمُؤَذَّنُ مُؤْتَمَنٌ وَ الإِمَامُ ضَامِنْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.282 • Shihab Al-Akhbar, Vol.1 p.74 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.617 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.378
source_scholar: Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurarah from Isa ibn
Abdullah Al-Hashimi from his father from his grandfather:
(Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Mu'adhdhin is entrusted, and the Imam
is responsible."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Sunnah regarding the Adhan on the
Day of Arafah is that the Adhan and Iqamah should be given for Dhuhr, then he should
pray, then he should stand and give the Iqamah for Asr without a new Adhan, and
likewise for Maghrib and Isha at Muzdalifah."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلسُنَّةُ فِي
الأَذَانٍ يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ أَنْ يُوَذِّنَ وَ يُقِيمَ الظُهْرَ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّيَ ثُمَّ يَقُومَ فَيُقِيمَ لِلْعَصْرِ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ وَ كَذَلِكَ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ وَ
الْعِشَاءِ بِمُزْدَلِفَةً ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.282 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.610 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.445
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Sunnah regarding the Adhan on the
Day of Arafah is that the Adhan and Iqamah should be given for Dhuhr, then he should
pray, then he should stand and give the Iqamah for Asr without a new Adhan, and
likewise for Maghrib and Isha at Muzdalifah."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah from Ammar Al-Sabati who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: "It is necessary for the sick person
to give the Adhan and the Iqamah when he wishes to pray, even if it is within himself if
he is not able to speak them."
Imam {a.s} was asked: “And if he is in intense pain?”
Imam {a.s} said: "It is still necessary for him to give the Adhan and the Iqamah, because
there is no prayer without Adhan and Iqamah."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدَّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ
السَّابَاطِيّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلامُ يَقُولُ: «لا بُدَ لِلْمَرِيضِ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ وَ يُقِيمَ إِذَا أَرَادَ الصَّلاةَ وَ لَوْ فِي
نَفْسِهِ إِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ بِهِ» سُئِلَ فَإِنْ كَانَ شَدِيدَ الْوَجَعِ قَالَ «لا بُدَّ مِنْ أَنْ يُؤَذِنَ وَ يُقِيمَ لِأَنَّهُ لاَ صَلاَةَ إِلاّا
بِأَذَانٍ وَ إِقَامَةٍ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.282 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.300 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.609 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.444 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.81 p.130
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn

I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: "It is necessary for the sick person
to give the Adhan and the Iqamah when he wishes to pray, even if it is within himself if

Imam {a.s} was asked: “And if he is in intense pain?”
Imam {a.s} said: "It is still necessary for him to give the Adhan and the Iqamah, because

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Isa who said:
I wrote to Imam {a.s}: “A man upon whom it is obligatory to repeat the prayer, does he
repeat it with Adhan and Iqamah?”
So Imam {a.s} wrote: "He repeats it with Iqamah."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةُ الصَّلاةِ أَيُعِيدُهَا بِأَذَانِ
وَ إقَامَةٍ فَكَتَبَ «يُعِيدُهَا بِإِقَامَةٍ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.446 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.81 p.166
source_scholar: Implicit (Muzmar)
text_chunk:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Isa who said:
I wrote to Imam {a.s}: “A man upon whom it is obligatory to repeat the prayer, does he
repeat it with Adhan and Iqamah?”
So Imam {a.s} wrote: "He repeats it with Iqamah."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Yunus
Al-Shaybani, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam {a.s}: “Should I give the Adhan while riding?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
I asked: “Then should I give the Iqamah while riding?”
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
I asked: “Should I give the Iqamah while my foot is in the stirrup?”
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
I asked: “Should I give the Iqamah while sitting?”
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
I asked: “Should I give the Iqamah while walking?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, while walking towards the prayer."
Imam {a.s} then said: "When you give the Iqamah for prayer, give it calmly, for you are in
the prayer."
I asked: “I had asked you if I could give the Iqamah while walking, and you said yes. So
is it permissible for me to walk during the prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if you enter through the door of the mosque and you say the Takbir
while following a just Imam, then walk to the prayer, that suffices for you. And if the
Imam (of prayer) has already said the Takbir for Ruku', you will catch up with him in the
rak'ah, because if you find him while he is bowing and you did not catch the Takbir with
him, then you would not have caught the Ruku' with him."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ يُونُسَ الشَّيْبَانِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أُوَذِّنُ وَ أَنَا رَاكِبٌ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ فَأَقِيمُ وَ أَنَا رَاكِبٌ قَالَ «لا» قُلْتُ وَ أَقِيمُ وَ رِجْلِي فِي
الرِّكَابٍ قَالَ «لا» قُلْتُ فَأْقِيمُ وَ أَنَا قَاعِدٌ قَالَ «لا» قُلْتُ فَأَقِيمُ وَ أَنَا مَاشٍ قَالَ «نَعَمْ مَاشٍ إلَى الصَّلاَةِ» قَالَ ثُمَّ قَالَ
«إِذَا أَقَمْتَ الصَّلاةَ فَأَقِمْ مُتَرَسِّلاً فَإِنَّكَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ قَدْ سَأَلْثُكَ أَقِيمُ وَ أَنَا مَاشِ قُلْتَ لِي نَعَمْ فَيَجُوزُ أَنْ
أَمْشِيَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ مِنْ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ فَكَبَّرْتَ وَ أَنْتَ مَعَ إِمَامِ عَادِلٍ ثُمَّ مَشَيْتَ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ
أَجْزَأَكَ ذَلِكَ وَ إِذَا كَانَ الْإِمَامُ كَبَّرَ لِلرُّكُوعِ كُنْتَ مَعَهُ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ لِأَنَّهُ إِنْ أَدْرَكْتَهُ وَ هُوَ رَاكِعٌ لَمْ تُدْرِكِ التَّكْبِيرَ لَمْ تَكُنْ
مَعَهُ فِي الرُّكُوعِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.282 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.403
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:

Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT}
bless him and his family, said: "Whoever gives the Adhan in a city among the cities of
the Muslims for one year, Paradise becomes obligatory for him."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ
اللّهِ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «مَنْ أَذَّنَ فِي مِصْرٍ مِنْ أَمْصَارِ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ سَنَةً وَجَبَثْ لَهُ الْجَنَّةُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.285 • Thawab Al-A’mal wa ‘Iqab Al-A’mal, Vol.1 p.31 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.283 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.327 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.567 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.371 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.81 p.146
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
text_chunk:
From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT}
bless him and his family, said: "Whoever gives the Adhan in a city among the cities of
the Muslims for one year, Paradise becomes obligatory for him."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zakariya, the companion
of Al-Sabiri:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Three will be in Paradise surrounded by
the purest musk: a Mu'adhdhin who gave the Adhan seeking reward, an Imam (of
prayer) who led a people and they were pleased with him, and a servant who obeys
Allah {SWT} and obeys his masters."
text_ar:
عَنَهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ زَكَرِيَّا صَاحِبِ السَّابِرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: «ثَلاَثَةٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ عَلَى ٱلْمِسْكِ الْأَذْفَرِ مُؤَذِّنْ أَذَّنَ اِحْتِسَابا وَ إِمَامٌ أَمَّ قَوْما وَ هُمْ بِهِ رَاضُونَ وَ مَمْلُوكٌ يُطِيعُ
اللَّهَ وَ يُطِيعُ مَوَالِيَهُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Bakr ibn Salim, from Sa'd Al-Iskafi who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: "Whoever gives the Adhan for seven
years seeking reward will come on the Day of Judgment without any sin upon him."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ سَعْدِ ٱلْإِسْكَافِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
يَقُولُ: «مَنْ أَذَّنَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ اِحْتِسَاباً جَاءَ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ وَ لا ذَنْبَ لَهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.286 • Thawab Al-A’mal wa ‘Iqab Al-A’mal, Vol.1 p.31 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.283 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.567 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.371 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.374 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.81 p.146 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.81 p.149

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Ahmad from Al-Barqi from Al-Nawfali from Al-Sakuni from (Imam) Ja'far {a.s} from his father {a.s}:
(Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The last thing upon which I parted from the
beloved of my heart (Prophet {saws}), was that He {saws} said:
‘O Ali, when you pray, pray the prayer of the weakest among those behind you, and do
not appoint a Mu'adhdhin who takes a wage for his Adhan.'"
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ عَنِ الْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ النَّوْفَلِيَّ عَنِ السَّكُونِيَّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «آخِرُ مَا فَارَقْتُ عَلَيْهِ
حَبِيبَ قَلْبِي أَنْ قَالَ «يَا عَلِيُّ إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ فَصَلَ صَلاةَ أَضْعَفٍ مَنْ خَلْفَكَ وَ لا تَتَخِذَنَّ مُؤَذّنا يَأْخُذْ عَلَى أَذَانِهِ أَجْراً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.283 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.283 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.592 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.371 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.447

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Isa ibn
Abdullah from his father from his grandfather:
(Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT} (may Allah {SWT}
bless him and his family) said: ‘For the Mu'adhdhin, between the Adhan and the
Iqamah, there is the reward similar to that of a martyr who is covered in his blood in
the way of Allah {SWT}.’"
Imam {a.s} said: "I asked: ‘O Messenger of Allah {SWT}, they strive against one another for
the Adhan!’"
He {saws} said: "No, indeed a time will come upon the people when they will cast the
Adhan upon their weak ones, and those (Mu'adhdhins) will be bodies whose flesh
Allah {SWT} has made forbidden to the Fire."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَسَّانَ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ
عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «قَالَ رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «لِلْمُؤَذِّنِ فِيمَا بَيْنَ ٱلْأَذَانِ وَ الْإِقَامَةِ مِثْلُ أَجْرٍ
الشَّصد المُتَشَحّط بدمه ف سَسا اللَّه»» قَال «قُلْتُ مَا دَسُواَ اللَّه انَّمُمْ يَحْتَلدُه: عَلَ. الْأَذَار قَالَ «كَلاَّ انَّهُ بَأْت
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.283 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.283 • Thawab Al-A’mal wa ‘Iqab Al-A’mal, Vol.1 p.32 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.565 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.372 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.81 p.147

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Mus'ab ibn Salam Al-Tamimi,
from Sa'd ibn Tarif:
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever gives the Adhan for ten years
seeking reward, Allah {SWT} will forgive him for the distance his sight and voice reach into
the sky, and every moist and dry thing that hears him will testify to his truthfulness,
and for every person who prays with him in his mosque, he will have a share, and for
every person who prays upon hearing his voice, he will receive a good deed."
text_ar:
عَنَهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ مُصْعَبِ بْنِ سَلاَّمِ التَّمِيمِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ طَرِيفٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ
عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ أَذِّنَ عَشَرَ سِنِينَ مُحْتَسِباً يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَهُ مَدَّ بَصَرِهِ وَ صَوْتِهِ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَ يُصَدَّقُهُ كُلُّ رَطبٍ
وَ يَابِسِ سَمِعَهُ وَ لَهُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَنْ يُصَلِّي مَعَهُ فِي مَسْجِدِهِ سَهْمٌ وَ لَهُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَنْ يُصَلِّي بِصَوْتِهِ حَسَنَةٌ».
cross_references: Thawab Al-A’mal wa ‘Iqab Al-A’mal, Vol.1 p.32 • Al-Khisal, Vol.2 p.448 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.284 • Rawdat Al-Wa’izin, Vol.2 p.312 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.567 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.372 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.86 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.104 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.4 p.23

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Al-Arzami:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, among the people with the longest
necks on the Day of Resurrection will be the Mu'adhdhins."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنِ الْعَرْزَمِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنَّ مِنْ أَطْوَلِ
اَلنَّاسِ أَعْنَاقاً يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ الْمُؤَذِّنِينَ».
cross_references: Thawab Al-A’mal wa ‘Iqab Al-A’mal, Vol.1 p.31 • Uyun Al-Akhbar, Vol.2 p.61 • Al-Majazat Al- Nabawiyyah, Vol.1 p.93 • Shihab Al-Akhbar, Vol.1 p.74 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.284 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.1 p.328 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.568 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.373 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.376 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol.7 p.303

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far, from his father who said:
A man from the people of Sham entered upon Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him,
and said to Imam {a.s}: "Indeed, the first to precede to Paradise was Bilal."
He asked: "And why is that?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Because he was the first to give the Adhan."
text_ar:
عَثَهُ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمِ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: دَخَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلشَّامِ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السْلاَمُ فَقَالَ لَهُ «إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ سَبَقَ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ بِلالٌ » قَالَ وَ لِمَ قَالَ «لِأَنَّهُ أَوَّلُ مَنْ أَذّنَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.284 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.568 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.373 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.2 2 p.142

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Ja'far who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, about giving the Adhan from the minaret,
is it a Sunnah?
Imam {a.s} said: "The Adhan was given for the Prophet, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his
family, on the ground, and at that time there was no minaret."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الْأَذَانِ
فِي الْمَنَارَةِ أَسُنَّةُ هُوَ فَقَالَ «إِنَّمَا كَانَ يُؤَذَّنُ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَ لَمْ تَكُنْ يَوْمَيِذٍ مَنَارَةٌ».
cross_references: Masa’il Ali Ibn Ja’far, Vol.1 p.233 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.284 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.600 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.230 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.410
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}

From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Ja'far who said:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sarri:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Sunnah is to place your two fingers in
your ears during the Adhan."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ السَّرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «السُّنَّةُ
أَنْ تَضَعَ إصْبَعَيْكَ فِي أُذُتَيْكَ فِي الْأَذَانِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.284 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.600 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.412
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Dharih Al-Muharibi who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to me: "Pray the Friday prayer according to
the Adhan of these people, for they are the most diligent in observing the time."
text_ar:
سَعدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ ذَرِيحِ ٱلْمُحَارِبِيّ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ: «صَلّ
الْجُمُعَةً بِأَذَانِ هَؤلاءِ فَإِنَّهُمْ أَشَدُّ شَيْءٍ مُوَاظَبَةً عَلَى الْوَقْتِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.291 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.284 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.378
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Dharih Al-Muharibi who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to me: "Pray the Friday prayer according to
the Adhan of these people, for they are the most diligent in observing the time."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from
Hammad ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Qasri who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I fear that we might pray on Friday
before the sun passes its zenith.”
Imam {a.s} said: "That responsibility is upon the Mu'adhdhins."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ وَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ
بْنِ خَالِدٍ الْقَسْرِيَّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَخَافُ أَنْ نُصَلِّيَ يَوْمَ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ الشَمْسُ فَقَالَ
«إِنَّمَا ذَاكَ عَلَى الْمُؤَذَّنِينَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.284 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.616 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.379

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Sa'd from Al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Muskan who
said:
I saw Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, give the Adhan and the Iqamah without
separating between them by sitting.
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ أَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ آللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَذَّنَ وَ أَقَامَ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَفْصِلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بِجُلُوسٍ.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.285 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.589 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.399
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

Sa'd from Al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Muskan who

I saw Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, give the Adhan and the Iqamah without
separating between them by sitting.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubayd
ibn Zurarah, from his father who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who forgot the Adhan and the
Iqamah until he had entered into the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should continue with his prayer, for the Adhan is a Sunnah."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا
جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ الْأَذَانَ وَ ٱلْإِقَامَةَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ قَالَ «فَلْيَمْضٍ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَإِنَّمَا الْأَذَانُ
سُنَّةٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.285 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.304 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.622 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.434

From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubayd

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who forgot the
Adhan and the Iqamah until he had entered into the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is nothing upon him."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ سِرْحَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السّلاَمُ :
فِي رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ الْأَذَانَ وَ الْإِقَامَةَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ قَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.285 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.305 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.622 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.434
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who forgot the
Adhan and the Iqamah until he had entered into the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is nothing upon him."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
From him, from Abu Al-Jawza' Munabbih ibn Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
We were with Imam {a.s} when He {a.s} heard the Iqamah of a neighbor for prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "Stand up."
We stood and prayed with Imam {a.s} without Adhan and without Iqamah.
Imam {a.s} said: "The Adhan of your neighbor suffices you."
text_ar:
عَنَهُ عَنْ أَبِي الْجَوْزَاءِ الْمُنَبِّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: كُنَّا مَعَهُ فَسَمِعَ إِقَامَةَ جَارٍ لَهُ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ «قُومُوا» فَقُمْنَا فَصَلَّيْنَا مَعَهُ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ وَ لاَ إِقَامَةٍ قَالَ «يُجْزِيكُمْ
أَذَانُ جَارِكُمْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.285 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.610 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.437
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Abu Al-Jawza' Munabbih ibn Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
We were with Imam {a.s} when He {a.s} heard the Iqamah of a neighbor for prayer.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Imran Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the Adhan at Fajr, whether it should
be before the two rak'ahs or after them.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you are an Imam (of prayer) waiting for a congregation, then the
Adhan should be before them. But if you are alone, it does not harm you whether you
give the Adhan before them or after them."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ الْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ
الْأَذَانٍ فِي الْفَجْرِ قَبْلَ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُمَا فَقَالَ «إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً تَنْتَظِرُ جَمَاعَةً فَالْأَذَانُ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ
فَلاَ يَضُرُّكَ أَ قَبْلَهُمَا أَذَنْتَ أَوْ بَعْدَهُمَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.285 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.616 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.448
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Imran Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the Adhan at Fajr, whether it should
be before the two rak'ahs or after them.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you are an Imam (of prayer) waiting for a congregation, then the
Adhan should be before them. But if you are alone, it does not harm you whether you

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abu Al-Walid Hafs ibn Salim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “When the Mu'adhdhin says ‘Qad qamati
al-salah’ (The prayer has been established), should the people stand on their feet or
should they remain seated until their Imam (of prayer) comes?”
Imam {a.s} said: "No, rather they should stand on their feet. If their Imam (of prayer)
comes, they pray with him. And if he does not come, then a man from among the
people should be taken by the hand and brought forward (to lead the prayer)."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي الْوَلِيدِ حَفْصِ بْنِ سَالِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ إِذَا قَالَ
الْمُؤَذِّنُ قَدْ قَامَتِ الصّلاَةُ أَ يَقُومُ ٱلْقَوْمُ عَلَى أَرْجُلِهِمْ أَوْ يَجْلِسُونَ حَتَّى يَجِيءَ إِمَامُهُمْ قَالَ «لا بَلْ يَقُومُونَ عَلَى
أَرْجُلِهِمْ فَإِنْ جَاءَ إِمَامُهُمْ وَ إِلاَّ فَلْيُوْخَذْ بِيَدِ رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ فَيُقَدَّمَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.285 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1269 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.450 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.379
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Al-Hakam from Abu Al-Walid Hafs ibn Salim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “When the Mu'adhdhin says ‘Qad qamati
al-salah’ (The prayer has been established), should the people stand on their feet or

Imam {a.s} said: "No, rather they should stand on their feet. If their Imam (of prayer)

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE ADHAN AND THE IQAMAH
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu
Ali, the companion of Al-Anmat:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, or Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
"The Adhan is to be given for Dhuhr after six rak'ahs, and the Adhan is to be given for
Asr after six rak'ahs following Dhuhr."
IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيَّ صَاحِبِ الْأَنْمَاطِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلَامُ أَوْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ: «يُؤَذِّنُ لِلظُهْرِ عَلَى سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ يُوَذَّنُ لِلْعَصْرِ عَلَى سِتَّ
رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ».
١٥ - باب كيفية الصلاة وصفتها والمفروض من ذلك والمسنون
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.286 • Falah Al-Sa’il, Vol.1 p.151 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.588 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.449 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.152 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.4 p.52
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al- Kadhim {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib'i ibn Abdullah from Al-
Fudayl ibn Yasar:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "(Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn {a.s}, peace be
upon them, when He {a.s} stood for prayer; his color would change, and when He {a.s}
would prostrate, He {a.s} would not lift his head until He {a.s} would pour with sweat."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ إِذَا قَامَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ تَفَيَّرَ لَوْنُهُ فَإِذَا سَجَدَ لَمْ
يَرْفَعْ رَأْسَهُ حَتَّى يَرْفَضَّ عَرَقاً».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.300 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.286 • Falah Al-Sa’il, Vol.1 p.117 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.846 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.474 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.4 6 p.64 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.4 6 p.79 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.261 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.1 8 p.128
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT
text_en:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “When you face the Qiblah with your face, do
not turn your face away from the Qiblah lest you corrupt your prayer, for Allah {SWT}, the
Exalted, said to His Prophet {saws} regarding the obligatory prayer: "So turn your face
toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it" (Surah
Baqarah 2:144 & 2:150)
And lower your gaze and do not raise it toward the sky, and let it be directed in front of
your face at the place of your prostration.”
text_ar:
علي بن إبراهيم عن أبيه عن حماد عن حريز عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال : إذا استقبلت القبلة
بوجهك فلا تقلب وجهك عن القبلة لتفسد صلاتك فان اللّٰه تعالى قال لنبيه في الفريضة : (فول وجهك شطر
المسحد الحداد محثها كيته فولها محمهكم شطيهل وأخشه يصك ولاتفعه ال السماء مليك. حناء محمك
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "It is proper for one who recites the Qur'an,
when he passes by a verse in the Qur'an that contains a supplication or a warning, that
he should ask at that moment for the best of what he hopes for, and seek safety from
the Fire and from punishment."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثُمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ : «يَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ قَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ إِذَا
مَرَّ بِآيَةٍ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ فِيهَا مَسْأَلَةٌ أَوْ تَخْوِيفٌ أَنْ يَسْأَلَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ خَيْرَ مَا يَرْجُو وَ يَسْأَلَ الْعَافِيَةَ مِنَ النَّارِ وَ مِنَ
الْعَذَابِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.301 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.286 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1743 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.69 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.171 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.3 p.312

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla from Al-Washsha' from Hammad ibn Uthman from Sa'id, the seller
of Al-Sabiri (a type of delicate cloth), who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “Should a man force himself to weep
during the prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Excellent, excellent (is such action); even if it is as little as the size of a
fly's head."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى عَنِ الْوَشَاءِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ بَيَّاعِ السَّابِرِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَيَتَبَاكَى الرَّجُلُ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «بَخْ بَخْ وَ لَوْ مِثْلَ رَأْسِ الذُّبَابِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.301 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.287 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.407 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.879 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.248

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban and Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "When you stand for prayer, say: 'O Allah
{SWT}, indeed I present Muhammad {saws} before my need and I turn towards You {AZJ}
through Him {saws}, so make me, through Him {saws}, honorable in Your {AZJ} presence in
this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near. Make my prayer
accepted, my sin forgiven, and my supplication through Him {saws} answered. Surely
You {AZJ} are the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.'"
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ وَ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالاَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : «إِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى
الصَّلاةِ فَقُلٍ - اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَقَدَّمُ إِلَيْكَ مُحَمَداً بَيْنَ يَدَيْ حَاجَتِي وَ أَتَوَجَّهُ بِهِ إِلَيْكَ فَاجْعَلْنِي بِهِ وَجِيها عِنْدَكَ «فِي
اَلدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ وَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ» اِجْعَلْ صَلاَتِي مَقْبُولَةً وَ ذَنْبِي مَغْفُوراً وَ دُعَائِي بِهِ مُسْتَجَاباً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلْغَفُورُ
الرَّحيم».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.309 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.302 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.287 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.635 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.509 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.370
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Imam (of prayer) suffices with one
Takbir, and it suffices for you to say it three times calmly if you are alone."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: «الْإِمَامُ يُجْزِيهِ تَكْبِيرَةُ وَاجِدَةٌ وَ
يُجْزِيكَ ثَلاَثٌ مُتَرَسِّلاً إِذَا كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.287 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.640 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.10
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the lightest form of Takbir in the
prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "Three Takbirs; and if there is recitation, then you should recite ‘Surah
Al Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al Kafirun’. And if you are the Imam (of prayer), it suffices for you
to pronounce one Takbir aloud and to say six (Takbirs) quietly."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَخَفَّ مَا
يَكُونُ مِنَ التَّكْبِيرِ فِي الصَّلاةِ قَالَ «ثَلاثُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ قِرَاءَةٌ قَرَأْتَ بِ «قُلْ هُوَ اللَهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يَا أَيْهَا
الْكَافِرُونَ» وَ إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَاماً فَإِنَّهُ يُجْزِيكَ أَنْ تُكَبِّرَ وَاحِدَةً تَجْهَرُ فِيهَا وَ تُسِرُّ سِتَّاً ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.287 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.640 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.33
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah
who said:
I saw Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, or he said: “I heard Imam {a.s}, begin the prayer
with seven consecutive Takbirs.
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَامُ أَوْ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ اِسْتَفْتَحَ الصَّلَاَةَ بِسَبْعِ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ وِلاءً.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.287 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.641 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.21
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Sa'd from Abu Ja'far from Musa ibn Al-Qasim Al-Bajali and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother
(Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far {a.s}, peace be upon them both:
(Imam {a.s}) said: "It is upon the Imam (of prayer) to raise his hand during the prayer; it
is not upon anyone else to raise his hand during the prayer."

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “The meaning in this narration is that the action of the
Imam carries greater merit and is more strongly emphasized than the action of the
follower, although the action of the follower also carries merit, as we have explained
previously.”
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ الْبَجَلِيَّ وَ أَبِي قَتَادَةَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ
عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ: «عَلَى الإِمَامِ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ يَدَهُ فِي الصَّلاةِ لَيْسَ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ يَدَهُ فِي الصَّلاةِ».
قال محمد بن الحسن: المعنى في هذا الخبر ان فعل الامام أكثر فضلا وأشد تأكيدا من فعل المأموم ، وإن كان فعل المأموم
أيضا فيه فضل على ما بيناه فيما مضى.
commentary:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “The meaning in this narration is that the action of the
Imam carries greater merit and is more strongly emphasized than the action of the
follower, although the action of the follower also carries merit, as we have explained
previously.”
cross_references: Masa’il Ali Ibn Ja’far, Vol.1 p.257 • Qurb Al-Isnad, Vol.1 p.208 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.287 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.645 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.27 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.362 • Mustadrak Al- Wasa’il, Vol.6 p.512
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from
Misma‘ Al-Basri who said:
I prayed with Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, and Imam {a.s} recited "In the name
of Allah {SWT}, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate” and then ‘Surah Al Fatiha’.
Then Imam {a.s} recited the Surah after Al-Hamd and did not recite "Bismillah Hir
Rahman Nir Rahim."
Then Imam {a.s} stood in the second unit and recited Al-Hamd and did not recite
"Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim" and then recited another Surah.

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “This narration does not contradict what we have
previously presented regarding the emphasis on reciting Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir
Rahim aloud, because it merely reports an action, and it is possible that Misma‘ did
not hear Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, reciting Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim
due to the distance between him and Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.” What
clarifies what we have mentioned is what has been narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مِسْمَعِ الْبَصْرِيِّ قَالَ:
صَلَّيْتُ مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ فَقَرَأً « «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ الْحَمْدُ لِلهِ رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ» » ثُمَّ قَرَأَ السُّورَةَ
اَلْتِي بَعْدَ الْحَمْدِ وَ لَمْ يَقْرَأُ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ » ثُمَّ قَامَ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ فَقَرَأَ الْحَمْدَ وَ لَمْ يَقْرَأ «بِسْمِ اللّهِ الرَّحْمْنِ
الرَّجِيمِ -» ثُمَّ قَرَأَ بِسُورَةٍ أَخْرَى.
قال محمد بن الحسن: لا ينافي هذا الخبر ما قدمناه من تأكيد الجهر ببسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم لانه يتضمن حكاية فعل
ويجوز أن يكون مسمع لم يسمع أبا عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام يقرأ ببسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم لبعد كان بينه وبينه ، والذي يكشف
عما ذكرناه ما رواه :
commentary:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “This narration does not contradict what we have
previously presented regarding the emphasis on reciting Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir
Rahim aloud, because it merely reports an action, and it is possible that Misma‘ did
not hear Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, reciting Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim
due to the distance between him and Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.” What
clarifies what we have mentioned is what has been narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى الْكَاهِلِيَّ

قَنَتَ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ وَ سَلَّمَ وَاحِدَةً مِمَّا يَلِي الْقِبْلَةَ.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Hammad from Hariz
from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who is an Imam (of prayer)
and begins with Al-Hamd without saying "Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim".
Imam {a.s} said: "It does not harm him, and there is no problem with that."

Scholar's Note:
The interpretation of this narration is that it pertains to the situation of taqiyya
(dissimulation), as we have explained, because under taqiyya it is permissible to recite
it quietly, as we have previously mentioned. It is also possible that the narration refers
to someone who omitted saying it out of forgetfulness, and not intentionally.
text_ar:
فَأَمًا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ السِّنْدِيّ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ
أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ إِمَاماً يَسْتَفْتِحُ بِالْحَمْدِ وَ لا يَقُولُ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ -» قَالَ « لا
يَضُرُّهُ وَلا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ».
فالوجه في هذا الخبر حال التقية على ما بيناه لان مع التقية يجوز اخفاته على ما قدمنا القول فيه، ويجوز أن يكون
الخبر تناول من لم يقل ذلك ناسيا دون أن يكون ذلك منه على جهة العمد.
commentary:
The interpretation of this narration is that it pertains to the situation of taqiyya
(dissimulation), as we have explained, because under taqiyya it is permissible to recite
it quietly, as we have previously mentioned. It is also possible that the narration refers
to someone who omitted saying it out of forgetfulness, and not intentionally.

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Al-Abbas from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from
Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about ‘the seven oft-repeated verses’ (al-
Sab‘ al-Mathani) and ‘the Great Qur'an’ (al-Qur’an al-‘Azim), is it Al-Fatiha?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
I asked: “Is ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ among the seven (al-Sab‘ al-Mathani)?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, it is the best of them."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ
أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ السَّبْعِ الْمَثَانِي وَ الْقُرْآنَ الْعَظِيمَ هِيَ الْفَاتِحَةُ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ: «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ
الرَّجِيمِ -» مِنَ السَّبْعِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ هِيَ أَفْضَلُهُنَ».

From him, from Abdul-Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan ibn Sadir who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, and Imam {a.s} sought refuge (with
Allah {SWT}) aloud, then Imam {a.s} recited aloud “Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abdullah ibn
Yahya Al-Kahili:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, from his father {a.s}, said: “Bismillah Hir Rahman
Nir Rahim” is closer to the Greatest Name of Allah {SWT} (al-Ism al-A'zam) than the pupil
of the eye is to its white.
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى الْكَاهِلِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: « «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ » أَقْرَبُ إِلَى اِسْمِ اللَّهِ الْأَعْظَمِ مِنْ نَاظِرِ الْعَيْنِ إِلَى بَيَاضِهَا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
From him, from Ali ibn Al-Sindi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about a man, should he recite aloud in his voluntary (nafl) prayers
during the day?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “This narration is a concession, and it is better that
nothing be recited aloud in the daytime prayers, and that nothing be concealed in the
nighttime prayers.” What indicates this is:
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ السِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ عُثُمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ
هَلْ يَجْهَرُ بِقِرَاءَتِهِ فِي التَّطَوْعِ بِالنَّهَارِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ».
قال محمد بن الحسن : هذه الرواية رخصة والافضل أن لايقرأ شئ في صلوات النهار جهرا ولا يخفي شئ من صلوات الليل
، يدل على ذلك :

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Al-Hasan ibn
Ali ibn Faddal from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The Sunnah in the daytime prayer is to
recite quietly, and the Sunnah in the nighttime prayer is to recite aloud."
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِي بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَ بْنِ فَضَالٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «السُّنَّةُ فِي صَلاَةِ النَّهَارِ بِالْإِخْفَاتِ وَ السُّنَّةُ فِي صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِالْإِجْهَارِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.289 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.313 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.691 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.77

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Sabbah Al-Hadhdha’ from a man from Abu Hamzah who
said:
(Imam) Ali ibn Al-Husayn {a.s}, peace be upon them, said: "O Thumali, when the prayer
is established, Satan comes to the companion of the Imam (of prayer) and says:
'Has he (Imam of Prayer) remembered his Lord {AZJ}?'
If he says, ‘Yes,’ he (Satan) departs.
But if he says, ‘No,’ he (Satan) mounts upon his shoulders and becomes the leader of
the people until they finish."
He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘May I be your ransom, do they not recite the Qur'an?’”
Imam {a.s] said: "Yes, but not in the way you think, O Thumali. What is meant is reciting
aloud ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’".
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَبَّاحِ الْحَذَّاءِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ قَالَ قَالَ عَلِيْ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا
السَّلامُ : «يَا ثُمَالِيْ إِنَّ الصَّلَةَ إِذَا أَقِيمَتْ جَاءَ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَى قَرِينِ الْإِمَامِ فَيَقُولُ هَلْ ذَكَرَ رَبَّهُ فَإِنْ قَالَ نَعَمْ ذَهَبَ
وَ إن قَالَ لا رَكِبَ عَلَى كَتِفَيْهِ فَكَانَ إمَامَ ٱلْقَوْمِ حَتَّى يَنصَرِفُوا» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَ لَيْسَ يَقْرَءُونَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ
قالَ «بَلَى لَيْسَ حَيْثُ تَذْهَبُ يَا تُمَالِيّ إِنَّمَا هُوَ الْجَهْرُ «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمْنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ -» ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.290 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.649 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.75 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.6 0 p.202

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Abdus from Muhammad ibn Zadawayh from Ibn Rashid who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, you wrote to
Muhammad ibn Al-Faraj informing him that the best of what is recited in the obligatory
prayers is ‘Surah Al-Qadr’ and ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’, but my chest feels tight when reciting
them at Fajr.”
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not let your chest be tight with them, for by Allah {SWT}, the virtue lies
within them."
text_ar:
سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُبْدُوسِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زَادَوَيْهِ [زَادَوَيْهِ خ ل] عَنِ اِبْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّكَ كَتَبْتَ إِلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْفَرَجِ تُعْلِمُهُ أَنْ أَفْضَلَ مَا يُقْرَأْ فِي الْفَرَائِضِ - «إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ» وَ
«قُلْ هُوَ اللَهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ إنَّ صَدْرِي لَيَضِيقُ بِقِرَاءَتِهِمَا فِي ٱلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ «لا يَضِيقَنَ صَدْرُك بِهِمَا فَإِنَّ
الْفَضْلَ وَ اللَّهِ فِيهِمَا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about the saying of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, "And do not
raise your voice in your prayer nor lower it too much" (Surah Al-Isra, 17:110).
Imam {a.s} said: "Lowering the voice (mukhafatah) is to recite below the level of your
own hearing, and raising the voice (jahr) is to raise your voice loudly and strongly."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثُمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «وَ لا تَجْهَزْ بِصَلاتِكَ وَ لا
تخافِتْ بِها» قَالَ «الْمُخَافَنَةُ مَا دُونَ سَمْعِكَ وَ الْجَهْرُ أَنْ تَرْفَعَ صَوْتَكَ شَدِيداً».
cross_references: Tafsir Al-’Ayyashi, Vol.2 p.318 • Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.315 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.290 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.689 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.96 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.3 p.599 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.3 p.600 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.72 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.3 p.233 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.7 p.536

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Al-Nawfali from Al-Sakuni:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who is praying in a place
and then wishes to move forward.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should stop reciting while walking until he reaches the place he
intends, then he should resume his recitation."
text_ar:
عَلِيْ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ النَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ السِّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي
مَوْضِعِ ثُمَّ يُرِيدُ أُنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ قَالَ «يَكُفُ عَنِ الْقِرَاءَةٍ فِي مَشِبِهِ حَتَّى يَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَى الْمَوْضِعِ اَلَّذِي يُرِيدُ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.316 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.290 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.697 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.190 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.98

text_chunk:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Al-Nawfali from Al-Sakuni:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who is praying in a place
and then wishes to move forward.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should stop reciting while walking until he reaches the place he
intends, then he should resume his recitation."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Aamir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-
Husayn ibn Uthman from Amr ibn Abi Nasr who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “A man stands in prayer and wants to
recite a Surah, but he recites ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’.
Imam {a.s} said: "He may turn back from any Surah except from ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and
‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."
text_ar:
الحسين بن محمد عن عبد الله بن عامر عن علي بن مهزيار عن فضالة بن أيوب عن الحسين بن عثمان عن
عمرو بن أبى نصر قال قلت لابي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام : الرجل يقوم في الصلاة فيريد أن يقرأ سورة فيقرأ قل
هو الله أحد وقل يا أيها الكافرون فقال : يرجع من كل سورة إلا من قل هو اللّٰه أحد وقل يا أيها الكافرون.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, was asked about a man who recites a verse of
prostration (sajdah) at the end of a Surah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should perform the prostration, then stand, recite the ‘Surah Al-
Fatiha’, then bow (for Ruku') and prostrate."
text_ar:
عَلِي بْنُ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ
الرَّجْلٍ يَقْرَأْ بِالسَّجْدَةِ فِي آخِرِ السُّورَةِ قَالَ «يَسْجُدُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقْرَأْ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ ثُمَ يَرْكَعُ وَ يَسْجُدُ».

Imam {a.s} said: "He should perform the prostration, then stand, recite the ‘Surah Al-

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you pray with a group and the Imam (of
prayer) recites ‘Surah Al-‘Alaq’ or something from the obligatory verses of prostration
(al-‘Aza’im), and he finishes his recitation without performing a prostration, then you
should gesture with an indication (for the prostration), and a woman in menstruation
should prostrate if she hears the verse of prostration."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بَنْ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثِمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنْ صَلَّيْتَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ فَقَرَا الْإِمَامُ - اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ اَلَّذِي خَلَقَ أَوْ شَيْئاً مِنَ الْعَزَائِمِ وَ فَرَغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَتِهِ
وَ لَمْ يَسْجُدْ فَأَوْمِ إِيمَاءً وَ الْحَائِضُ تَسْجُدُ إِذَا سَمِعَتِ السَّجْدَةَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.318 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.291 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.320 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.686 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.103

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who hears a verse of prostration being recited.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should not prostrate unless he is attentively listening to the
recitation or praying behind the one who is reciting. But if he is praying in one area and
you are in another, then do not prostrate for what you heard."
text_ar:
عَلِي بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ رَجْلٍ سَمِعَ السَّجْدَةَ تُقْرَأْ قَالَ «لا يَسْجُدُ إِلَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُنْصِتاً لِلْقِرَاءَةٍ مُسْتَمِعاً لَهَا أَوْ يُصَلِّي بِصَلاَتِهِ
فَأَمَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ يُصَلِّي فِي نَاجِيَةِ وَ أَنْتَ فِي نَاجِيَةِ أُخْرَى فَلا تَسْجُدْ لِمَا سَمِعْتَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.318 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.291 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1749 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.242
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "When you recite something from the obligatory verses of
prostration (al-‘Aza’im) in which prostration is required, do not say the Takbir before
your prostration, but say Takbir when you lift your head. And obligatory prostrations
are four; Surah Fussilat, Surah As-Sajdah, Surah An-Najm, and Surah Al-‘Alaq."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قَرَأْتَ شَيْئاً مِنَ ٱلْعَزَائِمِ
الَّتِي يُسْجَدُ فِيهَا فَلَا تُكَبِّرْ قَبْلَ سُجُودِكَ وَلَكِنْ تُكَبِّرُ حِينَ تَرْفَعُ رَأْسَكَ وَ الْعَزَائِمُ أَرْبَعَةٌ حم السَّجَدَةُ وَ الم تَنْزِيلٌ
وَ اَلنَّجْمُ وَ اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.291 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.239
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
From him, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir who said:
He said: "When something from the four obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im) is recited
and you hear it, then prostrate, even if you are without ablution, even if you are in a
state of major ritual impurity (junub), and even if it is a woman who is not praying. As
for the rest of the Qur'an, you have a choice: if you wish, you may prostrate, and if you
wish, you may not prostrate."
text_ar:
عَنَهُ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ: «إِذَا قُرِئَ شَيْءُ مِنَ الْعَزَائِمِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ
فَسَمِعْتَهَا فَاسْجُدْ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءِ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ جُنُباً وَ إنْ كَانَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ لا تُصَلِّي وَ سَائِرُ ٱلْقُرْآنِ أَنتَ فِيهِ
بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شِنْتَ سَجَدْتَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ لَمْ تَسْجُدْ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.318 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.291 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1749 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.2 p.341 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.240

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
As for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdul-Rahman
ibn Abi Abdullah from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a menstruating woman, does she recite the Qur'an and perform
the prostration if she hears a verse of prostration?
Imam {a.s} said: "She may recite but she does not prostrate."

Scholar's Note:
Thus, the first narration is not contradicted, because the first narration is to be
understood as recommending (the prostration) out of desirability, while this narration
is to be understood as permitting the omission of it, and there is no contradiction
between them. As for what was narrated:
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْحَائِضِ هَلْ تَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ وَتَسْجُدُ سَجَدَةً إِذَا سَمِعَتِ السَّجْدَةَ قَالَ « تَقْرَأُ وَ لا تَسْجُدُ».
فلا ينافي الخبر الاول لان الخبر الاول محمول على الاستحباب وهذا الخبر محمول على جواز تركه ولا تنافي بينهما، واما
ما رواه :
commentary:
Thus, the first narration is not contradicted, because the first narration is to be
understood as recommending (the prostration) out of desirability, while this narration
is to be understood as permitting the omission of it, and there is no contradiction
between them. As for what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abu Al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (narrated) from his father {a.s}, from (Imam) Ali {a.s},
peace be upon him, said: "If the prostration is at the end of the Surah, it suffices you
to bow (perform Ruku') for it."

Scholar's Note:
Thus, this does not contradict the narration of Al-Halabi mentioned earlier, because
this narration is understood to refer to one who is praying with a group and cannot
perform the prostration, stand up, and then recite Al-Hamd; in that case, there is no
harm in him bowing (with them). As for the narration of Al-Halabi and others who
reported similarly, it is understood to refer to one who is able to do so, such as when
he is praying individually. What supports this interpretation is what was narrated:
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْبَخْتَرِيِّ وَهْبِ بْنِ وَهْبِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ
عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا كَانَ آخِرُ السُّورَةِ السَّجْدَةَ أَجْزَأَكَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ بِهَا».
فلا ينافي خبر الحلبي المقدم ذكره لان هذا الخبر نحمله على من يصلي مع قوم لا يمكنه أن يسجد ويقوم ويقرأ الحمد
فانه لا بأس أن يركع معهم ، وخبر الحلبي وغيره ممن روى ذلك محمول على من تمكن من ذلك بأن يكون منفردا يدل على
ذلك ما رواه :
commentary:
Thus, this does not contradict the narration of Al-Halabi mentioned earlier, because
this narration is understood to refer to one who is praying with a group and cannot
perform the prostration, stand up, and then recite Al-Hamd; in that case, there is no
harm in him bowing (with them). As for the narration of Al-Halabi and others who
reported similarly, it is understood to refer to one who is able to do so, such as when
he is praying individually. What supports this interpretation is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah:
He said: "Whoever recites ‘Iqra' bismi Rabbik’ (Surah Al-‘Alaq), when he finishes it, he
should prostrate, and when he stands up, he should recite the ‘Opening of the Book’
(Surah Al-Fatiha) and then bow."
He said: "And if you are tested with this situation while praying behind an Imam who
does not perform the prostration, then gesturing and bowing suffices for you, and do
not recite it in an obligatory prayer; recite it in a voluntary prayer."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: «مَنْ قَرَأَ اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِذَا خَتَمَهَا فَلْيَسْجُدْ فَإِذَا قَامَ
فَلْيَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ وَ لَيَرْكَعْ» قَالَ «وَ إِنِ أبْثَلِيتَ بِهَا مَعَ إِمَامِ لا يَسْجُدُ فَيُجْزِيكَ الْإِيمَاءُ وَ الرُكُوعُ وَ لا تَقْرَأ فِي
اَلْفَرِيضَةِ اِقْرَأْ فِي التَّطَوْعِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.292 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.686
source_scholar: Implicit (Muzmar)
text_chunk:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah:
He said: "Whoever recites ‘Iqra' bismi Rabbik’ (Surah Al-‘Alaq), when he finishes it, he
should prostrate, and when he stands up, he should recite the ‘Opening of the Book’
(Surah Al-Fatiha) and then bow."
He said: "And if you are tested with this situation while praying behind an Imam who
does not perform the prostration, then gesturing and bowing suffices for you, and do
not recite it in an obligatory prayer; recite it in a voluntary prayer."

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "When you recite a verse of prostration,
then prostrate, and do not say the Takbir until you lift your head."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةً قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ : «إِذَا قَرَأْتَ السِّجْدَةَ فَاسْجُدْ وَ لا تُكَبِّرْ
حَتَّى تَرْفَعَ رَأْسَكَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.292 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1750 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.240
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "When you recite a verse of prostration,

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
From him, from Safwan, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon
them, said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who recites a verse of prostration and forgets it until he
bows and prostrates.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should prostrate when he remembers, if it was from the obligatory
prostrations (al-‘Aza’im)."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسَّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ السَّجْدَةَ فَيَنْسَاهَا
حَتَّى يَركَعَ وَ يَسْجُدَ قَالَ «يَسْجُدُ إِذَا ذَكَرَ إِذَا كَانَتْ مِنَ الْعَزَائِمِ ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.292 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.686 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.104 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.61

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Sa'd from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from
Ammar ibn Musa Al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who hears a verse of
prostration at a time when prayer is not valid, before the setting of the sun and after
the prayer of Fajr.
Imam {a.s} said: "He does not prostrate."
And (Imam {a.s} said) regarding a man who recites in an obligatory prayer a Surah that
contains a verse of prostration from the obligatory prostrations (al-‘Aza’im).
Imam {a.s} said: "When he reaches the place of the prostration, he should not recite it,
and if he wishes, he may go back and recite another Surah and leave the one that
contains the prostration, thus turning to another one."
And (Imam {a.s} said) regarding a man who prays among a group without following them
and prays for himself, and they might recite a verse from the obligatory prostrations
but they do not prostrate therein, what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He does not prostrate."
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدَّقِ بْنِ صَدَفَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى
اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ : فِي الرَّجْلِ يَسْمَعُ السِّجْدَةَ فِي السَّاعَةِ اَلَّتِي لا يَسْتَقِيمُ الصَّلَاَةُ فِيهَا قَبْلَ
غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ وَ بَعْدَ صَلاَةِ الْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ «لا يَسْجُدُ » وَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأْ فِي الْمَكْتُوبَةِ سُورَةً فِيهَا سَجْدَةٌ مِنَ
الْعَزَائِمِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا بَلَغَ مَوْضِعَ السَّجْدَةِ فَلا يَقْرَأُهَا وَ إِنْ أَحَبَ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ فَيَقْرَأَ سُورَةً غَيْرَهَا وَ يَدَعَ الَّتِي فِيهَا
السَّجْدَةُ فَيَرْجِعُ إِلَى غَيْرِهَا» وَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي مَعَ قَوْمٍ لا يَقْتَدِي بِهِمْ فَيُصَلِّي لِنَفْسِهِ وَ رُبَّمَا قَرَءُوا آيَةً مِنَ
الْعَزَائِم فَلا يَسْجُدُونَ فِيهَا فَكَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «لا يَسْجُدُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.293
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn Al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja'far
{a.s}, peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about an imam (of prayer) who recites a verse of prostration and then
becomes impure (loses his ablution) before he performs the prostration, what should
he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should appoint another person to lead; that person should perform
the tashahhud, prostrate, and then they should all finish their prayer, and the Imam
(of prayer) who became impure should withdraw, and the prayer of the congregation
is complete."
text_ar:
أحمَدُ بَنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ
عَنْ إِمَام قَرَأَ السَّجْدَةَ فَأَحْدَثَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يُقَدِّمُ غَيْرَهُ فَيَتَشَهَدُ وَ يَسْجُدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ هُوَ وَ قَدْ
تَمَّثْ صَلاَتُهُمْ».
cross_references: Masa’il Ali Ibn Ja’far, Vol.1 p.255 • Qurb Al-Isnad, Vol.1 p.205 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.293 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.687 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.106 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.240 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.427 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.15

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far
{a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who is being taught a Surah that contains an obligatory
prostration (from the 'Aza’im), and it is repeated to him several times in a single sitting.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is obligatory upon him to prostrate each time he hears it, and it is
also obligatory upon the one teaching him to prostrate."
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ بْنِ رَزِينِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ
الرَّجْلٍ يُعَلَّمُ السُّورَةَ مِنَ الْعَزَائِمِ فَتُعَادُ عَلَيْهِ مِرَاراً فِي الْمَقْعَدِ الْوَاحِدِ قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ كُلَّمَا سَمِعَهَا وَ عَلَى
الَّذِي يُعَلَّمُهُ أَيْضا أَنْ يَسْجَدَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.293 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1750 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.245 • Al- Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.3 p.320 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.179

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurarah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (was asked) regarding a man who intends to
recite a Surah but then recites another one instead.
Imam {a.s} said: "He is allowed to return (to the intended Surah) as long as he has not
recited two-thirds of it."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ
: فِي الرَّجْلِ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ السُورَةَ فَيَقْرَأَ غَيْرَهَا فَقَالَ «لَهُ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ أَنْ يَقْرَأْ ثُلْثَيْهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.293 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.674 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.101 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.17

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him: “A man recites a Surah in a rak'ah and
makes a mistake, should he leave the place where he made the mistake and continue
in his recitation, or should he leave that Surah and move to another Surah?”
Imam {a.s} said: "All of that is permissible; and if he recites even a single verse and then
wishes to bow with it, he may bow."

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: “This narration is to be understood as referring to the
supererogatory (nafl) prayers, because we have already explained that in the
obligatory (fard) prayer, it is not permissible to recite less than a complete Surah along
with Al-Hamd.” As for what was narrated:
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ قَرَأَ سُورَةً فِي
رَكْعَةٍ فَغَلِطَ أَيَدَعُ الْمَكَانَ آلَّذِي غَلِطَ فِيهِ وَ يَمْضِي فِي قِرَاءَتِهِ أَوْ يَدَعُ تِلْكَ السُورَةَ وَ يَتَحَوَّلُ مِنْهَا إِلَى غَيْرِهَا
فَقَالَ «كُلُ ذَلِكَ لا بَأْسَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ قَرَأَ آيَةً وَاجِدَةً فَشَاءَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ بِهَا رَكَعَ».

obligatory (fard) prayer, it is not permissible to recite less than a complete Surah along
with Al-Hamd.” As for what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yasin Al-Basri from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, was asked about a Surah, can a man pray with it
in the two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if it consists of six verses, he may recite half of it in the first rak'ah
and the other half in the second rak'ah."

Scholar's Note:
Thus, this narration is to be understood as referring to a situation of taqiyya
(dissimulation), because it agrees with the view of the general public (al-‘amma). What
indicates this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
سَعدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يَاسِينَ الْبَصْرِيِّ عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلَاَمُ
: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ السُّورَةِ أَيُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ بِهَا فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْفَرِيضَةِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ إِذَا كَانَتْ سِنَّ آيَاتٍ قَرَأَ بِالنِّصْفِ
مِنْهَا فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى وَ النَّصْفِ الْآخَرِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ».
فهذا الخبر محمول على ضرب من التقية لانه موافق لمذهب العامة ، والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه :
commentary:

(dissimulation), because it agrees with the view of the general public (al-‘amma). What
indicates this is what was narrated:

Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yasin Al-Basri from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, was asked about a Surah, can a man pray with it
in the two rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if it consists of six verses, he may recite half of it in the first rak'ah
and the other half in the second rak'ah." Scholar's Note:
Thus, this narration is to be understood as referring to a situation of taqiyya
(dissimulation), because it agrees with the view of the general public (al-‘amma). What
indicates this is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn Al-Fadl:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, and Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, prayed
with us, and they {a.s} recited the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha) and the end of
Surah Al-Ma'idah.
When they finished and gave the salam, they turned to us and said:
"Indeed, I only intended to teach you."
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ
اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ وَ أُبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ فَقَرَأْ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَ آخِرٍ سُورَةِ الْمَائِدَةِ فَلَمَا سَلَمَ اِلْتَفَتَ إِلَيْنَا فَقَالَ
«أَمَا إِنَّي إِنَّمَا أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُعَلَّمَكُمْ ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.294 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.316 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.677 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.46 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.28

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from
Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “What do you say about a man who is praying while looking
into the Mushaf, reading from it, and placing a lamp close to him?”
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with that."
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ
عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ زِيَادِ الصِّيْقَلِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ يَنْظُرُ فِي
الْمُصْحَفِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِ يَضَعُ السِّرَاجَ قَرِيباً مِنْهُ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.294 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.699 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.107 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.298

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about reciting behind the Imam (of
prayer) in the last two rak'ahs.
Imam {a.s} said: "The Imam (of prayer) recites the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-
Fatiha), and those behind him should glorify (say tasbih). If you are praying alone, then
you may either recite (Surah Al-Fatiha) in them or, if you wish, you may glorify."
text_ar:
عَلِي بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ عَنِ الْقِرَاءَةِ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَجِيرَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ «الإِمَامُ يَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ وَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا
كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَاقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا وَ إنْ شِئْتَ فَسَبَّحْ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.319 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.294 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.776 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.108
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, ITS DESCRIPTION AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about what the Imam (of prayer) recites
in the last two rak'ahs of the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He recites the ‘Opening of the Book’ (Surah Al-Fatiha), and those
behind him do not recite. And a man who is praying alone recites Al-Fatiha in them."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ السِّنْدِيَّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ آللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَمَّا يَقْرَأُ ٱلْإِمَامُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فِي آخِرِ الصّلاةِ فَقَالَ » بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَ لا يَقْرَأُ الَّذِينَ خَلْفَهُ وَ يَقْرَأْ
الرَّجُلُ فِيهِمَا إِذَا صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.295 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.777 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.108
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
