text_chunk:
my family, and I intend to travel, so I do not pray until I depart?” Imam {a.s} said: “Pray and shorten the prayer. And if you do not do so, then by Allah {SWT}, you have opposed the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family.” Scholar's Note:
If someone were to say: ‘Why do you say that if the time still remains after one returns
from travel, it becomes obligatory upon him to perform the prayer in full, and likewise
for the one who sets out for travel if the time still remains, he must shorten the prayer?
Whereas the report is unrestricted and simply states that whoever sets out for travel
after the time has entered must shorten (the prayer), and likewise, whoever returns
from travel must complete it. There is no mention in the report of considering whether
the time remains?!
We say: ‘We considered the remaining time so that the reports do not contradict one
another because we have already presented narrations stating that whoever departs
for travel after the entry of the prayer time must perform it in full.
And likewise, (there are narrations stating) that one who returns from travel must
shorten (the prayer).
And then came this report stating that whoever sets out for travel after the entry of the
prayer time must shorten (the prayer), and that whoever returns from travel after the
entry of the prayer time must complete it.
Therefore, we were compelled to reconcile these reports.
So we interpreted every narration that states; whoever sets out for travel after the entry
of time must perform it in full as referring to when the time has already passed.
And likewise, in the case of one who returns from travel.
And every narration that states; whoever sets out for travel after the entry of time must
shorten (the prayer) we interpreted it to mean, ‘if the time still remains’.
And the same applies to one who returns from travel.
So that the reports do not contradict one another. And what clarifies what we have
mentioned is the narration of Hariz that was cited earlier.
He (Hariz) said: “I said to Imam {a.s},
‘A man misses a prayer while on a journey, then remembers it while in residence’.”
Imam {a.s} said:
“He must make up what he missed in the same manner as it was missed.
If it was a prayer of travel, he performs it in residence in the same manner.
And if it was a prayer of residence, then let him make it up while traveling as a prayer
of residence.”
So this narration serves as an explanation for all the reports, because Imam {a.s} said:
“Whoever misses a prayer, let him make it up as it was missed.”
And the one who returns from travel while the time still remains has not yet missed the
prayer, and likewise, the one who departs for travel while the time still remains has not
yet missed the prayer.
And what also clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Ala ibn Razin from Muhammad
ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams {a.s}, peace be upon them:
Imam {a.s} was asked concerning a man who returns from a journey and the time of
prayer enters upon him.
Imam {a.s} said: “If he does not fear that the time will end, then let him enter and perform
it in full. But if he fears that the time will expire before he enters, then let him pray and
shorten (the prayer).”

Scholar's Note:
So, in this narration, the Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, encouraged that if one does
not fear the passing of the prayer time when delaying the prayer until he enters his
home, then he should delay it so that he may perform it in full.
If the expiration of the time were not a consideration in this matter, then there would
be no meaning in restricting the performance of the prayer in full to this specific
condition.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “A traveller should not
lead a resident in prayer, nor should a resident lead a traveller. The preferable and
better course is that a traveller should not pray behind a resident, nor a resident
behind a traveller. But if they do so, they have only abandoned what is better, and their
prayers are valid. And whenever a traveller prays behind a resident, he should pray two
rak’ahs and then leave. And if a traveller leads a group in prayer, he should lead them
in two rak’ahs, then appoint someone else to complete the prayer with them, and he
himself should leave.”
And what indicates what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنْ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيْوبَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا
عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ : فِي الرّجُلِ يَقْدَمُ مِنَ الْغَيْبَةِ فَيَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهِ وَقْتُ الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ لاَ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ ٱلْوَقْتُ
فَلْيَدْخُلْ فَلْيُتِمَّ وَ إِنْ كَانَ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ الْوَقْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فَلْيُصَلٌ وَ لَيُقَصِّرْ».
فرغب عليه السلام بهذا الخبر في ان من لم يخف فوت الوقت في تأخير الصلاة حتى يدخل البيت يؤخرها حتى يؤديها
على التمام، فلولا ان فوت الوقت كان مراعى في هذا الباب لم يكن لتقييد الاتمام بهذه الحال معنى. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه
: ولا يؤم المسافر الحاضر ولا الحاضر المسافر، الاولى والافضل ان لا يصلي المسافر خلف المقيم ولا المقيم خلف المسافر
، فان فعلا ذلك تركا الافضل وجازت صلاتهما ، ومتى صلى المسافر خلف المقيم يصلي ركعتين ولينصرف. وإذا صلى
المسافر بالقوم يصلي بهم ركعتين ثم يقدم من يتم الصلاة بهم ولينصرف هو. والذي يدل على ما ذكرناه ما رواه:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja’far from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from
Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “A resident should not lead a traveller in prayer, nor should a
traveller lead a resident.
But if one is put in a situation where this occurs, and he (the traveller) leads a group of
residents in prayer, then when he completes two rak’ahs, he should give salam and
then take the hand of one of them and bring him forward to lead them.
And if a traveller prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer as
two rak’ahs and give salam.
And if he prays Dhuhr with them, then let him consider the first two rak’ahs as Dhuhr
and the latter two as Asr.”
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ الْحُصَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ الْفَضْلِ
بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ قَالَ: «لا يَوُمُ ٱلْحَضَرِيُ ٱلْمُسَافِرَ وَ لاَ ٱلْمُسَافِرُ الْحَضَرِيَّ فَإِنِ أُبْثُلِيّ
بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَمَّ قَوْما حَاضِرِينَ فَإِذَا أَنَمَّ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ سَلَمَ ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِيَدِ بَعْضِهمْ فَقَدَّمَهُ فَأَمَّهُمْ وَ إِذَا صَلَّى ٱلْمُسَافِرُ
خَلْفَ قَوْمِ حُضُورِ فَلْيُتِمَ صَلاَتَهُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُسَلَّمُ وَ إِنْ صَلَّى مَعَهُمُ ٱلظُهْرَ فَلْيَجْعَلِ ٱلْأُولَيَيْنِ ٱلظُهْرَ وَ الْأُخْرَبَيْنِ
الْعصرَ».

And from him, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu al-Miza
Humayd ibn al-Muthanna from Imran from Muhammad ibn Ali:
(Muhammad ibn Ali) asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a traveller who
enters into prayer with residents.
Imam {a.s} said: “Let him perform his (own) prayer, then give salam, and make the last
two (rak’ahs) supererogatory (nafila) prayer.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ اللُوْلُوِيِّ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَالٍ عَنْ أَبِي ٱلْمِعْزَى حُمَيْدِ بْنِ ٱلْمُثَنَّى عَنْ عِمْرَانَ
عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ : أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الرّجُلِ الْمُسَافِرِ إِذَا دَخَلَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ مَعَ الْمُقِيمِينَ قَالَ
«فَلْيُصَلّ صَلاَتَهُ ثُمَّ لْيُسَلَّمْ وَ لَيَجْعَلِ الْأَخْرَبَيْنِ سُبْحَةً».

Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Husayn ibn Uthman from Abdillah ibn Muskan from Abu

Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “The traveller should not pray with the

الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mualla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha from
Aban ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazid. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays with the imam
(of prayer) and catches two rak’ahs of the prayer. Does that suffice him?
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ - عَنِ ٱلْمُسَافِرِ يُصَلِّي مَعَ ٱلْإِمَامِ فَيُدْرِكُ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَيُجَزِي ذَلِكَ عَنْهُ
فَقَالَ »نَعَمْ».

Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mualla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha from
Aban ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazid. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays with the imam
(of prayer) and catches two rak’ahs of the prayer. Does that suffice him?

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Maruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from
Abdillah ibn Muskan and Muhammad ibn al-Numan al-Ahwal from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He
said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “If a traveller joins a group of residents in their prayer, then if it
is the first (Dhuhr) prayer, let him make the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs.
And if it is the Asr prayer, let him make the first two (rak’ahs) supererogatory and the
last two obligatory.”

Scholar's Note:
The understanding of this hadith is that Imam {a.s} only said, ‘If it is Dhuhr, let him make
the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs,’ because when he does so, it becomes
permissible for him to make the last two rak’ahs into the Asr prayer.
And when it is the Asr prayer, he makes the last two rak’ahs his prayer, because it is
disliked to pray after Asr except as make-up (qadah).
So, whoever prays as we have described, nothing remains upon him, and the (extra)
rak’ahs are counted for him among the supererogatory (nafl) prayers.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “A person performing
tayammum should not lead those who have performed wudu, and likewise, one who
has performed wudu should not lead those performing tayammum.”
This matter is similar to the previous one, in that it is preferable that a person
performing tayammum not lead those who have performed wudu.
But if he does so, his prayer is not invalidated by that; rather, he has merely abandoned
what is more virtuous.”
As for what indicates the dislike (karahah) of that, it is what was narrated:
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ وَ
مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلنُّعْمَانِ الْأَحْوَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا دَخَلَ الْمُسَافِرُ مَعَ أَقْوَامِ حَاضِرِينَ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ
فَإِنْ كَانَتِ الْأُولَى فَلْيَجْعَلِ الْفَرِيضَةَ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ الْعَضْرُ فَلْيَجْعَلِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً وَ الْأَجِيرَتَيْنِ
فَرِيضَةٌ».
وفقه هذا الحديث انه انما قال ان كانت الظهر فليجعل الفريضة في الركعتين الاولتين لانه متى فعل ذلك جاز له ان يجعل
الركعتين الاخيرتين صلاة العصر، وإذا كان صلاة العصر انما يجعل الركعتين الاخيرتين صلاته لانه يكره الصلاة بعد صلاة
العصر إلا على جهة القضاء، ومن صلى على ما قلناه لم يبق عليه شئ ويحتسب به من النوافل. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : ولا
يؤم المتيمم المتوضئين ولا يؤم المتوضى ، المتيممين. وهذه المسألة مثل الاولى في ان الاولى ان لا يؤم المتيمم
المتوضئين ولو فعل ذلك لم يكن بذلك مبطلا لصلاته لكنه يكون قد ترك الافضل، فاما الذي يدل على كراهة ذلك ما رواه:
commentary:
The understanding of this hadith is that Imam {a.s} only said, ‘If it is Dhuhr, let him make
the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs,’ because when he does so, it becomes
permissible for him to make the last two rak’ahs into the Asr prayer.
And when it is the Asr prayer, he makes the last two rak’ahs his prayer, because it is
disliked to pray after Asr except as make-up (qadah).
So, whoever prays as we have described, nothing remains upon him, and the (extra)
rak’ahs are counted for him among the supererogatory (nafl) prayers.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “A person performing
tayammum should not lead those who have performed wudu, and likewise, one who
has performed wudu should not lead those performing tayammum.”
This matter is similar to the previous one, in that it is preferable that a person
performing tayammum not lead those who have performed wudu.
But if he does so, his prayer is not invalidated by that; rather, he has merely abandoned
what is more virtuous.”
As for what indicates the dislike (karahah) of that, it is what was narrated:

source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Maruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from
Abdillah ibn Muskan and Muhammad ibn al-Numan al-Ahwal from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He
said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “If a traveller joins a group of residents in their prayer, then if it
is the first (Dhuhr) prayer, let him make the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs.
And if it is the Asr prayer, let him make the first two (rak’ahs) supererogatory and the
last two obligatory.” Scholar's Note:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abbad ibn Suhayb. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “A person performing tayammum
should not lead a group who have performed wudu.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ صُهَيْبٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ
يَقُولُ: «لا يُصَلِّي الْمُتَيَمَّمُ بِقَوْمِ مُتَوَضِّئِينَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.166 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.424 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1177 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.328
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abbad ibn Suhayb. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “A person performing tayammum
should not lead a group who have performed wudu.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-
Sakuni from Imam Ja’far {a.s}, from his father Imam al-Baqir {a.s}, peace be upon them, said:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “A person who performs tayammum should not lead those who
have performed wudu, and a person afflicted with paralysis (al-falij) should not lead
those who are healthy.”

Scholar's Note:
If it is said: ‘The apparent meaning of these two narrations is that it is not permissible
for one performing tayammum, to lead those who have performed wudu at all.
So why did you interpret them as indicating mere dislike (karahah), rather than
prohibition (hurmah)?’
We say: ‘We did so because there are numerous narrations that explicitly indicate the
permissibility of this, so we were compelled to reconcile them.
Among those is what was narrated:’
text_ar:
وَرَوَى مُحَمّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِبِهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ السَّكُونِيّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ
عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «لا يَؤُمُّ صَاحِبُ التَّيَمُمِ ٱلْمُتَوَضَّئِينَ وَ لا يَؤْمُ صَاحِبُ ٱلْفَالِجِ الْأَصِحَاءَ».
فان قيل : ظاهر هذين الخبرين انه لا يجوز ان يؤم المتيمم المتوضئين على وجه فلم حملتم على الكراهة دون الحضر!!؟.
قلنا : انما فعلنا ذلك لورود اخبار كثيرة تتضمن جواز ذلك فاحتجنا ان نجمع بينها فمن ذلك ما رواه :
commentary:
If it is said: ‘The apparent meaning of these two narrations is that it is not permissible
for one performing tayammum, to lead those who have performed wudu at all.
So why did you interpret them as indicating mere dislike (karahah), rather than
prohibition (hurmah)?’
We say: ‘We did so because there are numerous narrations that explicitly indicate the
permissibility of this, so we were compelled to reconcile them.
Among those is what was narrated:’

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said concerning a man who enters a state of janabah (major ritual
impurity) and has no water, and he is the imam (of prayer) of the people.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, he performs tayammum and leads them in prayer.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيِى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلاَمُ
: فِي الرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ مَاءُ وَ هُوَ إِمَامُ الْقَوْمِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ يَتَيَمَّمُ وَ يَوْمُّهُمْ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.424 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.544 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.328
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said concerning a man who enters a state of janabah (major ritual
impurity) and has no water, and he is the imam (of prayer) of the people.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, he performs tayammum and leads them in prayer.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
And among them is what was narrated by Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn
ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdillah ibn Bukayr. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s} about a man who entered a state of janabah, then performed
tayammum and led us in prayer while we were in a state of full purity.
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in it.”
text_ar:
وَمِنْهُ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ
بُكَيْرِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَجْتَبَ ثُمَّ تَيَمَّمَ فَأَمَّنَا وَ نَحْنُ طَهُورٌ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.424 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.327
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
And among them is what was narrated by Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn

I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s} about a man who entered a state of janabah, then performed

Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in it.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from
Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj. They said:
I said to Aba Abdillah {a.s}: “An imam (of prayer) of a group, who becomes junub (ritually
impure due to major impurity) during travel, and does not have enough water for ghusl,
should someone among them who has wudu lead them in prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: “No. Rather, the one in a state of janabah should perform tayammum
and lead them in prayer, for Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Exalted, has made the earth a
purifier.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ وَ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ
قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ إِمَامُ قَوْمٍ أَصَابَثْهُ جَنَابَةٌ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ مِنَ ٱلْمَاءِ مَا يَكْفِيهِ لِلْغُسْلِ أَ
يَتَوَضَّا بَعْضُهُمْ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهمْ فَقَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ تَيَمَّمَ ٱلْجُنُبُ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ جَعَلَ التَّرَابَ طَهُوراً».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.66 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.109 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.425 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.543 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.386 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.327

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
And from him, from Abu Ja’far from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
I said to Imam {a.s}: “A man led a group in prayer while he was in a state of janabah and
had performed tayammum, while they were in a state of full purification (taharah).”
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in it.”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And a missed prayer
is to be made up with adhan and iqamah, if a person missed them.”
We have already presented what indicates this, and what further clarifies it is what
was narrated:
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ أَمَّ قَوْماً وَ هُوَ جُنْبٌ وَ قَدْ تَيَمَمَ وَ هُمْ عَلَى طَهُورِ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : وتقضى الصلاة بالاذان والاقامة إذا فات الانسان ذلك. فقد قدمنا ما يدل على ذلك وبزيده بيانا ما
رواه :
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And a missed prayer
is to be made up with adhan and iqamah, if a person missed them.”
We have already presented what indicates this, and what further clarifies it is what
was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amru ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who repeats a prayer does he also repeat
the adhan and the iqamah?
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes.”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah
{SWT} have mercy on him, said: “Missed
supererogatory prayers (nawafil) may be made up at any time, except during the time
of an obligatory prayer, or at sunrise or sunset. And it is disliked to make up nawafil
during the yellowing of the sun until it sets.”
What has preceded contains comprehensive evidence for this, and what further
clarifies it is what was narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ
السَابَاطِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ الرَّجْلِ إِذَا أَعَادَ الصَّلاَةَ هَلْ يُعِيدُ الْأَذَانَ وَ الْإِقَامَةَ قَالَ «نَعَمْ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : وتقضى فوائت النوافل في كل حال ما لم يكن وقت فريضة أو عند طلوع الشمس أو عند غروبها ،
ويكره قضاء النوافل عند اصفرار الشمس حتى تغيب.
فقد مضى فيما تقدم ما يدل عليه مستوفى ، ويزيد ذلك وضوحا ما رواه:
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah
{SWT} have mercy on him, said: “Missed
supererogatory prayers (nawafil) may be made up at any time, except during the time
of an obligatory prayer, or at sunrise or sunset. And it is disliked to make up nawafil
during the yellowing of the sun until it sets.”
What has preceded contains comprehensive evidence for this, and what further
clarifies it is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn
Yahya ibn Habib. He said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I have missed the supererogatory
prayers (nafilah), when should I make them up?”
So Imam al-Ridha {a.s} wrote: “Whenever you wish by night or by day.”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “A traveller is not
obligated to make up what he shortened from the obligatory prayer or the
supererogatory prayers, except for obligatory fasting, for that must be made up.”
It has been established by what we have mentioned earlier, that the prayer of a
traveller, whether from the obligatory or supererogatory acts, is limited to what we
have specified. So whenever a person performs that amount, he is not required to
make up what was neither obligatory upon him nor recommended to do. And this
much is sufficient on the matter.
What further affirms this is also what was narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى بْنِ حَبِيبِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى
أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ تَكُونُ عَلَيَّ الصَّلاةُ النَّافِلَةُ مَتَى أَقْضِيهَا فَكَتَبَ «أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : ولا يجب على المسافر قضاء ما قصر فيه من فريضة ولا نافلة إلا المفروض من الصيام فانه لابد من
قضائه. إذا ثبت بما قدمنا ذكره ان صلاة المسافر من الفرائض. النوافل هو القدر الذي ذكرنا فمتى فعله الانسان لا يلزمه
قضاء ما لم يفرض عليه ولم يندب إليه وهذا القدر كاف في هذا الباب ويؤكد ذلك ايضا ما رواه:

have specified. So whenever a person performs that amount, he is not required to
make up what was neither obligatory upon him nor recommended to do. And this
much is sufficient on the matter.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-
Rahman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before
them nor after them, except for Maghrib.
For after Maghrib, are four rak’ahs; do not leave them out whether in residence or
travel. And there is no make-up upon you for the daytime prayers, but pray the night
prayer and make it up (if missed).”

Scholar's Note:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And one who
completes (the prayer as four rak’ahs) while traveling, out of forgetfulness, must
repeat the prayer if the time still remains; but if the time has passed, then there is no
repetition upon him. However, whoever deliberately performs the prayer in full while
traveling, after the proof for shortening has been established for him, his prayer is not
valid and he must repeat it.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونَسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ
عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: «الصَلاَةُ فِي السَّفَرِ رَكْعَتَانِ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّ
بَعْدَهَا أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ لاَ تَدَعْهُنَّ فِي حَضَرٍ وَ لا سَفَرٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ صَلاَةِ النَّهَارِ وَ صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَ اِقْضِهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : والمتمم في السفر ناسيا يعيد إن كان الوقت باقيا وان خرج الوقت فلا اعادة عليه، ومن تعمد التمام
في السفر بعد الحجة عليه في التقصير لم يجزه ذلك ووجب عليه الاعادة.
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And one who
completes (the prayer as four rak’ahs) while traveling, out of forgetfulness, must
repeat the prayer if the time still remains; but if the time has passed, then there is no
repetition upon him. However, whoever deliberately performs the prayer in full while
traveling, after the proof for shortening has been established for him, his prayer is not
valid and he must repeat it.”

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-Is
ibn al-Qasim. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who was traveling and
performed the prayer in full.
Imam {a.s} said: “If it is still within the time (of the prayer), then he should repeat it. But
if the time has already passed, then no (he does not need to repeat it).”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ ٱلْعِيصِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا
عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ فَأْتَمَ الصَّلاَةَ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَلْيُعِدْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ الْوَقْتُ
قَدْ مَضَى فَلاَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RULINGS OF MISSED PRAYERS
text_en:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Numan from Suwayd al-Qalla from Abu Ayyub from
Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who forgets and prays four rak’ahs while
traveling.
Imam {a.s} said: “If he remembers on the same day, then let him repeat (the prayer). But
if he does not remember until that day has passed, then there is no repetition upon
him.”

Scholar's Note:
So this narration is to be understood as indicating a form of recommended
(mustahabb) action, while the first one indicates obligation (wujub).
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “You must face the
qiblah on a ship and pray standing if you are able; otherwise, (you may pray) sitting.
If the ship turns, you should turn your face toward the qiblah.
But if, after having initially faced it, the ship turns and you are unable to determine the
qiblah due to the movement, then your initial direction suffices, and you continue to
face wherever it turns.
And if the qiblah becomes unclear to you in supererogatory prayers or after seeking its
indications, then you should face the front of the ship and pray while it is ascending or
descending and however it turns.”
-----
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ عَنْ سُوَيْدِ الْقَلاءِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرّجُلِ يَنْسَى فَيُصَلِّي فِي السَّفَرِ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ ذَكَرَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ فَلْيْعِذْ
وَ إنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمُ فَلاَ إعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ».
فهذا الخبر محمول على ضرب من الاستحباب والاول على الوجوب.
١١ - باب صلاة السفينة
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : وتتوجه إلى القبلة في السفينة وتصلي قائما ان قدرت وإلا جالسا، وإذا دارت السفينة ادرت وجهك
إلى القبلة، فان عدمت معرفة القبلة بعد توجهك بدورانها اجزأك التوجه الاول ودرت معها حيث دارت ، وإذا التبست القبلة
عليك في النوافل أو بعد طلب علاماتها عليك توجهت إلى رأس السفينة فصليت مصعدة ومنحدرة وكيف دارت.
commentary:
So this narration is to be understood as indicating a form of recommended
(mustahabb) action, while the first one indicates obligation (wujub).

qiblah on a ship and pray standing if you are able; otherwise, (you may pray) sitting.

And if the qiblah becomes unclear to you in supererogatory prayers or after seeking its
indications, then you should face the front of the ship and pray while it is ascending or
descending and however it turns.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, being asked about prayer on a ship.
Imam {a.s} said: “If you are able to go out onto dry land, then go out. But if you are not
able, then pray standing, and if you cannot, then pray sitting. And strive to face the
qiblah.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يُسْأَلُ
عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي السَّفِينَةِ فَيَقُولُ «إِنِ اِسْتَطَعْثُمْ أَنْ تَخْرُجُوا إِلَى الْجَدَدِ فَاخْرُجُوا وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا فَصَلُوا قِيَاماً وَ
إِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا فَصَلُوا قُعُوداً وَ تَحَرَّوُا الْقِبْلَةَ».

text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, being asked about prayer on a ship.
Imam {a.s} said: “If you are able to go out onto dry land, then go out. But if you are not
able, then pray standing, and if you cannot, then pray sitting. And strive to face the
qiblah.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Ibrahim said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about prayer on a boat.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray while sitting if he is unable to stand in the boat, and he
should not pray in the boat if he is able to reach the shore.”
And Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray in the boat, turning his face towards the qiblah,
then he may continue the prayer however the boat turns.”
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةً عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ
فِي السَّفِينَةِ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ إِذَا لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ ٱلْقِيَامُ فِي السَّفِينَةِ وَ لا يُصَلِّي فِي السَّفِينَةِ وَ هُوَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى
الشَّطَّ» وَ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي فِي السَّفِينَةِ يُحَوِّلُ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي كَيْفَ مَا دَارَثْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “We were afflicted with a situation, and
we were on a boat, and evening came upon us while we were unable to find a place
where we could disembark.”
So Imam {a.s} said: “The people of the boat do not pray during the day, as long as they
hope to disembark.”
Then Imam {a.s} said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir {a.s}) used to say:
‘That is the prayer of Nuh {a.s}, peace be upon him.’
And are you not pleased to pray the prayer of Nuh {a.s}?”
I said: “Yes, may I be your ransom.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Do not let your heart be constricted, for Nuh {a.s} prayed on the boat.”
I asked: “While standing or sitting?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Rather, (it was whilst) standing.”
I asked: “Sometimes I face the qiblah, then the boat turns.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Strive to face the qiblah with the best of your effort.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ إِنَّا أُبْثُلِينَا وَ كُنَّا فِي سَفِينَةٍ فَأَمْسَيْنَا
وَ لَمْ نَقْدِرْ عَلَى مَكَانٍ نَخْرُجُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ «أَصْحَابُ السَّفِينَةِ لَيْسَ نُصَلِّي يَوْمَنَا مَا دُمْنَا نَطْمَعُ فِي الْخُرُوجِ» فَقَالَ
«إِنَّ أَبِي كَانَ يَقُولُ «تِلْكَ صَلاَةُ نُوحِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ» أَوَ مَا تَرْضَى أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ صَلاَةَ نُوحِ » فَقُلْتُ بَلَى جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ
قَالَ «لا يَضِيقَنَ صَدْرُكَ فَإنَّ نُوحاً قَدْ صَلَّى فِي السَّفِينَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ قَائِماً أَوْ قَاعِداً قَالَ «بَلْ قَائِماً» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنِّي
رُبَّمَا اِسْتَقْبَلْتُ الْقِبْلَةَ فَدَارَتِ السَّفِينَةُ قَالَ «تَحَرَّ الْقِبْلَةَ بِجَهْدِكَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.170 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.526 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.506

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid.
He (Sulayman) said: “I asked Imam {a.s} about prayer on a boat.”
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray while standing, and if he is unable to stand, then let
him sit and pray while facing the qiblah.
If the boat turns, then let him turn with the qiblah if he is able to do so, and if he is not
able to do so, then let him remain in his place and strive to face the qiblah with the
best of his effort.”
And Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray the supererogatory prayer facing the front of the
boat, while he is facing the qiblah when he says the takbir, and it does not harm him
wherever the boat turns afterward.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي السِّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ «يُصَلِّي
قَائِماً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعِ الْقِيَامَ فَلْيَجْلِسْ وَ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ فَإِنْ دَارَتِ السَّفِينَةُ فَلْيَدُرْ مَعَ الْقِبْلَةِ إِنْ قَدَرَ
عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَلْيَثْبُتْ عَلَى مَقَامِهِ وَ لَيَتَحَرَّ الْقِبْلَةَ بِجُهْدِهِ» وَ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي النَّافِلَةَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ
صَدْرِ السَّفِينَةِ وَ هُوَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ إِذَا كَبَّرَ ثُمَّ لا يَضُرُّهُ حَيْثُ دَارَتْ).
٨٦٢ 27

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq
from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about prayer on a boat.
Imam {a.s} said: “If it is loaded and heavy, such that when you stand in it, it does not
sway, then pray standing. But if it is light and sways, then pray sitting.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ حَمْرَةَ الْغَنَوِيَّ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي السَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَتْ مُحَمَّلَةً تَقِيلَةً إِذَا قُمْتَ فِيهَا لَمْ
تَتَحَرَّك فَصَلّ قَائِما وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ خَفِيفَةً تَكَفَّأ فَصَلٌ قَاعِداً».
١٢ - باب صلاة الخوف

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the prayer of fear.
Imam {a.s} said: “The imam (of prayer) stands, and a group from among his companions
comes and stands behind him, while another group positions themselves facing the
enemy. Then the imam (of prayer) leads that group in one rak’ah, then he stands and
they stand with him, and he remains standing while they complete the second rak’ah.
Then they give salam to one another and depart, and they go to take the place of their
companions. Then the others come and stand behind the imam (of prayer), and he
leads them in the second rak’ah, then the imam (of prayer) sits, and they (the second
group) stand and pray another rak’ah, then he gives salam to them, and they depart
with one taslimah.”
Imam {a.s} said: “And in Maghrib, it is similar to that; the imam (of prayer) stands, and a
group comes and stands behind him, and he leads them in prayer. Then he stands and
they stand, and the imam (of prayer) remains standing, and they pray two rak’ahs, then
recite the tashahhud and give salam to one another. Then they depart and go to the
position of their companions, and the others come and take the place of their
companions behind the imam (of prayer). Then he prays one rak’ah with them, reciting
in it, then he sits and recites the tashahhud. Then he stands and they stand with him,
and he prays with them another rak’ah. Then he sits, and they stand and pray another
rak’ah, then he gives salam to them.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ آللَّهِ
عَ عَنْ صَلاَةِ الْخَوْفِ قَالَ «يَقُومُ ٱلْإِمَامُ وَ يَجِيءُ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَهُ وَ طَائِفَةٌ بِإِزَاءِ الْعَدُوَّ فَيُصَلِّي
بِهِمُ الْإِمَامُ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقُومُونَ مَعَهُ فَيَمْثُلُ قَائِما وَ يُصَلُونَ هُمُ ٱلرَكْعَةَ الثَّانِيَةَ ثُمَّ يُسَلَّمُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ
ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَقَامِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ يَجِيءُ ٱلْآخَرُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمُ الرَكْعَةَ الثَانِيَةَ
ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ الْإِمَامُ وَ يَقُومُونَ هُمْ فَيُصَلُونَ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يُسَلَّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَتصَرِفُونَ بِتَسْلِيمَةِ» قَالَ «وَ فِي ٱلْمَغْرِبِ
مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ يَقُومُ الْإِمَامُ وَ تَجِيءُ طَائِفَةٌ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَهُ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقُومُونَ فَيَمْثَلُ الْإِمَامُ قَائِمَاً وَ
يُصَلُونَ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَتَشَهَدُونَ وَ يُسَلَّمُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضِ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَوْقِفِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ يَجِيءُ
الْآخْرُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَوْقِفٍ أَصْحَابِهِمْ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً يَقْرَأُ فِيهَا ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَقُومُ وَ
يَقُومُونَ مَعَهُ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَقُومُونَ هُمْ فَيُصَلُونَ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يُسَلَّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam,
from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his
family, prayed the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) with his companions in the
expedition of Dhat al-Riqa.
Prophet {saws} divided his companions into two groups;
He {saws} placed one group facing the enemy, and the other group behind him. He {saws}
said the takbir, and they said the takbir, then He {saws} recited and they listened.
Then He {saws} bowed and they bowed, and He {saws} prostrated and they prostrated.
Then the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, stood
upright, and they completed one rak’ah for themselves.
Then some of them gave salam to others, then they went to their companions and
stood facing the enemy,
And their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah
{SWT} bless him and his family. Then Prophet {saws} prayed one rak’ah with them, then
recited the tashahhud and gave salam to them. Then they stood and completed one
rak’ah for themselves and gave salam to one another.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلّى رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِأَصْحَابِهِ فِي غَزَاةِ ذَاتٍ
الرِّقَاعِ صَلَاةَ الْخَوْفِ فَفَرّقَ أَصْحَابَهُ فِرْقَتَيْنِ أَقَامَ فِرْقَةً بِإِزَاءِ الْعَدُوِّ وَ فِرْقَةً خَلْفَهُ فَكَبَّرَ وَ كَبَّرُوا فَقَرَأَ وَ أَنْصَثُوا
فَرَكَعَ وَ رَكَعُوا وَ سَجَدَ فَسَجَدُوا ثُمَّ اِسْتَتَمَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَائِماً وَ صَلَّوْا لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ رَكْعَةَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ
بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ أَقَامُوا بِإِزَاءِ الْعَدُوِّ وَ جَاءَ أَصْحَابُهُمْ فَقَامُوا خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى
اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَصَلّى بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ تَشَهْدَ وَ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَامُوا فَصَلُّوْا لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ رَكْعَةً وَ سَلَّمَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.456 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.172 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1064 • Tafsir Al-Safi, Vol.1 p.494 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.544 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.3 p.527
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
text_chunk:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam,
from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his
family, prayed the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) with his companions in the
expedition of Dhat al-Riqa.
Prophet {saws} divided his companions into two groups;
He {saws} placed one group facing the enemy, and the other group behind him. He {saws}
said the takbir, and they said the takbir, then He {saws} recited and they listened.
Then He {saws} bowed and they bowed, and He {saws} prostrated and they prostrated.
Then the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, stood
upright, and they completed one rak’ah for themselves.
Then some of them gave salam to others, then they went to their companions and
stood facing the enemy,
And their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah
{SWT} bless him and his family. Then Prophet {saws} prayed one rak’ah with them, then
recited the tashahhud and gave salam to them. Then they stood and completed one
rak’ah for themselves and gave salam to one another.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Hammad from Abu Basir. He said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: “If you are in a land of fear and you fear a thief or a wild
beast, then pray the obligatory prayer while you are on your mount.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنْ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِنْ كُنْتَ فِي
أَرْضِ مَخَافَةٍ فَخَشِيتَ لِصَّا أَوْ سَبُعاً فَصَلِّ الْفَرِيضَةَ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى دَابَّتِكَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.456 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.465 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.172 • Tafsir Al-Safi, Vol.1 p.269 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.442 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.239 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.2 p.370

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who fears a wild beast or a
thief, how should he pray?
Imam {a.s} said: “He should say the takbir and gesture with his head.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَخَافُ
مِنْ سَبُعٍ أَوْ لِضِّ كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ «يُكَبِّرُ وَ يُومِئُ بِرَأْسِهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.173 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1072 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.442

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn
ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah. He said:
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “The one who fears thieves and wild beasts
should perform the prayer of those in dangerous situations, by gesturing while on his
mount.”
I (Zurarah) asked: “What if the person in such a situation, is not in a state of ablution
and is unable to dismount, what should he do?”
Imam {a.s} said: “He performs tayammum from the felt of his saddle or from his mount
or from the mane of his mount, for there is dust in it, and he performs the prayer, and
makes his prostration lower than his bowing.
He does not turn toward the qibla, but rather wherever his mount turns except that he
must face the qibla for the first takbirah when he begins the prayer.”
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ
عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السّلاَمُ: «الَّذِي يَخَافُ اللَصُوصَ وَ السّبُعَ يُصَلِّي
صَلاةَ الْمُوَاقَفَةِ إِيمَاءً عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ أْرَأَيْتَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلْمُوَاقِفُ عَلَى وُضُوءِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ وَ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى
النْزُولِ قَالَ «يَتَيَمَّمُ مِنْ لِبْدِ سَرْجِهِ أَوْ دَابَّتِهِ أَوْ مِنْ مَعْرَفَةِ دَابَّتِهِ فَإِنَّ فِيهَا غُبَاراً وَ يُصَلِّي وَ يَجْعَلُ السَّجُودَ أَخْفَضَ
مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ وَ لَا يَدُورُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ وَ لَكِنْ أَيْنَمَا دَارَتْ دَابَّتُهُ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ يَسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةَ بِأَوَّلِ تَكْبِيرَةِ جِينَ يَتَوَجَّهُ».
١٣ - باب صلاة المطاردة والمسايفة

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER DURING PURSUIT AND SWORD FIGHTING
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, Fudayl, and Muhammad
ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “In the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) during pursuit,
skirmishes, and the intensification of fighting, each person among them should pray
by gesturing, wherever his face is.
But when there is close combat, grappling, and intense fighting, then indeed the
Commander of the Faithful {a.s}, peace be upon him, on the night of Siffin and it was the
night of al-Harir, had not led them in Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha at the time of each
prayer; except with takbir (‘Allahu Akbar’), tahlil (‘La ilaha illa Allah’), tasbih
(‘SubhanAllah’), tamjid (‘Al-hamdu lillah’), and supplication.
So that was their prayer, and Imam Ali {a.s} did not command them to make up the
prayer.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُدَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ فُضَيْلٍ وَ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «فِي صَلاَةِ ٱلْخَوْفِ عِنْدَ ٱلْمُطَارَدَةِ وَ ٱلْمُنَاوَشَةِ وَ تَلاَحُمِ ٱلْقِتَالِ فَإِنَّهُ يُصَلِّي كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ مِنْهُمْ بِالْإِيمَاءِ
حَيْثُ كَانَ وَجْهُهُ فَإِذَا كَانَتِ ٱلْمُسَايَفَةُ وَ ٱلْمُعَانَقَةُ وَ تَلاَحُمُ ٱلْقِتَالِ فَإِنَّ أَمِيرَ ٱلْمُوْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ لَيْلَةَ صِفِّينَ وَ
هِيَ لَيْلَةُ ٱلْهَرِيرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ صَلَّى بِهِمُ ٱلظُهْرَ وَ ٱلْعَصْرَ وَ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ وَ الْعِشَاءَ عِنْدَ وَقْتِ كُلِّ صَلاّةِ إِلاَّ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ وَ التَّهْلِيلِ
وَ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ وَ التَّمْجِيدِ وَ الدُّعَاءِ فَكَانَتْ تِلْكَ صَلاَتَهُمْ وَ لَمْ يَأْمُرْهُمْ بِإِعَادَةِ الصَّلاةِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.457 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.173 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1068 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.445 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.3 2 p.605
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Amir al-Mu’minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al- Murtadha {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER DURING PURSUIT AND SWORD FIGHTING
text_en:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about the prayer during combat.
Imam {a.s} said: “When they meet and engage in fighting, then at that time, the prayer is
only with takbir. And if they are standing still, then the prayer is by gesturing.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ ٱلْقِتَالِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا اِلْتَقَوْا فَاقْتَتَلُوا فَإِنَّمَا الصَّلاَةُ
جينَئِذٍ بِالتَكْبِيرٍ وَ إِذَا كَانُوا وُقُوفا فَالصَّلاَةُ إِيمَاءَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.174
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about the prayer during combat.
Imam {a.s} said: “When they meet and engage in fighting, then at that time, the prayer is
only with takbir. And if they are standing still, then the prayer is by gesturing.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER DURING PURSUIT AND SWORD FIGHTING
text_en:
Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from
Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The prayer during a march (of war), is performed at noon with
gesturing by your head and with takbir,
And during sword fighting, it is with takbir along with gesturing,
And during pursuit it is by gesturing each man prays individually in his position.”
text_ar:
عَبْدِ
سَعدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي
اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «صَلَاَةُ الزَّحْفِ عَلَى الظَّهْرِ إِيمَاءُ بِرَأْسِكَ وَ تَكْبِيرٌ وَ الْمُسَايَفَةُ تَكْبِيرٌ مَعَ إِيمَاءِ وَ الْمُطَارَدَةُ
إِيمَاءُ يُصَلِّي كُلُّ رَجُلٍ عَلَى جِيَالِهِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.466 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.174 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1069 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.443 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.86 p.110
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from
Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The prayer during a march (of war), is performed at noon with

And during sword fighting, it is with takbir along with gesturing,
And during pursuit it is by gesturing each man prays individually in his position.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER DURING PURSUIT AND SWORD FIGHTING
text_en:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, and from Ayyub
ibn Nuh from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah. He said: One of our companions narrated to me from Abu Abdillah
{a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The minimum that suffices in the case of close combat
(musayafah), in terms of takbir, is two takbirs for each prayer except for the Maghrib
prayer, for it requires three.”
OTHER SUCH CASES
IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND OTHER SUCH CASES

Scholar's Note:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “The one swimming in
water, at the time of drowning or due to necessity of swimming, should pray by
gesturing toward qibla if he knows its direction; otherwise, in the direction of his face.
His bowing should be lower than his prostration, because bowing is a form of lowering,
and prostration is gesturing toward qibla. And likewise is prayer of one stuck in mud.”.
-----
text_ar:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ وَ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوحِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي
بَعْض أَصْحَابِنَّا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلامُ قَالَ: «أَقَلُ مَا يُجْزِي فِي حَدّ ٱلْمُسَايَفَةِ مِنَ التَّكْبِيرِ تَكْبِيرَتَانِ لِكُلِّ
صَلاَةٍ إِلاَّ صَلاَةَ ٱلْمَعْرِبِ فَإِنَّ لَهَا ثَلاَثا».
١٤ - باب صلاة الغريق والمتوحد والمضطر بغير ذلك
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : ويصلي السابح في الماء عند غرقه أو ضرورته إلى السباحة مؤميا إلى القبلة ان عرفها ، وإلا ففي
وجهه ويكون ركوعه اخفض من سجوده لان الركوع انخفاض منه والسجود إيماء إلى القبلة وكذلك صلاة المتوحل.
commentary:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “The one swimming in
water, at the time of drowning or due to necessity of swimming, should pray by
gesturing toward qibla if he knows its direction; otherwise, in the direction of his face.
His bowing should be lower than his prostration, because bowing is a form of lowering,
and prostration is gesturing toward qibla. And likewise is prayer of one stuck in mud.”.
-----

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir. He said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever is in a place where he is unable
to reach the ground, should gesture with indications.”
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ :
«مَنْ كَانَ فِي مَكَانٍ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَلْيُومِ إِيمَاءَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO
text_en:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who gestures in the obligatory and
supererogatory prayers, when he does not find anything to prostrate upon and does
not have a place in which he can perform prostration.
Imam {a.s} said: “If it is like that, then let him gesture throughout the entire prayer.”
OTHER SUCH CASES
text_ar:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدَّقٍ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ
مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُومِ فِي الْمَكْتُوبَةِ وَ النَّوَافِلِ إِذَا لَمْ يَجِدْ مَا يَسْجُدَ
عَلَيْهِ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مَوْضِعْ يَسْجُدُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ هَكَذَا قَلْيُومِ فِي الصَّلاَةِ كُلِّهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.175 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.141 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.450

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
And with this same chain of transmission, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, he said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who is caught in the rain, while in a place where
he is unable to prostrate, due to mud and does not find a dry spot.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should begin the prayer, and when he bows, let him bow as he
would normally do in prayer.
And when he raises his head from the bowing, let him gesture for the prostration while
standing. He should continue in this manner until he completes the prayer, perform
the tashahhud while standing, and give the salam.”

Scholar's Note:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And if he is restrained by
shackles or something similar, he should pray according to his ability.”
text_ar:
وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصِيبْهُ ٱلْمَطَرُ وَ هُوَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ لا يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ فِيهِ
مِنَ الطَّينِ وَ لاَ يَجِدُ مَوْضِعاً جَافّاً قَالَ «يَفْتَتِحُ الصَّلاَةَ فَإِذَا رَكَعَ فَلْيَرْكَعْ كَمَا يَرْكَعُ إِذَا صَلَّى وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ
الرُّكُوعِ فَلْيُومِ بِالسُّجُودِ إِيمَاءً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنَ الصَّلاَةِ وَ يَتَشَهَدُ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ يُسَلَّمُ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : وإذا كان ممنوعا بالرباط وما أشبهه صلى بحسب استطاعته.
commentary:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And if he is restrained by
shackles or something similar, he should pray according to his ability.”
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.175 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1051 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.142

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his
father from Zur’ah from Sama’ah. He said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about a prisoner taken captive by the polytheists, and the time of
prayer comes, while the one who captured him, prevents him from performing it.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should gesture with indications.”
OTHER SUCH CASES

Scholar's Note:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And the sick person prays
standing if he is able,” up to his statement: “and it is disliked.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ
عَنِ الْأَسِيرِ يَأْسِرُهُ الْمُشْرِكُونَ فَتَحْضُرُهُ الصَّلاةُ فَيَمْنَعُهُ الَّذِي أَسَرَهُ مِنْهَا قَالَ «يُومِنُ إِيمَاءَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : والمريض يصلي قائما مع قدرته. إلى قوله : ويكره.
commentary:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And the sick person prays
standing if he is able,” up to his statement: “and it is disliked.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah from Ammar from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “If the sick person is unable to pray sitting, then he should pray
however he is able, either by being positioned and gesturing with indications.” And
Imam {a.s} said: “He should be positioned as a man is positioned in his grave, and lie on
his right side, then gesture for the prayer.
If he is unable to lie on his right side, then however he is able, it is permissible for him.
He should face the qibla with his face, then gesture for the prayer by indication.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «الْمَرِيضُ إِذَا لَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ قَاعِداً كَيْفَ قَدَرَ صَلَّى إِمَّا أَنْ يُوَجِّهَ فَيُومِئُ إِيمَاءَ»
وَ قَالَ «يُوَجَّهُ كَمَا يُوَجَّهُ الرَّجُلُ فِي لَحْدِهِ وَ يَنَامُ عَلَى جَنْبِهِ الْأَيْمَنِ ثُمَّ يُومِئُ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَنْ يَنَامَ عَلَى
جَنْبِهِ الْأَيْمَنِ فَكَيْفَ مَا قَدَرَ فَإِنَّهُ لَهُ جَائِزٌ وَ يَسْتَقْبِلُ بِوَجْهِهِ الْقِبْلَةَ ثُمَّ يُومِئُ بِالصَّلاَةِ إِيمَاءَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.175 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1043 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.483 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.81 p.337

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from
someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The sick person prays standing, and if he is unable to do that,
he prays sitting.
If he is unable to do that, he prays lying on his back he pronounces the takbir, then
recites. When he wishes to bow, he closes his eyes, then glorifies (‘SubhanAllah’).
When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is considered
his rising from bowing.
When he wishes to prostrate, he closes his eyes, then glorifies. When he has glorified,
he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is considered his rising from
prostration. Then he recites the tashahhud and ends the prayer.”
OTHER SUCH CASES
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَمَّنْ حَدَّتَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «يُصَلِّي الْمَرِيضُ قَائِماً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ صَلَّى جَالِساً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ صَلَّى مُسْتَلْقِياً
يُكَبِّرُ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأْ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ الرُّكُوعَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا سَبَّحَ فَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ فَيَكُونُ فَتَحُهُ عَيْنَيْهِ رَفْعَهُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ
الرُّكُوعِ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ غَمَضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا سَبَّحَ فَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ فَيَكُونُ فَتَحُهُ عَيْنَيْهِ رَفْعَهُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ
السُجُودِ ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ».

text_en:
And from him, from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “Do not hold your turban while you are praying, and do not lean
against a wall unless you are ill.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا ثُمْسِكْ بِخَمَرِكَ وَ أَنْتَ تُصَلِّي وَ لا تَسْتَنِذْ
إلَى جِدَارٍ إِلَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ مَرِيضاً».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.176 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.900 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.500

text_chunk:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar. He said:
I asked Imam al-Hadi {a.s} about a person who falls unconscious for a day or more than
that, does he make up the prayers he missed?
Imam {a.s} wrote: “He does not make up the fasts, nor does he make up the prayers.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَارِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْماً أَوْ
أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ هَلْ يَقْضِي مَا فَانَهُ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ فَكَتَبَ «لا يَقْضِي الصَّوْمَ وَ لا يَقْضِي الصَّلاةَ».

chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub by Ali from his father from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Hamzah by Abu Ja’far {a.s}:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} was asked regarding the saying of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic:
“Those who remember Allah {SWT} standing” (Surah Aal Imran 3:191)
Imam {a.s} said: “The healthy one prays ‘standing’. ‘And sitting’ (Surah Aal Imran 3:191),
for the sick person prays sitting. ‘And on their sides’ (Surah Aal Imran 3:191), for the
one who is weaker than the sick person who prays sitting.”
OTHER SUCH CASES

Scholar's Note:
Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And it is disliked for him to
place his forehead on a prayer mat held by someone else, or on a fan.”
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي قَوْلٍ
اللّه عَزّ وَ جَلَّ «آَلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللهَ قِياما» قَالَ «الصَّجِيحُ يُصَلِّي قَائِماً «وَقُعُوداً» الْمَرِيضُ يُصَلِّي جَالِساً «وَ عَلى
جُنُوبِهم» اَلَّذِي يَكُونْ أَضْعَفَ مِنَ ٱلْمَرِيضِ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي جَالِساً».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : ويكره له وضع الجبهة على سجادة يمسكها غيره ومروحة.

place his forehead on a prayer mat held by someone else, or on a fan.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Husayn from Sama’ah from Abu Basir. He said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about a sick person, can a woman hold something for him to
prostrate upon?
Imam {a.s} said: “No, unless he is in a state of necessity, having no one else with him
and nothing else available. There is nothing that Allah {SWT} has forbidden except that
He {AZJ} has made it permissible, for the one who is compelled to it.”
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمَرِيضِ هَلْ ثُمْسِكُ لَهُ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ
شَيْئاً يَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ «لا إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُضْطَرَاً لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ غَيْرُهَا وَ لَيْسَ شَيْءُ مِمَّا حَرَّمَ آللَّهُ إِلا وَ قَدْ أَحَلْهُ لِمَنِ
أضْطُرَ إِلَيْهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon
him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir {a.s} about the (prayer of a) sick person.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should prostrate on the ground, or on a fan, or on a tooth-stick
(siwak), something he raises up that is better than gesturing.
Those who disliked prostration on a fan, only disliked it because of the idols that used
to be worshipped besides Allah {SWT}.
And we have never worshipped anyone other than Allah {SWT}, ever. So prostrate on a
fan, or on a tooth-stick, or on a piece of wood.”
OTHER SUCH CASES
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْمَرِيضِ قَالَ
«يَسْجُدُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ أَوْ عَلَى مِرْوَحَةٍ أَوْ عَلَى سِوَاكٍ يَرْفَعُهُ هُوَ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ الإيمَاءِ إِنَّمَا كَرِهَ مَنْ كَرِهَ السُّجُودَ عَلَى
الْمِرْوَحَة مِنْ أَجْلِ الْأَوْثَانِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ تُعْبَدُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَ إِنَّا لَمْ نَعْبُدْ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ قَطْ فَاسْجُدْ عَلَى الْمِرْوَحَةِ أَوْ عَلَى
سِوَاكٍ أَو عَلَى عُودٍ».

text_en:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from someone who informed him from Abu
Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} was asked: “What is the degree of illness that compels its sufferer,
and what is the illness in which its sufferer should leave off praying while standing?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Rather, man is a witness against himself.” (Surah Al Qiyamah 75:14)
Imam {a.s} said: “That is up to him, he is more knowledgeable about himself.”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَمَّنُ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : أَنَّهُ سُيْلَ مَا حَدُ ٱلْمَرَضِ الَّذِي
يُضْطَرُ صَاحِبُهُ وَ ٱلْمَرَضِ الّذِي يَدَعُ صَاحِبُهُ فِيهِ الصَّلاَةَ قَائِما قَالَ « «بَلِ ٱلْإِنْسَانُ عَلىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةُ» قَالَ ذَاكَ
إِلَيْهِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِنَفْسِهِ».

text_en:
And from him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Jamil, and from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “What is the degree of illness for which a
person should pray sitting?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Indeed, a man may suffer fever or be wounded, but he knows himself
best. If he has the strength, then let him stand (for prayer).”
text_ar:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ مَا حَدْ
الْمَرَضِ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي صَاحِبُهُ قَاعِداً فَقَالَ «إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيُوعَكُ وَ يُجْرَحُ وَ لَكِنَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِنَفْسِهِ إِذَا قَوِيَ فَليَقُمْ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from Bakkar. He said:
My father, spoke to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, and asked Imam {a.s} while I
(Bakkar) was listening:
“What is the degree of illness in which fasting is to be abandoned?”
Imam {a.s} said: “When he is unable to partake in the pre-dawn meal (suhur).”
OTHER SUCH CASES
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ بَكَارِ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ أَبِي يَعْنِي أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ وَ أَنَا أَسْمَعُ
مَا حَدُّ الْمَرَضِ الَّذِي يُثْرَكُ فِيهِ الصَّوْمُ قَالَ «إِذَا لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ يَتَسَحِّرَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE DROWNING PERSON, THE ONE WHO IS ALONE, AND THE ONE IN NECESSITY, AND
text_en:
Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi. He said:
The Jurist (Faqih), Imam al-Hadi {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
“The sick person is to pray sitting only when he reaches the condition, in which he is
unable to walk the length of his prayer, from beginning to end while standing.”
text_ar:
الصِّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْص الْمَرْوَزِيّ قَالَ قَالَ ٱلْفَقِيهُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ : «الْمَرِيضُ إِنَّمَا يُصَلَّي
قَاعِداً إِذَا صَارَ بِالْحَالِ آلَّتِي لا يَقْدِرُ فِيهَا أَنْ يَمْشِيَ مِقْدَارَ صَلاتِهِ إِلَى أَنْ يَفْرُغَ قَائِماً».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE NAKED
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah. He said:
I said to Abu Ja’far {a.s}: “A man comes out of a ship naked, or his clothes have been
taken from him, and he does not find anything to pray in, what should he do?”
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray by gesturing. If it is a woman, she should place her
hand over her private part, and if it is a man, he should place his hand over his private
part. Then they should both sit and gesture with indications.
They should neither bow nor prostrate, as what is behind them (anus) would become
exposed. Their prayer should be by gesturing with their heads.”
Imam {a.s} said: “And if they are in water or in a deep sea, they should not prostrate in it,
and the requirement of facing the qibla is lifted from them in that case.
They should gesture therein with indications, their lifting is counted as turning toward
the qibla, and their lowering (is considered) likewise.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
رَجُلُ خَرَجَ مِنْ سَفِينَةِ عُزْيَاناً أَوْ سُلِبَ ثِيَابُهُ وَ لَمْ يَجِدْ شَيْئاً يُصَلِّي فِيهِ فَقَالَ «يُصَلِّي إيمَاءً وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ اِمْرَأَةً
جَعَلَتْ يَدَهَا عَلَى فَرْجِهَا وَ إِنْ كَانَ رَجْلاً وَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَى سَوْأَتِهِ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسَانِ فَيُومِيَانِ إِيمَاءً وَ لاَ يَرْكَعَانٍ وَ لاَ
يَسْجُدَانٍ فَيَنْدُوَ مَا خَلْفَهُمَا تَكُونُ صَلاَتُهُمَا إِيمَاءً بِرُءُوسِهِمَا» قَالَ «وَ إِنْ كَانَا فِي مَاءِ أَوْ بَحْرٍ لُجَيٍّ لَمْ يَسْجُدَا عَلَيْهِ
وَ مَوْضُوعٌ عَنْهُمَا التَّوَجُّهُ فِيهِ يُومِيَانٍ فِي ذَلِكَ إِيمَاءً رَفْعُهُمَا تَوَجُّهُ وَ وَضْعُهُمَا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE NAKED
text_en:
Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:

they were naked.
Imam {a.s} said: “The imam (of prayer) should go before them on his knees and lead
them in prayer sitting, while he is also sitting.”
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْمِ صَلَّوْا جَمَاعَةً وَ هُمْ عُرَاةً قَالَ «يَتَقَدَّمُهُمُ الْإِمَامُ بِرُكْبَتَيْهِ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ جُلُوساً وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE NAKED
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ayyub ibn Nuh from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah {a.s}:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The naked person, who has no garment, if he finds a pit, he
should enter it and perform his prostration and bowing in it.”

Scholar's Note:
And what he mentioned after that regarding the manner of performing the prayer over
a deceased person, if he is naked, is indicated by what is narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوحِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «الْعَارِي الَّذِي
لَيْسَ لَهُ ثَوْبٌ إِذَا وَجَدَ حُفْرَةً دَخَلَهَا فَسَجَدَ فِيهَا وَ رَكَعَ».
وما ذكره بعد ذلك من كيفية الصلاة على الميت إذا كان عريانا، يدل على ذلك ما رواه:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE NAKED
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Marwan ibn Muslim from
Ammar al-Sabati. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “What do you say about a group of people, who were on a
journey walking along the shore of the sea, when suddenly they came upon a dead
man; naked, whom the sea had cast ashore. These group of people are themselves
naked, having only a waist wrap or a cloak. How should they pray over him (the
deceased), while they are naked and have no extra garment to shroud him with?”
Imam {a.s} said: “A grave should be dug for him, and he should be placed in his burial
niche (lahd), and bricks should be placed over his private parts, so that his private area
is covered with the bricks and stones. Then the prayer should be performed over him,
and then he should be buried.”
I asked: “So, the prayer is not to be performed over him, if he has already been buried?”
Imam {a.s} said: “No, the prayer is not performed over the deceased after he has been
buried, nor is it performed over him while he is naked, until his private parts are
covered.”
text_ar:
أحمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ عَمَّارِ السَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ
الأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي قَوْمٍ كَانُوا فِي سَفَرٍ لَهُمْ يَمْشَونَ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ فَإِذَا هُمْ بِرَجُلٍ مَيَّتِ
عُزْيَانٍ قَدْ لَفَظَهُ الْبَحْرُ وَ هُمْ عُرَاةً لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَّ إِزَارُ أَوْ رِدَاءُ كَيْفَ يُصَلُونَ عَلَيْهِ وَ هُمْ عُرَاةً لَيْسَ مَعَهُمْ فَضْلُ
ثَوْبِ يُكَفَّنُونَهُ بِهِ قَالَ «يُحْفَرُ لَهُ وَ يُوضَعُ فِي لَحْدِهِ وَ يُوضَعُ اللَّبِنُ عَلَى عَوْرَتِهِ فَيُسْتَرُ بِاللّبِنِ وَ بِالْحَجَرِ ثُمَّ يُصَلّى
عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُدْفَنُ» قُلْتُ فَلاَ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ إِذَا دُفِنَ قَالَ «لا يُصَلِّى عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ بَعْدَ مَا يُدْفَنُ وَ لاَ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ وَ هُوَ
عُزيَانٌ حَتَّى تُوَارَى عَوْرَتُهُ».
١٦ - باب صلاة الاستخارة

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF SEEKING GUIDANCE
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn
Khalid from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Amr ibn Hurayth. He said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Pray two rak’ahs and seek guidance
(istikharah) from Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, for by Allah {SWT}, no Muslim ever
seeks guidance from Allah {SWT} except that Allah {SWT} surely grants him the best
outcome.”
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدِ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى
اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ حُرَيْثِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «صَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اِسْتَخِرِ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَوَ اللَّهِ
مَا اِسْتَخَارَ اَللهَ مُسْلِمٌ إِلَّ خَارَ اللهُ لَهُ الْبَنَّةَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF SEEKING GUIDANCE
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Uthman ibn Isa from ‘Amru ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon
him, said:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “When Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn {a.s}, peace be upon them both,
intended to perform the Hajj, or the ‘Umrah, or to engage in buying, or selling, or
manumission (of a slave);
Imam al-Husayn {a.s} would perform ablution, then he would pray the two units
(rak‘ahs) of the prayer of Istikharah, in which He {a.s} would recite Surah al-Hashr and
Surah al-Rahman.
Then He {a.s} would recite ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (the two chapters of refuge) and ‘Qul
Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas).
Then Imam al-Husayn {a.s} would say:
“O’ Allah {SWT}, if such and such a matter is good for me in my religion, my worldly life,
my hereafter, my immediate affairs, and my future ones, then facilitate it for me in the
best and most beautiful manner. O’ Allah {SWT}, and if such and such a matter is bad for
me in my religion, my worldly life, my hereafter, my immediate affairs, and my future
ones, then turn it away from me in the best manner. My Lord {SWT}, determine for me
what is right, even if I dislike it or my soul refuses it.”
text_ar:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثَمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «كَانَ عَلِيُ
بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ إِذَا هَمَّ بِأَمْرِ حَجِّ أَوْ عُمْرَةٍ أَوْ بَنْعِ أَوْ شِرَاءٍ أَوْ عِثقٍ تَطَهَرَ ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَي الإِسْتِخَارَةِ
يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا سُورَةَ الْحَشْرِ وَ سُورَةَ الرَّحْمَنِ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ ٱلْمُعَوِّدَتَيْنِ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُمْ يَقُولُ » آللّهُمْ إِنْ كَانَ كَذَا
وَكَذَا خَيْراً لِي فِي دِيني وَ دُنْيَايَ وَ آخِرَتِي وَ عَاجِلٍ أَمْرِي وَ آجِلِهِ فَيَسُرْهُ لِي عَلَى أَحْسَنِ ٱلْوُجُوهِ وَ أَجْمَلِهَا اللَّهُمَّ
وَ إِنْ كَانَ كَذَا وَ كَذَا شَرّاً لِي فِي دِينِي وَ دُنْيَايَ وَ آخِرَتِي وَ عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَ آجِلِهِ فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنَّي عَلَى أَحْسَنِ ٱلْوُجُوهِ
رَبّ اِغْزِمْ لِي عَلَى رُشَدِي وَ إِنْ كَرِهْتُ ذَلِكَ أَوْ أَبَثَهُ نَفْسِي »».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF SEEKING GUIDANCE
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Aba al-Hasan {a.s} on behalf of Ibn Asbat.
He (Al-Hasan) said to Imam {a.s}: “What do you see for him?”, and Ibn Asbat was
present, and we were all together,
(Al-Hasan asked) “Should he (ibn Asbat) travel by sea or by land to Egypt?”
Then he (Al-Hasan) informed Imam {a.s} about the condition of the land route.
Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Go to the mosque at a time other than the time
of obligatory prayer. Then pray two units (rak‘ahs) and seek the guidance of Allah {SWT}
(istikharah) one hundred times. Then look at what settles in your heart, and act upon
it.”
Al-Hasan said to Imam {a.s}: “The land route is more beloved to me for him (ibn Asbat).”
Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “And to me as well.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ الْجَهْمِ - أَبَا
الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ لاِبْنِ أَسْبَاطِ فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا تَرَى لَهُ وَ اِبْنُ أَسْبَاطِ حَاضِرٌ وَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعاً يَرْكَبُ الْبَحْرَ أَوِ الْبَرَّ إِلَى
مِصْرَ وَ أَخْبَرَهُ بِخَبَرِ طَرِيقِ الْبَرِّ فَقَالَ «فَأْتِ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتِ صَلاَةٍ فَرِيضَةِ فَصَلَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اِسْتَخْرِ ٱللَّهَ
مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ ثُمَّ أنْظُرْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ يَقَعُ فِي قَلْبِكَ فَاعْمَلْ بِهِ» قَالَ لَهُ الْحَسَنُ الْبَرْ أَحَبُ إِلَيَّ لَهُ قَالَ »وَ إِلَيَّ».
