author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “Prayer on a ship is by gesturing (ima’).”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ غَيْرٍ وَاجِدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «الصَّلاَةُ فِي
السَّفِينَة إيمَاء).

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
From him, from Uyaynah the seller of reeds, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “We travel to Ahwaz on ships, and we
combine the prayers in them.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, there is no harm in it.”
I asked: “And we prostrate on what is in them, and on pitch (al-qir)?”
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ عُيَيْنَةَ بَيَّاعِ الْقَصَبِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ نَخْرُجُ إِلَى الْأَهْوَازِ فِي
السُّفُنِ فَنَجْمَعُ فِيهَا الصَّلاةَ قَالَ «نَعَمْ لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسْ» قُلْتُ وَ نَسْجُدُ عَلَى مَا فِيهَا وَ عَلَى الْقِيرِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER IN THE SHIP
text_en:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Walad who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “I had gone out from Kufah on a ship to Qasr Ibn Hubayrah,
and it is about twenty farsakhs from Kufah by water. So I travelled that day, shortening
the prayer. Then in the night, I decided to return to Kufah, and I did not know whether I
should pray on my return with shortening or with full (prayer)? What should I do?
Imam {a.s} said: “If you had travelled on the day you departed, a distance of one ‘barid’,
then it was upon you, when you returned, to pray with shortening (the prayer), because
you remained a traveller until you reached your home.”
Imam {a.s} said: “And if you did not travel a distance of one ‘barid’ on the day you
departed, then it is incumbent upon you to make up every prayer you performed that
day with shortening (the prayer), with full prayers, before you move from that place.
This is because you did not reach the location in which shortening is permissible
before you returned. So it is obligatory upon you to make up what you shortened.
And when you return, you must perform the prayer in full until you reach your home.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي وَلادِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ إِنِّي كُنْتُ خَرَجْتُ مِنَ اَلْكُوفَةِ فِي
سَفِينَةٍ إِلَى قَصْرِ اِبْنِ هُبَيْرَةَ وَ هُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكُوفَةِ عَلَى نَحْوِ عِشَرِينَ فَرْسَخاً فِي الْمَاءِ فَسِرْتُ يَوْمِي ذَلِكَ أُقَصِّرُ ٱلصَّلاةَ
ثُمَّ بَدَا لِي فِي اللِّيْلِ الرُجُوعُ إِلَى الْكُوفَةِ فَلَمْ أَذْرِ أُصَلِّي فِي رُجُوعِي بِتَقْصِيرِ أَمْ بِتَمَامٍ وَ كَيْفَ كَانَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ أَصْنَعَ
فَقَالَ «إِنْ كُنْتَ سِرْتَ فِي يَوْمِكَ الَّذِي خَرَجْتَ فِيهِ بَرِيداً فَكَانَ عَلَيْكَ جِينَ رَجَعْتَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ بِالتَّقْصِيرِ لِأَنَّكَ كُنْتَ
مُسَافِراً إلَى أَنْ تَصِيرَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ» قَالَ «وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ لَمْ تَسِرْ فِي يَوْمِكَ الَّذِي خَرَجْتَ فِيهِ بَرِيداً فَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ
نَقْضِيَ كُلَّ صَلاةِ صَلَّيْتَهَا فِي يَوْمِكَ ذَلِكَ بِالتَّقْصِيرِ بِتَمَامِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَرِيمَ مِنْ مَكَانِكَ ذَلِكَ لِأَنَّكَ لَمْ تَبْلُغِ الْمَوْضِعَ
الَّذِي يَجُوزُ فِيهِ التَّقْصِيرُ حَتَّى رَجَعْتَ فَوَجَبَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ مَا قَصَّرْتَ وَ عَلَيْكَ إِذَا رَجَعْتَ أَنْ ثُتِمّ الصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى
تَصِيرَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ».
٢٩ - باب صلاة الخوف

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Zur’ah from Sama’ah who said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about the prisoner who is taken captive by the polytheists, and the
time of prayer comes, while the one who captured him prevents him from performing
it.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should gesture (perform the prayer) by gesturing (ima’a)”.
text_ar:
احمد بن محمد بن خالد عن ابيه عن زرعة عن سماعة قال : سألته عن الاسير يأسره المشركون فتحضره الصلاة
فيمنعه الذي أسره منها قال : يؤمي إيماءا.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.299
source_scholar: Implicit (Muzmar)

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma’il who said:
I asked Imam {a.s} and said: “I am on the road to Mecca, and we leave the prayer in
places where there are Bedouins.
Should we pray the obligatory prayer on the ground and recite only ‘Umm al-Kitab’
(Surah al-Fatiha), or should we pray on the mount and recite ‘al-Fatiha’ and a surah?”
Imam {a.s} said: “If you are afraid, then perform the obligatory prayer and others on the
mount. If you recite ‘al-Hamd’ and a surah, that is more beloved to me.
But I do not see any harm in what you did.”
text_ar:
أحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ أكُونُ فِي طَرِيقٍ مَكَّةَ فَنَثْرُكُ الصَّلاَةَ فِي مَوَاضِعَ فِيهَا
الْأَعْرَابُ أَنُصَلِّي الْمَكْتُوبَةَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فَنَقْرَأُ أُمَّ الْكِتَابِ وَحْدَهَا أَمْ نُصَلِّي عَلَى الرَّاجِلَةِ فَتَقْرَأْ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَّابِ وَ
السُّورَةَ فَقَالَ «إِذَا خِفْتَ فَصَلِّ عَلَى الرَّاحِلَةِ الْمَكْتُوبَةَ وَغَيْرَهَا فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْحَمْدَ وَسُورَةً أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ وَ لَا أُرَى بِالَّذِي
فَعَلْتَ بَأَساً».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.457 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.299 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1072 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.43 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.449

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “About the saying of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic:
“But if you fear, then (pray) on foot or riding” (Surah Al Baqarah 2:239).
How do we pray?
And what do you say if one fears a wild beast or a thief, how should he pray?”
Imam {a.s} said: “He says the takbir and gestures with his head.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ
عَنْ قَوْلِ اللّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجَالاً أَوْ رُكْبَانا» كَيْفَ نُصَلِّي وَ مَا تَقُولُ إنْ خَافَ مِنْ سَبْعِ أَوْ لِصِّ كَيْفَ
يُصَلِّي قَالَ «يُكَبِّرُ وَ يُومِئ بِرَأْسِهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.457 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.299 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1072 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.439 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.1 p.498 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.239 • Tafsir Kanz Al- Daqaiq, Vol.2 p.369

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Ali from his father from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon
him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “When the horses move about in turmoil with swords clashing,
two takbirs suffice him (for prayer). This is another form of shortening (taqsir).”
text_ar:
عَلِيْ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا جَالَتِ ٱلْخَيْلُ
تَضطَرِبُ بالسيُوفِ أَجْزَأَهُ تَكْبِيرَتَانِ فَهَذَا تَقْصِيرٌ آخَرُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.457 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.300 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1067 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.445

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked regarding the saying of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and
Majestic: ‘Then there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that
those who disbelieve may harm you’ (Surah An Nisa 4:101)
Imam {a.s} said: “In (from) the two rak‘ahs, one is reduced from them.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ: فِي قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنْاحٌ
أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلاةِ إِنْ خِفْثُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِئَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا» قَالَ «فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ يَنْقُصُ مِنْهُمَا وَاحِدَة».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.458 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.300 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1066 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.434 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.2 p.162 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.543 • Tafsir Kanz Al- Daqaiq, Vol.3 p.526

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-‘Amraki ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be
upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim {a.s} about a man who encounters a wild beast (al-sab‘) and
the time for prayer has arrived, but he is unable to walk out of fear of the beast.
If he stands to pray, he fears during his bowing and prostration, and the beast is in front
of him, not in the direction of the qiblah.
So if he turns to face the qiblah, he fears that the lion will leap upon him. What should
he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should face the lion and pray, and gesture with his head as
indication (of bowing and prostration), while standing, even if the lion is not in the
direction of the qiblah."
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيِى عَنِ الْعَمْرَكِيَّ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ
الرَّجُلٍ يَلْقَى السَّبُعَ وَ قَدْ حَضَرَتِ الصَّلاَةُ وَ لا يَسْتَطِيعُ ٱلْمَشيَ مَخَافَةَ السَّبُعِ فَإِنْ قَامَ يُصَلِّي خَاقَ فِي رُكُوعِهِ وَ
فِي سُجُودِهِ وَ السَّبْعُ أَمَامَهُ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَإِنْ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ خَافَ أَنْ يَثِبَ عَلَيْهِ الْأَسَدُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ فَقَالَ
«يَسْتَقْبِلُ الْأَسَدَ وَ يُصَلِّي وَ يُومِئُ بِرَأْسِهِ إِيمَاءً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ ٱلْأَسَدُ عَلَى غَيْرِ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ».
cross_references: Masa’il Ali Ibn Ja’far, Vol.1 p.173 • Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.459 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.300 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1073 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.439 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.86 p.117
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Basir who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “When they meet and engage in
battle, then the prayer at that time is with the takbir.
And if they are standing, then the prayer is by gesturing [ima'].”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا اِلْتَقَوْا
فَاقْتَتَلُوا فَإِنَّمَا الصَّلاَةُ حِينَئِذِ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ فَإِذَا كَانُوا وُقُوفا فَالصَّلاَةُ إِيمَاءَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya‘qub from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu
Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “When the Maghrib prayer is in a situation of fear, he (imam of
prayer) divides them into two groups.
He prays with one group two rak‘ahs, then sits with them. Then he signals to them with
his hand, so each person among them stands and prays one rak‘ah, then they say the
taslim. Then they take the place of their companions.
And the other group comes, says the takbir, and enters into the prayer, and the imam
(of prayer) stands and prays with them one rak‘ah, then says the taslim. Then each
man among them stands and prays one rak‘ah, pairing it with the one he prayed with
the imam (of prayer). Then he stands and prays a rak‘ah in which there is no recitation.
Thus, the imam (of prayer) completed three rak‘ahs, and the first group had two
rak‘ahs in congregation, and the latter group prayed individually. So the first group had
the takbir and the opening of the prayer, and the latter had the taslim.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ إِبْنِ أَزَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ
قَالَ: «إِذَا كَانَ صَلاَةُ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ فِي الْخَوْفِ فَرَّقَهُمْ فِرْفَتَيْنِ فَيُصَلِّي بِفِرْقَةٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ جَلَسَ بِهِمْ ثُمَّ أَشَارَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِيَدِهِ
فَقَامَ كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ مِنْهُمْ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ سَلَمُوا فَقَامُوا مَقَامَ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ جَاءَتِ الطَّائِفَةُ الْأُخْرَى فَكَبَّرُوا وَ دَخَلُوا
فِي الصَّلاَةٍ وَ قَامَ الْإِمَامُ فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ ثُمَّ قَامَ كُلُّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَةً فَشَفَعَهَا بِالَّتِي صَلَّى مَعَ
الإمَام ثُمَّ قَامَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَةً لَيْسَ فِيهَا قِرَاءَةٌ فَتَمَّتْ لِلْإِمَامِ ثَلاَثُ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ لِلْأَوَّلِينَ رَكْعَتَانٍ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ لِلْآخَرِينَ
وُحْدَاناً فَصَارَ لِلْأَوَّلِينَ التَكْبِيرُ وَ اِفْتِتَاحُ ٱلصَّلاَةِ وَ لِلْآخَرِينَ التَّسْلِيمُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.301 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.456 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1065 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.436

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
And this report was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr
from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Fudayl and Muhammad ibn Muslim from
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him: in the same manner.

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: “There is no contradiction between this report and the
report of al-Halabi which we previously presented, wherein the first group is led by the
imam (of prayer) in one rak‘ah, while in this narration he leads them in two rak‘ahs
because both reports indicate that the person has a choice between them, and
whichever of the two he acts upon, it suffices him.
There is no contradiction or opposition between them, especially since Zurarah, the
narrator of this hadith, also narrated a report similar to that of al-Halabi.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: “There is no contradiction between this report and the
report of al-Halabi which we presented earlier, wherein the first group is led by the
imam (of prayer) in one rak‘ah, and in this narration he leads them in two rak‘ahs.
This is because in both reports the individual is given a choice, so whichever of the two
is acted upon, it is sufficient. And there is no contradiction or conflict between them.
Moreover, Zurarah, the narrator of this hadith, also narrated a version similar to the
report of al-Halabi.”
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى هَذَا الْخَبَرَ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُدَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ فُضَيْلٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ
مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ : مِثلَ ذَلِكَ.
قال محمد بن الحسن : لا تنافي بين هذا الخبر وخبر الحلبي الذي قدمناه من أن الفرقة الاولى يصلي بهم الامام ركعة
واحدة وفي هذه الرواية انه يصلي بهم ركعتين ، لان الخبرين جميعا الانسان مخير فيهما فأيهما عمل به فقد أجزأه ، ولا
تنافي بينهما ولا تضاد على ان زرارة راوي هذا الحديث روى مثل رواية الحلبي

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurarah from
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “For the Maghrib prayer in a situation of fear (Salat al-Khawf),
he (imam of prayer) prays one rak‘ah with the first group, and they make up two
rak‘ahs, and he (imam of prayer) prays two rak‘ahs with the second group, and they
make up one rak‘ah.”
text_ar:
رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ ٱلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: «صَلاَةُ
اَلْخَوْفِ الْمَغْرِبَ يُصَلِّي بِالْأَوَّلِينَ رَكَعَةً وَ يَقْضُونَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُصَلِّي بِالْآخَرِينَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَقْضُونَ رَكْعَةً».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.301 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.457 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1065 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.436

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Abu al-Mi‘za from Abu Basir who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “What if you saw me at the bank of the
Euphrates, praying while I am afraid of a wild beast?”
Imam {a.s} said to me: “Should you not have prayed while you were mounted?”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبِي الْمِعْزَى عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ لَوْ رَأْيْتَنِي وَ
أَنَا بِشَطّ الْفُرَاتِ أَصَلِّي وَ أَنَا أَخَافُ السَّبْعَ فَقَالَ لِي «أَفَلا صَلَّيْتَ وَ أَنتَ رَاكِبٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.301 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1074 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.442
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Sa’ad from Ahmad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad from Hariz from
Zurarah who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear)
and the prayer of travel, Are both to be shortened?
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, and the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) has more right to be
shortened than the prayer of travel, in which there is no fear.”
text_ar:
سَعَدْ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا
جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ ٱلْخَوْفِ وَ صَلاَةِ السّفَرِ تُقْصَرَانٍ جَمِيعاً قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ صَلاَةُ ٱَلْخَوْفِ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تُقْصَرَ
مِنْ صَلاَةِ السَّفَرِ لَيْسَ فِيهِ خَوْفٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.302 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1066 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.2 p.162
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR
text_en:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa’adan from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from Ishaq ibn
Ammar from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “One who fears a wild beast, or fears an enemy that may attack
him, or fears thieves; he performs the obligatory prayer on his mount by gesturing
(ima’a).”
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ سَعْدَانَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَمَّنْ حَدَّتَهُ عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : «فِي الَّذِي يَخَافُ السَّبْعَ أَوْ يَخَافُ عَدُوَاً يَثْبُ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ يَخَافُ اللُصُوصَ يُصَلِّي عَلَى
دَابَّتِهِ إِيمَاءً الْفَرِيضَةَ».
٣٠ - باب صلاة المضطر
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.302 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1074 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.442

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace
be upon him, who said:
I heard Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} say, regarding one who is unconscious;
Imam {a.s} said: “Whatever Allah {SWT} has caused to overcome him (for him to faint), then
Allah {SWT} is more entitled to excuse.”
text_ar:
عَلِيْ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ الْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ
يَقُولُ: فِي الْمُغَمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ «مَا غَلَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.413 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.302 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.457 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.261
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who was unconscious for days, and did not
pray, then regained consciousness. Should he make up what he missed?
Imam {a.s} said: “There is nothing (of qadha) upon him.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْخَزَّازِ أَبِي أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ
رَجُلٍ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَيَّاماً لَمْ يُصَلِّ ثُمَّ أَفَاقَ أَيُصَلِّي مَا فَاتَهُ قَالَ «لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.412 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.302 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.457 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1055 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.261
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who was unconscious for days, and did not
pray, then regained consciousness. Should he make up what he missed?
Imam {a.s} said: “There is nothing (of qadha) upon him.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a sick person who is not able to
perform the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: “Whatever Allah {SWT} has caused to overcome him (to faint), then Allah
{SWT} is more entitled to excuse.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ مُرَازِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ الْمَرِيضِ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى
الصَّلاةٍ قَالَ فَقَالَ «كُلَّمَا غَلَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi

From him, from al-Hajjal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun from Ma‘mar ibn Umar who said:

Imam {a.s} said: “No.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَجَّالِ عَنْ تَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونِ عَنْ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ عَنِ الْمَرِيضِ يَقْضِي
اَلصَّلَاةَ إِذَا أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ «لا».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman who said:
I wrote to the jurist (faqih) Abu al-Hasan al-Askari {a.s}, peace be upon him, asking Imam
{a.s} about the one who falls unconscious for a day or more. Does he have to make up
the prayers that he missed or not?
So Imam {a.s} wrote: “He does not make up the fast, nor does he make up the prayer.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى ٱلْفَقِيهِ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْعَسْكَرِيَّ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَامُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْمًا أَوْ أَكْثَرَ هَلْ يَقْضِي مَا فَانَهُ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ أَمْ لا فَكَتَبَ «لا يَقْضِي الصَّوْمَ وَ لا
يَقْضِي الصَّلاةَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.303 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.458 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1056

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Sa’ad from Ayyub ibn Nuh who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s} (the Third), peace be upon him, asking Imam {a.s}
about the one who falls unconscious for a day or more. Does he have to make up the
prayers that he missed or not?
So Imam {a.s} wrote: “He does not make up the fast, nor does he make up the prayer.”
text_ar:
سَعدٌ عَنْ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوجِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلْهُ عَنِ الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْماً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ هَلْ
يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ أَمْ لا قَكَتَبَ «لا يَقْضِي الصّوْمَ وَ لاَ يَقْضِي الصّلاَةَ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about the sick person who falls unconscious.
He said: “If three days pass over him, then there is no obligation upon him to make it
up; and if he is unconscious for three days, then he must make up the prayers during
them.”
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةً عَنْ سَمَاعَةً قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمَرِيضِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ «إِذَا
جَارَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلاَثَةُ أَيَّامِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ وَ إِذَا أُعْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاء الصَلاَةِ فِيهِنَّ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.303 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.4 p.244 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.458 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1059 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.265

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about the one who falls unconscious.
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up the prayer of one day.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْمُغُمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ فَقَالَ «يَقْضِي صَلاةَ يَوْمٍ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.303 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.458 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1058 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.267
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about the one who falls unconscious.
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up the prayer of one day.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Alaa ibn al-Fudayl, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who falls unconscious from
the day until the night, then regains consciousness.
Imam {a.s} said: “If he regains consciousness before sunset, then he must make up the
prayer of that day.
But if he remains unconscious for a number of days, then he is only required to make
up the prayer of the last of those days, if he regains consciousness before sunset.
Otherwise, there is nothing upon him to make up.”

Scholar's Note:
So interpretation of these reports is that we understand them as indicating a kind of
recommendation (mustahabb), because earlier reports are to be understood to mean
that it is not obligatory upon him to make up what he missed during the state of
unconsciousness, while these (latter ones) are understood as recommended for him.
As for the prayer whose time he regains consciousness during, it is obligatory for him
to make it up in any case. And it was narrated:
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ بْنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ -
عَنِ الرّجُلِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْما إِلَى اللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ يُفِيقُ قَالَ «إِنْ أَفَاقَ قَبْلَ غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ يَوْمِهِ هَذَا فَإِنْ
أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَيَّاما ذَوَاتِ عَدَدٍ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ إِلاَّ آخِرَ أيَّامِهِ إِنْ أَفَاقَ قَبْلَ غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ وَ إِلاَّ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ
قَضَاءٌ».
فالوجه في هذه الاخبار ان نحملها على ضرب من الاستحباب لان الاخبار الاولة محمولة على انه لا يجب عليه قضاء ما
فاته في حالة الاغماء، وهذه محمولة على استحباب ذلك له ، فأما الصلاة التي يفيق في وقتها فانه يجب عليه قضاؤها
على كل حال ، وروى :

unconsciousness, while these (latter ones) are understood as recommended for him.
As for the prayer whose time he regains consciousness during, it is obligatory for him
to make it up in any case. And it was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
And Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Abu Basir from one
of the two Imams {a.s}, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about the sick person, who falls unconscious and then regains
consciousness, how does he make up his prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up the prayer whose time he caught.”
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْمَرِيضِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُفِيقُ كَيْفَ يَقْضِي صَلاَتَهُ قَالَ «يَقْضِي الصَّلاَةَ الَّتِي أَدْرَكَ وَقْتَهَا».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.412 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.304 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.459 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1055 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.262
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
And Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Abu Basir from one
of the two Imams {a.s}, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about the sick person, who falls unconscious and then regains
consciousness, how does he make up his prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up the prayer whose time he caught.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah al-
Halabi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about the sick person, does he make up the prayer if he falls
unconscious?
Imam {a.s} said: “No, except for the prayer during which he regained consciousness.”
text_ar:
سَعدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ الْحَلَبِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمَرِيضِ هَلْ يَقْضِي الصَّلاةَ إِذَا أُغْمِيّ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ «لا إلا الصَّلاةَ آلَّتِي أَفَاقَ فِيهَا».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.304 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.459 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1057
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

، أَفَاقَ
عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «يَقْضِي الصَّلاَةَ الَّتِي
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ عَنْ أَبِي

Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “He makes up the prayer during which he regained

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah {a.s}:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “Everything you left of your prayer due to an illness, in which
you were rendered unconscious, make it up when you regain consciousness.”
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «كُلُّ شَيْءٍ تَرَكْتَهُ
مِنْ صَلاَتِكَ لِمَرَضٍ أَغْمِيَ عَلَيْكَ فِيهِ فَاقْضِهِ إِذَا أَفَقْتَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.304
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah {a.s}:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from Safwan from al-Alaa from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir {a.s} about the man who falls unconscious, and then regains
consciousness.
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up what he missed, he gives the adhan for the first prayer
and gives the iqamah for the rest (when making up missed prayers).”
text_ar:
عَنهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجْلِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ
يُفِيقُ قَالَ «يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ يُؤَذِّنَ فِي الْأُولَى وَ يُقِيمُ فِي الْبَقِيَّةِ».

source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Safwan from al-Alaa from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir {a.s} about the man who falls unconscious, and then regains
consciousness.
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up what he missed, he gives the adhan for the first prayer
and gives the iqamah for the rest (when making up missed prayers).”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked regarding the one who falls unconscious.
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up everything that he missed.”
text_ar: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : فِي الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ «يَقْضِي كُلَّ مَا فَاتَهُ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.305 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1060 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.265

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifaa'ah from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about the one who falls unconscious for a month, what does
he make up of the prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: “He makes up all of it. Indeed, the matter of prayer is severe.”
text_ar:
عَنهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ شَهْراً مَا يَقْضِي مِنَ
الصَّلاةِ قَالَ «يَقْضِيهَا كُلَّهَا إِنَّ أَمْرَ الصَّلاةِ شَدِيدٌ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.305 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.4 p.244 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.459 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1061 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.265

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad who said:
I wrote to him; “May I be ransomed for you, it has been narrated from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, regarding a sick person who becomes unconscious for several
days.
Some have said he makes up the prayer of the day in which he regains consciousness,
and some have said he makes up the prayers of three days and leaves what is beyond
that, and some have said that there is no make-up upon him.”
So Imam {a.s} wrote: “He makes up the prayer of the day in which he regains
consciousness.”
text_ar:
عَنَهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ رُوِيَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ فِي الْمَرِيضِ يُغْمَى
عَلَيْهِ أَيَّاماً فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ يَقْضِي صَلَاَةَ يَوْمِهِ آلَّذِي أَفَاقَ فِيهِ وَ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ يَقْضِي صَلاَةَ ثَلَاَثَةِ أَيَّامِ وَ يَدَعُ مَا سِوَى
ذَلِكَ وَ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِنَّهُ لا قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ فَكَتَبَ «يَقْضِي صَلاَةَ اَلْيَوْمِ الَّذِي يُفِيقُ فِيهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.305 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.459 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1058 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.263

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who falls unconscious during the day and then
regains consciousness before sunset.
Imam {a.s} said: “He performs the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, and if he regains
consciousness during the night before dawn, he makes up the night (Isha) prayers.”

Scholar's Note:
This report confirms what we have stated earlier, that it is obligatory upon him to make
up the prayer whose time he regains consciousness during, and this time is the end of
the time allotted for one in difficulty (al-mudtar), so it becomes obligatory upon him at
that time to make it up.
text_ar:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ نَهَاراً ثُمَّ يُفِيقُ قَبْلَ غُرُوبِ الشَمْسِ فَقَالَ «يُصَلِّي الظُهْرَ وَ ٱلْعَصْرَ وَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِذَا
أَفَاقَ قَبْلَ الصُّبْحِ قَضَى صَلاَةَ اللّيْلِ».
فهذا الخبر توكيد لما قدمناه من انه يجب عليه قضاء الصلاة التي يفيق في وقتها ، وهذا الوقت هو آخر وقت المضطر
فيجب عليه حينئذ قضاؤها.
commentary:
This report confirms what we have stated earlier, that it is obligatory upon him to make
up the prayer whose time he regains consciousness during, and this time is the end of
the time allotted for one in difficulty (al-mudtar), so it becomes obligatory upon him at
that time to make it up.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the one suffering from abdominal
illness (al-mabtun).
Imam {a.s} said: “He builds upon his prayer.”
(meaning performs ablution again, and continues from where he left it)
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الْمَبْطُونِ
فقَالَ «يَبْنِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.411 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.305 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1047 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.297

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Muhammad ibn Nusayr from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir
from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “The one afflicted with overpowering abdominal illness (sahib
al-batn al-ghalib) performs ablution for his prayer and completes what remains.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ نُصَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ
بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «صَاحِبُ الْبَطْنِ الْغَالِبِ يَتَوَضَّأْ فِي صَلاتِهِ فَيُتِمُ مَا بَقِيَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.1 p.350 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.306 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1047 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.298

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from
al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about the dripping of urine (incontinence).
Imam {a.s} said: “He should place a pouch (khariitah, to absorb), when he prays.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ نُصَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ : سُئِلَ عَنْ تَقْطِيرِ الْبَوْلِ قَالَ «يَجْعَلُ خَرِيطَةً إِذَا صَلَّى».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.1 p.351 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.306 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.143 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1048 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.298

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about the sick person who is not able to sit.
He said: “Then let him pray while lying down, and let him place something on his
forehead when he prostrates, for it suffices for him. And Allah {SWT} will not burden a
soul beyond its capacity.”
text_ar:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْمَرِيضِ لا يَسْتَطِيعُ الْجُلُوسَ قَالَ «فَلْيُصَلِّ
وَهُوَ مُصْطَجَعٌ وَ لْيَضَعْ عَلَى جَبْهَتِهِ شَيْئا إِذَا سَجَدَ فَإِنَّهُ يُجْزِي عَنْهُ وَ لَنْ يُكَلِّفَ اللَّهُ مَا لا طَاقَةَ لَهُ بِهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.306 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1044 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.482 • Al- Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.1 p.624

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
From him, from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about a man who has water in his eyes and has it removed, and then lies
on his back for many days; forty days, less or more and refrains from prayer during
those days while he is in that condition.
He said: “There is no harm in that, and there is nothing among what Allah {SWT} has
forbidden except that He {AZJ} has made it lawful for the one who is compelled to it.”
text_ar:
عَنَهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونَ فِي عَيْنَيْهِ ٱلْمَاءُ فَيَنْزِعُ الْمَاءَ مِنْهَا فَيَسْتَلْقِي
عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ الْأَيَّامَ الْكَثِيرَةَ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْما أَقَلَّ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ فَيَمْتَنعُ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ الْأَيَّامَ وَ هُوَ عَلَى حَالٍ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ
وَ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِمَّا حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّ وَ قَدْ أَحَلَّهُ لِمَنِ أُضْطُرَّ إِلَيْهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.306 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1041 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.482 • Al- Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.1 p.621

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Iys who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man upon whom a year's worth
of prayer has accumulated, due to illness.
Imam {a.s} said: “He does not make them up.”

Scholar's Note:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: “This report is to be understood as referring to the
supererogatory prayers (nawafil).” What indicates this is what was narrated:
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عِيصِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ -
عَنِ الرَّجُلِ اِجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ صَلَاَةُ سَنَةٍ مِنْ مَرَضٍ قَالَ «لا يَقْضِي».
قال محمد بن الحسن : هذا الخبر محمول على النوافل ، يدل على ذلك ما رواه:

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: “This report is to be understood as referring to the
supererogatory prayers (nawafil).” What indicates this is what was narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I said to Imam al-Baqir {a.s}: “A man fell ill and left the supererogatory prayer (al-
nafilah).”
Imam said: “O Muhammad, it is not an obligation. If he makes it up, then it is a good
deed that he does, and if he does not do it, then there is nothing upon him.”
text_ar:
عَلِيّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلْ مَرِضَ فَتَرَكَ النَّافِلَةَ قَالَ «يَا
مُحَمَّدُ لَيْسَتْ بِفَرِيضَةِ إِنْ قَضَاهَا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ يَفْعَلُهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.412 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.499 • ‘Ilal Al-Shara’i’, Vol.2 p.361 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.306 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1025 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.79 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.84 p.41
source_scholar: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
text_chunk:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I said to Imam al-Baqir {a.s}: “A man fell ill and left the supererogatory prayer (al-
nafilah).”
Imam said: “O Muhammad, it is not an obligation. If he makes it up, then it is a good
deed that he does, and if he does not do it, then there is nothing upon him.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Ali from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah: that Sinan asked Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who stretches out one of his legs in front of
him while sitting.
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no problem, and I do not see it except, in the case of someone
afflicted (al-mu'tall) or sick (al-marid).”
text_ar:
عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ : أَنَّ سِنَاناً سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ
يَمُدُّ إِحْدَى رِجْلَيْهِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسْ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ وَ لاَ أَرَاهُ إِلاَّ فِي ٱلْمُعْتَلَ أَو الْمَرِيضِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.307
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from
Ammar from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about the sick person, whether it is permissible for him to
stand on his bed and prostrate on the ground?
Imam {a.s} said: “If the bed is thick to the extent of a brick (ajurrah) or less, then it is
correct for him to stand on it and prostrate on the ground. But if it is more than that,
then no.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدَّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةً عَنْ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْمَرِيضِ أَيَجِلُّ لَهُ أَنْ يَقُومَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ وَ يَسْجُدَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ قَالَ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ الْفِرَاشُ
غَلِيظاً قَدْرَ آجُرَّةٍ أَوْ أَقَلَّ اِسْتَقَامَ لَهُ أَنْ يَقُومَ عَلَيْهِ وَ يَسْجُدَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَلا».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.411 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.307 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1043 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.358

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Hamdawayh from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from
Abu Ayyub from Isma'il ibn Jabir who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, saying, and a man asked him about a
person upon whom the prayer becomes due while he is in water, wading through it,
and he is not able to reach the ground.
Imam {a.s} said: “If he is in war or on a path among the paths of Allah {SWT}, then let him
gesture with indication (yumi’ ima’an, with his head or eyes).
But if he is on a trade journey, then it was not proper for him to enter the water until he
had prayed.”
He (narrator) said: “I asked: ‘What should he do?’”
Imam {a.s} said: “He must make it up when he comes out of the water, and indeed he
has been neglectful (of prayer).”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ عَنْ حَمْدَوَيْهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ
جَابِرٍ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أُبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ وَ سَأْلَهُ إِنْسَانٌ عَنِ الرَّجْلِ تُدْرِكُهُ الصَّلاَةُ وَ هُوَ فِي مَاءِ يَخُوضُهُ
لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ فِي حَرْبٍ أَوْ سَبِيلٍ مِنْ سُبُلِ اللّهِ فَلْيُومِ إِيمَاءً وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِي تِجَارَةٍ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ
يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أنْ يَخُوضَ الْمَاءَ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ» قَالَ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يَقْضِيهَا إِذَا خَرَجَ مِنَ ٱلْمَاءِ وَ قَدْ ضَيَّعَ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.382 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.307 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.141
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ziyad al-Karkhi who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “An old man is unable to stand, to go to
the toilet, and he cannot perform bowing (rukuh) and prostration (sujud).”
Imam {a.s} said: “Then let him gesture with his head by indication (ima'a), and if there is
someone who can raise the khumrah (a small prayer mat or place of prostration) to
him, then let him prostrate on it. If that is not possible for him, then let him gesture
with his head in the direction of the qiblah by indication.”
I asked: “And what about fasting?”
Imam {a.s} said: “If he has reached that condition, then Allah {SWT} has lifted the obligation
from him. But if he is able, then giving in charity a mudd of food in place of each day is
more beloved to me. And if he does not have the means for that, then there is nothing
upon him.”
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدِ الطَّيَالِسِيَّ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي زِيَادِ الْكَرْخِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ
شَيْخٌ لا يَسْتَطِيعُ الْقِيَامَ إِلَى الْخَلَاءِ وَ لا يُمْكِنُهُ الرُّكُوعُ وَ السُّجُودُ فَقَالَ «لِيُومِ بِرَأْسِهِ إِيمَاءً وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ مَنْ يَرْفَعُ
الْخُمْرَةَ إِلَيْهِ فَلْيَسْجُدْ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ ذَلِكَ فَلْيُومِ بِرَأْسِهِ نَحْوَ الْقِبْلَةِ إِيمَاء» قُلْتُ فَالصِّيَامُ قَالَ «فَإِذَا كَانَ فِي ذَلِكَ
اَلْحَدِّ فَقَدْ وَضَعَ اللهُ عَنْهُ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَهُ مَقْدُرَةُ فَصَدَقَةُ مُدَّ مِنْ طَعَامٍ بَدَلَ كُلِّ يَوْمِ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ يَسَارُ
ذَلِكَ فَلا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.365 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.307

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' from Tha'labah ibn Maymun from
Hammad ibn Uthman from Abdurrahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who
said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “One does not perform the obligatory prayer on a riding animal
except a sick person, who faces the qiblah with it, and Surah al-Fatihah suffices him.
For the obligatory prayer, he should place his face on whatever he is able to from
anything, and in the supererogatory prayer, he gestures by indication (ima'a).”

Scholar's Note:
And this report does not contradict what was narrated:
text_ar:
سَعْدْ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ
اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «لا يُصَلِّي عَلَى الدَّابَّةِ الْفَرِيضَةَ إِلَّ مَرِيضٌ يَسْتَقْبِلُ
بِهِ الْقِبْلَةَ وَ يُجْزِيهِ فَاتِحَةُ الْكِتَابِ وَ يَضَعُ بِوَجْهِهِ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ عَلَى مَا أَمْكَنَهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَ يُومِئُ فِي النَّافِلَةِ إِيمَاءَ».
ولا ينافي هذا الخبر ما رواه:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:
Ahmad ibn al-Nu'man asked Imam {a.s}, saying: “I pray in my litter (mahmil) while I am
ill”
Imam {a.s} said: “As for the supererogatory prayer, then yes (it is allowed); but as for the
obligatory prayer, then no.”
He (Mansur) said: “And Ahmad mentioned the severity of his pain, so he said:
‘I was severely ill, and I used to instruct them when the time of prayer arrived to make
the camel kneel for me, and I would be carried on my bed and placed down, and I
would pray. Then I would be carried on my bed and placed back in my litter’.”

Scholar's Note:
Because this report is to be understood as referring to recommendation (mustahabb),
not obligation or requirement, and what we have stated is further clarified by what was
narrated:
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَشيَمَ عَنْ مَنصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ النُعْمَانِ فَقَالَ أُصَلِّي فِي
مَحْمِلِي وَ أَنَا مَرِيضٍ قَالَ فَقَالَ «أَمَّا النَّافِلَةُ فَنَعَمْ وَ أَمَّا ٱلْفَرِيضَةُ فَلا» قَالَ وَ ذَكَرَ أَحْمَدُ شِدَّةَ وَجَعِهِ فَقَالَ أَنَا كُنْتُ
مَرِيضاً شَدِيدَ الْمَرَضِ فَكُنْتُ آمُرُهُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَتِ الصَّلاةُ يُنيخُوا بِي فَأُحْتَمَلُ بِفِرَاشِي فَأُوضَعُ فَأُصَلِّي ثُمَّ أُحْتَمَلُ
بِفِرَاشِي فَأُوضَعُ فِي مَحْمِلِي.
لان هذا الخبر محمول على الاستحباب دون الفرض والايجاب ، ويزيد ما قلناه بيانا ما رواه :

Because this report is to be understood as referring to recommendation (mustahabb),
not obligation or requirement, and what we have stated is further clarified by what was
narrated:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE PRAYER OF THE ONE IN NECESSITY
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdullah ibn
Sinan who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “May a man perform any of the obligatory
prayers while riding?”
Imam {a.s} said: “No, except out of necessity.”
text_ar:
محَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلَالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي
عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَيُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ شَيْئاً مِنَ ٱلْفُرُوضِ رَاكِباً فَقَالَ «لا إِلاَّ مِنْ ضَرُورَةِ».
٣١ - باب من الصلوات المرغب فيها

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Sulayman who said:
I wrote to Imam al-Hadi {a.s}, peace be upon him, asking him: “What do you say about
the tasbih prayer in the litter (mahmil)?”
So Imam {a.s} wrote back: “If you are traveling, then pray (in the mahmil).”
text_ar:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَخْيَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى الرَّجُلِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي صَلاةٍ
اَلتَّسْبِيحِ فِي الْمَحْمِلِ فَكَتَبَ «إِذَا كُنْتَ مُسَافِراً فَصَلّ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.466 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.309 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1391 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.58
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hadi {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn Sulayman who said:
I wrote to Imam al-Hadi {a.s}, peace be upon him, asking him: “What do you say about
the tasbih prayer in the litter (mahmil)?”
So Imam {a.s} wrote back: “If you are traveling, then pray (in the mahmil).”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Dharih ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi who
said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’, may I count it
from my supererogatory prayers (nafilah)?
Imam {a.s} said: “Whenever you wish, by night or by day.”
text_ar:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ ذَرِيحِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ ٱلْمُحَارِبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ
عَنْ صَلاةٍ جَعْفَرِ أَحْتَسِبُ بِهَا مِنْ نَافِلَتِي فَقَالَ «مَا شِئتَ مِنْ لَيْلِ أَوْ نَهَارِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.309 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1391 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.58
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Dharih ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi who
said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’, may I count it

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Ja’far from Ali ibn al-Rayyan who said:
I wrote to the last (Imam al-Hadi {a.s}), peace be upon him, asking Imam {a.s}:
“About a man who performs two rak‘ahs of the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’, then is hurried by a
need or interrupted by an incident from completing the final two rak‘ahs.
Is it permissible for him to complete it after he finishes his need, even if he stood up
from his place, or is it not counted unless he begins the prayer anew and performs all
four rak‘ahs in one sitting?”
So Imam {a.s} wrote: “Yes, if something unavoidable interrupts him from that, then let
him interrupt it, then return and build upon what remains of it, Allah {SWT} willing.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الرِّيَّانِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى ٱلْمَاضِي الْأَخِيرِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أُسْأَلُهُ عَنْ رَجْلٍ صَلَّى
صَلاةَ جَعْفَرٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يُعَجَّلُهُ عَنِ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ حَاجَةً أَوْ يَقْطَعُ ذَلِكَ بِحَادِثِ أَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يُتِمَّهَا إِذَا فَرَغَ
مِنْ حَاجَتِهِ وَ إِنْ قَامَ عَنْ مَجْلِسِهِ أَمْ لا يَخْتَسِبُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّ أَنْ يَسْتَأْنِفَ الصَّلَاةَ وَ يُصَلِّيَ الْأَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ كُلِّهَا فِي مَقَامِ
وَاجدٍ فَكَتَبَ «بَلَى إِنْ قَطَعَهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ أَمْرٌ لا بُدَّ مِنْهُ فَلْيَقْطَعْ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ لْيَرْجِعْ فَلْيَبْنِ عَلَى مَا بَقِيَ مِنْهَا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
تَعَالَى».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.554 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.309 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1391 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.59 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.88 p.213
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hadi {a.s}
text_chunk:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Ja’far from Ali ibn al-Rayyan who said:
I wrote to the last (Imam al-Hadi {a.s}), peace be upon him, asking Imam {a.s}:
“About a man who performs two rak‘ahs of the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’, then is hurried by a
need or interrupted by an incident from completing the final two rak‘ahs.
Is it permissible for him to complete it after he finishes his need, even if he stood up
from his place, or is it not counted unless he begins the prayer anew and performs all
four rak‘ahs in one sitting?”
So Imam {a.s} wrote: “Yes, if something unavoidable interrupts him from that, then let
him interrupt it, then return and build upon what remains of it, Allah {SWT} willing.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurarah
from Isa ibn Abdullah from his father from his grandfather from Imam Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam Ali {a.s} said: “Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, has said:
‘Indeed, My servant seeks guidance from Me {AZJ} (performs istikhara), so I choose what
is best for him, yet he becomes angry.’” (Hadith Qudsi)
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ
أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَدِّهِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «قَالَ اللهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «إِنّ عَبْدِي يَسْتَخِيرُنِي فَأَجِيرُ لَهُ فَيَغْضَبُ» ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.309 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1418
source_scholar: Amir al-Mu’minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s} & Hadith-E-Qudsi
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zurarah
from Isa ibn Abdullah from his father from his grandfather from Imam Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam Ali {a.s} said: “Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, has said:

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad from Abu Abdillah
{a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, said:
“No servant appoints over his family a guardianship, better than two rak‘ahs that he
performs when he intends to travel. And he suplicates:
‘O’ Allah {SWT}, I entrust to You {AZJ} my self, my family, my wealth, my religion, my worldly
life, my Hereafter, my trust, and the ends of my deeds’,
except that Allah {SWT} grants him what he asks.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اِبْنِ أَبِي زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ
قَالَ رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «مَا اِسْتَخْلَفَ عَبْدٌ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ بِخَلافَةِ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ يَرْكَعُهُمَا إِذَا أَرَادَ
سَفَراً وَ يَقُولُ اللَّهُمّ إِنَّي أَسْتَوْدِعْكَ نَفْسِي وَ أَهْلِي وَ مَالِي وَ دِينِي وَ دُنْيَايَ وَ آخِرَتِي وَ أَمَانَتِي وَ خَوَاتِيمَ عَمَلِي
إلاَّ أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ مَا سَأَلَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.480 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.309 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.127
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
text_chunk:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad from Abu Abdillah

except that Allah {SWT} grants him what he asks.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from his father from al-Hasan
ibn al-Jahm from Abu Ali from al-Yasa‘ al-Qummi who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I desire something and I seek guidance
from Allah {SWT} (perform istikhara) about it, but no clarity comes to mind regarding it,
should I do it or leave it?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Observe when you stand for prayer, for Satan is furthest from the
human being when he stands for prayer. So observe what settles in your heart, and act
upon it.
And open the Mushaf and look at the first thing you see in it act upon it, if Allah {SWT}, the
Exalted, wills.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ الْجَهِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيَّ
عَنِ ٱلْيَسَعِ الْقُمِّيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أُرِيدُ الشَيْءَ فَأَسْتَجِيرُ اللَّهَ فِيهِ فَلا يُوفَقُ فِيهِ الرَّأْيُ أَفْعَلُهُ
أَوْ أَدَعُهُ فَقَالَ «أنظُر إِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَانَ أَبْعَدُ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ ٱلْإِنْسَانِ إِذَا قَامَ إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ فَانْظُرْ إِلَى
شَيْءٍ يَقَعُ فِي قَلْبِكَ فَخُذْ بِهِ وَ اِفْتَحِ ٱلْمُصْحَفَ فَانْظُرْ إِلَى أَوَّلِ مَا تَرَى فِيهِ فَخُذْ بِهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.310 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, Vol.1 p.324 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1416 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.78
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from his father from al-Hasan
ibn al-Jahm from Abu Ali from al-Yasa‘ al-Qummi who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I desire something and I seek guidance
from Allah {SWT} (perform istikhara) about it, but no clarity comes to mind regarding it,

Imam {a.s} said: “Observe when you stand for prayer, for Satan is furthest from the

And open the Mushaf and look at the first thing you see in it act upon it, if Allah {SWT}, the

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna al-Hannat from Abu Basir who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “Whoever prays four rak‘ahs with
two hundred recitations of ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas); fifty times in each
rak‘ah, will not finish the prayer while there remains between him and Allah {SWT}, the
Mighty and Majestic, a single sin except that it is forgiven for him.”
text_ar:
سَهَلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ مُثَنَّى الْحَنَاطِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أُبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:
«مَنْ صَلَّى أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ بِمِائَتَيْ مَرَّةٍ - قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدْ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً لَمْ يَنْفَتِلْ وَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ
وَ جَلَّ ذَنْبٌ إِلاَّ غُفِرَ لَهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.468 • Al-Amali (Lil-Saduq), Vol.1 p.98 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.310 • Al- Wafi, Vol.9 p.1395 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.113 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.88 p.171 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.5 p.703 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.6 p.296
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna al-Hannat from Abu Basir who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “Whoever prays four rak‘ahs with

Mighty and Majestic, a single sin except that it is forgiven for him.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yahya, by his chain of transmission, raised it to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “Whoever prays two rak‘ahs with ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’
(Surah Ikhlas) recited sixty times in each rak‘ah, will finish the prayer and there will
remain no sin between him and Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى بِإِسْنَادِهِ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ إِ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» فِي
كُلٍّ رَكْعَةٍ سِتَّينَ مَرَّةً اِنْفَتَلَ وَ لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ اللّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ ذَنْبٌ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.468 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.564 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.310
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Yahya, by his chain of transmission, raised it to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “Whoever prays two rak‘ahs with ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’
(Surah Ikhlas) recited sixty times in each rak‘ah, will finish the prayer and there will
remain no sin between him and Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from some of our companions from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha
{a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Ridha {a.s} said: “Whoever prays Maghrib and after it prays four rak‘ahs and
does not speak until he completes ten rak‘ahs, reciting in each rak‘ah ‘al-Hamd’
(Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), it will be equal to the
freeing of ten slaves.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ بَعْضٍ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرَّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلامُ قَالَ: «مَنْ صَلَّى
الْمَغْرِبَ وَبَعْدَهَا أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ عَشْرَ رَكَعَاتٍ يَقْرَأَ فِي كُلَّ رَكْعَةِ - بِالْحَمْدِ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ ٱَللَهُ
أَحَدٌ» كَانَتْ عِدْلَ عَشرٍ رِقَابٍ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.468 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.310 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1398 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.117 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.5 p.704
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from some of our companions from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha
{a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Ridha {a.s} said: “Whoever prays Maghrib and after it prays four rak‘ahs and
does not speak until he completes ten rak‘ahs, reciting in each rak‘ah ‘al-Hamd’
(Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), it will be equal to the
freeing of ten slaves.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, on behalf
of Ibn Asbat, and said to Imam {a.s}:
“What do you see for him (Ibn Asbat)?”, while Ibn Asbat was present and we were all
intending to travel by sea or land to Egypt, and he informed Imam {a.s} about the land
route.
So Imam {a.s} said: “Go to the mosque at a time other than the time of an obligatory
prayer, and pray two rak‘ahs, and seek guidance from Allah {SWT} (perform istikhara) one
hundred times, then see what settles in your heart, and act upon it.”
And al-Hasan said to Imam {a.s}: “The land route is more beloved to me.”
Imam {a.s} said: “And to me as well.”
text_ar:
احمد بن محمد عن ابن فضال قال : سأل الحسن بن الجهم ابا الحسن الرضا عليه السلام لابن أسباط فقال له :
ما ترى له وابن أسباط حاضر ونحن جميعا نركب البحر أو البر إلى مصر وأخبره بخبر طريق البر فقال : إنت
المسجد في غر وقت صلاة فريضة فصل ركعتين واستخر الله مائة مرة ثم انظر أي شئ يقع في قلبك فاعمل
به ، وقال له الحسن : البر أحب إلي قال : وإلي.
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.310
source_scholar: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
text_chunk:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, on behalf
of Ibn Asbat, and said to Imam {a.s}:
“What do you see for him (Ibn Asbat)?”, while Ibn Asbat was present and we were all
intending to travel by sea or land to Egypt, and he informed Imam {a.s} about the land
route.
So Imam {a.s} said: “Go to the mosque at a time other than the time of an obligatory
prayer, and pray two rak‘ahs, and seek guidance from Allah {SWT} (perform istikhara) one
hundred times, then see what settles in your heart, and act upon it.”
And al-Hasan said to Imam {a.s}: “The land route is more beloved to me.”
Imam {a.s} said: “And to me as well.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Isma'il by al-Fadl ibn Shadhan by Safwan from Ibn Muskan by Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi:
A man complained to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, of poverty and hardship in
trade after having previously been in ease, that whenever he set out for something, his
livelihood became constrained.
So Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, instructed him to go to the standing place of
the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, between His {saws}
grave and the pulpit, and to perform two rak‘ahs and to say one hundred times:
“O’ Allah {SWT}, I ask You {AZJ} by Your strength, by Your power, by Your might, and by that
which Your knowledge encompasses, to ease for me the most abundant in provision,
the most encompassing in bounty, and the best in outcome of trades.”
The man said: “So I did what Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, commanded me to
do, and thereafter I never set out in any direction except that Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and
Majestic, provided for me.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيّ الْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: شَكَا رَجُلْ
إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ ٱلْفَاقَةَ وَ الْحُرْفَةَ فِي التَّجَارَةِ بَعْدَ يَسَارٍ قَدْ كَانَ فِيهِ مَا يَتَوَجَّهُ فِي حَاجَةٍ إِلا ضَاقَتْ
عَلَيْهِ الْمَعِيشَةُ فَأَمَرَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ - مَقَامَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى آللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بَيْنَ ٱلْقَبْرِ وَ ٱلْمِنْبَرِ
فَيُصَلِّيَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَقُولَ مِائَةَ مَرَّةِ - « اللَّهُمّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلْكَ بِقُوَّتِكَ وَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ وَ بِعِزَّتِكَ وَ مَا أَحَاطَ بِهِ عِلْمُكَ أَنْ تُيَسِّرَ
لِي مِنَ التَّجَارَةِ أَسْبَغَهَا رِزْقاً وَ أَعَمَّهَا فَضْلاً وَ خَيْرَهَا عَاقِبَةً» قَالَ الرَّجُلُ فَفَعَلْتْ مَا أَمَرَنِي بِهِ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ فَمَا تَوَجَّهْتُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي وَجْهِ إِلاَّ رَزَقَنِيَ اللَهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَ

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
A man came to Imam al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, and said to him: “O’ son of the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, I have dependents and I am in debt, and my condition has
become severe, so teach me a supplication which, if I supplicate to Allah {SWT}, the
Mighty and Majestic, with it, He {AZJ} will provide for me.”
Imam {a.s} said: “O servant of Allah {SWT}, perform ablution and perfect your ablution,
then pray two rak‘ahs, completing the bowing and prostration in them. Then say;
‘O’ Majid, O’ Generous, O’ One, O’ Generous, I turn to You {AZJ} by (Prophet) Muhammad
{saws}, Your Prophet, the Prophet of mercy.
O’ Muhammad {saws}, O’ Messenger of Allah {SWT}, I turn through you to Allah {SWT}, your
Lord {AZJ} and the Lord {AZJ} of all things, that He {AZJ} may send blessings upon (Prophet)
Muhammad {saws} and upon the family of his household, and I ask You {AZJ} for a breath
of Your mercy, an easy opening, and a vast provision by which I may gather my
scattered state, settle my debt, and seek help through it for my dependents’.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي دَاوُدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى الرِّضَا
عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا اِبْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ إِنَّي ذُو عِيَالٍ وَ عَلَيَّ دَيْنٌ وَ قَدِ اِشتَدَّثْ حَالِي فَعَلَّمْنِي دُعَاءَ إِذَا دَعَوْتُ ٱَللَّهَ
عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ بِهِ رَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ فَقَالَ «يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ تَوَضَّأْ وَ أَسْبِغْ وُضُوءَكَ ثُمَّ صَلَّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ تُتِمُ الرُّكُوعَ وَ السُّجُودَ فِيهِمَا
ثُمَّ قُلْ يَا مَاجِدُ يَا كَرِيمُ يَا وَاجِدُ يَا كَرِيمُ أَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَيْكَ بِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيِّكَ نَبِيِّ الرَّحْمَةِ يَا مُحَمَّدُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي أَتَوَجَّهُ
بِكَ إِلَى اللّهِ رَبِّكَ وَ رَبِّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ وَ أَسْأَلُكَ نَفْحَةً مِنْ نَفَحَاتِكَ وَ فَثْحاً
يَسِيراً وَ رِزْقاً وَاسِعاً أَلُمُ بِهِ شَعْتِي وَ أَقْضِي بِهِ دَيْنِي وَ أُسْتَعِينُ بِهِ عَلَى عِيَالِي ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.473 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.311 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1430 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.124

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
From him, from Ibn Abi Najran from Sabbah al-Hadhdha’ from Abu al-Tayyar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “There was something in my possession
but it was lost and I fell into great distress because of it.”
Imam {a.s} said to me: “Do you have a shop in the market?”
I said: “Yes, but I have left it.”
Imam {a.s} said: “When you return to Kufa, sit in your shop and sweep it. And when you
intend to go out to your marketplace, then pray two or four rak‘ahs, then say at the end
of your prayer:
‘I turn with no power or strength from myself, but with Your power, O’ Lord {AZJ}, and
Your strength. I disassociate from any power and strength except through You {AZJ}. So
You {AZJ} are my strength, and from You {AZJ} is my power. O’ Allah {SWT}, provide me from
Your vast bounty a plentiful, good provision while I remain in ease and well-being, for
none possesses it besides You {AZJ}.”
He (Abu al-Tayyar) said: “So I did that, and I would go out to my shop until I feared that
the tax collector would seize me, for the rent of my shop, while I had nothing. Then a
merchant came with goods and said to me:
‘Will you rent me half of your house?’
So I rented him half of my house for the (amount equal to) rent of the whole house.
Then he (the merchant) showed me his merchandise, and someone offered him a
price for it but he did not sell it.
So I (Abu al-Tayyar) said to him (the merchant): “Would you like something better? Sell
me a bundle of your goods, and I will sell it and take the profit and return to you its
price.”
He (the merchant) said: “How can I trust you with that?”
I (Abu al-Tayyar) said: “You have my oath to Allah {SWT} for that.”
So he (the merchant) said: “Take a bundle of it.”
So I took it, marked it, and a severe cold came, and I sold the goods that same day.
I gave him his price and took the profit. I continued to take a bundle, sell it, take the
profit, and return to him the capital until I was able to ride animals, purchase slaves,
and build houses.
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَبَّاحِ الْحَذَّاءِ عَنْ أَبِي الطَيَّارِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي يَدِي
شَيْءُ فَتَفَرَّقَ وَ ضِقْتُ بِهِ ضَيْقاً شَدِيداً فَقَالَ لِي «أ لَكَ حَانُوتُ فِي السُّوقِ» فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ وَ قَدْ تَرَكْتُهُ فَقَالَ «إِذَا
رَجَفْتَ إِلَى الْكُوفَةِ فَاقْعُدْ فِي حَانُوتِكَ وَ أكُنُسْهُ وَ إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ إِلَى سُوقِكَ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ
ثُمَّ قُلْ فِي دُبُرٍ صَلاتِكَ - تَوَجَّهْتُ بِلاَ حَوْلٍ مِنَّي وَ لاَ قُوَّةٍ وَ لَكِنْ بِحَوْلِكَ يَا رَبِّ وَ قُوَّتِكَ وَ أَبْرَأَ مِنَ الْحَوْلِ وَ الْقُوَّةِ
إلاَّ بِكَ فَأَنْتَ حَوْلِي وَ مِنْكَ قُوَّتِي اللَّهُمَّ فَارْزُقْنِي مِنْ فَضْلِكَ ٱلْوَاسِعِ رِزْقاً كَثِيراً طَيِّباً وَ أَنَا خَافِضٌ فِي عَافِيَتِكَ
فَإِنَّهُ لا يَمْلِكُهَا أَحَدٌ غَيْرُكَ » قَالَ فَفَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ وَ كُنْتُ أَحْرُجْ إِلَى دُكَّانِي حَتَّى خِفْتُ أَنْ يَأْخَذَنِي الْجَابِي بِأْجْرَةِ
دُكَّانِي وَ مَا عِنْدِي شَيْءُ قَالَ فَجَاءَ جَالِبٌ بِمَتَاعِ فَقَالَ لِي تُكْرِينِي نِصْفَ بَيْتِكَ فَأْكْرَيْتُهُ نِصْفَ بَيْتِي بِكِرَى الْبَيْتِ
كُلَّهِ قَالَ وَ عَرَضَ عَلَيّ مَتَاعَهُ فَأُعْطِي بِهِ شَيْئاً لَمْ يَبِعَهُ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ هَلْ لَكَ إلَى خَيْرٍ تَبِيعُنِي عِدْلا مِنْ مَتَاعِكَ هَذَا
أَبِيعُهُ وَ آخُذُ فَضْلَهُ وَ أَدْفَعُ إِلَيْكَ ثَمَنَهُ قَالَ فَكَيْفَ لِي بِذَلِكَ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ لَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ بِذَلِكَ قَالَ فَخُذْ عِدْلاً مِنْهَا
فَأَخَذْتُهُ وَ رَقَمْتُهُ وَ جَاءَ بَرْدٌ شَدِيدٌ فَبِعْتُ ٱلْمَتَاعَ مِنْ يَوْمِي وَ دَفَعْتُ إِلَيْهِ التَمَنَ وَ أَخَذْتُ ٱلْفَضْلَ فَمَا زِلْتُ آخُذُ
عِدْلاً وَ أَبِيعُهُ وَ آخُذُ فَضْلَهُ وَ أَرُدُ عَلَيْهِ رَأْسَ الْمَالِ حَتَّى رَكِبْتُ الدَّوَابّ وَ اِشتَرَيْتُ الرَّقِيقَ وَ بَنَيْتُ ٱَلدُورَ.

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Abdullah ibn
Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Uruwah, the nephew of Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from his uncle Shu'ayb who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever feels hunger, let him perform
ablution, and let him pray two rak‘ahs, completing their bowing and prostration, and
say: ‘O’ Lord {AZJ}, I am hungry, so feed me’, for indeed he will be fed immediately.”
text_ar:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ إبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ إسْحَاقَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ
عُرْوَةَ اِبْنِ أُخْتِ شعَيْبِ الْعَقَرْقُوفِيَّ عَنْ خَالِهِ شَعَيْبٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ : «مَنْ جَاعَ فَلْيَتَوَضَّاْ وَ
ليُصَلٌ رَكْعَتَيْنٍ وَ يُتِمُّ رُكُوعَهُمَا وَ سُجُودَهُمَا وَ يَقُولُ يَا رَبّ إِنَّي جَائِعٌ فَأَطْعِمْنِي فَإِنَّهُ يُطْعَمُ مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ».
cross_references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.312
source_scholar: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Abdullah ibn
Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Uruwah, the nephew of Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from his uncle Shu'ayb who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever feels hunger, let him perform
ablution, and let him pray two rak‘ahs, completing their bowing and prostration, and
say: ‘O’ Lord {AZJ}, I am hungry, so feed me’, for indeed he will be fed immediately.”

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Salih who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “Whoever performs ablution and
perfects the ablution, and then prays two rak‘ahs, completing their bowing and
prostration, then sits and praises Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, and sends
blessings upon the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family,
and then asks Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, for his need;
Then indeed he has sought goodness in its proper place. And whoever seeks goodness
in its proper place will not be disappointed.”
text_ar:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ صَالِحِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: («مَنْ تَوَضّاً
فَأَحْسَنَ الْوُضُوءَ وَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَتَمَّ رُكُوعَهُمَا وَ سُجُودَهُمَا ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فَأَثْنَى عَلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ صَلَّى عَلَى
رَسُولٍ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ثُمَّ سَأَلَ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ حَاجَتَهُ فَقَدْ طَلَبَ الْخَيْرَ فِي مَظَانِّهِ وَ مَنْ طَلَبَ ٱلْخَيْرَ فِي
مَظَانِّهٍ لَمْ يَخِبُ».

author: Shaykh al-Tusi
chapter_title: THE RECOMMENDED PRAYERS
text_en:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abdullah ibn Uthman, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from
Abdullah ibn Waddah and Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Isma'il ibn al-Arqat and his mother Umm Salamah, the
sister of Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I (Isma'il ibn al-Arqat) fell severely ill during the Month of Ramadan, to the point that I
was near death, and the Banu Hashim gathered at night for the funeral, believing that
I was dead.
My mother (Umm Salamah) became distressed over me, so Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be
upon him, my maternal uncle, said to her:
“Go up to the roof of the house, face the sky, and pray two rak‘ahs. When you finish
the prayer with the salam, then say;
‘O’ Allah {SWT}, You {AZJ} granted him to me when he was nothing.
O’ Allah {SWT}, I now ask You {AZJ} to grant him to me anew so lend him to me.’”
He (Isma'il ibn al-Arqat) said:
“So she did that, and I regained consciousness and sat up, and they brought suhur for
themselves harisah, and they ate it for suhur, and I ate with them.”
text_ar:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْمَاعِيلَ السِّرَّاجِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ وَضَاحِ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ
أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ الْأَرْقَطِ وَ أَمْهُ أُمْ سَلَمَةَ أُخْتُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: مَرِضْتُ فِي شَهْرٍ رَمَضَانَ
مَرَضاً شَدِيداً حَتَّى تَلِفُتُ وَ اِجْتَمَعَتْ بَنُو هَاشِمِ لَيْلاً لِلْجَنَازَةِ وَ هُمْ يَرَوْنَ أَنَّي مَيّتْ فَجَزِعَتْ أَمِّي عَلَيّ فَقَالَ لَهَا
أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ خَالِي «اِصْعَدِي إِلَى فَوْقِ البَيْتِ فَابْرُزِي إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَ صَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَإِذَا سَلَّمْتِ فَقُولِي
- آَللَّهُمّ إِنَّكَ وَهَبْتَهُ لِي وَ لَمْ يَكُ شَيْئاً اللَّهُمَّ وَ إِنِّي اِسْتَوْهَبْتُكَهُ مُبْتَدِئاً فَأْعِرْنِيهِ » قَالَ فَفَعَلَتْ فَأَفَقْتُ وَ قَعَدْتُ وَ
دَعَوْا بِسَحُورٍ لَهُمْ هَرِيسَةٍ فَتَسَحِّرُوا بِهَا وَ تَسَحِّرْتُ مَعَهُمْ.
